EVIDENCE DIGEST: NBC 1821 BG II (cotton)

Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers and trials, seed availability). Both names were searched: "variety_name" NBC 1821 BG II and "seednet_variety_name" NBC 1821 BG II. - Heat, salinity, flood, submergence, drought (trial-based): No evidence found.

- Disease resistance (wilt, leaf curl, blight, etc.): No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

- Sowing window: June to July; well-drained black and loam soil; sowing depth 3–5 cm. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-nath-bio-genes-nbc-1821-rana-900-bg-ii-cotton-seeds.php

- Multi-location or AICRP trial results for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL

No evidence found for NBHB-1851 or NBHB-11. No field-trial or agronomy result named either name. A Nath Bio-Genes Kashinath 2 cotton product was listed, but it is a different variety and was excluded. -- https://agroinfomart.com/Nath-Bio-genes-India-Ltd (background only, excluded for relevance)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NCS 2778 Bt2 / NCS 2778 BT2 (cotton). The evidence below mostly refers to the brand names "Armita NCS-2778 Bt-2" and "Armitha (NCS 2778)". I could not reach the Seednet portal, so the Seednet name has no direct evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds
A retailer page claims resilient performance in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh field conditions, but it gives no trial data, so I have not treated this as stress-tolerance evidence. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds

DISEASE AND PEST
The retailer lists the hybrid as carrying Bollgard II (Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab) technology for pest protection. This is a trait description on a sales page, not an efficacy study. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds
No disease-resistance evidence found. -- (none)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The 2025 CAI newsletter names "Armitha (NCS 2778)" as the hybrid used by a farmer in Nalgonda district, Telangana, in the 2023 season, under high-density planting at 90 cm x 18 cm spacing. The newsletter cites ICAR-CICR AICRP Bt cotton trial and evaluation reports for 2022-23 and 2023-24, but the text I retrieved gives no variety-level yield figures. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf
The retailer describes the hybrid as suited to high-density planting systems, with an erect canopy suited to mechanised operations. This is a sales claim. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Yield, maturity and fibre data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for parentage, marker or QTL studies for this variety. The Bollgard II trait description above is the only genetic detail, and it comes from the retailer page. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No lead breeder or scientist name found. -- (none)
Institution: the retailer attributes the variety to Nuziveedu Seeds. Armita (NCS-2778 Bt-2) by Nuziveedu Seeds is a Bollgard II hybrid cotton variety. This is a company attribution, not a public-institute record. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/armita-ncs2778-bt2-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Developing station or division: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
No official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page found for this variety or for Nuziveedu Seeds. The search returned only retailer and newsletter pages. A phone number that appeared in results belongs to a different variety (Nuziveedu Bhakti NCS BG-2) and was discarded. -- (none)

PUBLICATIONS

pest_resistance.summary: Leafhopper: in a 2011-12 and 2012-13 Warangal trial, non-Bt Orugallu Krishna had the lowest leafhopper count (1.53 per top three leaves); Neeraja was the only entry statistically on par. Chewing and other pests: Helicoverpa armigera, Spodoptera litura and Erias vitella larvae were present on non-Bt Orugallu Krishna but below the economic threshold; pink bollworm incidence was nil. These are comparative field observations in one trial series, not formal resistance ratings.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Orugallu Krishna (WGHH-2), cotton (Gossypium hirsutum)**

Name note: The CSC name "Orugallu Krishna" and the Seednet name "Orugallu Krishna (WGHH-2)" refer to the same entry. Every source below uses the WGHH-2 code or the bare name for this variety, so the evidence applies to both headings.

Search coverage: 4 web_search queries (release/traits, breeder/institution, research, seed). The Seednet portal, KrishiKosh, and AICRP annual reports were not queried directly. Release year (2010) and parentage (WGHP-1 x WGHP-2) come from the input record; I found no search source confirming either.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/central-telangana-zone/
- Early maturity and big boll size are described, but not as stress tolerance. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- In a 2011-12 and 2012-13 Warangal trial, the non-Bt Orugallu Krishna had the lowest leafhopper count (1.53 per top three leaves). Neeraja was the only entry statistically on par. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Helicoverpa armigera, Spodoptera litura, and Erias vitella larvae were present on non-Bt Orugallu Krishna but below the economic threshold. Pink bollworm incidence was nil. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Disease resistance: No evidence found.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Yield is given as 30-40 q/ha, with staple length of 26-28 mm, under wide adaptability. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf
- Listed among intra-specific cotton varieties/hybrids in the RARS Warangal cotton package of practices. -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/Cotton.pdf
- Used as the non-Bt comparison entry in the dual-toxin Bt hybrid trial at RARS Warangal, kharif 2011-12 and 2012-13. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Multi-location or AICRP yield data: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- No evidence found (no QTL, marker, or parentage-confirmation study located).

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing station: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Warangal, now under Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTAU/PJTSAU). The input record says ANGRAU; the search sources name PJTAU. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. Kaderbad Ravindranath is a cotton breeder linked to ANGRAU, but no source links him to Orugallu Krishna, so he is not attributed here. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaderbad_Ravindranath
- The station's mandate includes developing high-yielding G. hirsutum hybrids and varieties for rainfed and irrigated systems. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Station in-charge: Dr. Ravula Uma Reddy, Associate Director of Research, RARS Warangal. Email: adrwgl@pjtau.edu.in. Mobile: 8332970385. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/central-telangana-zone/
- Postal address: Office of the Associate Director of Research, RARS Warangal, Mulugu Road, Hanamkonda (Warangal). -- https://pjtau.edu.in/central-telangana-zone/
- Lead cotton breeder: No evidence found; institute-level contacts above.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Authors not captured in search snippet (2011-13). "Evaluation of dual toxin transgenic Bt cotton hybrids against insect pests of cotton." Semantic Scholar record (Kumar et al. listed by URL slug; verify before citing). -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/EVALUATION-OF-DUAL-TOXIN-TRANSGENIC-Bt-COTTON-PESTS-Kumar/ff339baebed6b00c9191cde23c1d1518263457ca
- Authors not captured in snippet (c. 2017-18). "Incidence and management of sucking pest complex in dual toxin transgenic Bt cotton hybrids." ResearchGate record; the abstract confirms the RARS Warangal trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324571370_Incidence_and_management_of_sucking_pest_complex_in_dual_toxin_transgenic_Bt_cotton_hybrids
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or release-notification record was found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- The Ekapas Telangana list includes Orugallu Krishna (WGHH-2) among recommended cotton options. This is not a seller listing. -- http://ekapas.com/telangana/
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales, or private dealer listing for Orugallu Krishna was found. The dealer pages returned were for other hybrids.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- The input record says "Not specified," and no source gave a notified state list. The only geographic evidence ties the variety to the Warangal station in Telangana. -- https://www.pjtau.edu.in/pdf1/7.pdf
- Official CSC/gazette notification, including states of recommendation: No evidence found.

The institution field in the input record combines three different bodies (TNAU Cotton Research Station, the ICAR-AICRP on Cotton, and VNMKV), and no search result confirmed which one released this variety. CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No institute-level or breeder contact was found for either name. The TNAU Cotton Research Station, Srivilliputhur "Varieties Released" page (https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/) is an unverified lead, since it lists released cotton varieties, but the retrieved text did not show PA 833 or PA-183.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No journal paper, AICRP or ICAR report, thesis, or KrishiKosh record named either variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Results were retail listings for generic "Kapas cotton seeds" with no variety name, plus Pakistani and US cultivar pages. None of them is a Tamil Nadu, NSC, state corporation, KVK, or SAU source for PA 833 or PA-183.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The states in the input record (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) could not be checked against any search result.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches used "PA-740" and "PA 740". All relevant pages use "PA 740" (the CSC/variety name and the Seednet name "PA-740" refer to the same variety). The Seednet portal itself returned no results in these searches. The crop is desi cotton, Gossypium arboreum, not G. hirsutum.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The release paper reports the variety as tolerant to bacterial blight and Alternaria leaf spot, and tolerant to sucking pests. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The paper only describes consistent yield across the South Zone under rainfed conditions. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight and Alternaria leaf spot tolerance and sucking-pest tolerance, as listed above. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- No evidence found for specific pest or disease ratings beyond these.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mean seed cotton yield was 13.63 q/ha, against 13.67 q/ha for the zonal check and 13.50 q/ha for the local check. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- On-farm trials showed about 17.81% higher seed cotton yield than check PA 402. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Fibre traits: mean length 27.86 mm, strength 25.06 g/tex, micronaire 5.06. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- The release paper describes the fibre as long staple with high strength and acceptable micronaire. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Maturity, plant density and fertiliser recommendations: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Breeding method: pedigree method. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- Parentage "PA 183 x PA 375" comes from the task input only. No search result confirmed it.
- QTL, marker or genomic studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety was developed at the Cotton Research Station, Maheboob Baugh Farm, Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth (VNMKV), Parbhani. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
- The research station page lists PA 740 among its desi cotton releases (PA 528, PA 740, PA 810, PA 812, PA 837). -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php
- The university's Nanded station page records PA 740 as released by the Central Variety Release Committee in 2019. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- Named lead breeder: No evidence found. The release-paper authors are VN Chinchane, KS Baig, SB Borgaonkar and AH Rathod. Their roles as breeders are not stated in the search results. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or direct contact was found in the search results.
- Institute-level: Cotton Research Station Mahboob Baugh Farm, Parbhani - 431 401 (MS), as listed. No email or phone shown. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php
- University postal address, Parbhani - 431 402, from a VNMKV document (MoU text). No email or phone shown. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- The Nanded station page shows an "Officer Incharge" label, but the name is cut off in the search result, so it is not recorded here. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/research_ResearchStations.php

PUBLICATIONS
- Chinchane, V. N.; Baig, K. S.; Borgaonkar, S. B.; Rathod, A. H. (2020). PA 740: High yielding, superior fibre quality Desi cotton (Gossypium arboreum) variety for South zone of India. The Pharma Innovation Journal (chemijournal.com), Vol. 8, Issue 6, pp. 1951-1954 -- https://www.doi.org/10.22271/chemi.2020.v8.i6ab.11051
- Journal name is taken from the chemijournal.com site. The search result does not show the journal title explicitly.
- No AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, or QTL papers on PA 740 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers for PA 740. The seed-related results returned unrelated products (US cotton seed, a Punjab subsidy notice that does not name PA 740, and craft threads). Seednet was not returned by any search.
- The VNMKV accreditation report mentions a state seed corporation (Mahabeej) producing seed of a different cotton variety (NHH-44), not PA 740. -- https://vnmkv.ac.in/static/documents/accreditation/UNIVERSITY_VNMKV_SSR.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released for rainfed South Zone (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu) by the Central Variety Release Committee in 2019. Telangana is included in this source but was not in the task input. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- Also released for Marathwada region of Maharashtra by Joint AGRESCO and notified in 2019. -- https://www.vnmkv.ac.in/Research/CottonResearchStationNanded
- The release paper gives the same South Zone rainfed recommendation. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=11051&issue=6&si=false&vol=8&year=2020

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PBH 115 (cotton, Gossypium hirsutum)

Name checked: "PBH 115" (CSC minutes name) and "PBH 115" (Seednet name). The two names are identical, so one search set covered both.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The search returned a Pakistani cotton line, NIBGE-115, and it is not this variety.
DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The search returned NIBGE-115 (CLCuD tolerance) and Prabhat Supercot PCH-115 (a Bt hybrid), and neither is this variety.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The search returned no trial or agronomy page naming PBH 115.
GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The search returned no marker or QTL study naming PBH 115.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page names a breeder or developing station for PBH 115.
CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No Punjab Agricultural University contact page or PBH 115 contact turned up.
PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis names PBH 115.
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The only "PCH 115" listings are for Prabhat Seeds Supercot PCH-115 BG-II, a private hybrid, and they are discarded as a different product. Other listings for it (IndiaMART, Kisan Center) are discarded for the same reason.
RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. No page links PBH 115 to Punjab, Haryana or Rajasthan.

Discarded results (name resemblance only): NIBGE-115 (Pakistan, not PBH 115); Prabhat Supercot PCH-115 BG-II hybrid (private, not PBH 115); DMC 115 pearl cotton thread (not a crop).

Unverified lead, not attributed to PBH 115: a PAU Bt cotton release named "PAU Bt 5 (PBH Bt 21)" was found. Its DOI is 10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z and it is at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z. It reports release in 2023 for Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan, and its pedigree is LH 2298 × PAU Bt 1. The "PBH Bt 21" designation is different from "PBH 115", and the 2023 release year differs from the 2022-06-17 date in the record, so I have not linked it to this variety. The record's name and release date should be checked against the CSC minutes and the Seednet entry before any link is made.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule Satpuda (JLA-1207), cotton (Gossypium arboreum, desi)**

**Name check:** The search results used "Phule Satpuda (JLA-1207)" for both the CSC-minutes name (variety_name) and the Seednet name (seednet_variety_name). The only difference is spacing, so I treat them as one variety. No Seednet portal page was retrieved directly, so the Seednet evidence below comes from the notification lists and the ICAR report. The searches did not return CSC minutes themselves.

**Discrepancies to resolve:**
- Release year: the record says 2023-05-02. A notification dated 25 September 2023 is reported in news coverage (The notification was released by Pankaj Yadav, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare on 25th September 2023. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/). A review lists JLA-1207 with the year 2022 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review).
- Institution: the record names the Oilseeds Research Station. The review attributes the desi cotton varieties, including JLA-1207, to Agriculture Research Station; Jalgaon, Maharashtra, Agriculture Research Station, Jalgaon; affiliated to MPKV, Rahuri is the prime research center (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review).
- Parentage (JLA-794 x JLA-104): not confirmed by any retrieved source.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Suitable for rainfed conditions; resistant to jassids and bacterial leaf blight, and moderately resistant to grey mildew -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Desi cotton in general is described as resilient to drought and pests, but this is not variety-specific (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review).

**DISEASE AND PEST**

- Pest resistance beyond jassids: No evidence found.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**

- Multi-location trial data and the original release trial details: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Parentage JLA-794 x JLA-104: No evidence found in retrieved sources.
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing institution: the Agriculture Research Station, Jalgaon, affiliated to MPKV Rahuri, is credited with desi cotton varieties including JLA-1207 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378713890_Significance_of_desi_Cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_-A_Brief_Review
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RVA 1001 / RAH-100 (cotton, Kapas): EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search log: 4 web_search queries run. Query 1 covered "RVA 1001 asalio cotton variety". Query 2 covered "RAH-100 cotton variety developed by". Query 3 covered "RVA 1001 cotton research paper trial". Query 4 covered "RVSKVV KNK College of Horticulture Mandsaur cotton variety RVA 1001 seed". None returned a page that names RVA 1001 or RAH-100 together with cotton. Nothing below is attributed to this variety.

Name check: the evidence refers to neither name. "RVA 1001" and "RAH-100" both returned zero matching pages, and no Seednet page was returned. The "asalio" crop name also matched nothing, and the Seednet crop is COTTON (KAPAS).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Query 1 and query 3 returned only unrelated cotton trials and products: desi cotton varieties such as Aravinda, Srinandi, Yaganti and Veena, plus Kanchana (LPS 141) and LK-861 from a Rajendranagar package-of-practices PDF (https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/Cotton.pdf). None of these is RVA 1001 or RAH-100.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned US and Australian variety records (for example, cotton variety 781000G exhibits resistance to bollworm, cotton leafworm, pink bollworm, and tobacco bud worm, https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/7714201). These are other varieties and are discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Query 3 returned trial reports for other cultivars, such as the University of Georgia study on the cotton cultivar Deltapine 2038 B3XF (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378429025005507). It does not mention RVA 1001 or RAH-100 and is discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or pedigree source for RVA 1001 or RAH-100 was returned. The parentage string in the record, "( RAMPBS 155 X MCU5) X RAS- 299 - 1 X LARA 5166)", was not found in any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for this variety. The only Indian cotton breeder returned was Kaderbad Ravindranath, who at ANGRAU developed ten new cotton varieties such as Narasimha and Aravinda (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaderbad_Ravindranath). He is not linked to this variety, so he is not attributed to it. The institution in the record, RVSKVV's KNK College of Horticulture, Mandsaur, is a horticulture college. A RVSKVV page lists 12 departments including plant breeding and genetics and plant pathology (https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/institutions). No cotton programme or RVA 1001 release by that college was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only; no breeder contact found. Institute contact for College of Horticulture, Mandsaur (listed as the institution in the record; not confirmed as this variety's developer): contact info dean[dot]mandsaur[at]rvskvv[dot]net, address Mandsaur-485001, Mandsaur, Madhya Pradesh (https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/college-horticulture-mandsaur-0). Institution website: http://www.rvskvv.net (https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/institutions). The email address above is written in obfuscated form in the source; verify it on the official site before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming RVA 1001 or RAH-100 was returned. Query 3 returned only unrelated cotton items, such as USPTO patents for other cotton varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Query 4 returned a RVSKVV seed production page that describes Raj Vijay seed and planting materials produced as per state and national requirement (https://www.rvskvv.net/index.php/research/seed-production-programme). It does not name this variety, so it is not counted as a finding. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or dealer listing for RVA 1001 or RAH-100 was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record lists Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat, but no search result confirms this for the variety. The MP-state context above (the Mandsaur institution) is institutional, not variety-specific.

Overall: the record for RVA 1001 / RAH-100 could not be verified from these sources. The listed institution is a horticulture college, and the record's parentage and crop name should be checked against the CSC release minutes and the Seednet portal directly.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance mechanisms or trial data. Retailer pages state that the variety suits both irrigated and rain-fed conditions. This is a suitability claim, not a drought-tolerance finding. Gujarat is listed in the release record for irrigated conditions only.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. No evidence on heat tolerance was returned for this variety.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No evidence on salinity tolerance was returned for this variety.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No evidence on flood tolerance was returned for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerance to viral disease is claimed on retailer listings (not trial data). Tobacco streak virus (TSV) tolerance is claimed on a retailer listing. A general claim of disease, virus and pest resistance appears on another retailer page; this is a marketing claim, not trial data. No official trial evidence for disease resistance was found in the searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerance to the sucking pest complex is claimed on retailer listings, and one retailer page lists natural resistance to sucking insects. These are marketing claims, not trial data. Bollworm protection is stated on retailer pages as Bollgard II (Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab) transgenic protection. Pest-resistance evaluation in official trials: Not found in searched sources. IPM and Cry-toxin papers returned in the search did not name this variety and were excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. One retailer page states yield is 'based on agricultural practices' with no figure. No kg/ha value is available.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment or multi-location stability data for this variety were returned. The AICRP summary that came up names RCH 659, not RCH-971, and was excluded.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Retailer pages state suitability for irrigated and rain-fed conditions. EVIDENCE DIGEST: RCH-971 BG II (cotton)

Name check: the CSC release-minute name and the Seednet name are both "RCH-971 BG II", so every item below refers to the same name. I did not retrieve a seednet.gov.in page. All evidence comes from commercial seed-retailer pages and one 2025 journal article, so none of it is an official ICAR, CICR, or SAU source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Retailer pages describe tolerance to sucking pests and to viral disease, and say the variety suits both irrigated and rain-fed conditions. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://managramasethu.in/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-cotton-hybrid-seed
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no claims on these stresses for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Tolerance to TSV (tobacco streak virus) and the sucking pest complex is claimed on a retailer listing. -- https://kisanestore.com/products/cotton-rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii
A retailer page also lists "natural resistance to sucking insects" and a general claim of disease, virus and pest resistance. These are marketing claims, not trial data. -- https://agribegri.com/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.php
Bollgard II (Cry1Ac + Cry2Ab) bollworm protection is stated on retailer pages. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Pest-resistance evaluation in official trials: No evidence found. The IPM and Cry-toxin papers that came up do not name this variety, so I excluded them.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity of 150–160 days, early flowering, and boll weight of 6–7 g are listed. -- https://agribegri.com/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.php ; https://managramasethu.in/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-cotton-hybrid-seed
Sowing and agronomy: May–July sowing, dibbling at 2–3 cm depth, 4 ft row spacing, a seed rate of about 950 g per acre, and 5–7 irrigations. These are retailer specifications. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds ; https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Field demonstrations: a 2025 article reports 60 high-density planting (HDPS) demonstrations of RCH-971 BG-II, at 90 x 15 cm spacing against a 120 x 30 cm control, in Nandyal district, Andhra Pradesh, 2023-24 to 2024-25. The work was under an ICAR-CICR special project. The article does not report yield figures in the retrieved text. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue7S/PartD/S-8-7-12-416.pdf
Yield data for this variety: No evidence found. One retailer page says yield is "based on agricultural practices," with no figure.
Multi-location AICRP yield results for this variety: No evidence found. The AICRP summary that came up covers BG II hybrids in general and names RCH 659, not RCH-971, so I excluded it. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf (excluded)

GENETICS AND QTL
Trait construction: the hybrid is described as carrying BollGard II (two Cry genes). No parentage is given. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/rasi-swift-rch-971-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds
Parentage: No evidence found. The registration record says "Not specified".
QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developer and marketer: Rasi Seeds Pvt. Ltd. is the brand and company named on retailer listings. -- https://agribegri.com/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.php ; https://managramasethu.in/products/rasi-swift-rch-971-bgii-cotton-hybrid-seed

Institute or company contact page for Rasi Seeds: No evidence found for this variety. A Coimbatore address appears on a listing for RCH 2 BG II, a different variety, so I did not use it. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rch-2-bg-ii-cotton-21125879333.html (excluded)

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Health-desk HDPS demonstration study of RCH-971 BG-II in Nandyal district, Andhra Pradesh (exact title not retrieved). International Journal of Research in Agronomy 8(SP-7): 252-255 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue7S/PartD/S-8-7-12-416.pdf
Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP or ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, and conference papers naming this variety: No evidence found beyond the item above. The KrishiKosh and AICRP searches were not run as separate queries.

State Seed Corporation, NSC, KVK, or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

The same Rasi page describes RCH 951 as a CLCuV tolerant hybrid, meaning tolerance to cotton leaf curl virus. This is a manufacturer claim with no trial data attached. -- https://www.rasiseeds.com/cotton/rch-951/

Rasi Seeds' own corporate page describes its early cotton research hybrids (RCH 1 and RCH 2 in 1992), which is company history, not a link to this variety. -- http://www.rasi.in/rasiseeds/products.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found that RG-18 (or "RGT ��� 1") has any tested stress tolerance. Searches 1 and 3 returned no RG-18 record. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Nandyal Sanaga 1 (NBeG 3), released 2013 by ARS Nandyal for irrigated Andhra Pradesh, is listed as tolerant to drought and wilt. This matches the release year only, not the name, so it is not a confirmed match to this record. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gaur et al. (2019) reviews breeding for drought and heat adaptation in chickpea, with ANGRAU Nandyal among the contributing institutes. It does not mention RG-18. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/pbr.12641

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for RG-18 disease or pest resistance. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Nandyal Gram 452 (ANGRAU, RARS Nandyal, 2020) is listed as tolerant to pod borer Helicoverpa. It is a different variety. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Nandyal Sanaga 1 (unconfirmed match, see STRESS TOLERANCE) is listed as tolerant to wilt. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No RG-18 yield, maturity, or trial data found. Searches 1 and 3 returned no record of the name. Search 3 found no RG-18 trial data. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Nandyal Sanaga 1 (unconfirmed match): about 110 days, yield 23-24 q/ha, irrigated. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- A 2017-18 Rabi trial at RARS Nandyal (ANGRAU) evaluated chickpea cultivars for mechanical-harvest suitability. Its cultivar list was not captured, so RG-18 cannot be confirmed as included. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2018/vol7issue5/PartAJ/7-5-220-230.pdf
- Ratnam, Sowmya and Kishore Babu (2023) studied foliar nutrition on chickpea at RARS Lam, which is not variety-specific. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/TJRA/article/view/148699

GENETICS AND QTL
- No RG-18 genetic, pedigree, or QTL evidence found. The parentage SC-75 x RG-2-1 was not found in any result. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Barmukh et al. (2022) characterises QTL-hotspot introgression lines for drought adaptation. It is not about RG-18. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9730794/
- Bajaj et al. (2015) reports seed-weight and yield-component QTLs in a desi x kabuli mapping population. It is not about RG-18. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4365403/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Identity note: the variety name "RGT ��� 1" is corrupted in the input, and no search result matched it. The Seednet name "RG-18" is listed under cotton (kapas), which conflicts with the chickpea crop in the release record. No evidence was found linking RG-18 to chickpea. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No breeder name for RG-18 was found. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Institution context: ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Nandyal, is the chickpea research station in the search results and is the only ANGRAU chickpea centre named in the results. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34961053
- Veera Jayalakshmi is a Principal Scientist at ANGRAU RARS Nandyal and a chickpea breeder. Her link to RG-18 is not established. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/women-scientists-create-top-3-climate-smart-chickpea-varieties-in-india-for-2022

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. Name: Veera Jayalakshmi, role: Principal Scientist, ANGRAU RARS Nandyal (not confirmed as RG-18 breeder). Email as found: veera.jayalakshmi@gmail.com. Phone: not found. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/

PUBLICATIONS

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for either name. -- searched: https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html (no such data on page)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for RAHH 455 or Raichur Shakthi-455 (maturity, yield, trials). The AICRP page lists duration and seed-cotton yield only for other entries (LHDP 1, LAHB Cotton-1, LHDP Cotton-5), which do not concern this variety -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The page says the centre derived its varieties and hybrids, including RAHH 455, by the pedigree method, but it gives no parentage -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
RAHH 455 is listed among three intra-hirsutum hybrids developed at the AICRP on Cotton centre, UAS Raichur (Karnataka). The page does not name a breeder for RAHH 455 specifically -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
Name match: evidence refers to "RAHH 455" (code RAHH-455). No source used the name "Raichur Shakthi-455". The record's parentage ("Not specified") is unchanged.
Release date: the page gives release in 2015 and notification in 2016 (S.O. 3540(E)). The record's 2016-08-12 matches the notification year, not the 2015 release.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level contact on the AICRP on Cotton centre page (no breeder-specific contact found for RAHH 455): Dr. Jayaprakash Mohan Nidagundi, AICRP on Cotton, Main Agricultural Research Station, UAS Raichur, Karnataka, India, Pincode 584104; Mobile +91 9480653790; E-mail jaysun050@uasraichur.edu.in and jaysun050@rediffmail.com -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
Dr. Shivanand Hanchinal is listed on the same page as Scientist (Agricultural Entomology). He is not linked to RAHH 455 and is not a breeder for it; his contact details are not recorded here.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record for RAHH 455 or Raichur Shakthi-455 appeared in the search. The research search returned only unrelated pages (a Raichur cotton note on Scribd, a US patent for a different cultivar DP 455 BG/RR, and a Chinese cotton paper).

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed search returned only market price pages for cotton seed in Karnataka, which do not name this variety. No Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found. A dedicated Seednet query was not run because the four-search limit was reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Partly supported. The AICRP page says RAHH 455 was released for South Zone rainfed situations, without naming states. The state list (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh) on that page belongs to SUJAY (SCS 793), a different variety, so it must not be attributed to RAHH 455 -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html

The only pages that name this variety use "Ankur Samir BG II" (retailer spelling). They describe a commercial hybrid from Ankur Seeds, not a CSC-notified variety. Parentage is not specified, and no notification or release-minute record turned up.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to SAMIR BGII. The one page that names it describes irrigated cultivation only, not stress tolerance. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg

DISEASE AND PEST
Retailer listing says the hybrid carries Bollgard II (Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab) protection against specified bollworms. No disease-resistance data was given. This is a seller claim, not a trial result. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Retailer listing gives a crop duration of about 160–170 days and says the seed is suited to irrigated cultivation with medium maturity. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
Retailer listing reports an average yield of about 20.91 q/ha "under evaluated conditions" but names no trial, season or location. Treat as unverified. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No AICRP, ICAR or SAU trial entry for SAMIR BGII was found. The AICRP/CICR Bt cotton reports that appeared cover other entries. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Retailer listing gives the transgenic event as MON 15985 (Bollgard II). This is a transgene description, not QTL or marker work. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No QTL or marker study for SAMIR BGII was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: the retailer listing attributes the product to Ankur Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (brand "Ankur Seeds"). -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No breeder or lead scientist was named for SAMIR BGII. Company-level location only: an IndiaMART listing describes Ankur Seeds Pvt. Ltd. as a manufacturer based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. No email, phone or street address was given. -- https://www.indiamart.com/ankur-seeds-pvt-ltd-ahmedabad/

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches of journal and thesis-type results returned papers on other BG II lines (e.g., MRC-7201 BGII, heterosis studies on unnamed BG II hybrids) and none named SAMIR BGII. These are excluded.

Retailer listing: "Ankur Samir BG II Hybrid Cotton Seeds", 475 g pack, sold online by kisanshop.in. -- https://www.kisanshop.in/product/ankur-samir-bg
No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or official seed-portal listing was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SHAIV MC5444 BGII (Seednet name: SHAIV MC5444 BG II), cotton (kapas), code A050117783

Searches run: 4 (variety and crop; breeder and developer; research papers; seed availability). No retrieved page names either form of this variety, so every heading below reports no evidence. Pages about similarly named products were discarded under the strict-relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The variety-and-crop search returned only unrelated pages: US patent texts for other cotton cultivars (DP 543, DP 546, DP 579, 18R445B3XF, 565452G, PX4433-25WRF) and a Crystal Crop Protection page for SP 7272 BGII (https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Cotton/SP_7272_BGII). None of these mention MC5444.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The Springer pink bollworm study on BGII cotton in India (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-021-00393-7) concerns BGII cotton in general, not this variety, so it is discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The only trial-type hit was a ResearchGate study on Bt BGII upland cotton hybrids (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389601710_Assessment_of_heterosis_and_combining_ability_for_fibre_yield_its_contributing_and_quality_traits_in_Bt_BGII_upland_cotton_Gossypium_hirsutum_L). It names other parental lines and does not name MC5444, so it is discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The only QTL/marker hit was a Ravnaq upland cotton study (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9168987/), which concerns a different cultivar series and is discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No breeder or scientist is named for this variety. The Rallis Seeds page (https://www.rallis.com/innovation/seeds) describes the company's cotton and hybrid programmes but does not mention MC5444, so it is company context only. The Rallis About page (https://www.rallis.com/about-us) mentions its 2010-11 acquisition of Metahelix Life Sciences, which is also company context only. Parentage is not specified in the input, and no parentage was found.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute email, phone, postal address or contact page was found for this variety. Rallis's general corporate pages were retrieved but are not variety-specific, so they are not recorded here as contacts.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper names this variety. Retrieved items about BGII cotton in general (Springer and ResearchGate pink bollworm study, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-021-00393-7; ResearchGate refugia-in-bag study, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382146455_Blending_procedure_is_crucial_for_BG-II_cotton_hybrids_to_adhere_to_the_prescribed_'Refugia_in_Bag'_standards) do not name this variety and are discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. Retrieved listings were for other products: Tata Pravir (MC5403) BG II (https://www.kisanshop.in/product/tata-pravir-mc5403-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds) and Tata Diggaz (MC 5408 BGII), which appeared only in a snippet from https://agribegri.com/products/rasi-prime-rch-947-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.php. Both are different varieties, so they are discarded. Dealer listings for Speedboll, Brazil BG II, Nagraj, V-Sport, Sawaj, Sangram and Fortuner 555 were also returned and are discarded. The name "MC5444" does not appear in any retrieved listing.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No web evidence found. No evidence found for SRCH 207 BG II specifically. The only pest-related text came from pages about other products. The Nath KSCH 207 Himalaya BG II page claims sucking-pest tolerance, and the Nuziveedu Mallika NCS 207 BG II page claims resistance to American bollworm and spotted bollworm. Both were discarded as different varieties. Sri Rama's own product page for SRCH 207 BG II gives no pest-resistance information.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- The company listing gives plant height of 150-160 cm and 45-50 days to 50% flowering for Srch-207 BG II -- https://www.sriramaseeds.co.in/srch-207-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds.htm

drought.details: The SVPR 4 release description reports tolerance to drought, and a related publication describes it as highly tolerant to drought in the summer irrigated season. This agrees with the CSC record of tolerance to drought and high summer temperature. No physiological mechanism, stress index or field measurement for SVPR 4 appears in the search results.

heat.details: The CSC record states tolerance to the high temperature of the summer season. It is recommended for February-March sowing in summer irrigated tracts. The search results give no independent quantitative heat-tolerance data, so the rating rests on the CSC record and the season of adaptation.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance data for SVPR 4 appear in the search results.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for SVPR 4 appear in the search results.

disease_resistance.summary: No specific disease resistance is recorded for SVPR 4 (CSC: Not Specified). The search results mention disease-resistance donor screening in TNAU cotton proceedings, but nothing specific to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: SVPR 4 is moderately resistant to leaf hopper (jassid), according to the release description. It can spin 40s counts, which is a fibre quality trait and not a pest trait.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative yield for SVPR 4 is given in the snippets. It is described as a high yielding, superior medium staple cotton. SVPR 6 (TSH 04/115) was reported superior to SVPR 4 and Suraj in seed cotton yield. In the TNAU cotton proceedings, SVPR 4 x SCS 1001 gave 2138 kg/ha in 2024 and 2546 kg/ha in 2022 and was compared against SVPR 5, SVPR 6 and SVPR 3 as checks.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability analysis is available in the search results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Summer irrigated tracts of Tamil Nadu, sown in February-March. The TNAU crop production guide lists it for districts including Madurai, Virudhunagar, Tirunelveli, Trichy and Salem. Medium staple, spins 40s counts.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: STEM IS SLIGHTLY PUBESCENT, PIGMENTED WITH PURPLE COLOUR WHEN EXPOSED TO SUNLIGHT, AS IN MCU5. BRACT IS PIGMENTED WITH PURPLE COLOUR WHEN EXPOSED TO SUNLIGHT
agronomic_details.field_trials: SVPR 4 was included in frontline demonstrations (FLD) with SVPR 5, SVPR 6 and CO 17. Abstracts also report comparisons with MCU 5, in which MCU 5 registered a higher span length (2.5%) than SVPR 4. SVPR 4 is used as a check in TNAU cotton trials.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL, SNP or SSR markers for SVPR 4 are reported in the search results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: None found. Parentage is a hybrid derivative of MCU 5 and S 4727 (CSC record). The varieties have been used as parents in crosses, for example SVPR 4 x SCS 1001 and SVPR 4 x GJHV 398, in TNAU trials and studies.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CNA 1003 (Roja), G. arboreum cotton, ICAR-CICR

Name note: The release minutes name is "Cotton" and the Seednet name is "cotton." I did not search the Seednet portal directly. My queries used "CICR NA 1003" and "CNA 1003," and the only variety-name match was "CNA 1003 (Roja)" in an institutional review. The evidence below refers to that CNA 1003 name, not to the generic "Cotton" entry. Four searches were run, and the results are generic or institute-level unless stated otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for CNA 1003 specifically. The AICRP on cotton programme says it screens cotton genotypes for resistance to major pests and diseases, and for salinity and drought tolerance, but this is not tied to the variety -- https://circot.icar.gov.in/all-india-coordinated-research-project-cotton-quality-research

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for CNA 1003 specifically. The 2024-25 AICRP annual report describes disease surveillance across 364 villages in 42 districts, not this variety -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The 2024-25 AICRP report shows 10 non-Bt varieties notified that year, but CNA 1003 is not among the results shown -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for CNA 1003. Institute-level only: the CICR director's profile reports a genetic linkage map built from a wild species and fibre-quality gene mapping, not linked to this variety -- https://cicr.org.in/present/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- CNA 1003 (Roja) is listed among G. arboreum varieties from CICR -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140
- CNA1003 is among varieties that CICR's Crop Improvement Division maintains and multiplies, with single-plant selection over 2023-24 -- https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/
- Lead breeder or scientist name: not found in results.
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur, established 1976 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research (secondary source)
- Varietal release route: the Varietal Identification Committee and state release committees handle release, as described in -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- Institute-level: Director Dr. V. N. Waghmare (ICAR-CICR, Nagpur) -- https://cicr.org.in/present/
- Nagpur campus address: NH 44 (Nagpur Wardha Road), about 14 km from Nagpur Railway Station -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
- Sirsa campus: NH9, Sirsa, Haryana -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
- Official institute site domain: cicr.org.in (email and phone not found in results)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a paper, thesis, or report specific to CNA 1003. I did not search KrishiKosh directly.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer sales of CNA 1003.
- CICR tracks breeder seed production of its varieties for 2015-2025, but the table values were not visible in the result -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found confirming Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka or Tamil Nadu for CNA 1003. These states come from the input record only. Release year (2015-06-25) and parentage ("Not specified") are also unverified by search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: UPC 621 (variety_name "UPC 621"; seednet_variety_name "UPC-621")

Name note: The CSC name is "UPC 621" and the Seednet name is "UPC-621". Seednet lists the crop as "COWPEA (FODDER)", not field pea. The evidence below concerns a Pantnagar cowpea line, so it is about a cowpea and not a field pea. Where a finding is for UPC 628 (a sister forage cowpea) rather than UPC 621, I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No UPC 621-specific stress data found. The ICAR release notice that describes field resistance to yellow mosaic virus, leaf spot, anthracnose, root rot, aphid, flea beetle and root-knot nematode concerns UPC 628, not UPC 621 -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- The same ICAR notice says that UPC 628 was released in 2010 and is named in the notice as a forage cowpea from G.B. Pant University -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**Name and crop check:** The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "UPC 628", so the evidence below applies to both. The Seednet crop is "COWPEA (FODDER)", i.e. forage cowpea (*Vigna unguiculata*), not field pea. The crop field in the input is wrong, and I searched on cowpea. The searches ran 4 times. Searches 2 and 4 returned no usable breeder, contact or seed-source evidence for UPC 628, so those headings say so.

**EVIDENCE DIGEST**

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Field resistance to cowpea yellow mosaic virus, leaf spot, anthracnose, collar/root rot, aphid, flea beetle and root-knot nematode is reported, and pods are tolerant to seed shattering -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence result specific to UPC 628 was found. UPC 628 appears only as one of 30 genotypes in a heat-stress study with no variety-specific result retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397217111_Genotypic_Variation_in_Fodder_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_for_Adaptability_to_Heat_Stress_An_Evaluation_of_Growth_Physio-Biochemical_Traits_and_Fodder_Quality

DISEASE AND PEST
- Field resistance to the diseases and pests listed under STRESS TOLERANCE -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- No separate disease or pest trial data for UPC 628 was retrieved.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notified yield potential is 350-425 q/ha green fodder and 50-55 q/ha dry matter at 85-90 days, with 6-8 q/ha seed yield -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- Fodder digestibility is reported at 65-70% and crude protein at 16-18%; pods are 15-17 cm -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- A review table lists UPC 628 under pedigree breeding with 340-360 q/ha -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- In a 2008 Raipur kharif trial, UPC-628 was one of six cowpea varieties tested under three phosphorus levels; the highest green fodder yield was UPC-626, not UPC-628 -- https://rjstonline.com/HTML_Papers/Research%20Journal%20of%20Science%20and%20Technology__PID__2009-1-3-2.html
- A 2017 IJCMAS trial with UPC 628 as entry V4 reports growth and seed-yield values in a table, and the text does not name UPC 628's own performance -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-10-2017/Anjum%20Ahmad,%20et%20al.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or genomic study specific to UPC 628 was found. The review above records its breeding method as pedigree breeding -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, and released and notified by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Variety in Agricultural Crops at its meeting on 27-28 June 2010 in Chennai -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593
- Breeder name(s) and station not found in the retrieved evidence. The Pantnagar release list shows UPC 628 under field crops -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for UPC 628 was found in the retrieved evidence.
- Institute-level page only: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar. The released-varieties list is at https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/Released_crop_varieties.pdf. No contact page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Ahmad, A.; Tomar, G.S.; Taunk, S.K.; Verma, N. (2017). Evaluation of New Cultivars of Fodder Cowpea in Terms of Growth Attributes and Seed Yield as Influenced by Various Doses and Varieties. Int. J. Curr. Microbiol. App. Sci. 6(10): 937-944 -- https://doi.org/10.20546/ijcmas.2017.610.112
- Thakur, M.K. et al. (year not shown in retrieved text). Enhancing Fodder Cowpea through Breeding and Omic Innovations: A Review. Journal not confirmed in retrieved text -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- Authors not retrieved (year not shown). Effect of phosphorus levels on fodder and seed yields of cowpea varieties including UPC-628, IGKV Raipur, kharif 2008. Research Journal of Science and Technology -- https://rjstonline.com/HTML_Papers/Research%20Journal%20of%20Science%20and%20Technology__PID__2009-1-3-2.html
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report or DOI-indexed paper specific to UPC 628 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The one search for this returned only unrelated products.
- Dairy cooperatives are reported to lift breeder seed of UPC 628 from ICAR and agricultural institutes, but the retrieved text gives no supply details -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381409043_Role_of_dairy_cooperatives_in_fodder_seed_production_system

RECOMMENDED STATES
- ICAR notice: Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Assam, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/1593

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: MODERATE TOLERANCE TO LEAF HOPPERS AND FLES BEELTE.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bundel Lobia-4 / BUNDEL LOBIA-2 (IL-1177)

Name and crop caveat: The variety_name is garbled in the input ("Bundel Lobilya ��� 4"). I read it as Bundel Lobia-4. The Seednet name is BUNDEL LOBIA-2, and the Seednet crop is cowpea (lobia), while the input crop says "fieldpea". The evidence below relates to cowpea/lobia lines and does not confirm that IL-1177 is the same entry as either name.

Search budget: All 4 permitted web_search calls were used. A fifth call was blocked by the tool limit. I reviewed only the truncated snippets from the first batch and did not open full pages, so some findings may be incomplete.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION: No evidence found for a CSC notification, release gazette, or Seednet record for IL-1177 or Lobia-4 with the 2015-06-25 date. The release year and region come only from the input.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No direct evidence found for Bundel Lobia-4 or BUNDEL LOBIA-2. A general cowpea overview says the crop is drought hardy with wide, droopy leaves that help hold soil moisture -- http://dpd.gov.in/Cowpea.PDF (this is general cowpea, not this variety).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for this variety. The TNAU research highlights describe a different fodder cowpea, CO 9, with moderate resistance to blast, RTD and brown spot -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf (CO 9 is not Bundel Lobia-4 or Lobia-2).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A ResearchGate study reports that three cowpea fodder varieties, BL-1, BL-2 and BL-4, were developed by IGFRI and evaluated against a check. The snippet reports a high green fodder yield, but the figures were truncated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325626254_Nutritive_value_of_cowpea_fodder_cultivars_and_their_effect_on_nutrients_intake_digestibility_and_nitrogen_balance_in_sheep (BL-4 may correspond to Bundel Lobia-4; this is not confirmed).

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The TNAU page notes that CO 9 derives from a CO 5 / Bundel Lobia 2 cross, which suggests Bundel Lobia 2 has been used as a parent -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf. No QTL or marker studies were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The institution is IGFRI, as stated in the input. The ResearchGate study credits IGFRI with developing BL-1, BL-2 and BL-4 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325626254_Nutritive_value_of_cowpea_fodder_cultivars_and_their_effect_on_nutrients_intake_digestibility_and_nitrogen_balance_in_sheep. No breeder name was found. The parentage "Selection from I.L. 978 (ACC. No. 978)" comes only from the input.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, scientist, email, phone, postal address or IGFRI contact page appeared in the search results. Verify the IGFRI contact page directly before use.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Authors not identified (year not identified). Nutritive value of cowpea fodder cultivars and their effect on nutrients intake, digestibility and nitrogen balance in sheep. ResearchGate entry, journal not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325626254_Nutritive_value_of_cowpea_fodder_cultivars_and_their_effect_on_nutrients_intake_digestibility_and_nitrogen_balance_in_sheep
- Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (2015-2017). 49th Research Council Meeting, Research Highlights. TNAU report -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf (cites Bundel Lobia 2 as a parent of CO 9; not a direct study of this variety).
- No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR reports or journal papers found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No official source found (no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet listing). A commercial listing for "Bundel Lobia" dried white cowpea seed appears at https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/white-cowpea-seed-2851737418091.html. This is a trader listing for a dried grain product, not evidence of certified seed of this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found beyond the input value "North Eastern region". Nothing in the search results confirms this.

seednet_fields.Parentage: Selection from KM-1 x GL; KM-1 is a mutant derivative of KBC1
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Northern traditional zone(Agroclimatic zone 8) of Karnataka state in late kharif situations under well drained Light/ Red loamy and Non fertile marginal soils
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features:
1. Sowing dates-,2. Spacing-45x20cm.,3.  Fertilizer responsiveness-NPK 25:50:25 kg/ha., 	4. Seed rate-
25-30 kg/ha, 5. Resistant to lodging and shattering etc.-Tolerant to lodging and shattering., 6. Suitability to early or late sown conditions and intercropping situations-Most suitable in well drained light/ loamy red soils and Marginal soils with less ., 7. 	Late Kharif August I week till III week- fertility for late during late sown conditions.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi determinate to interminate bushy, Extra long 20 cm. Avg. Length; Pod colour Pale Straw, Seed colour Light-medium brown 4. Seed shape Rhomboid bold 9.03 g Twt., Flower colour : purple, Leaf shape : Lanceolate tapering & pointed at end.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Both under field and controlled conditions, it is resistant o rust compared to susceptible check C152.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Under field conditions, it is tolerant to pod borer Maruca testulasis compared to susceptible check C152.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for GC 7 / GC 1501. The ICAR 2023-24 report snippet (maturity 130 days, seed yield 16.48 q/ha) is for an unidentified rabi field pea entry and cannot be attributed to this variety -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-04/ICAR%20Annual%20Report%202023-24-english.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KBC-9 (cowpea)

Name note: The CSC release minutes name this variety "KBC-9" and the crop "fieldpea". The Seednet portal lists the crop as "COWPEA (LOBIA/ASPARAGUS BEAN/YARD LONG BEAN)". The evidence below concerns cowpea (Vigna unguiculata). None of the retrieved sources links KBC-9 to field pea (Pisum sativum). The field pea list I found (dpd.gov.in) does not show KBC-9. Searches were run under both names and the crop label mismatch should be checked against the CSC minutes. Parentage was not found in any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No KBC-9-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data found in the retrieved text. No evidence found. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/varieties-hybrids-recommended-for-release-during-2019-20/ (other KBC/KC cowpea entries only)

DISEASE AND PEST
- A 2026 agronomy paper describes KBC 9 as erect, with purple flowers, grey pubescence, light-yellow seeds, an 80-85 day maturity, and resistance to pod borer. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2026/vol9issue9/PartH/9-9-56-884.pdf
- No KBC-9-specific data on yellow mosaic virus, rust, leaf spot, or bacterial leaf blight was found. The UAS 2019-20 release notice for KC-8 (KBC-11), a sister line, reports YMV, rust and leaf spot resistance. This does not apply to KBC-9. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/varieties-hybrids-recommended-for-release-during-2019-20/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In AICRP/ICAR arid legume trials (2019-20), KBC 9 served as the check. Its mean yield across the listed centres was about 953 kg/ha (Ananthapuram, Bangalore, Pattambi, Coimbatore, Vamban, Madurai, Warangal, Pandharpur). The table's "yield advantage" column for KBC-12 versus checks is ambiguous; treat it cautiously. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12119430/
- KBC-9 was used as the best check in farm trials of KBC-12 in Zones 5 and 6 of Karnataka. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12119430/
- A 2026 Shivamogga trial used KBC 9 for growth-retardant (cycocel) and NPK studies. It is an agronomy trial, not a release trial. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2026/vol9issue9/PartH/9-9-56-884.pdf
- A Hisar (CCSHAU) kharif 2017 evaluation placed KBC 9 in the medium fodder, medium-to-low grain yield group. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343696597_Meteroglyph_Analysis_of_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_LWalp_Elite_Genotypes

GENETICS AND QTL
- No KBC-9-specific marker, QTL, or genetic-diversity study was found. KBC-9 appears as a standard in an UAS GKVK mini-core-set selection study, but that paper's SSR or trait-marker content was not retrieved. No evidence found. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/9-1.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The Mysore Journal of Agricultural Sciences text states that KBC-9 was developed at University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore (GKVK). The authors are from the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, AICRN on Potential Crops, and Plant Pathology at GKVK. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/9-1.pdf
- The breeder's name was not found. No evidence found. -- (no breeder-level source retrieved)
- The institution is the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru (GKVK campus, Bengaluru). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhi_Krishi_Vigyana_Kendra

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder: No evidence found.
- Institute: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, GKVK campus, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560065, India. Website: www.uasbangalore.edu.in. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhi_Krishi_Vigyana_Kendra (address and website). No official email or phone was found in the retrieved text.
- Seed (Crops) unit, GKVK: Scientific staff listed are Dr. K. Madhusudan (Special Officer, Seeds) and Dr. T.M. Ramanappa (Principal Scientist, Genetics and Plant Breeding). Their emails and phones were not in the retrieved text. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/seed-crops-gkvk-bengaluru/
- Quality Seed Production, GKVK: Dr. Krishna T V (Senior Scientist, Plant Breeding). Email and phone not in the retrieved text. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/quality-seed-production-gkvk-bengaluru/

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Mini core set selection of cowpea accessions for rabi, including KBC-9 as standard C7. Mysore Journal of Agricultural Sciences -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/9-1.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2026). Growth and yield of cowpea under fertilizer levels and cycocel, Kharif 2025, Shivamogga; cultivar KBC 9. International Journal of Research in Agronomy 9(9): 593-595 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2026/vol9issue9/PartH/9-9-56-884.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2025). Marker-assisted introgression of bacterial leaf blight and cowpea mosaic virus resistance into cultivar C-152 (KBC-12 release; KBC-9 check). Molecular Breeding -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-025-01570-4 (DOI 10.1007/s11032-025-01570-4)
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2020). Meteroglyph analysis of cowpea (Vigna unguiculata L. Walp) elite genotypes, CCSHAU Hisar kharif 2017. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343696597_Meteroglyph_Analysis_of_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_LWalp_Elite_Genotypes
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report specific to KBC-9 was found. No evidence found. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in (not retrieved)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No KBC-9 seed source (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, UAS sales, or dealer) was found. No evidence found.
- The GKVK Seed (Crops) unit's mandate covers breeder-seed production and supply, plus quality seed through university seed farms and farmer fields. This is an institutional mandate, not a KBC-9 availability listing. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/seed-crops-gkvk-bengaluru/
- UAS Bengaluru district-level recommendation PDFs list cowpea varieties including KBC-1, KBC-2, KM-9, KC-8 (KBC-11) and others, but KBC-9 was not seen in the retrieved excerpts. -- https://rawe2020.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GKMS-E-12.05.2026-Kodagu-District.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The CSC/Seednet recommended states (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, part of Odisha) were supplied in the input record only. No retrieved source confirmed them. -- (input record; not independently verified)
- Karnataka zones 5 and 6 were named as the target zones for the related release KBC-12, with KBC-9 as the check. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11032-025-01570-4

drought.details: The provided search results contain general information on drought-resistant plants, including mention of cowpea, and note that some yard long bean varieties experienced 100% mortality under combined drought and heat stress. However, no specific information regarding drought tolerance for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

heat.details: The search results indicate that some yard long bean varieties (MATTATHRIVENI, PARAMBUVATTAN) were found moderately tolerant to heat stress, while others showed 100% mortality under combined drought and heat stress. Cowpea does not tolerate frost. No specific information regarding heat tolerance for the fieldpea variety MFC-08-14 was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MFC-09-1

Name and crop note: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both MFC-09-1, so the names match. The input crop is "fieldpea", but the seednet crop is cowpea, and every relevant source describes MFC-09-1 as a forage cowpea (Vigna unguiculata). No source describes it as field pea. All findings below refer to forage cowpea. Searches used: release/traits, breeder/institute, research papers, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to MFC-09-1. The only stress-related text was general cowpea background, which I did not attribute to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for MFC-09-1. A DUS characterization paper on elite forage cowpea genotypes reports yellow mosaic virus in KBC-2, which is a parent, not MFC-09-1, so I discarded it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318593466_CHARACTERIZATION_OF_ELITE_FORAGE_COWPEA_GENOTYPES_FOR_VARIOUS_DUS_TRAITS

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Five-location South Zone trial: the trial compared MFC-09-1 with RR-3, BL-1, UPC-5286 and UPC-9202 ZC at five locations in the South Zone, in a randomized complete block design with three replications. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Trial sites: Vellayani, Mandya, Hyderabad and Dharwad were named as test centres for MFC-09-1. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Green forage yield: MFC-09-1 gave 246.9 q/ha in the South Zone, 14.2% above the zone comparison, and ranked first nationally with 1.4% superiority in GFY. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Dry matter yield: 42.5 q/ha in the South Zone (19.4% above comparison), and 4.9% superiority nationally. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- A review table lists MFC-09-1 with a pedigree-breeding origin and a yield of 321.7 q/ha, with no trial conditions given; treat this figure as unverified. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- Maturity/habit: a draft DUS test guideline for cowpea uses MFC-09-1 as reference material and places it in plant-habit and flowering classes. The table layout is ambiguous, so no days-to-maturity figure is stated here. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/DraftCowpeaDUSguideline11019.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker, or genomic studies on MFC-09-1. The only genetic information is the pedigree, KBC-2 x CoFC-8, from the trial paper. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Origin: the trial paper states that MFC-09-1 was developed at the Mandya centre by crossing KBC-2 with CoFC-8. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- Parent sources: a DUS paper lists CoFC-8 as coming from TNAU, Coimbatore, and KBC-2 as coming from UAS Bangalore. These are parent-line sources, not confirmed developers of MFC-09-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318593466_CHARACTERIZATION_OF_ELITE_FORAGE_COWPEA_GENOTYPES_FOR_VARIOUS_DUS_TRAITS
- Breeder name: no evidence found. The input "University of Agricultural Sciences." is incomplete, and no source names the university for MFC-09-1.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, postal address, or contact page for MFC-09-1 appeared in the searches. The UAS Bangalore release page that appeared lists other varieties (for example MFC-09-3), so I did not use it. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/varieties-hybrids-recommended-for-release-during-2019-20/

PUBLICATIONS
- Thakur et al. (year not found). Enhancing Fodder Cowpea through Breeding and Omic Innovations: A Review. Plant Archives -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/116-Enhancing%20Fodder%20Cowpea%20through%20Breeding%20and%20Omic%20Innovations%20A%20Review.pdf
- Authors not shown in the indexed text (2015 conference paper, listed on a ResearchGate profile for Narasimhan Manasa; authorship not confirmed from the PDF). MFC-09-1: A new forage Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp) variety for south zone of India. Conference paper, Nov 2015 -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc ; https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Narasimhan-Manasa
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report, or peer-reviewed journal paper on MFC-09-1 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Searches returned only unrelated seed retailers and Niger cowpea seed data. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for MFC-09-1 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Source evidence: the trial paper recommends MFC-09-1 for farmers' fields in southern India, based on the South Zone results. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2052&context=igc
- The state list in the input record (Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry) is not confirmed by any search result. The release date of 2016-08-12 in the input record is also not confirmed; the earliest evidence found is the 2015 conference paper.
- Release notification: no CSC notification or seednet page was found for MFC-09-1 in these searches.
