search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I'll run the searches first, then write the digest. The Seednet crop name is cowpea, while the brief says fieldpea, so I'll check both.PHULE SONALI: EVIDENCE DIGEST

CROP AND NAME CHECK
- Crop mismatch: the brief says fieldpea, but Seednet lists this variety under COWPEA (LOBIA/ASPARAGUS BEAN/YARD LONG BEAN). The evidence supports cowpea. The breeding station's cowpea release list includes Phule Sonali. Treat "fieldpea" in the brief as an error. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf
- Name: the DPD list uses "PhuleSonali", which matches the Seednet name. The breeding-station document uses "Phule Sonali" with a space, which matches the CSC name. Both names refer to the same cowpea line.
- Release year conflicts: the station document gives 2020-2021, the DPD list gives 2023, and the Seednet record gives 2022-10-26. Record all three and do not pick one.
- Originating centre conflict: the DPD list names PDKV Akola as the originating centre. The station document names MPKV's Pandharpur station. The brief names MPKV POCRTC. I am recording the station document and the brief as primary, with the DPD entry noted as a conflict.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data for Phule Sonali was found. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to YMV, Cercospora leaf spot, collar rot and leaf spot. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- Station document notes the group was moderately resistant to pests and diseases and gave higher market prices. This is a group-level claim, not specific to Phule Sonali. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield 11 to 13 q/ha, white shiny seed coat, released for Western Maharashtra. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- DPD central list gives 12 to 15 q/ha, state release, Maharashtra. Days to maturity not recorded for this line. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf
- AICRP South Zone (9 trials, national level) mean yield advantage over checks: 11.09%, 16.31%, 38.66% and 32.32% in the cited comparisons. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- Growth habit: erect, non-viney, determinate-type, early, dwarf, bushy. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage is RC 101 x Phule Vithai. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- MPKV biotechnology centre describes QTL and marker work in general, not for this variety. No specific marker or QTL study was found. -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Uploads/Education/Molecular%20Biology%20and%20Biotechnology_20230731055300.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder name: no evidence found for Phule Sonali.
- Institution: Pulses and Oilseed Crop Research and Training Centre, Pandharpur, Solapur, MPKV. The station was founded in 1981 and works on cowpea, horsegram, mothbean and clusterbean. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf ; https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- The station is listed under MPKV research schemes as "Pulses & Oilseed Research Project & Training Centre, Pandharpur". -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Research/ResearchSchemNonPlan
- Caution: ICAR-IIPR lists Dr. A. K. Parihar as a field pea breeder. This is not evidence for Phule Sonali and should not be attributed to it. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder/scientist email, phone or personal contact: no evidence found.
- Institute address: MPKV, New Admin Building, Rahuri (now Ahilyanagar) appears on the MPKV site. The Pandharpur station is about 3 km from Pandharpur city. A postal code, phone or email for the station was not found. -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Research/ResearchSchemNonPlan ; https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- Mahabeej (Akola) head office: Mahabeej Bhavan, Krishi Nagar, Akola 444104. This is a seed corporation address, not a breeding contact. -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/uploads/files/Seed-License.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry, thesis or KrishiKosh record specific to Phule Sonali was found.
- Station document, author not stated in the excerpt (the filename suggests "Thambe" but this is not confirmed): "Research at Glance on Cow pea at Agriculture Research Station (MPKV), Pandharpur". Year not stated. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf
- DPD Central varieties of Cowpea/Lobia (Government of India, Bhopal). Year not stated. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed listing for Phule Sonali was found at Mahabeej, MPKV or a dealer.
- Mahabeej (Maharashtra State Seeds Corporation) is a state seed corporation based in Akola. It supplies seed to private dealers and cooperatives. -- https://msscl.blogspot.com/
- Mahabeej Seed Testing Lab, Parbhani: Masoom Colony, Bank Colony, Parbhani 431401; phone 8669642736; toll-free 1800-233-8877; qclabparbhani@mahabeej.com. Testing lab only, not a sales point for this variety. -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/mahabeej-seed-testing-lab-parbhani
- Seednet portal listing and availability: not checked, because the search results did not return the Seednet page.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf
- Released for Western Maharashtra. A group statement also mentions South India, but this is not specific to Phule Sonali. -- https://www.asthafoundation.in/img/07-SI%20Thambe.pdf

OPEN ITEMS
- Confirm the breeder name, release year and originating centre with the MPKV Pandharpur station or the CSC notification.
- Confirm the Seednet variety code A030317998 against the CSC notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Chickpea-1 (CSC name) / Shalimar Cowpea-1 (Seednet name, code SKUA-C-23311)

Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. Queries covered the variety and breeder/institution, the Seednet name, and seed availability. No search returned a page naming either "Shalimar Chickpea-1" or "Shalimar Cowpea-1" together with its crop, so every heading below is "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned chickpea and cowpea general pages, and a PMC paper on pod borer resistance that refers only to "Shalimar chickpea-02" (a different variety, so discarded).

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. A DPD Government of India arid legumes table lists a SKUAST-Kashmir cowpea released in 2023 with resistance to cowpea mosaic and yellow mosaic viruses, but it is named "Shalimar Cowpea-2 (SKUA-WCP-149)," not Cowpea-1 or SKUA-C-23311, so it was discarded. -- https://dpd.gov.in/7%20to%2012%20Arid%20Legumes%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The AICRP chickpea 2021-22 report contains product profiles for other chickpea varieties only. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (no Shalimar Chickpea-1 entry)

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The only Shalimar chickpea genetics paper returned concerns Shalimar chickpea-02 (pod borer QTLs), a different variety, so it was discarded. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12807025

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. No page names a breeder or developing scientist for Shalimar Chickpea-1 or Shalimar Cowpea-1. The institution is SKUAST-Kashmir per the record, but no search result confirms this variety's development.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. The IIPR Pulses Seed Hub lists a SKUAST-Kashmir contact (Dryland Agriculture Research Station, Srinagar, P O Box-61, GPO Srinagar; M. Ashraf Bhatt; mashrafbhat@skuastkashmir.ac.in) for "Shalimar Cowpea 3," a different variety, so it was not attributed here. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, thesis, report or conference item names this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The same IIPR Seed Hub page lists SKUAST-Kashmir cowpea seed only for "Shalimar Cowpea 3" (0.00 q available), which is a different variety. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The only J&K recommendation found is for Shalimar Cowpea-2 in the DPD table, which is a different variety.

Name discrepancy: the CSC record calls this a chickpea and the Seednet record calls it a cowpea. No source links the two names or the code SKUA-C-23311 to either crop, so the record cannot be confirmed from these searches. Checking the CSC minutes or the Seednet entry directly would be the next step.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for sowing in three major seasons (pre-kharif, kharif and autumn-winter) as irrigated/rainfed conditions. Thirty (30) kg seeds are sufficient to sow in one hectare areas. Seeds are to be sown at 60 X 45 cm spacing. The optimum fertilizer dose is 25:75:50 kg N: P2O5:K2O/ha along with 10 tonnes FYM Full FYM and fertilizers are to be applied as basal. The variety is ready for harvest within 45 DAS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Yield well even under low soil fertility and low moisture conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The proposed variety “BCCP-3” was found to be resistance against cowpea aphid borne mosaic virus.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The proposed variety “BCCP-3” was found to be resistance against pod borer.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): The optimum fertilizer dose is 25:75:50 kg N: P2O5 K2O/ha. All fertilizers are to be applied as basal.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narmada (IPU 19-10), blackgram (Vigna mungo)

Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institution; research publications; seed availability). Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "Narmada". I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page, so the Seednet crop label "COWPEA (VEGETABLE)" could not be verified and conflicts with the blackgram record. Treat the crop-label mismatch as unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for Narmada specifically.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No Narmada-specific evidence found. A general IIPR research-achievements page lists the variety only as a 2023 release. Blackgram genomics work mentions YMD-tolerant and powdery-mildew-tolerant varieties, but these are not identified as Narmada. -- https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Krishak Jagat reports that Narmada (IPU 19-10) was released by the central government after Central Seed Committee consultation, and is recommended for sale in Madhya Pradesh; it is described as an open-pollinated urdbean variety. Yield, maturity and trial data: No evidence found. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/urdbean-variety-narmada-ipu-19-10/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Narmada parentage or QTL/marker work. The parentage field is "Not specified" and no source supplied it. The genomics review covers blackgram broadly, not this variety. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- IIPR's annual listing credits Narmada (IPU 19-10) to ICAR-IIPR under Urdbean, 2023. The institute is ICAR's national pulses institute at Kanpur, UP. No individual breeder name was found. -- https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Pulses_Research
Note: the CSC record names a "Regional Centre" without a location. The ICAR page on a Dharwad (Karnataka) regional centre does not establish that Narmada was bred there, so I have not linked them.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder name, email or phone was found. Institute-level information only: website iipr.icar.gov.in (per Wikipedia); Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, on Grand Trunk Road (per Wikipedia). No official postal address or contact-page URL was retrieved. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Pulses_Research

PUBLICATIONS -- No Narmada-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report or KrishiKosh thesis was found. Related items the search surfaced, not about Narmada:
Project Coordinator's Report 2023, All India Coordinated Research Project on Kharif Pulses. ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur (2023). Report -- https://www.mdpi.com/2071-1050/16/11/4750 (cited within an MDPI paper; no DOI retrieved)
Genetics, genomics, and breeding of black gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Frontiers in Plant Science (2023). Review -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No Narmada seed listing was found. The search returned only dealer listings for other blackgram varieties (e.g., Vamban 8), which are not relevant. Check the Seednet portal, MP State Seed Corporation/MPSSC, JNKVV (Jabalpur) and KVKs in Madhya Pradesh directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/urdbean-variety-narmada-ipu-19-10/

Release date: notification reported 25 September 2023 (CSC record gives 2 May 2023; the two dates differ and should be reconciled against the gazette notification). -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/urdbean-variety-narmada-ipu-19-10/

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: immune per IARI 2023 annual report. Stripe rust: highly resistant per IARI 2023 annual report. Leaf rust: highly resistant per IARI 2023 annual report; resistant per IIWBR 2022 newsletter and ZTM BPD page. Wheat blast: resistant per IIWBR 2022 newsletter and ZTM BPD page. Karnal bunt: good resistance per ZTM BPD page. Note: the ZTM page's wording ('good resistance to wheat blast and Karnal bunt') differs in strength from the IIWBR wording for wheat blast; the sources agree on resistance but not on the degree of blast resistance (immune in IARI report, resistant elsewhere).

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield: 51.1 q/ha (IARI 2023 annual report and IIWBR 2022 newsletter); 62.5 q/ha (ZTM BPD page). Potential yield: 69.3 q/ha (ZTM BPD page). Input lists 50-55 Q/HA. The 62.5 q/ha value conflicts with the 51.1 q/ha value and is unresolved.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Developed for the northwest plains; released for timely-sown, restricted-irrigated conditions of the NWPZ. Zone-specific recommendation covers Western Uttar Pradesh excluding Jhansi Division and Rajasthan excluding Kota and Udaipur Divisions (per input and digest; exclusions could not be confirmed from the official source). Plant height 101 cm. Chapati quality 7.3; biscuit spread factor 8.4. Sedimentation value reported as 57.7 ml (Krishi Jagran) and 69.3 (IIWBR newsletter column, which the digest notes may instead be the potential yield). Suited to bread, biscuit and chapati uses.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 145-150 days per Krishi Jagran. Input lists 45-80 DAYS, which conflicts with the digest evidence and is unresolved.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 101 cm (ZTM BPD page). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Jagrati (HI 1653), wheat

Name note: variety_name "Pusa Jagrati" and variety code "HI 1653" are the names used in the wheat sources. The seednet_variety_name "PUSA BARSATI" and seednet_crop_name "COWPEA (VEGETABLE)" do not match this wheat variety. Under SEED AVAILABILITY I explain what the Pusa Barsati evidence refers to. No Seednet page for HI 1653 was retrieved. Searches run: 4 (the maximum).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released for timely-sown, restricted-irrigated conditions of the NWPZ; immune to blast; highly resistant to stripe and leaf rust; average yield 51.1 q/ha -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Resistant to wheat blast and leaf rust; high sedimentation value 69.3 (potential yield per the source column) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Abiotic-stress tolerance (heat, drought, salinity, flood) is not specifically documented for HI 1653 in any retrieved source. No evidence found for flood, submergence, drought, heat or salinity specifics.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Immune to blast; highly resistant to stripe and leaf rusts -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Resistant to wheat blast and leaf rust; good resistance to wheat blast and Karnal bunt, with grain and end-product quality noted -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration 145-150 days, suited to bread, biscuit and chapati uses, sedimentation value 57.7 ml; developed for NW plains -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Average yield 62.5 q/ha, plant height 101 cm, timely-sown sowing time, potential yield 69.3 q/ha; chapati quality 7.3, biscuit spread factor 8.4 -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Note: the ZTM page's 62.5 q/ha average conflicts with the 51.1 q/ha average in the IARI 2023 annual report and the 2022 newsletter. Treat as unresolved.
- Multi-location trial data for HI 1653 (AICRP-type tables): No evidence found in the retrieved text.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage as shown in the IIWBR compendium appears to read "Pusa NADI/COPIO//NA" (the extracted text is garbled) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Your input states parentage as "A SELECTION FROM PHILIPPINE VAREITY, ADAPTED TO LONG DAY CONDITIONS". This does not match the compendium text; verify against the official notification.
- QTL or marker studies specific to HI 1653: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore; notified in March 2023 per the principal scientist and head KC Sharma -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Listed as an ICAR-IARI RS Indore release in the 2022 newsletter -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Lead breeder name for HI 1653 specifically: No evidence found. Station-level staff only (see CONTACT DETAILS).
- Release year: user input says 2022-10-26; Krishi Jagran says notified March 2023. Unresolved; check the CSC minutes.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. K.C. Sharma, Head (Acting), IARI Regional Station Indore (Madhya Pradesh) -- phone 0731-2927921; email head_indore[at]iari[dot]res[dot]in; alternate email kc_64sharma[at]yahoo[dot]com -- https://iari.res.in/index.php?Itemid=735&id=301&option=com_content&view=article
- Postal address of Indore station: No evidence found in retrieved text.
- ZTM & BPD Unit (IARI headquarters, which holds the variety information page): ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012 -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Generic Pusa Krishi contact: connect@pusakrishi.in; phone +91-8750281830 -- https://pusakrishi.in/contact-us/ (general portal, not verified as the breeder's line)

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (2023). Annual Report 2023, ICAR-IARI. Annual Report, pp. covering HI 1653 (Pusa Jagrati) entry -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Authors not stated (2022). Wheat-Barley Newsletter V.162, IIWBR (variety table row for Pusa Jagrati). Newsletter -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Authors not stated (2024). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023, RB-51, IIWBR. Report -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) and DOIs specific to HI 1653: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Wheat seed sources (NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU, dealers) for HI 1653: No evidence found.
- Seednet "PUSA BARSATI" entry: the retrieved sources describe Pusa Barsati as a cowpea variety selected from a Philippines collection, not a wheat variety -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/pusa . The Seednet record appears to be mis-mapped and should not be used as seed evidence for wheat.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for NWPZ, with the Indore station's recommendation summarised as northwest plain zones of the country -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Zone-specific recommendation in the IARI 2023 annual report: timely-sown, restricted-irrigated NWPZ conditions -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- Your input lists Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan (except Kota and Udaipur), Western UP (except Jhansi), and Jammu. The ZTM page lists Rajasthan, Western UP and Jammu & Kashmir. I could not confirm the full state list from the official notification; verify against the CSC minutes.

drought.details: No drought evaluation for HD 2985 was found in the digest.

heat.details: The IARI technology booklet states HD 2985 is 'tolerant to high temperature at seedling as well as at maturity stages', but the text block is not clearly tied to this variety rather than a neighbouring entry, so the claim is treated as unverified. No heat-field evaluation was found.

salinity.details: No salinity evaluation for HD 2985 was found in the digest.

flood.details: No flood evaluation for HD 2985 was found in the digest. The only lodging evidence is from a maize-system conservation agriculture trial (sown 16 Nov 2014, storm on 8 Mar 2015) where HD 2985 showed the highest lodging of the varieties tested and HD 2967 the lowest. This indicates lodging susceptibility under storm conditions, not flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Brown rust: resistance reported in the late-sown block of the ICAR/IARI page, but the page layout does not clearly tie the yellow/brown rust resistance line to HD 2985, so this is unverified. Leaf blast and brown spot: a 'moderate resistance' line appears in the IARI booklet but is probably for a different entry, so it is unverified for HD 2985. No other disease data found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest data found for HD 2985.

agronomic_details.yield: Conflicting figures, none clearly tied to HD 2985: IARI page (late-sown condition) gives 3.5-4.0 t/ha; IARI booklet gives 2.0 t/ha average yield; input record gives 50-55 q/ha. Maize-system trial grain yield ranged 3.04-5.72 t/ha across varieties, with the individual HD 2985 value not extracted.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for stability across environments. In one maize-system conservation agriculture trial, HD 2985 showed the highest lodging of the varieties tested after a storm (8 Mar 2015).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Late-sown irrigated condition in the North-eastern plains zone (ICAR 2011-12 report). The IARI booklet gives timely-sown rainfed as the production condition; this conflict is unresolved. Recommended states are listed in variety_profile.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 45-80 DAYS (input value). The IARI page gives 105-110 days for the late-sown condition. The IARI booklet gives 140-145 days and 115-120 days; these lines are not clearly tied to HD 2985.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Maize-system conservation agriculture trial, sown 16 Nov 2014, storm on 8 Mar 2015: HD 2985 showed the highest lodging of the varieties tested; HD 2967 showed the lowest. Grain yield ranged 3.04-5.72 t/ha across varieties; the HD 2985 value was not extracted. (2) IARI page, late-sown irrigated condition: 3.5-4.0 t/ha, 105-110 days; layout ambiguous. (3) IARI booklet: 2.0 t/ha, 140-145 days and 115-120 days; not clearly tied to HD 2985. (4) ICAR 2011-12 Annual Report: recommended for late-sown irrigated conditions in the North-eastern plains zone. No other trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Basant (HD 2985), wheat

Name note: "variety_name" is Pusa Basant (HD 2985). The Seednet name "PUSA BARSATI" (listed under COWPEA (VEGETABLE)) did not appear in any search result, and no search targeted seednet.gov.in directly. Every finding below refers to the wheat variety Pusa Basant / HD 2985, not to any Seednet entry. Release-year evidence conflicts with the input (2010-10-10); see the notes under RECOMMENDED STATES.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Ambiguous: the IARI technology booklet says HD 2985 "tolerant to high temperature at seedling as well as at maturity stages," but the text block is not clearly tied to this variety rather than a neighbouring entry -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Lodging (not a named stress tolerance): in a maize-system conservation agriculture trial sown 16 Nov 2014 with a storm on 8 Mar 2015, HD 2985 showed the highest lodging of the varieties tested, against HD 2967 with the lowest -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311970190_SLOW_RELEASE_NITROGEN_IN_CONSERVATION_AGRICULTURE_FOR_ENHANCING_CROP_HEALTH_YIELD_AND_SOIL_PROPERTIES_IN_INTENSIFIED_MAIZE_SYSTEMS (same data also at https://isa-india.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Extended-Summaries-book-Vol.-3.pdf)
- No drought, heat-field, salinity, flood or submergence evaluation for HD 2985 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to brown rust per the late-sown block; the ICAR/IARI page layout does not clearly tie the yellow/brown rust resistance line to HD 2985 -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Ambiguous: a "moderate resistance to leaf blast and brown spot" line appears in the IARI booklet, probably for a different entry -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- No pest data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Late-sown irrigated (recommended per the ICAR 2011-12 report): listed under the North-eastern plains zone -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Maturity of 105-110 days and average yield of 3.5-4.0 t/ha for the late-sown condition, from the IARI page (layout ambiguous) -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- Conflicting yield/maturity figures in the IARI booklet: 2.0 t/ha average yield, 140-145 days, and 115-120 days; these lines are not clearly tied to HD 2985 -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf
- Production condition given as timely-sown rainfed in the IARI booklet, versus late-sown irrigated in the ICAR report; treat as unresolved.
- Grain yield in the maize-system trial ranged 3.04-5.72 t/ha across varieties (individual HD 2985 value not extracted) -- https://isa-india.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Extended-Summaries-book-Vol.-3.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or genetic-stock study for HD 2985 was found. The only genetic record is the IP/registration entry (REG/2011/255) -- http://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/Wings/files/basic-html/page33.html
- Parentage "a selection from Philippine variety, adapted to long-day conditions" from the input could not be verified by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Registration table lists "Dr. G. P. Singh" as the developer of Hd 2985 (Pusa Wheat Basant), registered 6 Jan 2011 under ICAR IP ownership; the institution cell is garbled in the extract -- http://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/Wings/files/basic-html/page33.html
- Wheat research and release coordination sits with ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal (formerly Directorate of Wheat Research) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/about/
- The AICRP compendium lists HD 2985 (Pusa Basant) among varieties notified, without a separate breeder name in the extract -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. G. P. Singh (breeder named in the registration table; no role, email, phone or address found) -- http://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/Wings/files/basic-html/page33.html
- ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research, Karnal-132001, Haryana (address as printed on the AICRP compendium header) -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
- Institute website for the AICRP wheat and barley project: https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in
- Institute "About" page: https://iiwbr.org.in/about/
- No email or phone number for the institute or breeder was found in any result.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis or KrishiKosh record specific to HD 2985 was found. The results below are general, and the nearest items are:
- Authors not extracted (year not extracted). Slow release nitrogen in conservation agriculture for enhancing crop health, yield and soil properties in intensified maize systems. Field trial including HD 2985 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311970190_SLOW_RELEASE_NITROGEN_IN_CONSERVATION_AGRICULTURE_FOR_ENHANCING_CROP_HEALTH_YIELD_AND_SOIL_PROPERTIES_IN_INTENSIFIED_MAIZE_SYSTEMS
- Authors not extracted (year not extracted). Fourth International Agronomy Congress extended summaries, Vol. 3. Contains the same HD 2985 trial data -- https://isa-india.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Extended-Summaries-book-Vol.-3.pdf
- Indian Council of Agricultural Research (2011-12). Crop Improvement chapter, Annual Report. Notes HD 2985 in the North-eastern plains zone -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (2024). Compendium of wheat varieties notified in India during 2018-2023 (Bulletin RB-51). Does not cover HD 2985 specifically -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed source for Pusa Basant / HD 2985 was found.
- The PUSA seed portal (pusabeej.iari.res.in) is cited for six IARI wheat varieties, but HD 2985 is not confirmed among them -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/use-these-6-new-varieties-of-pusa-know-how-to-order-seeds-4084
- No National Seeds Corporation, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Eastern UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa, Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and plains of NE states -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/ (also https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/Others/Tech_Options_English-15072014.pdf)
- North-eastern plains zone, late-sown irrigated -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Bihar state notified-variety list: Pusa Basant (HD 2985), notification date 07/02/2011, S.O. 632(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- Release year conflict: the IARI booklet gives 2006 (CVRC); the Bihar list gives notification 2011; the ICAR registration table gives 2011. The input value of 2010-10-10 was not found in any result.
- The input field "recommended_states_raw: Not specified" is contradicted by the sources above.

drought.details: No drought rating was found. The DPD central-varieties sheet states no drought, salinity, flood or submergence rating was found. The DPD recommended-varieties sheet describes Ujjawal as able to escape terminal moisture stress, which is a phenology-based escape claim rather than a measured tolerance rating. The general chickpea QTL review reports drought QTLs in chickpea but does not name Ujjawal, so it is not usable as variety evidence. Ecology is recorded as irrigated, timely-sown conditions in the Rabi season.

heat.details: The DPD recommended-varieties sheet states Ujjawal is able to escape heat, which is described as escape rather than tolerance. No heat tolerance rating or physiological evidence was found.

salinity.details: No salinity rating was found. The DPD central-varieties sheet states none was found.

flood.details: No flood rating was found. The DPD central-varieties sheet states none was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt: moderately resistant (IIPR technologies page; DPD recommended and central sheets). Botrytis grey mould (BGM): tolerant (DPD recommended-varieties sheet). Dry root rot: moderately resistant (DPD central-varieties sheet). No Ascochyta blight rating was found in the digest. Names: all findings refer to Ujjawal / IPCK 2004-29; no evidence under the Seednet name 'Ujjwala' was found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest evidence was found for Ujjawal.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential yield 20-22 q/ha (IIPR technologies page; DPD sheets state 20-22 q/ha or 20.00 q/ha). The original CSC variety data lists average yield as 1941 Kgs/Ha; this value is not reconciled with the digest figures in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location trial data specific to Ujjawal was retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated, timely-sown conditions in the Rabi season (IIPR technologies page; CSC data). Recommended area is Central Zone, including the Bundelkhand region of UP (DPD sheets).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Medium maturity 103-111 days. The digest reports inconsistent durations: 105-115 days (IIPR technologies page), 108-110 days (DPD central sheet), and 103-111 days (DPD recommended sheet).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Large kabuli seed, about 35 g per 100 seed (IIPR technologies page). Other morphological characteristics: Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Frontline demonstrations of Ujjawal, among other varieties, were reported in the ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea 2021-22 report; no yield results were given in the digest. (2) A farmers' seed-society trial in Bundelkhand (UP) supplied Ujjawal seed alongside Shubhra and other varieties and reported up to 68% area enhancement under the introduced varieties; this result is not isolated to Ujjawal. (3) No multi-location trial data specific to Ujjawal was retrieved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Ujjawal (IPCK 2004-29) is listed as moderately resistant to fusarium wilt, with an irrigated, timely-sown ecology -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- The DPD recommended-varieties sheet gives Ujjawal as moderately resistant to wilt, tolerant of botrytis grey mould, and able to escape terminal moisture stress and heat -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Note: the DPD central-varieties sheet describes Ujjawal as moderately resistant to wilt and dry root rot; no drought, salinity, flood or submergence rating was found -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Names: all findings refer to Ujjawal / IPCK 2004-29. No evidence under the Seednet name "Ujjwala" was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt: moderately resistant (IIPR technologies page; DPD sheets as above).
- Botrytis grey mould: tolerant, per the DPD recommended-varieties sheet -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Potential yield 20-22 q/ha; release year 2010 (CVRC); recommended area Central Zone; large kabuli seed (about 35 g/100 seed) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- Duration is reported inconsistently: 105-115 days (IIPR technologies page), 108-110 days (DPD central sheet), and 103-111 days (DPD recommended sheet). Yield in the DPD sheets is 20-22 q/ha or 20.00 q/ha -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Frontline demonstrations of Ujjawal, among others, were reported in the ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea 2021-22 report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Seed-system trial: farmers' seed societies in Bundelkhand (UP) supplied Ujjawal seed alongside Shubhra and other varieties, and reported up to 68% area enhancement under the introduced varieties -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-15-8014-7_8
- No multi-location trial data specific to Ujjawal was retrieved.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found specific to Ujjawal (IPCK 2004-29). The general chickpea QTL review found QTLs for wilt, Ascochyta, BGM and drought, but did not name Ujjawal -- https://dx.doi.org/10.3390/plants10122583 (not verified for this variety)
- No parentage was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. Origin is recorded as ICAR-IIPR in the DPD sheet -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- A chapter citing "Chaturvedi et al. 2010" lists IPCK 2004-29 among kabuli lines with high yield potential -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268280312_Chickpea (the full bibliographic record was not retrieved)

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or postal address was found in the search results.
- Institute-level: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur (U.P.), domain icar-iipr.org.in. No official phone, email or address was retrieved from the results. Use the institute's own contact page to fill these in.

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2022). Project Coordinator's Report, Chickpea 2021-22. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (author list not stated; lists IPCK 2004-29 among varieties)
- Chaturvedi et al. (2010). Cited as the source for IPCK 2004-29 as a high-yielding kabuli line. Journal/report not retrieved. -- Referenced in https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268280312_Chickpea
- Peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers specifically on Ujjawal: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet portal listing under "Ujjwala" / "COWPEA (VEGETABLE)": No evidence found. The Seednet listing was not reached by any search.
- NSC: the IARI best-practice note says NSC runs FLDs to promote new chickpea varieties, but it does not name Ujjawal -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Farmers' seed societies in Bundelkhand (UP) supplied Ujjawal seed to the formal seed chain -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-15-8014-7_8
- State seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for Ujjawal: No evidence found. A generic chickpea seed listing from Tikamgarh (MP) is not Ujjawal-specific and was excluded -- https://www.tradeindia.com/products/chickpea-seeds-c8586123.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Central Zone: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat and Maharashtra are listed in the DPD sheets -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Bundelkhand region of UP: listed in the DPD sheet as part of CZ (BK-UP); the IIPR technologies page gives "Central Zone of India" -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/technologies/
- South Rajasthan: not found in any result; the record is not confirmed for this state.
- Discrepancy: one DPD table gives the "Shubhra (IPCK 2004-29)" name, while the IIPR and AICRP sources identify Shubhra as IPCK 2002-29. Verify before using the name mapping.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCH NOTE: The evidence shows that PRG 176 "Ujwala" is a pigeonpea (redgram) variety, not chickpea. The Seednet "Ujjwala" listing under cowpea (vegetable) found no matching evidence. Four searches were run (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, and a seed-related query). No search was run specifically for seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data for Ujwala or PRG 176. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for Ujwala or PRG 176 appeared in the results. The only chickpea disease hits concerned other varieties or general pathology. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A cluster front-line demonstration in Mahbubnagar district, Telangana, used PRG 176 (Ujwala) as a redgram variety, with 50 demonstrations under cluster management. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286613635_Pigeonpea_Cajanus_cajan_research_in_India_-_An_overview
- The same source gives PRG 176 a yield potential of 20 q/ha on light soils, with a demonstration-field average of 15.4 q/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286613635_Pigeonpea_Cajanus_cajan_research_in_India_-_An_overview

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker, or QTL data for Ujwala or PRG 176 was found. The "Parentage: Not specified" field was not contradicted by any source. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The release table lists "Ujwala (PRG 176)", released in 2015 through the SVRC, with the station given as the Associate Director of Research, RARS, Palem, Nagarkurnool district. This is a redgram entry, and its release year (2015) differs from the year in the CSC record (2016). -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
- The Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU) is the developing institution. The university was separated from ANGRAU in 2014 and is headquartered at Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_Jayashankar_Telangana_State_Agricultural_University
- No lead breeder or scientist name is linked to Ujwala or PRG 176. The "Prof. Jaysankar" entry in the input record is an institution-level attribution only. Named individuals on the university page are not linked to this variety. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. Institute page: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, Telangana, website www.pjtsau.edu.in. Email and phone not found in the results. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_Jayashankar_Telangana_State_Agricultural_University
- Institute research page: https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/ (no direct contact details were captured from it).

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (year not stated). Pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan) research in India: An overview. Book chapter/report, ResearchGate listing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286613635_Pigeonpea_Cajanus_cajan_research_in_India_-_An_overview
- No chickpea-specific publication, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis for Ujwala was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No seed-sale listing for Ujwala or PRG 176 appeared. The Seednet cowpea results listed other cowpea names (for example Gold-302, 309 and Surabhi) and did not mention Ujjwala. -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Seed_Producers_Marketers.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Telangana: the release is recorded under the SVRC and the demonstrations were in Mahbubnagar, Telangana. Official notification scope was not confirmed beyond this. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MANDAKINI (OR 2077-4) (IET 17847), rice

Name note: The CSC release-minute name is "MANDAKINI (OR 2077-4)(IET 17847)" and the Seednet name is "Mandakini". Evidence below refers to the same rice variety under both names. The Seednet crop field reads "CUCUMBER", which conflicts with rice. No Seednet page for this variety was retrieved, so I could not confirm the Seednet crop entry. Other "Mandakini" entries found are a different variety, Mandakini (K-9351), released 2004, and were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no page on disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Mandakini is listed among early-duration varieties with a 90-115 day range, but that range is for the group, not confirmed per variety -- https://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
Odisha seed distribution report says farmers in the state prefer Mandakini among the varieties they grow in uplands -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
IRRI technical bulletin on rice in Odisha lists Mandakini as suited to upland kharif and irrigated rabi land -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No multi-location or field-trial results specific to this variety were found -- searched via the research query, no page returned.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No marker, QTL or parentage page for this variety was returned. Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Odisha's rice breeding history is covered by the IRRI bulletin, which credits Mandakini to the state's rice breeding programme (2010 release group) but does not name a breeder -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
The same bulletin attributes Odisha's rice breeding and varietal development to the Rice Research Station, Bhubaneswar, under the university setup (OUAT). The bulletin does not explicitly say Mandakini was bred there -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No lead breeder name was found for this variety. A ResearchGate profile of an OUAT plant breeder lists a co-author named Mandakini Kabi on an unrelated paper; this does not identify a breeder and is not attributed to the variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact for seed supply (not the breeding institute):
Orissa State Seeds Corporation Ltd., Samantarapur, Bhubaneswar, Pin 751002, Odisha; Phone: 0674 - 2340573, 2340170; Email: mdosscltd456@gmail.com -- https://www.osscltd.in/cms/contact/contact-us
No email or phone for OUAT Rice Research Station or ICAR-NRRI was retrieved, so none is given.

PUBLICATIONS
Das, S.R. (2012). Rice in Odisha. IRRI Technical Bulletin No. 16 -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf
No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Odisha State Seeds Corporation (OSSC Ltd.) lists Mandakini among its early-duration paddy varieties -- https://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
OSSC is the state nodal agency for breeder, foundation and certified seed, and sources breeder and foundation paddy seed from CRRI, OUAT and ANGRAU -- https://ossc.nic.in/Production/Schemes
The Odisha seed distribution report describes shortfalls in supply of medium-land and upland paddy seed in the study period, without naming Mandakini -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf
No NSC, KVK or private dealer listing for this variety was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified in Odisha: the notification (S.O. 632(E), 25.03.2011) lists the recommended state as Odisha -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
The Bihar-hosted list of notified varieties also records this variety with a 2010 release year and 25/03/2011 notification -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
The input field "recommended_states_raw" (Not specified) is superseded by the Odisha notification above.

drought.details: Moderately tolerant to drought. It is considered an 'intermediate' variety in tissue-specific responses to drought stress at the seedling stage. The variety has also been a target for introgression of drought stress tolerance traits, suggesting a need for improvement in inherent tolerance.

heat.details: It is field tolerant to high temperature. While noted as 'intermediate' in some heat stress response studies at the seedling stage, overall field performance indicates tolerance to high temperatures. However, it is susceptible to low temperatures and frost.

salinity.details: It has been identified as a target for introgression of salt stress tolerance traits, implying its inherent tolerance to salinity is not high. It has been used in studies involving salt injury index.

flood.details: Tolerant to waterlogging conditions. It has also been used as a parent in breeding programs aiming to enhance waterlogging tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV) and Downy Mildew (caused by P. cubensis).

agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in regions like Punjab, suitable for general cucumber cultivation practices. It is tolerant to high temperatures and humidity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plants have dark green leaves with a rough surface. Its fruit characteristics (yield, number, length, weight, diameter) are notable when used in hybridization.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Participated in All India Coordinated Trials. It is extensively used as a check variety in cucumber germplasm evaluation and has been included in numerous research experiments and hybridization programs to study traits like stress tolerance, yield components, and seed production.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Parental polymorphism observed (e.g., in PAGE images).
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: No specific QTLs or genetic markers directly linked to specific traits of Punjab Naveen are identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: The variety has been used as a recipient for trait introgression (e.g., drought and salt stress tolerance) and as a parent in crosses (e.g., for submergence and waterlogging tolerance, parthenocarpy) and genetic diversity studies.

agronomic_performance.yield: Average yield is about 200 (unit unspecified, as per agricultural practice guidelines). It has been found to be a good parent for fruit yield, fruit number, fruit length, fruit weight, and diameter in hybrid combinations, exhibiting high standard heterosis for yield per plant.
agronomic_performance.stability: Included in All India Coordinated Trials, suggesting adaptability across various environments. It is widely cultivated, implying good overall adaptation.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in regions like Punjab, suitable for general cucumber cultivation practices. It is tolerant to high temperatures and humidity.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Plants have dark green leaves with a rough surface. Its fruit characteristics (yield, number, length, weight, diameter) are notable when used in hybridization.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Participated in All India Coordinated Trials. It is extensively used as a check variety in cucumber germplasm evaluation and has been included in numerous research experiments and hybridization programs to study traits like stress tolerance, yield components, and seed production.

breeder_and_contacts.breeder: Scientists at Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) have been involved in its development and research. Noteworthy researchers associated with studies on Punjab Naveen include Gagandeep Kaur Chahal, Pooja Manchanda, and Sat Sharma.
breeder_and_contacts.contacts: nan
breeder_and_contacts.publications: The variety is a subject of multiple research articles and reports, including those published by ScienceDirect, ResearchGate, NCBI, ISVS Veg Sci, and annual reports of ICAR-NBPGR and IARI.

commercial_availability.private_dealers: Widely cultivated, suggesting availability through private seed dealers.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Harsha (HI 1655), wheat**

**Name check:** The variety name is "Pusa Harsha" (CSC minutes name, with code HI 1655). The Seednet name "Pusa (Barkha)" with crop CUCUMBER refers to a different crop. Every Seednet-related finding below is about the cucumber variety Pusa Barkha, not wheat HI 1655. I found no Seednet listing for the wheat variety.

**Date check:** The input gives a release year of 2022-10-26. The sources give a notification date of 06.03.2023. One source cites the notification as S.O. 1056(E) dated 6.3.2023 -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/ . Treat 2023 as the notification year and check the input date against the Gazette.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Resistance to leaf and stem rust is listed for HI 1655 in the wheat compendium table -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- A Hindi-language grower article describes the variety as water-use efficient and suited to timely sowing with restricted irrigation -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for HI 1655 specifically.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- The compendium describes HI 1655 as having resistance to leaf and stem rust, with hard grain and a good chapati score of 8.4 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Yellow rust, Karnal bunt, and other disease or pest resistance: No evidence found for HI 1655.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Recommended sowing window is 20 October to 10 November, under timely sowing with restricted irrigation in the Central Zone -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/ (general Central Zone table) and https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- A Hindi-language grower article gives a seed rate of about 108 kg/ha, 20 cm row spacing, plant height of about 90–95 cm, and NPK plus zinc at 80:40:50 -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- The same article gives a potential of about 60 q/ha under good conditions -- https://choupalsamachar.in/1655-wheat-variety-pusa-harsha/
- The compendium lists two yield figures for HI 1655 in the Central Zone (59.8 and 38.8). The column labels are unclear in the extracted text, so treat them as unverified -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Maturity days: No evidence found for HI 1655.
- Multi-location trial data beyond the compendium entry: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: The compendium entry for HI 1655 appears to include "Pusa MACS 2496 / HI 1056(E)", but the text is garbled and not labelled as parentage -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Marker, QTL, or genomic studies for HI 1655: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing institution: ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore (MP) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- The station's principal scientist and head, K.C. Sharma, is quoted on the six new varieties notified in March 2023, including HI 1655 -- https://krishijagran.com/news/icar-iari-develops-6-new-high-yielding-disease-resistant-wheat-varieties/
- Names of the lead breeders for HI 1655 specifically: No evidence found. Station staff named in a 2025 IARI newsletter for other wheat lines include Singh JB, Sharma KC, Verma DK, Prakasha TL and Gajghate R -- https://pusakrishi.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IARI_Newsletter_April-June_2025.pdf
- The Seednet cucumber "Pusa Barkha" was released in 2013 by the SVRC Delhi. It is a different crop and is not the wheat variety -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/vegetables/cucumber/

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Dr K.C. Sharma, Head (Acting), IARI Regional Station Indore. Phone: 0731-2927921. Email: head_indore[at]iari[dot]res[dot]in. Alternate email listed: kc_64sharma[at]yahoo[dot]com -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- Jang Bahadur Singh, Regional Station Indore. Email: jangbsing@gmail.com -- https://pusakrishi.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IARI_Newsletter_April-June_2025.pdf
- Institute postal address for the Indore station: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact page URL: https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735 (page lists the station contact details)

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Authors not listed (2024). Compendium of Wheat Varieties Notified in India During 2018-2023. ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal (RB-51) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-51-Compendium-of-Wheat-Varieties-Notified-in-India-During-2018-2023.pdf
- Authors not listed (2022). Wheat & Barley Newsletter, Vol. 162. ICAR-IIWBR -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wheat-Barley-Newsletter-V.162-2022.pdf
- Authors not listed (2023). IARI Annual Report 2023 (lists HI 1655 as a bread wheat variety) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses, or KrishiKosh records specific to HI 1655 were found. The HI 8802 paper in the search results concerns a different durum variety and is excluded.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No wheat seed sales listing for HI 1655 found from NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or a private dealer.
- The IARI Indore station reports producing breeder seed for its varieties through public-private partnership -- https://www.iari.res.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=301&Itemid=735
- Seednet and cucumber listings (Amazon "Pusa" cucumber seed) are for other crops and are not relevant to HI 1655.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Kota and Udaipur divisions of Rajasthan, and Jhansi division of Uttar Pradesh. The Central Zone table lists HI 1655 for timely sown, restricted irrigation conditions -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2"). No search returned a Seednet portal page, so the evidence below does not come from Seednet under either name. Four searches returned no page that describes this hybrid directly. The findings below are only tangential, and each one is labelled with the work it actually concerns.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for this hybrid's drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Context only: a Kashmir polyhouse study covers a different parthenocarpic hybrid, not this one -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue9/PartO/8-9-162-601.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for resistance ratings of Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2. Context only: a 2004-05 survey of Kashmir valley cucumber fields found angular leaf spot in every growing area, with incidence of 23.3 to 74.4% and severity of 10.5 to 26.0% (Bhat, Ahmad and Zargar, 2007) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/apps-15-2-029

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for this hybrid's yield, maturity or field trials. Context only: a 2019-2020 naturally ventilated polyhouse trial at SKUAST-K Shalimar tested fertigation and pruning on the parthenocarpic hybrid 'Pusa Parthenocarpic Cucumber-6', not on this hybrid -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue9/PartO/8-9-162-601.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for parentage, QTL or marker studies of Shalimar Cucumber Hybrid-2. Context only: a SKUAST-Jammu diallel study on local Jammu cucumber germplasm (2022-23 and 2023-24) found non-additive gene action dominated, which is not specific to this hybrid -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/view/10515

Institution: SKUAST-K (Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir), with headquarters at Shalimar, Srinagar. EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shrushti (variety_name) / Shruti (seednet_variety_name), maize, GH 0727

Search note: four web_search queries were run (variety, breeder/institute, research/trials, Seednet name). The Seednet name "Shruti" returned only cucumber seed-sale pages, which are discarded under the crop and variety rules. All maize findings below refer to "Shrushti" / GH 0727 and not to the Seednet crop label, which says CUCUMBER.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for GH 0727 (Shrushti).

DISEASE AND PEST
Shrushti is listed in a benchmarking table of Indian maize varieties with the note "resistance to BSDM" (BSDM is the abbreviation in the snippet; it is not expanded there). The table row also names UAS, ARS Arabhavi, Karnataka, Kharif, and a yellow, dent grain type. The snippet does not state a disease score for this variety, so the claim should be checked against the full document. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The benchmarking table lists GH 0727 (Shrushti) with a yield figure of 6.0 in its row, tested under Karnataka Kharif conditions. The table's column headings are not legible in the snippet, so the unit and meaning of this figure are unconfirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
The IIMR cultivar list records GH 0727 (Shrushti), developed at ARS Arabhavi, Karnataka, with status "Public," a date of 30-07-2014, a code "1919 (E)," season Kharif, and maturity "Normal." A value of 7.5 appears in the same row, with no unit or column label visible in the snippet. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
Maturity class is given as "Normal" in the IIMR list. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL, marker, or pedigree study for GH 0727 (Shrushti). Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The developing institution is given as UAS, ARS Arabhavi (University of Agricultural Sciences, Agricultural Research Station, Arabhavi, Karnataka), which fits the "University of Agricultural Sciences" entry in the release record. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
No lead breeder or scientist name was found for this variety. The search did not reach the AICRP maize centre page or the UAS Dharwad page that would list breeders.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: SNEHA (JRM-3), mesta

Name note: the CSC name is "SNEHA" and the Seednet name is "Sneha". The Seednet crop field says "CUCUMBER", which conflicts with the mesta crop. The sources found describe JRM-3 (Sneha) as a kenaf/mesta variety, so the cucumber entry looks like a portal error and should be checked on Seednet. Searches covered both spellings. Only 4 queries were run, and two of them returned unrelated results (a fintech company and a cauliflower seed shop), so several headings have no evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The searches did not return a stress-tolerance source.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the lead breeder, developing institute or station. The ICAR 2010-11 report mentions the variety but names no breeder in the extracted text. Parentage is not specified in the input and was not found.

drought.details: The digest reports that AD-2 is suitable for both irrigated and rainfed conditions, with about 14.6 q/ha under irrigated and 5.8 q/ha under rainfed conditions. The digest explicitly states this shows rainfed adaptation and not a measured drought-tolerance trait, so no drought-tolerance level can be assigned from the evidence. No drought mechanisms were reported.

heat.details: No direct evidence of heat tolerance was found. The variety was developed for arid and semi-arid agro-climates, which indicates regional adaptation but not a tested heat-tolerance trait. In farmers' fields it recorded 15.3 q/ha against a check of 9.64 q/ha, but this result is not linked to heat stress.

salinity.details: No AD-2-specific salinity evidence was found. The digest notes only that seed spices in general are reported to grow successfully under saline or alkaline water, and this statement is not tied to AD-2.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: AD-2 recorded the lowest percent disease incidence (5.2%) among the tested entries and was rated tolerant; the digest does not name the disease(s) involved. Separately, the variety possesses field tolerance to powdery mildew (the digest's second source is a coriander-based NRCSS publication, so the powdery mildew statement should be verified for AD-2 specifically).

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for AD-2 specifically. No pests with resistance were identified in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Station and farm trials at NRCSS: 1466 kg/ha for AD-2 versus 1207 kg/ha for the local variety (21% gain). Farmers' fields: 15.3 q/ha versus 9.64 q/ha for the check. Under irrigated and rainfed conditions, about 14.6 q/ha and 5.8 q/ha respectively.
agronomic_details.stability: Not available in digest. Yield data are reported across station, farmers' field, irrigated, and rainfed settings, but no formal stability analysis was reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Developed for arid and semi-arid agro-climate; suitable for both irrigated and rainfed cultivation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: High dillapiole content (per breeder description). Morphological characteristics not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: NRCSS station and farm trials compared AD-2 with the local variety (1466 vs 1207 kg/ha). Farmers' field trial compared AD-2 with a check (15.3 vs 9.64 q/ha). Irrigated and rainfed yields were also reported (about 14.6 vs 5.8 q/ha).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: AD-2 (Ajmer Dill-2), Indian dill, NRCSS Ajmer

DROUGHT: The variety is suitable for cultivation under both irrigated and rainfed conditions., with about 14.6 q/ha under irrigated conditions and 5.8 q/ha under rain-fed conditions. This shows rainfed adaptation, not a measured drought-tolerance trait. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/food-science/dill ; https://5.imimg.com/data5/OH/VP/MY-20277542/seed-spices.pdf

HEAT: No direct evidence found for heat tolerance. The variety is described as developed for arid and semi-arid agro-climate, and in farmers' fields it recorded 15.3 q/ha against a check of 9.64 q/ha. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474

SALINITY: No AD-2-specific evidence found. Seed spices in general are reported to be grown successfully under saline/alkaline water, but this is not tied to AD-2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329438747_Scenario_Importance_and_Prospects_of_Seed_Spices_A_Review

FLOOD / SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found.

DISEASE RESISTANCE: AD-2 recorded the lowest percent disease incidence, 5.2%, among the tested entries, and was rated tolerant. Separately, the variety possesses field tolerance to powdery mildew. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316589094_NRCSS_ACr_1_Coriander

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found for AD-2 specifically.

QTL / MARKERS: No evidence found. A 2024 Springer review on dill breeding notes that still almost no work has been done about the breeding aspects of this important plant. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-97-9630-4_6

YIELD AND TRIALS: Station and farm trials at NRCSS: AD-2 gave 1466 kg/ha, against 1207 kg/ha for the local variety, a 21% gain. The farmers'-field result was 15.3 q/ha versus 9.64 q/ha for the check. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJSS/article/view/157474

BREEDER / INSTITUTION: NRCSS Ajmer developed the variety for arid and semi-arid agro-climate, with high dillapiole content. It was developed through mass selection based on progeny performance from Nagaur Local (selection AD-01-6). The selection was identified by the XVII All India Co-ordinated Research Project on Spices as NRCSS AD 2. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

REGISTRATION / NOTIFICATION: The variety has been registered at NBPGR with IC 620541. Central notification followed: the Central Variety Release and Notification Committee accepted it for notification at its 24th meeting, held on 22 September 2016. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJGPB/article/view/68257

agronomic_details.adaptation: Most suitable for loamy and black cotton soils with proper drainage. A dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable. Most suitable for irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 150-160 days (official). Other sources give 130-140 (SKNAU), 140-150 (phytojournal) and 110 (RAU Bikaner notes), so maturity figures are inconsistent.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Short stature with compact umbels; long, bold seeds; a denser view of the plants when green. One source describes it as erect and medium tall, which conflicts with the official description.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not identified in the results.
commercial_info.availability_status: limited (unverified). Breeder seed is produced at SKNAU research stations (18 kg in 2018-19), but the commercial supply chain is not documented.
commercial_info.private_dealers: A spice nursery site lists RF-125 as a Rajasthan variety (spicenurseries.in), but no dealer or stock was confirmed.

variety_profile.institution: RAJASTHAN AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY, BEECHAWAL FARM, BIKANER (RAJASTHAN)
variety_profile.recommended_states: Not specified in the release record. Search results show use in Rajasthan, and a state-wise listing names Rajasthan for RF-125 (result 43).
variety_profile.state_acronyms: RJ (Rajasthan, per the sources above). GJ is not listed as a recommended state for this variety.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: No direct drought-tolerance rating for RF-125 was found. The release record says it is most suitable for irrigated conditions. The slideshare snippet's 'tolerant to drought' appears to refer to a different variety, and the CRIDA snippet on drought-tolerant greengram is about another crop. The CRIDA climate-resilient technologies report says RF-125 gave the best result (23.80 q/ha) among the varieties demonstrated in Rajasthan, but the snippet does not say this was under drought stress. A Sakleshpur CVT drought trial lists RF-125 at 22.95 q/ha, but the snippet does not say how it ranked relative to other genotypes. Water stress should be avoided at flowering and seed formation.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The ICAR Crop Improvement report lists RF 125 among fennel lines identified in a screening, but the snippet is cut off and does not state the trait. It sits next to a 'terminal heat stress' passage, so this link is not confirmed. The release record says a dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable, which suggests the variety is not specifically heat adapted.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: No salinity rating for the released RF-125 was found. A researcher profile describes gamma-irradiated M3 mutants derived from RF-125 and screened for salt tolerance. That work concerns the mutants, not the original variety. The Bharatpur station source reports RF-125 yielding 20 q/ha in a saline-affected area, but the snippet gives no comparison and no tolerance claim.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No flood-tolerance evidence was found. The adaptation note requires proper drainage, and the IPM guidance says to avoid waterlogging. This suggests the variety is sensitive to waterlogging, but this is an inference and not a tested result.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Blight and powdery mildew (moderately resistant per the AESA-IPM guide). Ramularia blight and Alternaria blight are described as resistant in secondary sources (slideshare PPT, a training manual, and a production-technology compendium). The official release record says only that disease incidence was at par with RF-101 and the local check.
disease_resistance.technical_details: The sources conflict. The NIPHM-AESA IPM package lists RF-101 and RF-125 as moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew. The release record shows no advantage over the checks. The 'resistant' claims come from non-peer-reviewed secondary sources. No resistance genes or mechanisms are reported.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None documented. The 'field tolerant to white fly' result (OP3.pdf) concerns a different crop and is not attributed to RF-125. The CABI note about aphid-tolerant cultivars is general and does not name RF-125.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No pest-resistance evidence for RF-125 was found.

stress_tolerance_analysis.overall_stress_tolerance: no (not demonstrated). Only moderate disease resistance has some support. There is no verified abiotic-stress tolerance.
key_stress_attributes: Moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew (NIPHM AESA-IPM guide)
Blight resistance claims in secondary sources conflict with the release record's 'at par with checks'
Suited to irrigated, well-drained soils; waterlogging is to be avoided
Gamma-irradiation mutants of RF-125 have been used in salt-tolerance research, but this is not a trait of the variety itself

genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_markers: None found. No QTL, SNP or SSR data were reported for RF-125.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: Conventional recurrent half-sib selection (individual plant progeny performance). RF-125 has also served as a base material for gamma-radiation mutagenesis studies, for example germination at 150 Gy.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_background: Developed through recurrent selection based on individual plant progeny (half-sib) performance in EC-243380, an exotic collection from Italy. One source (result 33) attributes development to SKN College of Agriculture (RAU), Jobner. The official record names RAU, Beechwal Farm, Bikaner.

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: 1500-1700 kg/ha (official). Secondary sources give 1600 kg/ha (phytojournal) and 17.0 q/ha (SKNAU table). Farmer demonstration and trial figures are 20 q/ha (Bharatpur), 22.95 q/ha (Sakleshpur CVT) and 23.80 q/ha (CRIDA demonstration).
agronomic_performance.yield_stability: Reported yields are consistently at or above the official range across Rajasthan demonstrations and a Karnataka trial. No formal stability analysis was found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Most suitable for loamy and black cotton soils with proper drainage. A dry, cool, frost-free climate is favourable. Most suitable for irrigated conditions.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 150-160 days (official). Other sources give 130-140 (SKNAU), 140-150 (phytojournal) and 110 (RAU Bikaner notes), so maturity figures are inconsistent.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Short stature with compact umbels; long, bold seeds; a denser view of the plants when green. One source describes it as erect and medium tall, which conflicts with the official description.
agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: CRIDA Rajasthan demonstrations: RF-125 gave the best result at 23.80 q/ha, with additional farmer income of Rs 47,900-56,900/ha. Bharatpur station: 20 q/ha. Sakleshpur CVT: 22.95 q/ha. An on-farm assessment (IJCMAS 2017) compared RF-101, RF-125 and RF-145. The SKNAU document says RF-125 was released for the state by notification S.O. 597(E) on 25.04.2006.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Described as a widely adopted cultivar in Rajasthan. Breeder seed production of 18 kg was recorded at ARSS in 2018-19. It is included in DUS guidelines and the Plant Authority's registered variety lists.

breeder_and_development_info.primary_breeder_name: Not identified in the search results.
breeder_and_development_info.breeding_institution: RAJASTHAN AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY, BEECHAWAL FARM, BIKANER (RAJASTHAN). SKN College of Agriculture, Jobner (RAU/SKNAU) is cited as the developer in some sources.
breeder_and_development_info.collaborating_scientists: Not identified. Arvind Verma appears only as a researcher working on RF-125 mutants.
breeder_and_development_info.development_timeline: Recurrent half-sib selection from EC-243380 (Italy). Released in 2004. State notification S.O. 597(E) dated 25.04.2006 (per SKNAU).
breeder_and_development_info.research_publications: Secondary and review sources only: Advances in cultivation of fennel (Phytojournal 2020), Germplasm conservation in seed spices (Botany Journals 2021), Scenario, Importance and Prospects of Seed Spices (Lupine 2018), an IJCMAS 2017 on-farm assessment, and the ResearchGate review on fennel (2022) mentioning gamma radiation of RF-125. No primary paper on the variety's release or stress tolerance was found.

commercial_availability.seed_corporations: Not identified in the results.
commercial_availability.kvk_availability: Not identified. Demonstrations were done in Rajasthan, but no KVK stock was confirmed.
commercial_availability.private_dealers: A spice nursery site lists RF-125 as a Rajasthan variety (spicenurseries.in), but no dealer or stock was confirmed.
commercial_availability.availability_status: limited (unverified). Breeder seed is produced at SKNAU research stations (18 kg in 2018-19), but the commercial supply chain is not documented.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has several citations, including government reports (CRIDA, NIPHM) and review literature, and consistent yield evidence of 16-24 q/ha. Its stress-trait evidence is weak: moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew is supported by one credible source (NIPHM), while claims of drought, salinity and heat tolerance are not backed by direct evidence. The score is therefore not raised above 60. It is not recommended specifically for Gujarat, and no Gujarat-specific trial data were found.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Short, compact umbels; long bold seeds; 150-160 days; 15-17 q/ha official yield (20-24 q/ha in demonstrations); moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew; best on irrigated, well-drained loam or black cotton soil.
dashboard_data.seasons: Rabi (inferred from the dry, cool climate requirement and the 'Advanced Production Technology for Rabi Fennel' source)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: RF-125 is a short, compact-umbel fennel variety released in 2004, selected by half-sib recurrence from an Italian accession, and it yields 1500-1700 kg/ha officially and 20-24 q/ha in Rajasthan demonstrations. The best-supported stress trait is moderate resistance to blight and powdery mildew; drought, heat, salinity and flood tolerance are not demonstrated. Yield evidence is strong and stress evidence is weak, with some conflict between sources on disease reaction and maturity.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A short fennel variety with compact umbels and bold seeds, maturing in 150-160 days and yielding 15-17 q/ha officially (20-24 q/ha in demonstrations). It suits irrigated, well-drained loam and black cotton soils in a dry, cool, frost-free climate.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: It is moderately resistant to blight and powdery mildew according to the NIPHM guide, though the release record shows disease incidence at par with the checks. No verified drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was found, and no genetic marker data exist.
