Management in the trial/recommendation data: spacing 50 x 50 cm with 40,000 rooted slips per hectare, basal FYM at 25 t/ha, and NPK at 50:50:40 kg/ha; first harvest at 75-80 days, then every 40-45 days. Note: the digest gives year of release as 2009 in agronomy sources and 2010 in the release paper, which differs from the ground-truth release date of 2014-06-02.

disease_resistance.summary: DGGV-2 is susceptible to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). It is explicitly used as a 'susceptible check' in studies evaluating resistance to MYMV in other breeding lines and genotypes. There is no direct evidence that DGGV-2 itself possesses resistance to bruchid (Callosobruchus maculatus); rather, a cross involving DGGV-2 (V-02-802×DGGV-2) was noted to show resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: While a cross involving DGGV-2 (V-02-802×DGGV-2) showed resistance to bruchid, DGGV-2 itself is not explicitly stated to possess resistance to bruchid or other pests in the provided information.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields for DGGV-2 vary across studies. It was observed as a 'lowest yielder' at 393 kg/ha in one analysis. Another study recorded a seed yield of 701.3 kg/ha. However, with optimal management (sowing during the first fortnight of June and foliar spray of 2% DAP), DGGV-2 demonstrated a higher seed yield of 1380 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: The varying yield performance across different studies (393 kg/ha, 701.3 kg/ha, 1380 kg/ha) suggests its yield can be influenced by environmental conditions and specific agronomic practices.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DGGV-2 is suitable for sowing up to the end of June but not suitable for late sowing. It exhibits tolerance to shattering compared to Chinamung and Sel-4 varieties. It is responsive to fertilizer application at 25 N & 50 P kg/ha. Optimal performance was noted with first fortnight of June sowing combined with 2% DAP foliar spray.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GBM-1 (greengram)

Name note: CSC minutes and Seednet both use "GBM-1". The only matching source, the DPD mungbean table, writes it as "GBM 1". None of the four searches returned a seednet.gov.in page, so Seednet's own listing (variety code A0305222) is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in GBM-1 returned only other moong varieties (Gujarat Mung-4, Gujarat Mung-7, Pusa Vishal) and unrelated pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
GBM 1, released 2016 by NAU, Gujarat, is listed as moderately tolerant to MYMV -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (same table repeated at https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf, entry 34-9:10)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
GBM 1 is listed with a yield of 11-12 q/ha and 102-105 days to maturity, suited to rabi cultivation in Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
No multi-location trial data, field-trial reports or AICRP reports naming GBM-1 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker or QTL study for GBM-1 was returned. The parentage field ("Not specified") was not confirmed.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The DPD table lists the originating centre as NAU, Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
No breeder name for GBM-1 was found. The Navsari Agricultural University pages returned (https://old.nau.in/alloprtitle.php, https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676) name pulse scientists and the Pulses and Castor Research Station, but none mentions GBM-1, so they are not attributed to it.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No NAU Pulse Research Station contact page or GBM-1 breeder contact was returned. The Pulse Research Station page returned (https://www.aau.in/college-menu/507) belongs to Anand Agricultural University, Vadodara, a different institution, and was not used.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The search returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper that names GBM-1. Greengram results were about other varieties or agronomy (for example https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/102-4-6-103-107.pdf on COGG 973, and https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5417, which cites NAU theses on nutrient management rather than varieties).

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seller pages returned (https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/research-moong-seeds-8745067873.html, https://agribee.in/agriculture-seed/greengram-seeds/greengram-gujarat-4/, https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mung-seeds-guj-4-11807325230.html) sell other moong varieties (Partech-668, Gujarat-4, Guj-4) and do not name GBM-1. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for GBM-1 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Gujarat -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (matches the CSC input "['Gujarat']" and the 2016 release year)

drought.details: Identified as a drought-tolerant genotype. It is among the high-yielding varieties recommended for adoption by farmers under drought conditions. Studies indicate it shows low genotype x environment interaction, contributing to yield stability. Physiological mechanisms contributing to tolerance include the overaccumulation of glycine betaine and adaptive morphological traits like higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD) and Membrane Stability Index (MSI).

heat.details: Recognized as a heat-tolerant green gram genotype capable of setting pods at high temperatures. It is discussed among heat-tolerant mung bean cultivars and genotypes that accumulate glycine betaine, which enhances tolerance to heat stress. IPM 02-3 also exhibits higher Canopy Temperature Depression (CTD), Membrane Stability Index (MSI), and total chlorophyll content under stress, indicating adaptive physiological responses.

salinity.details: Included in studies investigating abiotic stresses like salinity affecting mungbean production. It is mentioned in contexts related to mitigating NaCl stress and examining interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant cultivars, suggesting some level of tolerance or inclusion in salinity tolerance research.

flood.details: Listed among varieties affected by waterlogging stress and included in studies on the response of mungbean to transient waterlogging at germination and seedling stages, but its specific tolerance level is not stated.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV).

pest_resistance.summary: Screened against Meloidogyne incognita (root-knot nematode), but specific resistance level is not provided.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 994 kgs/ha was originally reported. Specific trials showed variations, with yields up to 1409 kg/ha (14.09 q/ha) in comparison trials, and 912 kg/ha (9.12 q/ha) in specific regional projects (Jammu, 2015-2016). It serves as a standard check variety against which newer varieties exhibit yield superiority.
agronomic_details.stability: Demonstrates low genotype x environment interaction, indicating good yield stability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for normal sown conditions during the Kharif season, particularly adapted to the North West Plain Zone of India (Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Rajasthan). Historically, it has been a highly preferred variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed are shiny green and medium seed size with high protein content.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensive field trials include its evaluation under different NPK doses, inclusion in State Adaptive Trials, and performance comparisons against other varieties (e.g., Pusa M 2131, MH 02-15, ML 818). Its performance has been assessed in various regions including Jammu and Central Uttar Pradesh.

seednet_fields.Parentage: (IPM 3-1 X SPS 5) 1.	IPM 3-1: A superior mungbean advanced line with medium tall plants, large, green and shining seeds, resistant to MYMV. 2.	SPS 5: A superior urdbean donor registered as INGR12006, having sympodial pod bearing and high level of resistant to MYMV.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for normal conditions during Spring and kharif season with recommended agronomic practices.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Erect plant with pubescent, green leaves, black pods at maturity, green, shining and medium large seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Highly resistant to MYMV and Cercospora leaf spot and resistant to leaf crinkle and leaf curl diseases.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 1.	Basal: NPKS @ 20:50:40: 20 kg./ha, in case of zinc deficiency: 20 kgZnSo4. 2.	Foliar spray of 2% urea at the time of flowering.

disease_resistance.summary: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): Central variety listing records IPM 312-20 as having moderate resistance to MYMV (Kharif season). The parent IPM 3-1 is described as resistant to MYMV, and the second parent SPS 5 as having high-level resistance to MYMV, which supports the MYMV resistance origin. Cercospora leaf spot: IPM-312-20 was included in a CLS resistance screening of mungbean germplasm, but the search snippet does not state its resistance rating. Host-plant resistance: a ResearchGate review of green gram and black gram diseases lists IPM 312-20 (Vasudha) among varieties cited for host-plant resistance in disease management. Anthracnose and powdery mildew: an InTechOpen listing describes a different variety as moderately resistant to these diseases, and the snippet does not attribute this to IPM 312-20.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests: IPM 312-20 appears in a screening of mungbean germplasm against major sucking pests, but the snippet does not show the column headings, so no resistance rating can be assigned. seednet_fields.Parentage: IPM 99-125 X Co-5 IPM 99-125: An elite mungbean variety released notified in 2004 for Spring cultivation in NEPZ, It has medium tall plants, large, green and shining seeds, and is resistant to yellow mosaic disease. Co 5: an elite mungbean variety released in 1991 for kharif season in Tamil Nadu. This variety is tolerant to yellow mosaic disease.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: North East condition during Spring season.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for normal sown conditions with recommended agronomic practices.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Erect East upright plant with pubescent green leaves, black pods at maturity, green shining and medium large seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to yellow mosaic and cercospora leaf disease.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to thrips and white fly.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Basal: NPKS @ 20: 50: 40: 20 kg/ha, in case of zinc deficiency: 20 kg ZnSo4 Foliar spray of 2% urea at the time of flowering.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: MH-125 (chickpea / green gram)**

**Name check:** The CSC/chickpea name "MH-125" and the Seednet name "MH 125" point to the same entry. In the sources I retrieved, though, the record is a green gram (mungbean) variety, and the Seednet crop field reads GREEN GRAM. The retrieved sources give MH 125 the local name Basanti. Each line below says which name the evidence refers to. Treat the chickpea classification as unconfirmed.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Resistance to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) is recorded for MH 125 / Basanti, shown as a resistance trait in the mungbean release table -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- A chickpea-listing row for "MH 125" (CCSHAU, 2010, Haryana) is marked resistant to MYMV, leaf crinkle, web blight and anthracnose, and moderately resistant to cercospora leaf spot. This row sits in a chickpea table but uses mungbean-type disease traits, so the classification is doubtful -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pest resistance specific to MH-125: No evidence found.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Maturity of 64-70 days and average yield of 12-15 q/ha are listed for Basanti (MH 125) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (also https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf)
- A grower guide gives 64 days to harvest for MH 125 and recommends a seed rate of 8-9 kg/acre for kharif and 12-15 kg/acre for summer, with seed treated with Captan or Thiram at 3 g/kg -- https://apnakhetibazar.com/green-gram-moong/
- A Tamil Nadu multi-location stability study (33 mungbean genotypes, 3 locations) includes MH-125 in its tables. The extracted table is garbled, and one seed-yield-per-plant value of 17.239 appears against MH-125 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324637241_Stability_Analysis_in_Mungbean_Vigna_radiata_L_for_Micronutrients_Fe_Zn_and_Seed_Yield (refers to MH-125 as a mungbean line)
- Chickpea trials: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Parentage: the mungbean table lists Basanti's cross as Asha x PDM 90-1, released 2010 at 12-15 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339424589_Breeding_Progress_and_Future_Challenges_Biotic_Stresses (refers to Basanti / MH 125, mungbean)
- A 2021 mungbean association-mapping study lists Basanti with the pedigree Asha x PDM 90-1, developed at CCS HAU, Hisar, and genotyped with 89 SSR markers -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.749439/full (refers to Basanti, mungbean)
- QTL or marker studies specific to MH-125: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar, per the state release listing -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (refers to Basanti / MH 125, mungbean)
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
- Station or division: The 2021 study attributes Basanti to CCS HAU, Hisar, without naming a division -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.749439/full
- A Haryana varieties list from CCS HAU is available as a PDF, but it gives no breeder names -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1550223744.pdf (refers to chickpea varieties recommended for Haryana, not confirmed for MH-125)

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute contact (CCS HAU, Hisar): No email, phone or postal address found in retrieved results. The only institute-linked source is the varieties PDF at https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1550223744.pdf
- Seed-company contact found, but not an institute or breeder contact: Shakti Vardhak Hybrid Seeds, Tilak Bazaar, Talaki Gate, Hisar, Haryana 125001; 80901 00540 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/moong-seed-8981382030.html (listing reviewed as a dealer lead only; it does not confirm MH-125 stock)

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2021). Association mapping for yield-attributing traits and yellow mosaic disease resistance in mung bean [Vigna radiata (L.) Wilczek]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.749439/full (DOI not retrieved; DOI likely 10.3389/fpls.2021.749439)

- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Stability analysis in mungbean (Vigna radiata L.) for micronutrients (Fe and Zn) and seed yield. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324637241_Stability_Analysis_in_Mungbean_Vigna_radiata_L_for_Micronutrients_Fe_Zn_and_Seed_Yield
- AICRP on MULLaRP, ICAR-IIPR Project Coordinator's Reports, 2017-18 and 2020 (cited as the source of the mungbean release table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (reports themselves not retrieved)
- Chickpea-specific publications on MH-125: No evidence found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME AND CROP CHECK -- "MH 2114" (code DHBH 1397) appears only as a pearl millet hybrid, not green gram. The Seednet name "MH-1142" appears only as a green gram (moong) variety. The "millet" crop field matches MH 2114, and the Seednet crop field matches MH-1142. The two names look like different varieties, so I have kept their evidence under separate labels. The parentage "MH 421" is a green gram name, and no source links it to MH 2114. Searches: 4 of 4 used.

STRESS TOLERANCE
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397, pearl millet] The AICPMIP release table describes the entry as highly resistant to downy mildew and tolerant to rust and insect pests, but the table text is ambiguous about which row these traits belong to -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
[MH 2114] Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.
[MH-1142, green gram] A seller page says it does not tolerate waterlogging; this is a commercial claim, not an official trial result -- https://sanjivaniseeds.com/product/moong-mh-1142

DISEASE AND PEST
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] Same AICPMIP table entry as above (downy mildew, rust, insect pests); row assignment uncertain -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
[MH-1142] Official-style release table lists it as moderately resistant to anthracnose and powdery mildew and resistant to MYMV -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] The same claims appear in a Hindi release summary (CVRC 2020) -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-1142/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] The 52nd Annual Pearl Millet Workshop proceedings list MH 2114 among hybrids in a trial at Jamnagar, SK Nagar, Aurangabad and Dhule -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf
[MH 2114] Yield and maturity data from a verified source: No evidence found.
[MH-1142] The release table gives 11-12 q/ha yield and 60-65 days to maturity -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] Commercial pages give different figures (63-70 days; 5-6 quintals per acre), so the figures conflict -- https://market.plantix.net/en/products/seeds/fa0224bd-83b8-42ce-972d-3eb10b39329e/moong-mh1142-truthfully-labelled-seed-4-kg-cloth-bag/

GENETICS AND QTL
[MH 2114] No evidence found for markers, QTL or parentage (Muskan x BDYR 2 / MH 421).
[MH-1142] No evidence found for markers, QTL or parentage. The search returned a green gram Zn fertilizer study on MH 421, which is a different topic and is not attributed to this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
[MH 2114 / DHBH 1397] No breeder name found. Results about MPKV Dhule pearl millet units concern other hybrids and varieties (e.g., Dhanshakti, Phule Mahashakti) and are not attributed here -- https://www.acdhule.edu.in/wDepartment/Bajara-Research-Station.pdf
[MH-1142] The release table lists the originating centre as HAU Hisar, not MPKV Dhule -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
[MH-1142] No breeder name found.

CONTACT DETAILS
[MH 2114] No evidence found (no breeder, institute email, phone or address).
[MH-1142] No evidence found (no breeder, institute email, phone or address).

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated (2017). Proceedings of the 52nd Annual Pearl Millet Workshop, trial listing for MH 2114. AICPMIP -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf (year taken from file name)
Authors not stated (n.d.). Table

drought.details: No specific information provided regarding MH 1772's drought tolerance level.

heat.details: Genotype MH 1772 has been studied for its heat tolerance and anatomical modifications in response to heat stress to mitigate impact on mungbean yield under different sowing conditions. It is one of the genotypes assessed for heat tolerance.

salinity.details: MH 1772 is identified as a salt-tolerant genotype and is recommended for cultivation in salt-affected regions to enhance mungbean production. Studies have focused on its response to salinity (NaCl) on germination and seedling growth.

flood.details: No specific information provided regarding MH 1772's tolerance to flood stress.

disease_resistance.summary: MH 1772 is a high-yielding disease-resistant variety, specifically resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). It has also been included in screenings against web blight disease (Macrophomina phaseolina infection), although a specific resistance level for MH 1772 against web blight is not explicitly stated as 'resistant' in the provided results.

pest_resistance.summary: MH 1772 has been included in germplasm screening trials against major insect pests such as the gram pod borer and sucking insects. However, its specific level of resistance to these pests is not explicitly detailed as 'resistant' or 'tolerant' in the provided results.

agronomic_details.yield: MH 1772 is a high-yielding variety, with an average yield of 11-13 quintals per hectare (q/ha). Farmers have reported achieving 10-15% more yield by cultivating this variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified in the provided results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The variety has been notified for cultivation during the Kharif season in the North East Plain Zones (NEPZ).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in the provided results.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials were conducted in farmers' fields in a participatory research mode, indicating adaptability and performance in real-world conditions.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: MH 1772 was included in association mapping studies for yield attributing traits and Yellow Mosaic Disease Resistance in Mungbean. While specific genetic markers (QTL/SNP/SSR) directly identified for MH 1772 are not detailed, its involvement in such studies indicates its genetic characterization.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MH 318 (greengram / moong)
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "MH 318", so every finding below refers to that one name. Seednet (seednet.gov.in) did not appear in any search result, so no Seednet record was checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to MYMV (mungbean yellow mosaic virus); no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Listed as resistant to yellow mosaic virus, with its main characteristics described as well under rice-wheat rotation -- https://krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/ (the search result shows the URL with "www." omitted in the source: https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to MYMV; no other disease or pest resistance recorded for MH 318 -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Dealer page says it has resistance to yellow mosaic virus; this is a commercial claim, not a trial result -- https://drseeds.in/moong/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 60-65 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Yield 14 q/ha in kharif and 10 q/ha in spring/summer -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Dealer page gives 8-9 quintals per acre; units differ from the official figures, so treat it as unverified -- https://drseeds.in/moong/
- Pot-trial comparison of MH 318 with other genotypes under zinc fertilisation (CCS HAU, 2010-11). Per the snippet, MH 318 had among the lowest pods per plant (5.28) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317594571_Green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_Productivity_and_Grain_Quality_enrichment_through_Zinc_Fertilization
- No multi-location AICRP trial result for MH 318 found

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (no parentage, breeding method or QTL/marker study in results). The DPD record gives no parentage either.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar, released 2015 per DPD -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Release year conflict: a 2022 Krishakjagat article gives 2016 (SVRC), while DPD gives 2015 -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/news/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-mh-318/
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found
- Institution page: https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-11 (lists MH-318 among moong varieties with raw seed production in 2022-23; the figure's unit is not shown in the snippet)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder: No evidence found
- Institute: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, Haryana, India (postal code 125004, from departmental affiliations in a ResearchGate listing) -- https://researchgate.net/institution/CCS_Haryana_Agricultural_University
- Institute website: https://hau.ac.in ; no official email or phone number for the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding appeared in any result

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (2010-11 pot study; year of publication not shown). Title: "Green gram (Vigna radiata L.) Productivity and Grain Quality enrichment through Zinc Fertilization", CCS HAU, Hisar -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317594571_Green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_Productivity_and_Grain_Quality_enrichment_through_Zinc_Fertilization
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (screen-house iron-enrichment study on seven greengram genotypes including MH 318; year and journal not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317594571_Green_gram_Vigna_radiata_L_Productivity_and_Grain_Quality_enrichment_through_Zinc_Fertilization

drought.details: ML 267 has been consistently reported as drought-resistant. It was utilized in studies evaluating source leaf responses to water-deficit stresses and in experiments where drought was induced by PEG (Polyethylene glycol). Agrobacterium mediated genetic transformation attempts were made for ML 267 specifically to enhance drought stress tolerance, indicating its potential or existing tolerance. It has also been used as a test crop in drought-related experiments.

heat.details: ML 267 is identified as a heat-tolerant mungbean genotype based on morpho-physiological parameters. It has been evaluated in crosses (e.g., ML 267 × LGG 528) for heat stress tolerance and yield attributes using generation mean analysis. Studies have also evaluated stress tolerance indices to identify heat tolerance, including ML 267.

salinity.details: ML 267 is listed among varieties for developing bio-fortified mungbean lines with enhanced stress tolerance, including salinity. Specific studies have investigated salt tolerance in mungbean cultivars like ML 267 and the interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant mungbean involving this genotype.

flood.details: Waterlogging is mentioned as a key abiotic stress for mungbean generally, but no specific information on ML 267's tolerance or susceptibility to flood or waterlogging was found.

disease_resistance.summary: ML 267 is reported to be resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). However, it is classified as Highly Susceptible (HS) to the root-knot nematode, *Meloidogyne incognita*.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance details found, apart from its susceptibility to *Meloidogyne incognita* (a nematode pest), which is listed under disease resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: While specific average yield values are not provided, ML 267 has been evaluated for yield and yield attributes in genetic crosses. Its 100-seed weight is reported as 12.0g. It is considered a popular cultivar.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly specified.
agronomic_details.adaptation: ML 267 is a popular cultivar of greengram, adaptable for cultivation during both Kharif and Summer seasons. It is particularly recommended for the North Western Plain Zone. It shows good tolerance to the post-emergence herbicide imazethapyr, which is beneficial for weed management. It is also suitable for sowing as sprouted seeds in short-duration pulse rotations.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: HAIRINESS OF STEM AND BROAD; SLIGHT TINGE OF PURPLE COLOUR. The seed size is described as small.
agronomic_details.field_trials: ML 267 has been used as a test crop in strip plot design experiments investigating different tillage methods. It has also been extensively used in generational studies (P1, P2, F1, F2, B1, and B2 generations) to analyze yield and stress tolerance traits.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (e.g., SNPs, SSRs) or QTL positions are directly reported for ML 267 in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: ML 267 has been utilized in genetic crosses for research purposes. A cross of ML 267 × LGG 528 was used for generation mean analysis to study the inheritance of yield, yield attributes, Water Use Efficiency (WUE), and heat stress tolerance. This cross also produced transgressive segregants for traits such as harvest index, Specific Leaf Area (SLA), Specific Leaf Weight (SLW), and relative injury (stress-related traits). Additionally, a cross between ML 267 and urdbean cv. Mash 114 was made for mapping Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) resistance, indicating that MYMV resistance in this cross is controlled by digenic recessive genes.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: ML 267 has been included in studies aimed at identifying heat-tolerant genotypes through morpho-physiological parameters and gene expression analysis related to abiotic stress tolerance. However, specific genes or pathways linked directly to ML 267's tolerance mechanisms are not detailed.

It has been evaluated in crosses (e.g., ML 267 × LGG 528) for heat stress tolerance and yield attributes using generation mean analysis. Studies have also evaluated stress tolerance indices to identify heat tolerance, including ML 267.

salinity.details: ML 267 is listed among varieties for developing bio-fortified mungbean lines with enhanced stress tolerance, including salinity. Specific studies have investigated salt tolerance in mungbean cultivars like ML 267 and the interactive effects of sodium and calcium on proline metabolism in salt-tolerant mungbean involving this genotype.

flood.details: Waterlogging is mentioned as a key abiotic stress for mungbean generally, but no specific information on ML 267's tolerance or susceptibility to flood or waterlogging was found.

submergence.details: While submergence tolerance is mentioned generally in research contexts, there is no direct evidence within the provided results regarding ML 267's specific reaction to submergence.

disease_resistance.summary: ML 267 is reported to be resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). However, it is classified as Highly Susceptible (HS) to the root-knot nematode, *Meloidogyne incognita*.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance details found, apart from its susceptibility to *Meloidogyne incognita* (a nematode pest), which is listed under disease resistance.

genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: ML 267 has been utilized in genetic crosses for research purposes. A cross of ML 267 × LGG 528 was used for generation mean analysis to study the inheritance of yield, yield attributes, Water Use Efficiency (WUE), and heat stress tolerance. This cross also produced transgressive segregants for traits such as harvest index, Specific Leaf Area (SLA), Specific Leaf Weight (SLW), and relative injury (stress-related traits). Additionally, a cross between ML 267 and urdbean cv. Mash 114 was made for mapping Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) resistance, indicating that MYMV resistance in this cross is controlled by digenic recessive genes.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: ML 267 has been included in studies aimed at identifying heat-tolerant genotypes through morpho-physiological parameters and gene expression analysis related to abiotic stress tolerance. agronomic_performance.adaptation: ML 267 is a popular cultivar of greengram, adaptable for cultivation during both Kharif and Summer seasons. It is particularly recommended for the North Western Plain Zone. It shows good tolerance to the post-emergence herbicide imazethapyr, which is beneficial for weed management. Treat the crop as green gram (Vigna radiata) unless the Seednet record shows otherwise. The Seednet portal itself was not reachable in these searches, so variety code A0305151 is unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PKV GREEN GOLD (also AKM 9911). Evidence refers to the green gram / mungbean variety. Seednet lists the crop as green gram, but the input says chickpea. Chickpea sources in the results are about other varieties or are a probable listing error, so no chickpea evidence is attributed to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
[Name: PKV Green Gold / AKM 9911; crop: green gram]
Moderately resistant to powdery mildew (PM abbreviation as printed; expansion inferred) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Searches 1 to 3 returned no such data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
[Name: PKV Green Gold / AKM 9911; crop: green gram]
Moderately resistant to PM (powdery mildew); bold seed and long pod noted as salient features -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
Chickpea listing gives "Tolerant to PM, suitable for kharif" for "PKV green gold PDKV" (crop mismatch; likely a misplaced row) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
[Name: PKV Green Gold / AKM 9911; crop: green gram]

disease_resistance.summary: PA 9072 (pearl millet): the AICPMIP table row associates it with resistance to downy mildew, blast, smut and ergot (garbled; low-to-medium confidence). The ProAgro dealer page lists downy mildew resistance (secondary, brand conflict). Mungbean PUSA-9072 (not attributed to PA 9072): resistant to dry root rot in a poly-house screen of 47 genotypes; moderately susceptible to mungbean yellow mosaic virus in a West Bengal field study; moderately resistant to YMV in a Pharma Innovation Journal screen of AICRP mungbean entries (rabi 2017).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PA 9072 EVIDENCE DIGEST

NAME AND CROP NOTE
- The CSC name PA 9072 (crop: millet) matches the Bayer pearl millet hybrid. The AICPMIP table lists PA 9072 among pearl millet hybrids from Bayer Bio Science, Hyderabad -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- The Seednet name PUSA-9072 (crop: green gram) is a different entity. Every source found for "Pusa 9072" concerns mungbean, not the Bayer hybrid. Treat the two names as unresolved and do not merge the evidence.
- The release date in the input (2018-08-10) could not be verified. The table's notification rows are garbled and I could not reliably tie any S.O. number to PA 9072 -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Parentage: not found. The table text near the PA 9072 row contains fragments such as "PSP91 x" and "PP107", but the alignment is unclear, so I did not assign them -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
- PA 9072 (pearl millet) is listed with moisture stress tolerance and lodging tolerance -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf (garbled row; medium confidence)
- A dealer page for "PROAGRO PA 9072 HYBRID BAJRA" describes tolerance to moisture stress, suitability for low-rainfall areas, and tolerance to lodging -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072 (brand conflict: ProAgro, not Bayer; treat as secondary)
- PUSA-9072 (mungbean): one drought-related remark is only general to the crop, not to this variety -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/growing-of-green-gram-vigna-radiata-l-in-an-inceptisol-of-alluvial-soil/ (no variety-specific drought data found)
- No heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data found for either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The pearl millet table row for PA 9072 associates it with downy mildew, blast, smut and ergot resistance, and shoot-fly tolerance -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf (garbled; low-to-medium confidence)
- The ProAgro dealer page lists downy mildew resistance -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_PA_9072

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE --
- Pairy Mung is not described with stress-tolerance traits in any source I found. A central-release table lists a powdery mildew resistance entry on the row beside a "TM 2000-2 (Pairy Mung)" line, but the layout is garbled and does not clearly attach that trait to Pairy Mung. Resistant to Powdery Mildew -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Pairy Mung. (Searched: Pairy Mung green gram variety.)

DISEASE AND PEST --
- The same table lists Pairy Mung's originating centre as IGKV, Raipur, but gives no MYMV, Cercospora or other disease reaction for it. Resistant to Powdery Mildew -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for insect or nematode reaction specific to Pairy Mung.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
- Central-release table entry: Pairy Mung, 2010 (SVRC), originating centre IGKV Raipur, yield 12 q/ha, 65-70 days to maturity, area of adoption CG -- https://www.journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45672_1.pdf
- The same review lists a second row, TM 2000-2 Pairy Mung, with 88-90 days and 10-11 q/ha. The day-count conflict between rows is unresolved.
- Multilocation rabi trial (2017-18 to 2019-20): entry IGKM 05-18-2 showed an 8.29% yield increase over the best check, Pairy Mung (833.27 kg/ha). Pairy Mung served as the check, not the entry. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333435816_Towards_Development_of_Climate_Smart_Mungbean_Challenges_and_Opportunities
- AICRP on MULLaRP overview (general mandate, no Pairy Mung data): Summer and kharif pulses Mungbean and Urdbean, plus rabi pulses, are covered by the year-round project -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/aicrp-on-mullarp-en

GENETICS AND QTL --
- No evidence found on parentage, pedigree, QTL or marker studies for Pairy Mung. Parentage field "Not specified" remains unresolved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION --
- Originating centre: IGKV, Raipur (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya), per the central-release table -- https://www.journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45672_1.pdf
- No breeder or lead scientist name found for Pairy Mung. (Searched: Pairy Mung green gram breeder developed by institute.)
- Institution field "Not explicitly stated" is resolved as IGKV, Raipur, based on the table only.

CONTACT DETAILS --
- No evidence found for breeder names, emails, phone numbers or postal addresses for Pairy Mung or IGKV Raipur. No IGKV institute contact page was retrieved. -- Searched: https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (no contact data)

PUBLICATIONS --
- Central Released Varieties of Green Gram/Mungbean in India (table compiled from AICRP on MULLaRP Project Coordinator's Reports and ICAR annual reports, seednet.gov.in cited as source). Authors not stated. (2021-23). Central released varieties of Green Gram/Mungbean in India. ICAR-IIPR/DPD compilation -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Review article on mung bean origin, genetics and breeding, incl. the release table above. Author: Principal Scientist & Head, Division of Vegetable Crops, IIHR Bangalore (retired; name not given in snippet). Year not given. Mung bean review. Journal CRA -- https://www.journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45672_1.pdf
- Climate Smart Mungbean: Challenges and Opportunities (Year not confirmed; authors not in snippet). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333435816_Towards_Development_of_Climate_Smart_Mungbean_Challenges_and_Opportunities
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or AICRP annual report entry specific to Pairy Mung was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY --
- No evidence found for Pairy Mung seed from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, IGKV or private dealers. Search results were generic moong retailers that do not name Pairy Mung. Seednet portal listing not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES --
- Area of adoption recorded as CG (Chhattisgarh) in the central-release table -- https://www.journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45672_1.pdf
- Release year recorded as 2010 (SVRC) in the same table. Release year field "NaT" is resolved to 2010 from this source only.

NAME AND CROP NOTES --
- variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Pairy Mung". Evidence refers to this name. The Seednet portal was not retrieved directly; table entries cite seednet.gov.in as a data source.
- Crop mismatch: the input record says chickpea, but the Seednet crop name is green gram (moong, Vigna radiata). All evidence found concerns green gram. Chickpea was not searched. Check the variety code A0305149 against the Seednet record before using this digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I ran four searches, but the search tool then hit its usage limit, so I could not re-query the one source that mentions Pant Mung-5. Only one result (the DPD central-release compilation) contains the variety, and I saw only its first ~600 characters. Treat the findings below as thin and unverified.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The search used "Pant Mung-5" for both the CSC release name and the Seednet name. Seednet did not appear in any result, so I could not confirm the portal name or variety code A0305153. The evidence below refers to "Pant Mung-5" as written in the DPD compilation.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Not found in the captured text. The snippet truncated before the salient-features column for this entry. No evidence on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was captured. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Pant Mung-5 is listed in the salient-features column as resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (the text reads "Res. to mungbean yellow", truncated). The full resistance wording and rating were not captured. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The compilation lists yield of 10-12 q/ha and days to maturity of 62-79 for Pant Mung-5. The source gives these as a single row, so I cannot confirm the exact mapping of each number to each column. drought.details: No search result attributes drought tolerance to Pusa 1641. The IARI Annual Report 2021 mentions a QTL introgressed from ICC 4958 for drought tolerance, but the snippet does not state which variety carries it, so it cannot be assigned to Pusa 1641.

heat.details: Pusa 1641 is described as suitable for the summer season, with a short maturity of 62-64 days, which supports adaptation to high-temperature summer cropping. No physiological heat-tolerance data (e.g., pollen viability, membrane stability) were found in the search results, so this rating is inferred from season suitability rather than measured tolerance.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence for Pusa 1641 in the search results.

flood.details: No waterlogging or flood tolerance evidence for Pusa 1641 in the search results.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV). The IARI Annual Report 2021 describes Pusa 1641 as a MYMV-resistant mungbean variety with improved yield and resistance to MYMV. The DPD compendium lists it as resistant to MYMV with low incidence of major diseases in its summer-season row. No resistance to powdery mildew, Fusarium wilt, or other diseases is confirmed for this variety. The Fusarium wilt resistance mentioned in the IARI 2021 report is not attributed to Pusa 1641 in the snippet.

pest_resistance.summary: Not confirmed. The DPD compendium includes a pod-borer tolerance statement in a table row near Pusa 1641, but the snippet does not clearly tie it to this variety. No other insect-pest resistance data were found for Pusa 1641.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for summer-season cultivation in the NCR/Delhi region, based on IARI and DPD references.

seednet_fields.Parentage:
AAU 34 x T44
AAU 34 is a state recommended high yielding mungbean variety from AAU jorhat for summer sowing in Assam. T 44 is a national variety from CSAUAT, Kanpur.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Moderately resistant to pod borer, aphids, leaf rolleran to 15 kg N, 35 kg P2O5 15 kg K2O. Seed rate 20-22 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 10-15 kg N+35kg P2O5 15 kg K2O as basal application. DAP @ 75 kg/ha may be applied in lieu of urea and SSP in non- inoculated crop.

disease_resistance.summary: Cercospora Leaf Spot (CLS): listed as resistant (AAU source states SGC 20 and Sonai were recommended for kharif season endowed with CLS and YMV resistance capacity). pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence specific to SGC 20 found in searched sources. A pod bug management recommendation (quinalphos then dimethoate sprays) was accepted for kharif 2020 for greengram, but the source is not variety-specific and does not indicate SGC 20 pest resistance. No evidence on whitefly, thrips, aphid or other pest reactions.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for summer and kharif seasons in Assam. Assam Package of Practices lists suitability for all zones of Assam except BVZ. A source mentioning Zone-III (West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh) for an AAU mungbean variety was not attached to SGC 20 in the digest and is excluded.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Duration of 65-68 days is reported in the Assam Package of Practices, which conflicts with the 35-40 day maturity in the original variety data. Protein content of 24.40% is reported in the same source. Morphological characteristics not found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Summer phosphorus and potassium fertilization trial: SGC-20 gave net returns of Rs 31464 and a B:C ratio of 1.25, with IPM 02-3 at the top of the comparison. (2) Assam summer greengram recommendation lists SGC-20 among high-yielding varieties for Goalpara district (no yield values given in digest). No other trial results for SGC 20 were found. An AAU extension programme (2020-2023) demonstrated SGC-16 through 14 KVKs, not SGC 20.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SGC 20 (AAU SHN Mung 02) greengram: evidence digest

Search budget: 4 web_search calls used (the maximum). The Seednet portal was not searched directly, so no evidence was found under the Seednet name "SGC 20 (AAU SHN Mung 02) (Buroi)" itself. The evidence below refers to the CVRC/AAU name "SGC 20 (AAU SHN Mung 02)" unless noted. Sources call it "AAU SGC 20 (AAU-SHN Mung 02)-Buroi", so the Buroi suffix appears only in some sources. Parentage (AAU 34 x T44) was not confirmed by any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
SGC 20 and Sonai were recommended for kharif season endowed with Cercospora Leaf Spot (CLS) and Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) resistance capacity. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/127
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to SGC 20.

DISEASE AND PEST
SGC 20 is listed as resistant to CLS and YMV, with a grain yield of 12-13 q/ha, 65-68 days duration and 24.40% protein -- https://www.aau.ac.in/ (Assam Package of Practices for Kharif Crops, 2015; https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf)
Pod bug management in greengram (quinalphos then dimethoate sprays) was accepted for recommendation in Kharif 2020, but the source is not variety-specific -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117
No evidence found for resistance to powdery mildew, anthracnose, or MYMV specific to SGC 20.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield, duration and protein figures above -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
In one summer P and K fertilization trial, SGC-20 gave net returns of ₹31464 and a B:C ratio of 1.25, compared with IPM 02-3 at the top -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/126362/52260/383879
Assam recommendation for summer greengram lists SGC-20 among high-yielding varieties for the Goalpara district -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP-2012/statewiseplans/Assam/ASSAM26-Goalpara-10.02.2017.pdf
Sowing window for kharif is mid-August to mid-September, with PSB inoculation at 50 g/kg seed -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
Basal 40 kg P2O5/ha and Rhizobium plus PSB seed inoculation are recommended for greengram at Shillongani (not variety-specific) -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/117

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or genetic studies specific to SGC 20. A DST-funded marker-assisted study on synchrony in greengram at AAU Jorhat is listed, but it is not variety-specific -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/12

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Release route: the variety was identified by the SSSC meeting held on 06-05-2022 for forwarding to CVRC -- https://www.aau.ac.in/research/directorate/directorate-of-research(agri)/rars-shillongani/faculty/10/117/profile/Dr.-Hironya-Kumar-Borah/249
Notification: Greengram variety AAU SGC 20 (AAU-SHN Mung 02)-Buroi was notified by the 90th CVRC meeting held on 02-05-2023 at New Delhi. -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Hironya-Kumar-Borah/249
Lead breeder (per AAU profile): Dr. Hironya Kumar Borah, Assistant Pulse Breeder background at RARS Shillongani, who developed 4 greengram, 5 blackgram and three fieldpea varieties till date -- https://www.aau.ac.in/faculty/profile/Dr-Hironya-Kumar-Borah/249

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Moong-3 (greengram)

Name note: I searched both "Shalimar Moong -3" (CSC name) and "SHALIMAR MOONG-3" (Seednet name). The only variety-specific match used the spelling "Shalimar Moong-3."

Search limitation: the search tool hit its usage limit during my follow-up check. I could not reopen the full text of the pages, so the findings below come from the search snippets only. The institutional and trial details need checking against the full pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page describing disease or pest resistance for this variety was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage "SL44xTM-98-3" comes from the input record, not from any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. A central release listing groups "Shalimar Moong-3" under SKUAST-Jammu, Kashmir -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf. No breeder name was found. The Rangreth station attribution comes from the input record only.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, postal address or contact page was returned for this variety. Institute-level contact should be taken from the SKUAST-Kashmir or Dryland Agriculture Research Station site, which I could not retrieve.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The searches returned no paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming this variety. An arccjournals Legume Research page was returned for a greengram query, but its snippet did not mention this variety, so I have not listed it.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The only seed listing returned was an Amazon page for "Green World IPM 205-7 (Virat)" -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-205-7-Researched-Farming/dp/B0C82J75T3. It is a different variety and product, so I discarded it.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Partial. The same central release listing gives Shalimar Moong-3 a Kashmir/SKUAST-Jammu entry -- https://dpd.gov.in/3.%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf. drought.details: General stress tolerance is mentioned, but specific drought tolerance mechanisms or direct evidence for SML-832's drought tolerance is not detailed in the provided results. It is listed among varieties tolerant to stress.

heat.details: SML-832 is identified as a heat-tolerant mungbean genotype, found to be more tolerant to heat stress than SML-668. Studies have investigated its reproductive biology, leaf function, yield traits, and morphological and physio-biochemical adaptive responses under heat stress conditions (e.g., >40/25°C day/night temperatures). It is used as a reference for heat tolerance in studies.

salinity.details: SML-832 has been included in studies investigating salt stress tolerance in mungbean and its quality under salt-affected conditions on farmer's fields. This suggests a degree of tolerance or focus on its performance in such environments.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance for SML-832 is available in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: SML-832 is tolerant to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) and resistant to powdery mildew. The establishment of bacterial leaf spot of green gram was also noted in studies related to PAU.

pest_resistance.summary: SML-832 has been screened against Meloidogyne incognita (root-knot nematode), but its specific reaction (resistance/susceptibility) is not provided.

agronomic_details.yield: 11-12 quintals per acre (or hectare, unit not explicitly stated but common for such tables)
agronomic_details.stability: It is tolerant to general stress and YMV, contributing to yield stability. Its suitability for both Spring and Summer seasons indicates adaptability across different cultivation periods.
agronomic_details.adaptation: SML-832 is well-adapted for cultivation in Punjab, particularly establishing a sizeable niche for summer moong in the central districts of the state. It is suitable for both spring and summer sowing.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Leaves are large in size and dark green in colour. Pods are dark brown colour at maturity. Pod husk/cover is thick. Seed septation in pods is distinct. It has an erect plant type with medium stature and bears pods. It produces shining medium bold grains.
agronomic_details.field_trials: SML-832 has been extensively used as a test cultivar in field and experimental studies focusing on heat tolerance, salinity tolerance, yield, and water use efficiency.

drought.details: The variety SML 1827 has been the subject of investigation concerning germination parameters under drought stress during the Zaid season of 2022. Studies explored the effects of zinc and boron foliar application on primed SML 1827 mung bean under drought conditions.

heat.details: While Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) has conducted genetic mapping for heat stress tolerance in mungbean, specific details or resistance levels for SML 1827 are not provided in the search results.

salinity.details: SML 1827 has been used as a genotype in studies investigating Salicylic Acid- and Ascorbic Acid–Induced Salt Tolerance in Mung bean. It is also mentioned as a cross involving a salt-tolerant parent (S100), suggesting its potential or relevance in salt tolerance breeding, with a QTL for salt tolerance having been identified in related research.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance is available in the provided search results.

disease_resistance.summary: SML 1827 is resistant and tolerant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV) / Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV), a significant threat to greengram production. It is specifically recommended for cultivation in Punjab to manage this disease.

pest_resistance.summary: No information regarding pest resistance is available in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been a focus of investigations conducted during the Zaid season, including studies on drought stress and the effects of zinc and boron foliar application.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: A QTL related to salt tolerance has been identified in a cross involving SML 1827, specifically in the context of its parentage with salt-tolerant S100.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: A QTL linked to salt tolerance was studied in a cross where SML 1827 was involved, specifically between S100 (salt tolerant) x Tokyo (salt sensitive).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: SML 1827 was developed from the cross ML 881 × RBL 35. It is a highly YMD disease resistant variety, indicating successful breeding for this trait.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST
Variety: 4216 (CSC minutes name) / S 4216 (Seednet name, listed under GREEN GRAM). Crop: maize. Institution: Rasi Seeds. Four searches were run. No result named 4216 or S 4216 as a maize variety, so most headings are empty.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searched under "4216" and "S 4216". Results were general maize release and trial pages with no mention of this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for 4216. The only company claim is general: It focuses on producing hybrid seeds for Indian agriculture, aiming to support farmers by improving yields and addressing nutritional needs through seeds with traits that resist biotic and abiotic stresses across varied agro-climatic conditions. This is company-level and does not name 4216. -- https://www.leadiq.com/c/rasi-seeds/5a1d7cb6240000240056990e

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for 4216. Discarded: a Rasi listing for "RASI - 4212" gives a duration of 100-110 days and medium plant height. seednet_fields.Parentage: (TKG 19A x Kadiri 3) x TKG 19A cross was made at DGR, Junagadh and supplied to RARI Durgapura for further selection at F5 stage.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The proposed variety has responded well to the higher than recommended doses of nitrogenous and plosphatic fertilizers. RG 559-3 gave 7219 pod yield at 125% recommended dose of fertilizer compare to 7061 kg/ha at 100% RDF.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Virginia bunch, intermediate: growth habit; leaflets, medium green and lanceolate; Pod bold, Prominently reticulated, slight curved beak, slight constricted, 2-seeded: Kernels bold with saloman colour testa.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: For peanut bud necrosis disease the proposed variety RG 559 – 3 has shown much lower incidence (12.65%) as compared to all seven zonal checks viz; Girnar 2 (23.9%), GG 21 (32.83%) HNG 69 (15.23%), Utkarsh (22.93%) CSMG 19 (23.57%), Raj munfali-1 (20.23%) and HNG 123 (16.73%).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: For  thrips, the vector  of  Pernut  bud necrosis disease, the proposed variety RG 559-3 has shown lower damage of leaves (17.84%) compared to HNG 69 (19.98%), Raj mungfa1i-1 (18.54%) anti HNG 123 (17.95%). Similarly for leaf hopper, RG
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 60 kg phosphate and 15 kg nitrogen before sowing, through 8 bags of SSP and 33 kg urea.  400 kg gypum/ha at the time of field preparation once in two  years.

disease_resistance.summary: Peanut bud necrosis, late leaf spot and rust: the variety shows lower incidence than zonal check varieties (AICRP-G/ICAR-IIGR text). No formal resistance rating (for example, a scale score) was found for this variety, so the level of resistance is not quantified.

pest_resistance.summary: Reported tolerance to Spodoptera litura (tobacco caterpillar), leaf miner, leafhopper and thrips, with a reported 10-15% saving in plant-protection cost (AICRP-G success stories). A secondary source lists tolerance to Spodoptera litura, leaf miner and thrips. No formal resistance rating was found, and the digest does not give the mechanism or quantitative pest scores.

agronomic_details.yield: Pod yield 3173 kg/ha, 17-29% above zonal checks (Girnar 2, GG 21, HNG 69, Utkarsh, CSMG 19, Raj Mungfali-1, HNG 123). Kernel yield 2201 kg/ha. Oil content 49% (1078 kg/ha oil). Fertilizer trial (CSC data): 7219 kg/ha pod yield at 125% recommended dose of fertilizer compared with 7061 kg/ha at 100% RDF. The two pod yield figures come from different sources and conditions and are not reconciled in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources, beyond use as a check entry in an AMMI/GGE genotype-by-environment study (kharif 2019-2020, 43 confectionery groundnut genotypes). The digest gives no stability parameters for this variety.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the North-Western zone (Zone I), kharif season, in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab. Developed and tested at RARI Durgapura. Response to higher-than-recommended fertilizer doses is reported. No agro-climatic or soil-type detail was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 125 days (medium maturity), per AICRP-G/ICAR-IIGR variety listing
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Virginia bunch type. Shelling out-turn 69%, 100-kernel weight 65 g, fodder 2500-3000 kg/ha. Listed as large-seeded (secondary source). Morphological characteristics beyond growth habit and seed traits: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location testing carried out at RARI Durgapura before release (AICRP-G success stories). (2) Pod yield 3173 kg/ha, 17-29% above seven zonal checks (AICRP-G success stories). (3) Kernel yield 2201 kg/ha (AICRP-G success stories). (4) Shelling out-turn 69%, 100-kernel weight 65 g, oil content 49% (1078 kg/ha oil), fodder 2500-3000 kg/ha (ICAR-IIGR AICRP-G listing). (5) Fertilizer response trial: 7219 kg/ha at 125% RDF versus 7061 kg/ha at 100% RDF (CSC data). (6) Used as a check entry in an AMMI/GGE study of confectionery groundnut, kharif 2019-2020, 43 genotypes (Scientific Reports). Plot-wise yields, trial sites and seasons: Not found in searched sources beyond these summaries.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DH-245 (groundnut)

STRESS TOLERANCE
Foliar disease resistance is the only stress trait reported for this variety; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence was found for DH-245. A Dh 245 description says it is resistant to fungal foliar diseases and high-oleic (>70%) with about 10% higher pod yield than the check G2-52 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
DH-245 is described as notable for high oleic content and resistance to late leaf spot (LLS) and rust, and as suited to Karnataka -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Drought tolerance, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for DH-245. The drought-tolerant lines Dh-256 and Dh-257 appear in a Pharma Innovation Journal paper, but those are different varieties and were discarded -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue9/PartE/11-8-475-872.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to late leaf spot and rust; no insect-pest reaction was given for DH-245 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
DH-245 is listed as high oleic acid (>70%) with resistance to foliar diseases, recommended for Karnataka, in an AICRP-era variety table -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
Stem rot, collar rot, root rot and pest reactions specific to DH-245: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Pod yield reported as 1500-2900 kg/ha, kharif season, maturity group 105-108 days (medium), on the CSC/gazette description -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
A different summary gives DH-245 (2019) a yield of 1480-2340 kg/ha; this conflicts with the 2018 CSC record and the 2019 date should be treated as unverified -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Multi-location or on-station trial data for DH-245 beyond the 10% yield-over-check figure: No evidence found. The conference entry below uses DH-245 as a check at UAS Dharwad in kharif 2016 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274256904_Marker_assisted_selection_for_high_oleate_trait_in_groundnut
Field-level farmer adoption of DH-245: No evidence found. A Karnataka extension study mentions Dh 245 only in its introduction -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/uploads/archives/8-6-102-410.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Origin: DH-245 is a gamma-ray (300 Gy) induced mutant of GPBD 4, which conflicts with the "Not specified" parentage on the input record -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
Mutagenesis origin is also described in a genetic enhancement review, which credits EMS/induced mutagenesis of GPBD 4 with producing Dh 245 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
QTL or marker study naming DH-245 as a mapped population or result: No evidence found. The QTL for LLS and rust found in the search came from donor GPBD 4 and does not name DH-245 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Groundnut-varieties-released-in-the-last-20-years-2000-2020-for-their-cultivation-in_tbl2_357544986

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: AICRP Groundnut, UAS Dharwad centre developed the high-oleic mutant Dh-245 -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88
Developer citation: Nadaf et al. (2017) is cited as the source for Dh 245 in a genetic-enhancement review. Only the surname and year were found; the full paper was not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
Lead breeder full name and station address: No evidence found beyond the surname above.
Seednet lists the institution only as "University of Agricultural Sciences", which is consistent with UAS Dharwad but does not confirm it -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=88

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder name, role, email, phone, postal address and institute contact page for DH-245: No evidence found in any search result. The search returned no UAS Dharwad or AICRP-Groundnut contact page. Do not use contacts from the Junagadh (JAU) or Directorate of Groundnut Research pages, which concern other stations -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh

PUBLICATIONS
Patel, S. V., & Radhakrishnan, T. (2015). Marker assisted selection for high oleate trait in groundnut. National Conference on Biodiversity and Bioresource Utilization, Saurashtra University (conference paper). DH-245 is used as a check in a kharif 2016 trial at MARS, UAS Dharwad -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274256904_Marker_assisted_selection_for_high_oleate_trait_in_groundnut
Nadaf et al. (2017). Dh 245 development paper (full title, journal and DOI not retrieved). Cited in a review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report, or peer-reviewed DH-245 paper: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers for DH-245: No evidence found. The seed-related results were generic groundnut sellers or unrelated seed-chain studies, and were discarded -- https://www.usaseedslimited.com/groundnut.html
Seednet portal listing (variety code A0402232): not retrieved in the search results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka (Seednet and the reference lists agree on this state) -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits

NAME AND SEARCH NOTES
Variety name: input "DH-245" and Seednet "DH-245" are identical. The CSC/gazette sources write it as "Dh 245" or "Dh-245"; all evidence above refers to that same variety.
Crop: groundnut (Arachis hypogaea) confirmed.
Searches run: 4 (variety and release; breeder and institute; research papers; seed availability).

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The variety has responded to higher fertilizer dose of 150% RDF but has not responded to higher seed rate with closer spacing.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Medium size leaf of wide elliptic shape. Pods with moderate constriction. Kernels have tan colour.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: The variety has drought tolerance as indicated by less reduction in pod yield at different moisture stress condition over control condition
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Dh 257 has on par tolerance to rust under field conditions compared to the susceptible check, TAG 24
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Dh 257 has on par reaction to leaf miner, thrips, leaf hopper and Spodoptera litura.

drought.details: The CSC record states drought tolerance as indicated by less reduction in pod yield under different moisture stress conditions compared with control. Secondary sources describe DH 257 as a drought and foliar-disease tolerant rabi-summer groundnut bred for intermittent drought in northern Karnataka's dry tract. A 2018 kharif breeding study at AICRP-G MARS Dharwad names Dh-257 as drought-tolerant, and Dh-257 was used as a drought-tolerant parent in two F2 populations (Dh-256 x Dh-257; Dh-257 x TG-76). The digest contains no quantified moisture-stress trial values, so the level is rated medium rather than high.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the searched sources.

flood.details: No measured flood tolerance result was found. A Deccan Herald report says farmers in north Karnataka asked UAS Dharwad for a groundnut resistant to wet drought (waterlogging) and that Dh-257 was released in response, but the article does not report a measured waterlogging-tolerance result. A farmer's own estimate reports 16 q/ha on waterlogged land in a bad year versus 28 q/ha in normal seasons; this is not a trial result.

disease_resistance.summary: Described as tolerant to late leaf spot and rust (secondary technology description; 'foliar-disease tolerant' also stated). No measured scoring data, pathogen strains, or trial conditions were found in the digest. The CSC record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence was found for insect pest resistance (e.g., Spodoptera, leaf miner) specific to Dh 257.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 3000-3500 kg/ha. Technology sheet: pod yield 3200-3500 kg/ha (range differs from CSC). Rabi trial, Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka: mean pod yield 3240 kg/ha; highest 3442 kg/ha when sown at the 48th standard meteorological week.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for formal multi-environment stability analysis. The farmer-level report indicates a yield difference between normal seasons (28 q/ha) and a waterlogged bad year (16 q/ha), but this is an estimate, not a trial.
agronomic_details.adaptation: All India Zone IIIA (Karnataka and Maharashtra states) per CSC. Described as a rabi-summer groundnut for northern Karnataka's dry tract with intermittent drought. Rabi trial site: Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka. Reviews list DH-257 among cultivars widely grown in rainfed Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka (no release details given).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC record: Na. Kharif 2018 evaluation at AICRP-G MARS Dharwad (parsed table, column headers partly garbled): plant height 25.20, primary branches 4.00, pod yield per plant 17.00, kernel yield 10.39, test weight 25.03, shelling 60.72. Technology sheet lists maturity as 120-125 days (medium group) and season as rabi-summer. CSC agronomic feature: responds to a higher fertilizer dose (150% RDF) but not to higher seed rate with closer spacing.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Rabi trial, Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka: mean pod yield 3240 kg/ha, at par with Dh-256; 83.56% above check TMV-2; highest yield 3442 kg/ha at 48th MW sowing; net returns about Rs 131,489/ha (Rs 143,423/ha at 48th MW sowing). (3) Farmer-level report (not a trial): 28 q/ha in normal seasons; 16 q/ha on waterlogged land in a bad year.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STATUS: The search budget ran out. I ran 4 searches, but the last code run hit the tool limit before I could re-read full page text. I only saw the first ~400 characters of each result, so the findings below are partial and most headings are unverified.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GG 40 (Gujarat Groundnut 40) / seednet name GG-6 (Gujarat Groundnut-6), ICGV 16668, groundnut

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in the retrieved excerpts. The excerpts did not cover drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence traits. Not verified.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found in the retrieved excerpts. Not verified.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Junagadh Main Oilseeds Research Station page describes intercropping recommendations for semi-spreading groundnut in South Saurashtra (groundnut + sesame 2:1 in kharif), but does not mention GG 40 in the excerpt -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found in the retrieved excerpts. The parentage (CGC-3 x FESR-5-P6-B1-B1 1-1-1-B-B) is from the input record only, not verified externally.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- GG40 (ICGV 16668) was reported as developed by a team of groundnut breeders at ICRISAT in partnership with the Main Oilseeds Research Station (MORS), Junagadh Agricultural University, Gujarat -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/new-variety-of-heart-healthy-groundnut-to-benefit-all-of-india
Individual breeder names were not seen in the retrieved text.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder names, emails, phone numbers or postal addresses were seen in the retrieved excerpts. Institute-level pages to check: Main Oilseeds Research Station, Junagadh -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh ; ICRISAT press office -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/new-variety-of-heart-healthy-groundnut-to-benefit-all-of-india (contact fields not seen in the excerpt).

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or DOIs were identified in the retrieved excerpts. Not verified.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No GG 40 or GG-6 seed source was seen in the retrieved excerpts. The Directorate of Oilseeds Development groundnut page has a state-wise notified varieties list under the Seeds Act, but its excerpt did not show GG 40 or GG-6 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input record lists Rajasthan, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana. I did not confirm this against the CSC minutes or any official notification. The DOD page is the right place to check the notified-variety list.

NAME DISCREPANCY -- The ICRISAT evidence refers to "GG40" with code ICGV 16668. No retrieved source linked "GG-6" on the Seednet portal to this line. Both names still need confirmation on seednet.gov.in.

Suggested next steps (outside the search budget): check the seednet.gov.in entry for GG-6, the CSC release notification for the official name and states, and the JAU/MORS and ICAR-AICRP groundnut pages for breeder names, contact details and trial data.

drought.details: The Andhra Pradesh scarce-rainfall trial credits GJG-32 with resistance to several biotic and abiotic stresses, but the trial does not isolate drought tolerance as a mechanism. In that trial GJG-32 gave about 30.3% higher pod yield than the K-6 check in rainfed red soils in 2019 and 2020. The level is medium because the evidence is yield performance under rainfed conditions, not a characterised drought mechanism. Original variety data gives adaptation to Zone-V (Southern Maharashtra and Telengana).

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence was found from an institute source in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance evidence was found from an institute source in the searched sources.

flood.details: No flood tolerance evidence was found from an institute source. A commercial seller (Reno Agrigenetics) claims waterlogging resistance for a 'Reno GJG 32' product. This is unverified marketing and is not treated as evidence of flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Tikka (late leaf spot) and rust: rated resistant in the 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper, with comparable reactions to other major diseases relative to checks. A JAU variety sheet (reproduced on a commercial page, treated as secondary) records resistance to tikka and rust, with comparable reactions to collar rot and stem rot. A 2025 agronomy review table lists GJG 32 (code ICGV 03043) as tolerant of rust and collar rot. Commercial listings (Pooja Hybrid Seeds) claim resistance to leaf spot and rust but are not official sources. A ResearchGate copy of the JOR paper reports moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, but it carries different yield and oil figures and may describe a different entry, so it was excluded from this summary.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance is established. The JAU variety sheet (reproduced on a commercial page, treated as secondary) records thrips damage comparable to checks and low leaf defoliator damage. These are observations relative to checks, not confirmed resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Twenty-location, five-year rainfed kharif trials (2011-2016) gave a mean pod yield of 3392 kg/ha, 15-23% above the checks GG 7, GJG 9 and TG 37A. Yield figures conflict across records: 2909 kg/ha is listed for the 2016 Zone V release, 3392 kg/ha for the 2017 Gujarat release, and a second version of the paper gives 2710 kg/ha at national level.
agronomic_details.stability: Mean performance across 20 locations over five years is reported in the 2020 JOR paper. Variation across environments beyond the mean is not found in searched sources. The Andhra Pradesh trial reports about 30.3% higher yield than K-6 in rainfed red soils in 2019 and 2020.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Original variety data gives adaptation to Zone-V of India (Southern Maharashtra and Telengana). Recorded trial evidence comes from Gujarat rainfed kharif trials and rainfed red soils in the Andhra Pradesh scarce-rainfall zone.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Recorded inconsistently across sources: 109 days (JAU station table), 112 days (JAU station table, Gujarat row), 115-124 days (fuleseeds), 110-120 days (Pooja Hybrid Seeds) and 120-125 days (Reno Agrigenetics).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Kernel traits: 100-kernel weight 35.9 g, shelling 68.5%, oil 53.9%. Plant architecture and other morphological traits are not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Twenty-location, five-year rainfed kharif trials, 2011-2016: mean pod yield 3392 kg/ha, 15-23% above GG 7, GJG 9 and TG 37A. (2) Andhra Pradesh scarce-rainfall trial, 2019 and 2020, rainfed red soils: about 30.3% higher pod yield than K-6 check, with resistance to several biotic and abiotic stresses reported and drought tolerance not isolated.
