disease_resistance.summary: Listed as tolerant to early leaf spot (ELS), late leaf spot (LLS) and peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND) in two sources. The 2025 review table lists tolerance for Rajasthan as leaf spots and PBND. The input record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified', and the digest does not give a tolerance level or screening method. Early maturity is also listed, but it is not a disease-resistance trait.

pest_resistance.summary: Listed as tolerant to jassids, thrips and leaf miner in two sources. Spodoptera litura tolerance is listed in the 2025 review table, but the source text is fragmented and the exact wording could not be confirmed. The input record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Input record (CSC): dry pod yield 1600-2200 kg/ha; kernel yield 1300-1500 kg/ha. The digest contains no independent kg/ha yield evidence. Trial data are given per plant (see field_trials).

agronomic_details.adaptation: Input record: suited to heavy soils and the entire bunch groundnut growing belt of Rajasthan for kharif and summer seasons; sowing at the onset of monsoon while maintaining plant geometry. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratap Raj Mungphali (groundnut)

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Pratap Raj Mungphali"), and all evidence below refers to that name. I did not find evidence for the separate, similarly named Pratap Mungphali-1, -2, -3 or -4, so I have excluded them. Searches were run for the release/variety, breeder/institution, research and seed-availability topics. The Seednet portal page itself was not retrieved; the release year and variety code come from the input record only.

STRESS TOLERANCE

- Listed as early maturing and tolerant to ELS, LLS, PBND, jassids, thrips and leaf miner -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396544544_Improved_production_practices_for_sustainable_groundnut_cultivation_An_Indian_perspective
- The same trait summary appears in a 2025 review; the table lists it for Rajasthan with early maturity and tolerance to leaf spots, PBND, jassids, thrips and leaf miner -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance evidence found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST

- Early and late leaf spot, PBND, jassid, thrip and leaf miner tolerance (as above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396544544_Improved_production_practices_for_sustainable_groundnut_cultivation_An_Indian_perspective
- Spodoptera litura tolerance is listed in the same table entry (the source text is fragmented; I could not confirm the exact wording for Spodoptera) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf
- Note: the ICAR-DGR compendium entry for this variety was truncated in the search result, so no pest/disease details from that source were captured -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

- In a 2021 kharif trial at Sub-Humid Southern Plains of Rajasthan (Pratap Raj Mungphali as a check, among 36 genotypes), it recorded 16.33 g dry pod yield per plant, 11.98 g kernel yield per plant and 73.33% shelling -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313510785_Variability_Assessment_and_Path_Coefficient_Analysis_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_Genotypes_in_Sub-_Humid_Southern_Plains_of_Rajasthan
- The same study ranked it among the top genotypes for kernel yield per plant and shelling percentage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313510785_Variability_Assessment_and_Path_Coefficient_Analysis_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_Genotypes_in_Sub-_Humid_Southern_Plains_of_Rajasthan
- Maturity (days) and recommended kg/ha yield for this variety: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL

- Pedigree is given as selection from ICGV 98223 -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/download/3716/1194/2369
- A 2014 D2 genetic-diversity study at MPUAT Udaipur used Pratap Raj Mungphali as a check among 30 genotypes -- https://ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJBSM/article/download/3716/1194/2369
- QTL, marker or genomic studies specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

- Developing institution: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Rajasthan College of Agriculture, MPUAT (Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology), Udaipur. Source for the institution, as given in the input record: the variety record; corroborated for the department in the sister varieties' releases -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1203/1/RA_00419.pdf
- Named breeders found in the department's releases (AK Nagda, Abhay Dashora, VN Joshi) are associated with Pratap Mungphali-1 and -2, not confirmed for Pratap Raj Mungphali -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1201/1/RA_00417.pdf ; https://oar.icrisat.org/1203/1/RA_00419.pdf
- Lead breeder for Pratap Raj Mungphali: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS

- Institute-level only: Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics, Rajasthan College of Agriculture, MPUAT, Udaipur (Rajasthan) 313 001 (postal code as printed in the release notes for sister varieties) -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1201/1/RA_00417.pdf
- Official email, phone, or institute contact page URL for this variety: No evidence found.

Kharif 2021 trial. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RG 425 (groundnut)

Name note: The CSC name (variety_name) and the Seednet name (seednet_variety_name) are both "RG 425," so every search result refers to the same name. I could not reach the Seednet portal record or the CSC release minutes, so the code A0402190, the 2010 release year, and the parentage ICG 5013 x RG 340 rest on the input record alone and are unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
RARI Durgapura describes RG 425 as a semi-spreading variety with drought tolerance and collar rot resistance -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
ICAR-IIGR research achievements lists RG 425 among cultivars identified as iron chlorosis tolerant -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/2015/06/research-achievements/
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Collar rot resistance (RARI page above) -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
Rust, leaf spot, bud necrosis and pest resistance specific to RG 425: No evidence found (the RG 382 and RG 141 entries on the same RARI page are different varieties)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Listed among Spanish-bunch varieties recommended for Rajasthan (Zone I), with a suggested spreading-type spacing of 45-60 x 20 cm and sowing from late June to mid July -- https://www.isasat.org/Volume-1,issue-2,july-2017/AARJ_1_2_8_Waghmode.pdf
Note: the same source classes RG 425 as Spanish bunch while RARI describes it as semi-spreading; this discrepancy is unresolved.
Maturity days, pod yield, and multi-location trial results for RG 425: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (ICG 5013 x RG 340) and any QTL or marker study on RG 425: No evidence found (only general groundnut genetics reviews, listed under PUBLICATIONS)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
RARI Durgapura is a constituent institute of Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University (SKNAU), Jobner, Jaipur, and runs the AICRP on Groundnut centre there -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
RARI Durgapura's groundnut programme is credited with developing six varieties, including RG 425 -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
Lead breeder name for RG 425: No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. Ashok Kumar Meena, Name of Incharge, AICRP on Groundnut, RARI Durgapura; mobile 918432719252; email akmeena.pbg.rari@sknau.ac.in -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Groundnut.htm
RARI Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan 302018 (institute address as printed in a best-management-practices document) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379814988_Best_Management_Practices_for_Groundnut_Cultivation_in_India
Official institute contact page URL: raridurgapura.org (homepage; the specific contact page was not found)

PUBLICATIONS
No RG 425-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper found.
Related general reference only (not about RG 425): Desmae, H., Janila, P., Okori, P., et al. (2019). Genetics, genomics and breeding of groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Plant Breeding 138: 425-444 -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.12645 (DOI: 10.1111/pbr.12645)

SEED AVAILABILITY
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SKNAU seed-sales, or private dealer listing specific to RG 425 was found. Generic groundnut seed dealers in Rajasthan appeared in search, but none named RG 425 -- https://www.exportersindia.com/rajasthan/groundnut-seed.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
Listed under Rajasthan among varieties notified under the Seeds Act from 2008 to 2019 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
The input record lists recommended states as "Not specified," so this is the only state evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: Collar rot (seedling stage, Aspergillus niger): no field resistance rating found. An in vitro seed-treatment study by Sekhon, Sandhu, Sharma and Belludi (2019) used SG-99 seed. Tebuconazole gave the highest healthy-seedling percentage for SG-99 (88.00%). The authors report that collar rot markedly reduced germination and seedling vigour. This is a laboratory fungicide test, not evidence of genetic resistance. Rust and late leaf spot: no evidence found for SG 99. The QTL-seq papers that mention these diseases concern other parents and are not attributed to SG 99. A ResearchGate publication link is referenced in the source figure page, but its full URL was not retrieved, so it is not listed here.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SG 99 groundnut: evidence digest

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "SG 99", so every search used the same name. I did not find a separate Seednet portal page for SG 99, so no finding below comes from Seednet.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for SG 99. The only SG 99 agronomy text describes it as grown in loamy sand to sandy places during summer months, which is a soil description, not a stress rating. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut

DISEASE AND PEST
Collar rot (seedling stage): an in vitro study by Sekhon, Sandhu, Sharma and Belludi (2019) tested fungicide seed treatments against Aspergillus niger, using SG-99 seed. Tebuconazole gave the highest healthy-seedling percentage for SG-99 (88.00%), and the authors report that collar rot markedly reduced germination and seedling vigour. This is a laboratory germination test, not a field resistance rating. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Germination-status-of-groundnut-seeds-variety-SG-99-treated-with-different_fig1_337737539 (also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/... linked from the same figure page, "In Vitro Evaluation of Fungicides against Aspergillus niger causing Collar Rot Disease in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.)")
Pest resistance: No evidence found.
Rust or late leaf spot resistance for SG 99: No evidence found. The QTL-seq papers that mention rust and late leaf spot name other parents (GPBD 4 and others), not SG 99. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbi.12686 (not SG 99; listed for exclusion only)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and plant traits: an SG 99 entry in a Punjab groundnut extension page gives maturity of 124 days, principal stalk length 66-68 cm, 22-24 mature pods per plant, 100-kernel weight of 54 g, and shelling outturn of 66%. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut
Oil content: the same page gives 52.3% oil for the SG 99 entry. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut
Spacing and seed rate: the page advises a 30 x 15 cm spacing for bunch-type varieties including SG 99. The page does not separate the yield figures per variety, so no yield figure is attributed to SG 99. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/groundnut
Field-trial or multi-location results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: a review table lists SG 99 as released in India in 2004 from the breeding programme entry "ICGV 89280", which matches the parentage in the record. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/
QTL or marker studies naming SG 99: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: No evidence found that PAU developed SG 99. The record's parentage points to ICRISAT germplasm (ICGV 89280). The review table lists SG 99 with ICGV 89280 as the breeding programme name but does not name the developing institution or breeder. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
Context: ICRISAT's groundnut program is the source of ICGV-series germplasm. -- https://www.icrisat.org/crops/groundnut/overview
Context: the ICAR Directorate of Groundnut Research at Junagadh names SG 99 among cultivars with low phytic acid, but it does not say who bred it. -- https://www.icar-iigr.org.in/index.php/directors-desk/

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact for SG 99 found. Institute-level contacts below are not linked to SG 99 by any retrieved text except where noted.
ICAR-Indian Institute of Groundnut Research (Directorate of Groundnut Research), Junagadh: address "At & Post: Ivnagar, Ivnagar Road, Junagadh-362015, Gujarat, India"; email director.groundnut@gmail.com. The page naming SG 99 is the Director's Desk page; the address and email appear on the breeder seed section page. -- https://icar-iigr.org.in/service-support/breeder-seed-section/ ; https://www.icar-iigr.org.in/index.php/directors-desk/
Junagadh Agricultural University, Main Oilseeds Research Station (groundnut), unit head: Dr. N. D. Dholariya, Research Scientist (Groundnut) (I/C); office (0285) 2672080-90, PBX-325; (0285) 2670205; mobile +91-7777930601; email rsoilseed@jau.in. This station page does not name SG 99. -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh
PAU (Punjab Agricultural University): no PAU contact found, and no PAU link to SG 99 found. No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Sekhon, A. S., Sandhu, P. S., Sharma, P., & Belludi, R. (2019). In Vitro Evaluation of Fungicides against Aspergillus niger causing Collar Rot Disease in Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Journal not shown in retrieved text (ResearchGate record, November 2019) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Germination-status-of-groundnut-seeds-variety-SG-99-treated-with-different_fig1_337737539
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Genetics, genomics and breeding of groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Journal not shown -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/ (the SG 99 entry is a table row, not the paper's main text)
AICRP or ICAR annual reports on SG 99: No evidence found. KrishiKosh theses on SG 99: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. None of the seed-supplier results named SG 99. Results for GG-20, AgriBee 999 and INDO-US 999 are other varieties and were excluded. The Junagadh station page says it supplies breeder seed for Gujarat and national indents, but it does not name SG 99. -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/main-oilseeds-research-station-junagadh
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing for SG 99 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found that SG 99 is recommended for Gujarat or Rajasthan. The Gujarat variety compendium found did not name SG 99 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-and-popular-varieties-recommended-for-gujaratenglishpdf/252255631
Release year conflict: the record gives 2016-08-12. The review table gives 2004 for SG 99. Neither the 2016 CSC notification nor a 2004 release notice for SG 99 was retrieved. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6774334/
No CSC release minutes or gazette notification for SG 99 were found. The record's release date and recommended states remain unverified.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Tamil Nadu (TNAU groundnut guidance lists TMV-10 as a semi-spreading variety for early Adipattam sowing in all districts; not a CSC-listed state). Southern Maharashtra (Jalgaon station paper describes TMV-10 as high-yielding for southern Maharashtra; partial support only). No evidence for Andhra Pradesh, Odisha or Bihar.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in CSC record. TMV-10 source (TNAU table) lists semi-spreading habit, 135-day duration, 54% oil and high shelling. These are attributed to the Seednet name only and are not confirmed for AMV-10.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) TNAU table (TMV-10, Seednet name): about 1650 kg/ha yield, 135-day duration, 54% oil, high shelling; described as high-yielding and high-oil. (2) Desale et al. Maharashtra paper (TMV-10, Seednet name): described as a high-yielding groundnut variety for southern Maharashtra from the Jalgaon station; no trial data figures given in the digest. (3) TNAU groundnut page (TMV-10, Seednet name): listed under semi-spreading varieties for early Adipattam sowing in all districts; listing only, no trial result. No AMV-10 trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no stress-tolerance data for TMV-10 (Seednet name) or AMV-10 (CSC name). Derivative lines (Tirupati-3, a TMV-10 selection) were excluded because they describe a different variety. -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/Research_Varieties.pdf ; https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Groundnut.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for TMV-10 or AMV-10. The only pest and disease notes located concern other groundnut varieties and were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
TMV-10 (Seednet name): a TNAU table lists it as a 1970 release from Argentine selection, with 135-day duration, semi-spreading habit, about 1650 kg/ha yield, 54% oil, and high shelling, described as high-yielding and high-oil. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
TMV-10 (Seednet name): a TNAU groundnut page lists it under semi-spreading varieties for early Adipattam sowing in all districts (Tamil Nadu). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Oilseeds/oilseeds_groundnut01.html
TMV-10 (Seednet name): a Maharashtra Agricultural Universities journal paper (Desale et al.) describes it as a high-yielding groundnut variety for southern Maharashtra, from the Jalgaon station. -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN8102359
Release-year conflict: the CSC record gives 2020, but every TMV-10 source gives 1970 or 1980-era release. The 2020 date appears to belong to a different record. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
AMV-10 (CSC name): no evidence found in any search result.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage in the CSC record ("natural mutant from Argentina") matches the source description of TMV-10 as a natural mutant from Argentina, but no genetic or QTL study was located. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Oilseeds/oilseeds_groundnut01.html ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/suitable-groundnut-varieties-for-kharif-and-rabi/251178470

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No breeder name found for TMV-10 or AMV-10. The Maharashtra paper lists the authors Desale, S.C.; Patil, P.S.; Pawar, J.K.; Patil, G.D., at the Agricultural Research Station, Jalgaon (TMV-10 name). -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN8102359
Institution note: ANGRAU (CSC listed institution) is named as the developer in the CSC record, but no search result tied TMV-10 or AMV-10 to ANGRAU. ANGRAU's groundnut work centres on other varieties (Kadiri series, Dharani). -- https://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=4 (index 11-4)

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level, not breeder-specific (ANGRAU):
Administrative office: Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University Administrative Office, Lam, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, 522 034; email registrar@angrau.ac.in -- https://angrau.ac.in/
General email: info@angrau.ac.in; address Lam, Guntur-522034; phone +91-11-26562122/25/33/44, 26567373, 26962819 (listed by India Science and Technology portal) -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/acharya-ng-ranga-agricultural-university-angrau
Media contact (Facebook page): +91 94949 21873; media@angrau.ac.in -- https://www.facebook.com/ANGRAU.University/
Vice Chancellor (2015-era listing): Dr P.V. Satyanarayana; telephone 0863-2347011; vicechancellor@angrau.ac.in -- https://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=4
No breeder or TMV-10 specific contact found.

PUBLICATIONS
Desale, S.C.; Patil, P.S.; Pawar, J.K.; Patil, G.D. (1980/1982). TMV 10, a high yielding variety of groundnut for southern Maharashtra [India]. Journal of Maharashtra Agricultural Universities 5(3): 192-194 (AGRIS record gives 1980 and 1982) -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN8102359
No other publications for TMV-10 or AMV-10 were found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for TMV-10 or AMV-10 seed sale. ANGRAU seed lists (as of 10.11.2022) show Kadiri 6, Kadiri 7, Kadiri 9, Nithya Haritha, and TCGS 1694, but not TMV-10 or AMV-10. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Seed_Production_Targets/balance%20of%20seed%2010.11.22.pdf
The indiamart listing for groundnut seeds names no variety and is not relevant. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/groundnut-seeds-2850781083933.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar: No evidence found for TMV-10 or AMV-10 in these states.
Maharashtra: partial support only, from the Jalgaon paper describing TMV-10 for southern Maharashtra. -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=IN8102359
Tamil Nadu (not in the CSC list): TMV-10 is recommended in TNAU's groundnut guidance. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/CropProduction/Oilseeds/oilseeds_groundnut01.html

MESTA CROP CHECK
No evidence found. None of the four searches returned any mesta (Hibiscus) result. The Seednet record lists groundnut, and all evidence is groundnut. The crop field "mesta" appears to be a data error and should be verified against the CSC minutes.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: the ORS Tindivanam page reports the culture as completely resistant to rust disease; the EJPB paper reports only moderate resistance to rust compared with check varieties. These sources conflict and the conflict is unresolved. Late leaf spot (LLS): the ORS page reports tolerance with a score of 2.0; the EJPB paper reports moderate resistance compared with check varieties; a separate leaf spot score reports a medium resistant reaction (score 6.0) against 9.0 for susceptible checks VRI 2, CO 2 and TMV 2. Multiple sources agree on LLS tolerance or moderate-to-medium resistance, though the scales differ.

pest_resistance.summary: TMV 14 showed tolerance to Spodoptera litura, thrips, Helicoverpa armigera and leaf miner (reported in the EJPB paper and the Academia.edu copy of the same work). No quantitative pest scores were found.

agronomic_details.yield: Kharif: 2124 kg/ha, 11.5% above VRI (Gn) 6 (1904 kg/ha) and 15.2% above TMV Gn 13 (1844 kg/ha). Rabi (irrigated): 2286 kg/ha, 29.7% above VRI (Gn) 6 and 32.3% above TMV Gn 13. Agritech averages: 2222 kg/ha (rainfed) and 2360 kg/ha (irrigated). The ORS record gives average yield as Kg/Ha without a value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Multi-location trial designs are reported, but no stability analysis or cross-environment results were found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released for Tamil Nadu groundnut cultivation under rainfed and irrigated conditions. The Agritech page lists kharif, rabi and summer seasons across Tamil Nadu. Tested in multi-location trials in kharif 2013, 2014 and 2015 (rainfed) and rabi 2013-14.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 95-100 days (ORS Tindivanam). Agritech gives 105-110 days, which conflicts with the ORS figure.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed quality: shelling of 70.6%, 92% SMK, 38 g 100-kernel weight (ORS Tindivanam). Oil content of 45.01% (Agritech). Spanish bunch growth habit (EJPB paper title). Pod and kernel traits are described as acceptable to farmers (ORS Tindivanam).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif multi-location/adaptive trial: 2124 kg/ha, 11.5% above VRI (Gn) 6 and 15.2% above TMV Gn 13. (2) Rabi irrigated trial: 2286 kg/ha, 29.7% above VRI (Gn) 6 and 32.3% above TMV Gn 13. (3) Agritech reported averages of 2222 kg/ha (rainfed) and 2360 kg/ha (irrigated). (4) Rainfed weed-management trial using TMV 14 in late rabi (Swetha et al., 2022); the digest gives no yield or weed-control result. (5) Multi-location trials in kharif 2013, 2014 and 2015 (rainfed) and rabi 2013-14; no results were reported in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TMV 14 (groundnut)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "TMV 14", so one set of searches covered both. The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-sourced evidence was found. Variety code A0402230 and the CSC release minutes were not found either.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The culture is completely resistant to rust disease and tolerant to late leaf spot (score 2.0), and it matures in 95-100 days. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Drought: No TMV 14-specific drought result was found. A PEG-6000 germination screen (Umadevi et al.) lists TMV 14 in a table, but the retrieved text does not show its classification, so I have not counted it. -- https://masujournal.org/view_journal.php?id=658

DISEASE AND PEST
- For late leaf spot and rust, TMV 14 showed moderate resistance compared with check varieties, and it showed tolerance to Spodoptera litura, thrips, Helicoverpa armigera and leaf miner. -- https://www.academia.edu/90525667/Groundnut_TMV_14_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety (also in the EJPB paper, https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00039.5)
- Leaf spot score: medium resistant reaction to leaf spot (score 6.0), against 9.0 for susceptible checks VRI 2, CO 2 and TMV 2. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf
- Note the conflict: the ORS page reports complete rust resistance, while the EJPB paper reports only moderate resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield: 2124 kg/ha in kharif, 11.5% above VRI (Gn) 6 (1904 kg/ha) and 15.2% above TMV Gn 13 (1844 kg/ha). -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Rabi yield: 2286 kg/ha under irrigation, 29.7% above VRI (Gn) 6 and 32.3% above TMV Gn 13. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Seed quality: shelling of 70.6% with 92% SMK and 38 g of 100-kernel weight. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Agritech gives a different maturity (105-110 days), rainfed/irrigated averages of 2222/2360 kg/ha, and oil content of 45.01%. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMV%2014.html
- Rainfed weed-management trial using TMV 14 in late rabi (Swetha et al., 2022). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366555054_Novel_method_to_manage_weeds_in_the_rainfed_groundnut_var_VRI_8_and_TMV_14_using_nano_encapsulated_herbicide_formulations
- Multi-location and adaptive trials: multi-location trials were run in Kharif 2013, 2014 and 2015 under rainfed conditions, and rabi 2013-14. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL, marker or genetic-mapping study for TMV 14. The only marker paper retrieved (Mol Biol Rep 2024) does not name TMV 14 in the retrieved text. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-024-09633-z
- Pedigree: cross derivative of VRI 6 x R 2001-(2), developed by pedigree method of breeding. -- https://doaj.org/article/fc2c92a9a86244b39def39f3826126e9
- Parentage conflict: agritech.tnau.ac.in lists "VR12 x TVG 0004" instead. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMV%2014.html

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead scientist: M. Vaithiyalingan (Assistant Professor, PBG), with K. Ganesamurthy, G.V. Ramasubramanian, Sangeetha Panicker and R. Vaidyanathan. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Developing station: Oilseeds Research Station, Tindivanam-604 002. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf
- Origin: culture TVG 0856 was identified as best in station trials, tested in MLT and ART, and released as TMV 14 (2018). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/annual-report/
- Release year conflict: 2018 (ORS, EJPB) versus 2019 (agritech). Release-minute number not found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Oilseeds Research Station, Tindivanam: postal address "Oil Seeds Research Station, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Tindivanam 604 002" -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9a45/4207f9b78a29dc7b42acf70e2eff76030c6b.pdf
- Institute e-mail as printed on the TNAU page: "ars tmv @tnau.ac.in" (the space is in the source; it is probably "arstmv@tnau.ac.in", but this is unverified) -- http://www.tnau.ac.in/tvm/
- Corresponding author: M. Vaithiyalingan, e-mail printed in the paper: mvaithiyalingan@gmail.com (a personal address, not an institutional one) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-10-1-039
- Phone: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page URL: http://www.tnau.ac.in/tvm/

PUBLICATIONS
- Vaithiyalingan, M., Ganesamurthy, K., Ramasubramanian, G.V., Panicker, S., & Vaidyanathan, R. (2019). Groundnut TMV 14 – A new high yielding Spanish bunch groundnut variety. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, 10(1), 307–311. -- DOI 10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00039.5 (https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00039.5)
- Swetha, S. et al. (2022). Novel method to manage weeds in the rainfed groundnut (var. VRI 8 and TMV 14) using nano encapsulated herbicide formulations. Journal of Applied and Natural Science, 14(4), 1341–1350. -- DOI 10.31018/jans.v14i4.3920
- Umadevi, M., Mohammed, D., Rajeswari, R., Shanthi, P., & Kalaiyarasi, R. (year not retrieved). Screening of groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) varieties for drought tolerance using polyethylene glycol. -- https://masujournal.org/view_journal.php?id=658 (TMV 14 appears only in a table; not confirmed as a finding)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**VL Moongphali 1 (groundnut): EVIDENCE DIGEST**

Name note: the CSC release-minute name is "VL Moongphali 1" and the Seednet name is "VL Moongphali-1". Every source found used the hyphenated form or the "VL-Moongphali-1" spelling, and none came from the Seednet portal itself. The findings below therefore refer to the same variety under both names, but no Seednet record was retrieved.

Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institute; Seednet code; research/parentage). Seednet was not reachable through search, so the variety code A0402180 is unverified.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Resistant to late leaf spot (LLS) and root rot, per the DAC notified-variety table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The sources found name only LLS and root rot resistance.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- Resistant to late leaf spot and root rot. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx ; https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
- Pest resistance: No evidence found for this variety. Pest tolerance cited for the parent ICGV 86590 is resistance to Spodoptera litura and Sclerotium rolfsii. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Yield potential about 1943 kg/ha, listed in the DAC table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Recommended production system: kharif (rainy season). -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
- Maturity days, oil content and multi-location trial data for VL-Moongphali-1: No evidence found. The 96–123 day maturity and 48% oil figures belong to the parent ICGV 86590. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/
- Pod yield per hectare and oil content for ICGV 86590 in its own release, from the ICAR-DGR compendium: 1,785 kg/ha pod yield and 48% oil. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: selection from ICGV-86590 (X 14-4-B-19-8 x PI 239747), breeding method pureline selection. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- The same parentage appears in the compendium as "X14-4-B-19-8", while the ICRISAT monograph gives the parent as "X14-4-B-19-B" crossed with PI259747. Flag this discrepancy for checking. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/538/
- QTL or marker studies for this variety: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1 ; https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

- Institute director named on the ICAR page (2021): Dr. Lakshmi Kant. This is an institutional role, not a breeder credit. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Director, ICAR-VPKAS Almora: Dr. Lakshmi Kant (as named on the 2021 ICAR page). Email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in the retrieved text. -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127

drought.details: No evidence found. The digest lists rainfed and irrigated yields (2448 and 2535 kg/ha, TNAU) but retrieved no explicit drought-tolerance rating or mechanism for VRI 10. The 2024 on-farm rainfed trial reports pod yield of 2493 kg/ha, which is not a stress-tolerance rating.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance in VRI 10.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in VRI 10.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in VRI 10.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf spot: described as moderately resistant by TNAU (the TNAU entry is truncated after this point, so the full list is unverified) and as moderate resistance to late leaf spot in the 2024 on-farm trial paper. Root wilt: the 2024 on-farm trial paper reports higher tolerance to root wilt than some comparators, ranking second to TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha); no quantitative resistance score is given. Rust, stem rot, peanut bud necrosis and PBND: no evidence found for VRI 10 specifically (the DAC listing of notified varieties has no VRI 10 row). A general tnbrdngo claim of built-in pest and disease defences has no quantitative data.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests and defoliators: described as moderately resistant by TNAU (the entry is truncated, so the full list is unverified). No other pest-resistance evidence found for VRI 10.

agronomic_details.yield: TNAU: 2448 kg/ha rainfed and 2535 kg/ha irrigated (units as reported by TNAU; the CSC record lists average yield in Kg/Ha without a value). On-farm rainfed trial (2024 paper, trial around 2022-23): pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest haulm yield among varieties tested), BCR 2.86. Cluster frontline demonstrations in Cuddalore district (VRI 8 and VRI 10 combined, 2020-21 to 2022-23, 175 demonstrations, about 70 ha): yield gain over farmers' practice of 53.34 per cent (another version of the study reports 62.13 per cent). The gain is not separated by variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Season-wise recommendation across Tamil Nadu zones (kharif, rabi and summer) is reported by TNAU, naming Villupuram, Thiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore, Perambalur/Ariyalur, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur and others. The digest does not explicitly confirm VRI 10 in each listed zone. tnbrdngo cites suitability for short-duration cropping. Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trial data: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 100 To 105Days (CSC record). Conflicting duration reported by TNAU and tnbrdngo: 90-95 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: THE PODS ARE LONG WITH MEDIUM TO DEEP CONSTRICTION, PROMINANT BEAK (CSC record). TNAU additionally reports growth habit bunch and oil content of 46-48%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 2024 on-farm rainfed trial: pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest among varieties tested), BCR 2.86, second-ranked for root wilt tolerance behind TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha as reported). (2) Cluster frontline demonstrations, Cuddalore district, VRI 8 and VRI 10, 2020-21 to 2022-23: 175 demonstrations on about 70 ha, yield gain of 53.34 per cent (or 62.13 per cent in the other version) over farmers' practice. (3) TNAU reports rainfed 2448 kg/ha and irrigated 2535 kg/ha; the trial design behind these figures is not stated. (4) Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trials: not found in searched sources.

agronomic_performance.yield: TNAU: 2448 kg/ha rainfed and 2535 kg/ha irrigated (units as reported by TNAU; the CSC record lists average yield in Kg/Ha without a value). On-farm rainfed trial (2024 paper, trial around 2022-23): pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest haulm yield among varieties tested), BCR 2.86. Cluster frontline demonstrations in Cuddalore district (VRI 8 and VRI 10 combined, 2020-21 to 2022-23, 175 demonstrations, about 70 ha): yield gain over farmers' practice of 53.34 per cent (another version of the study reports 62.13 per cent). The gain is not separated by variety.

The digest does not explicitly confirm VRI 10 in each listed zone. tnbrdngo cites suitability for short-duration cropping. Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trial data: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 100 To 105Days (CSC record). Conflicting duration reported by TNAU and tnbrdngo: 90-95 days.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: THE PODS ARE LONG WITH MEDIUM TO DEEP CONSTRICTION, PROMINANT BEAK (CSC record). TNAU additionally reports growth habit bunch and oil content of 46-48%.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) 2024 on-farm rainfed trial: pod yield 2493 kg/ha, haulm yield 4587 kg/ha (highest among varieties tested), BCR 2.86, second-ranked for root wilt tolerance behind TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha as reported). (2) Cluster frontline demonstrations, Cuddalore district, VRI 8 and VRI 10, 2020-21 to 2022-23: 175 demonstrations on about 70 ha, yield gain of 53.34 per cent (or 62.13 per cent in the other version) over farmers' practice. (3) TNAU reports rainfed 2448 kg/ha and irrigated 2535 kg/ha; the trial design behind these figures is not stated. (4) Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trials: not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderately resistant to sucking pests and defoliators, and to leaf spot (the TNAU entry is truncated after this point, so the full list is unverified) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Moderate resistance to late leaf spot per the 2024 on-farm trial paper -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Showed higher tolerance to root wilt than some comparators, ranking second to TCGS 1694 (pod yield 2493 kg/ha) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Described as having moderate resistance, with a general claim of built-in pest and disease defenses; no quantitative data -- https://tnbrdngo.org/how-the-wonder-nut-vri-10-is-elevating-farmers-standard-of-living/
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found (the rainfed/irrigated yields are listed, but no explicit stress-tolerance rating for VRI 10 was retrieved)

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to sucking pests, defoliators and leaf spot -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Moderate resistance to late leaf spot; no in-situ germination of mature pods before harvest -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Rust, stem rot, peanut bud necrosis and PBND resistance: No evidence found for VRI 10 specifically (DAC listing of notified varieties does not include a VRI 10 row) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Parentage conflict: TNAU lists the cross as VRI 2 x NRCG CS 349 (derivative), duration 90-95 days, oil 46-48%, growth habit bunch, average yield 2448 kg/ha rainfed and 2535 kg/ha irrigated -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
The parentage given in the brief (TMV 7 x FSB 7-2) is the documented pedigree of VRI 1 (released 1986, 105 days), not VRI 10; the brief's parentage was not confirmed for VRI 10 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/ and https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html
Duration 90-95 days and suitability for short-duration cropping -- https://tnbrdngo.org/how-the-wonder-nut-vri-10-is-elevating-farmers-standard-of-living/
On-farm rainfed trial (2022-23 or thereabouts): pod yield 2493 kg/ha and haulm yield 4587 kg/ha, the highest haulm yield among the varieties tested; BCR 2.86 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
Cluster frontline demonstrations in Cuddalore district with VRI 8 and VRI 10 (2020-21 to 2022-23, 175 demonstrations, about 70 ha) reported a yield gain over farmers' practice of 53.34 per cent (the other version of the same study reports 62.13 per cent) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/lr-47-7-016 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379741722_A_Study_on_Yield_and_Value_Sustainability_in_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_Through_Cluster_Frontline_Demonstrations_Approach_in_Cuddalore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu
Multi-location or AICRP/ICAR trial data for VRI 10: No evidence found

QTL, marker-assisted or molecular characterization studies naming VRI 10: No evidence found
Combining ability (line x tester) study using VRI 10 as a line: see PUBLICATIONS below (not genetic-marker work)

Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Regional Research Station, Vriddhachalam (Cuddalore district) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20VRI%2010.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VRI 9 / VRI-4 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC name is "VRI 9" and the Seednet name is "VRI-4". The parentage in the record (VG 5 x NC AC 17090) matches the TNAU record for VRI 4, not VRI 9. The 2022 release year does not match the TNAU record for VRI 4, which was released in 1996 and notified in 1997. I could not confirm that VRI 9 and VRI-4 are the same variety, so the findings below are labelled by name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- VRI 9 (name match): Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, plus some thrips and leafhopper tolerance, is reported for VRI 9 in a 2024 trial. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for VRI 9 were found. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI 9 (name match): The same trial describes VRI 9 as showing low disease incidence and suitability for rainfed conditions, but this is a qualitative statement, not a stress-tolerance test. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI-4 (Seednet name, TNAU record): The record gives no stress-tolerance data. The Radhamani and Singh (2008) germplasm table describes VRI 4 only as high yielding and early. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322066029_Radhamani_J_and_Singh_AK_2008_Conservation_and_Utilization_of_Genetic_Resources_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India_Proc_Indian_Natn_Sci_Acad_74_3131-147

DISEASE AND PEST
- VRI 9: Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust, with thrips and leafhopper also noted. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI-4: The TNAU record lists no disease or pest resistance. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research-vridhachalam/crop-improvement/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- VRI 9 (2024 on-farm/trial comparison): Pod yield 2340 kg/ha and haulm yield 4486 kg/ha, with a duration of 115 days and an average yield of 2500 kg/ha reported. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6/PartD/7-5-116-794.pdf
- VRI 9 (breeding line use): VRI 9 was used as a parental line in a combining-ability study at TNAU Vridhachalam, where it had higher mean pods per plant. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5929

That pedigree matches the parentage in this record, and the Seednet crop is GROUNDNUT. The sesame-specific page gives a different parentage (VRI 2 x GT 10) and a 2022 release year. STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) itself. The searches did not return any stress-tolerance record under that name or code.
- Related line, Karan Guar 14 (RGr 18-1), not Karan Guar-2: It also showed resistance/tolerance to important diseases and insects and was recommended for different states of India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Different cultivar, HG 2-20 (CCS HAU, Hisar): suitable under rain fed situations and this variety is tolerant to drought conditions. -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/officially-released-guar-varieties-details-from-agri-univerity.103226/

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3). Karan Guar 14 is reported as resistant/tolerant to disease and insects (see above, https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597).
- Different cultivar: This variety is resistant to BLB and (RGC 1066, Guar Lathi; text truncated in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384757778_Cluster_Bean_Cyamopsis_tetragonoloba

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) yield, maturity or trial data. Note the name and code were not matched in any record.
- Karan Guar 14 was tested at one station: its seed trials ran at RARI, Durgapura, Jaipur during the rainy (kharif) season of 2016 and 2017 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Karan Guar 14 yield comparison: The newly developed variety Karan Guar-14 has good galactomannan over the check RGC 1066 (1773 kg/ha), RGC 1033 (2110 kg/ha) and HG 2-20 (2180 kg/ha). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/133493/49907/359597
- Zone-specific agronomy for Rajasthan (AINP on Arid Legumes, SKNAU Jobner) is available but does not name Karan Guar-2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391521739_PRODUCTION_TECHNOLOGY_OF_GUAR_FOR_ZONE-IIIA_RAJASTHAN

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for Karan Guar-2 (RGS-3) parentage, markers or QTL. The user-supplied parentage is "Not specified", and no source confirmed it.
- Karan Guar 14 was developed from a cross: developed by crossing two genotypes, RGC 1038 (RGC 516 × HG 75) and RGC 1017 (Naveen × HG 75) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety
- Genome reference (RGC-936, not Karan Guar-2): a chromosome-scale assembly was reported at ICAR-NIPB New Delhi -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-33762-3

Verified for the sister cultivar Karan Guar 14: at Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, (Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner, Rajasthan) Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370515204_Karan_guar_14_A_new_high-yielding_and_quality_gum_content_variety

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I used all four allowed searches, but the fourth call hit the tool's usage limit while I was pulling full page text. I could only read the first 200 characters of most results, so the digest below is partial. Several headings are unverified rather than confirmed empty.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Not verified. No stress-tolerance text was visible in the retrieved snippets.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Not verified. No pest or disease text was visible in the retrieved snippets.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ResearchGate article on Maru Gaurav includes planting guidance: hedge spacing of about 0.90 to 2.0 m, and 4 to 5 m for block plantation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342521287_Maru_Gaurav_New_Karonda_Variety
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A ResearchGate profile snippet describes Maru Gaurav as an extra-ordinary high-yielding karonda variety giving more than 40 kg fruit per plant. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/P-Meghwal-2 (the profile page is not a trial report, and the snippet does not confirm the author's role in the variety)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found in the retrieved results. No QTL or marker study for this variety appeared.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The same ResearchGate profile snippet says Maru Gaurav was released by the Central Arid Zone Research Institute, Jodhpur. The snippet does not name a lead breeder. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/P-Meghwal-2
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Seednet name MARU GUAR (cluster bean/guar): No evidence found. The "MARU GUAR" search returned only a general cluster bean agronomy chapter and a guar gum review, neither of which names this variety, so I have not attributed them to it.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No institute email, phone, postal address or contact page URL was visible in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS -- Authors not visible (year not visible). Maru Gaurav: New Karonda Variety. ResearchGate preprint/PDF -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342521287_Maru_Gaurav_New_Karonda_Variety

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not verified. No seed source (NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, dealer) was visible.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not verified. The record field is "Not specified", and no state recommendation appeared in the visible text.

Notes on the record:
- Crop mismatch: the variety is karonda (Carissa), but the Seednet entry is filed under GUAR (cluster bean/field vetch). The evidence I found concerns karonda only. Nothing I found links MARU GUAR on Seednet to this karonda variety, so the Seednet record needs manual checking.
- Parentage, variety code CZK-2011 and the 2015-04-07 release date were not confirmed by any retrieved source.
- To complete the record, check the CAZRI Jodhpur website, the CSC release notification, the Seednet portal entry, and KrishiKosh for karonda theses.

drought.details: The original CSC record (ground truth) states the variety is tolerant to drought conditions, but the evidence digest contains no quantitative or source-backed drought evaluation specific to NRC 197. The level is set to medium only to reflect the unqualified 'tolerant' designation in the CSC record; the digest does not grade the degree of tolerance and no mechanisms were found. The sources cited below do not support drought tolerance: the stem fly screening paper classed NRC 197 as resistant to pests, not drought, and the khetivyapar source describes lodging tolerance and non-shattering pods. The digest also notes that the variety is reported as suitable for rainfed kharif conditions, which is not a drought-tolerance measurement.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found for resistance to yellow mosaic virus (YMV), pod blight, Rhizoctonia or other diseases specific to NRC 197. The digest notes that a different ICAR variety, NRC 149, is reported for those diseases, but not NRC 197. The original CSC record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem fly: in a field screening trial, NRC 197 showed low stem fly infestation and tunnelling and was classed as resistant; the digest reports it among the genotypes with the lowest infestation (pooled two-year data). The khetivyapar source states the variety is resistant to pest attacks, particularly stem fly. Semilooper: high resistance. Spodoptera litura: moderate resistance. The original CSC record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SEARCH NOTE: Four searches were run. The Seednet name RGC-197 and the crop label "GUAR (CLUSTER BEAN/FIELD VETCH)" returned no evidence. The evidence below refers to NRC-197 (soybean), and the Seednet crop label appears to be an error.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Found as a stem fly screening trial: NRC 197 showed low stem fly infestation and tunnelling, and was classed as resistant, not as drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- The variety is non-shattering, tolerant to lodging, and resistant to pest attacks, particularly stem fly. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to NRC 197.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Additionally, it exhibits high resistance to semilooper and moderate resistance to Spodoptera litura. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Stem fly resistance is reported in the field screening paper, which found NRC 197 among the genotypes with the lowest infestation. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- No evidence found for YMV, pod blight, Rhizoctonia or other disease resistance specific to NRC 197. (A different ICAR variety, NRC 149, is reported for those, but not NRC 197.) -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Soybean Variety NRC 197 is an early duration variety maturing in 113 days which is a very suitable option for hilly areas. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- A different source gives about 112.67 days to maturity. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Its average productivity was observed to be 1624 kg/ha and a maximum production capacity of 2072 kg/ha was observed in the trials. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- A different source gives about 16.24 quintals per hectare. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Rainfed kharif suitability is reported. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- Trial details (number of locations, seasons, check varieties, plot design) were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- The variety was developed through marker-assisted selection. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- It is reported to be free of Kunitz trypsin inhibitor (KTI). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- No QTL, marker names, or linked-marker studies specific to NRC 197 were found.
- Parentage ("selection from local collection of Nagour district") was not confirmed by any search result. No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.khetivyapar.com/en/two-advanced-soybean-varieties-developed-by-icar-3888
- The institute is also named ICAR-NSRI (National Soybean Research Institute) on its own pages and posts. -- https://x.com/ICARNSRI/status/1826264887900918126
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Institute director named in the 2024 AICRP meeting report: Dr. K.H. Singh. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean
- Earlier director named in a news report: Dr Nita Khandekar (older source, may be outdated). -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/icar-develops-new-climate-smart-soyabean-varieties-for-cultivation/
- Release context: Four soybean varieties namely NRC 197, JS 23-03, JS 23-09, and RSC 11-42 were identified for notification. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean
- The Prime Minister dedicated NRC 197 and NRC 149 to the nation, as reported by ICAR-NSRI. -- https://x.com/ICARNSRI/status/1826264887900918126

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No evidence found for a named breeder's email or phone.
- Institute website as given on Wikipedia: iisrindore.icar.gov.in -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Soybean_Research
- Institute location: Indore, Madhya Pradesh (coordinates only; no postal address text found). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Soybean_Research
- Institute website from the ICAR-NSRI variety page: icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html
- No official email, phone or postal address for IISR was found in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS
- Field screening of soybean genotypes for stem fly resistance, including NRC 197 (pooled two-year data). Authors, year and journal not shown in retrieved text. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
- Proceedings of the 54th Annual Group Meet of AICRP on Soybean, held 13-14 March 2024 at UAS Dharwad, where NRC 197 was identified for notification. Report or proceedings title and DOI not found. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean
- No KrishiKosh theses, peer-reviewed NRC 197 papers, or DOIs specific to the variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for NRC 197 or RGC-197.
- Institute-level context: There are about 30 varieties are in seed chain at present. -- https://icar-nsri.res.in/varieties.html (the page does not confirm NRC 197 is among them).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- It is the first variety of the northern hilly region which is free from the non-nutritious Kunitz Trypsin Inhibitor and has been found suitable for the hill districts of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/soybean-variety-nrc-197/
- Identified as the northern hill zone variety at the 2024 Variety Identification Committee meeting. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/top-4-recommended-varieties-of-soybean-for-2024/
- Release year: the evidence supports identification in March 2024 and a formal dedication around August 2024. The record's year_of_release (2024-08-02) could not be checked against a notification gazette. -- https://icar.gov.in/en/annual-group-meet-aicrp-soybean

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for "Selection 1" or "Selection-1" specifically. Generic guinea grass tolerance is described for the species, not this clone: KAU's ad hoc Package of Practices says the grass tolerates drought and deep seasonal flooding, and it grows under coconut shade -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- A general guinea grass review notes drought tolerance from a deep root system, again species-level, not variety-level -- https://masjaps.com/index.php/mas/article/download/12/8/8

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Selection 1 or Selection-1 disease or pest resistance in any search result.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Selection 1 or Selection-1 yield or trial data. KAU's Package of Practices gives species-level figures (about 80-100 t/ha green fodder per year, six to seven harvests) -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- KAU Vellayani's 2021-22 ZREAC report lists guinea grass varieties under evaluation as Harithasree, Culture-2 and CO(GG)-3, with no mention of Selection 1 -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/soft_copy_of_xxxix_zreac_meeting.pdf
- Tamil Nadu's forage package lists CO(GG)3 as a clonal selection from Mombasa, with 340-360 t/ha/year green fodder, but this is a different variety -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/10_Guinea_Grass.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for the parentage "clonal selection from JHGG-96-3" or for the JHGG-96-3 accession. The JHGG prefix appears in an IGFRI-style listing for Bundel Guinea-4 (JHGG-08-1), which is a different variety; any link to Selection 1 is unverified -- https://www.leafconagro.com/guinea-grass-variety-bundel-guinea-4-jhgg-08-1/
- Background only: a 2025 GWAS of 124 guinea grass accessions from CIAT's collection (not this clone) -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41469560/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found for a breeder or developing institute for Selection 1 or Selection-1. The "Institution" field in the record is unresolved.
- The Indian guinea grass varieties found in search (Bundel Guinea series, Harithasree, Punjab Guinea grass-1) are attributed to other programmes, not to Selection 1 -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1046&context=igc
- KAU lists guinea grass varieties Haritha, Marathakom and Harithashree on its Regional Agricultural Research Station (Vellanikkara/Vellayani-region) crop page; none is Selection 1 -- https://rarsvni.kau.in/crops-0

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. No email or phone number for any Selection 1 breeder was in the results.
- Institute-level fallback: Kerala Agricultural University, Thrissur (established 1971, KAU research directorate at Vellanikkara) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7
- KAU Directorate of Seeds and Planting Material Production, Vellanikkara (price proceedings signed there, 2025). No phone or email shown in the extract -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- Regional Agricultural Research Station (Southern Zone), Vellayani, KAU: Dr. Usha C. Thomas, Professor and Head, Instructional Farm, is the PI on the fodder variety evaluation trial. This is not a Selection 1 breeder contact; no email or phone found -- https://kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/soft_copy_of_xxxix_zreac_meeting.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for any paper, report or thesis on Selection 1 or Selection-1. The KrishiKosh search returned only the KAU community page, not a Selection 1 record -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/communities/f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7?spc.page=1&spc.sf=dc.date.accessioned&spc.sd=DESC&scope=f7008b74-5b73-4d58-9553-330fd59e07c7

SEED AVAILABILITY
- KAU sells guinea grass fodder slips ("Guinea grass & other varieties") at 0.75 per slip under the 2025-26 price revision. The variety name is not specified, so Selection 1 availability cannot be confirmed -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- KAU's 2025 price order says sale is permitted only for varieties recommended by ICAR institutes or SAUs. Selection 1 is not listed as a recommended variety, which conflicts with a Seednet release record and should be checked -- https://www.kau.in/sites/default/files/documents/price_list_seeds_and_planting_materials_2025-26_website.pdf
- No NSC, state seed corporation or private dealer listing for Selection 1 was found. The search covered this only in part, as the fourth search was used for KAU sources.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The raw record says "Kerela", which I read as Kerala. KAU's package of practices calls guinea grass suited to Kerala conditions, but it names no release for Selection 1 -- https://pop.kau.in/foddercrops.htm
- Name note: the record uses "Selection 1" (CSC minutes) and "Selection-1" (Seednet). Searches returned no evidence under either name.
- Year of release is unknown ("NaT" in the record). No CSC or Seednet notification was found, so the release status is unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The search for "GM-6 greengram variety" returned CO 6 greengram (a different variety, Tamil Nadu) and nothing naming GM-6 or GPM-6 for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The same searches returned only a CO 6 yellow mosaic resistance paper (https://masujournal.org/view_archive_journal.php?id=1821), which is a different variety and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. The search returned a seed biopriming study using "GM-3" greengram seed (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336513295_In_vitro_Investigation_of_Seed_biopriming_in_Green_gram). GM-3 is a different variety, so it was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No search result mentioned QTL, marker or pedigree work for GM-6 or GPM-6.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The query on GM-6 with Navsari Agricultural University returned a ResearchGate paper with a Navsari author (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336513295_In_vitro_Investigation_of_Seed_biopriming_in_Green_gram). It does not mention GM-6 and cannot be attributed to this variety. The release metadata supplied with the request (institution: Pulses and Castor Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University; parentage: pureline selection from Bijarpur local) is input data, not search evidence, and no page confirmed it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No institute page, email, phone or address for the Pulses and Castor Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, was returned.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The only greengram research result was the seed biopriming paper, which concerns GM-3 and was discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The search for "GPM-6 horse gram Kulthi variety seed" returned only a Vikaspedia horse gram cultivation page (https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en). That page is about horse gram, a different crop, so it was discarded. The Seednet name "GPM-6" is listed under horse gram, which conflicts with the greengram crop in the record. No Seednet entry was retrieved to confirm this.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in search results. The only state listed is the one supplied in the request, Gujarat (release date 2018-08-10). Neither is confirmed by any retrieved page.

Search log: 4 searches were run (the cap). Queries: "GM-6 greengram variety"; "GM-6 greengram breeder Navsari Agricultural University"; "GM-6 greengram research paper"; "GPM-6 horse gram Kulthi variety seed". Recommended next steps: search seednet.gov.in directly for GPM-6 and check its crop field, and search the Navsari Agricultural University or KrishiKosh site for the Pulses and Castor Research Station's release notification.

seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: IT RESEMBLES WITH THE VARIETY MARU KULTHI WITH RESPECT TO SEED COLOUR.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR (RAJASTHAN, GUJARAT, M.P., HARYANA, ETC) IN KHARIF SEASON (NORTHERN ZONE) FOR GRAINS AS WELL AS FODDER PURPOSE IN MARGINAL LANDS. IT IS HIGHLY DROUGHT TOLERANT AND CAN BE GROWN WHERE THE RAINFALL IS UNCERTAIN AND ERRATIC.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: IT IS MAINLY SOWN IN KHARIF SEASON WITH ONSET OF MONSOON UNDER RAINFED CONDITIONS. MOSTLY SOWN AFTER COMPLETION OF SOWING OF OTHER CROPS AND ON LOW FERTILE AS WELL AS ON MARGINAL LANDS, WHICH RESULTS IN LOWER YIELDS; SPACING : NARROW ROW SPACING (30 CM) GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD IN COMPARISON TO BROAD SPACING (45 CM); FERTILIZER : APPLICATION OF 10 KG. N AND 30 KG. PHOSPHORUS GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD IN COMPARISON TO 5 KG. N AND 15 KG. PHOSPHORUS APPLICATION. FURTHER IT DID NOT RESPOND SIGNIFICANTLY TO SULPHUR APPLICATION 20-25 KG/HA; SOWING TIME : KHARIF SEASON (ONSET OF MONSOON). THE VARIETY GAVE HIGHER SEED YIELD (13.9, 17.6 AND 17.3%) OVER CHECK IN EARLY, NORMAL AND LATE SOWN CONDITIONS, RESPECTIVELY IN DIFFERENT YEARS. IT SHOWS ITS SUITABILITY FOR ALL THE SOWING CONDITIONS; IRRIGATION : RAIFNED.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 30-50 CM; IT IS HAVING LUSH GREEN FOLIAGE WITH SOME WAXY DEPOSITION. IT HAS 2-12 PRIMARY BRANCHES WITH 23-65 PODS PER PLANT. SEED IS BOLD WITH BRICK RED COLOUR, WHICH IS PREFERRED BY THE CONSUMERS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: NO SUCH STUDY WAS MADE BUT IT WAS OBSERVED THAT IT CAN GROW SUCCESSFULLY IN POOR SOILS AND MOISTURE STRESS CONDITION IN BARANI LANDS WHERE NO OTHER CROPS COULD PROFITABLY GROWN. BEING TOLERANT TO DROUGHT IT MAKES EFFICIENT UYSE OF AVAILABLE SOIL MOISTURE AND THRIVES WELL IN AREAS HAVING SCANTY RAINFALL. THIS WAS OBSERVED AT DFRS, ARJIA, BHILWARA IN THE YEAR 2002 THAT ALMOST ALL THE CROPS FAILED TO PRODUCE SEED YIELD EXCEPT HORSEGRAM, PARTICULARLY VARIETY AK-42 WHICH GAVE HIGHEST SEED YIELD (301 KG/HA.) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) IN COMPARISON TO CHECK AK-21 (218 KG/HA) WHICH WAS 38 PERCENT HIGHER, INDICATES ITS TOLERANCE TO STRESS CONDITION.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: NO INCIDENCE OF ANY DISEASES UNDER NATURAL CONDITIONS WAS OBSERVED.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: NO INSECT PEST ATTACK WAS OBSERVED UNDER NATURAL CONDITIONS.

drought.details: The variety is observed to grow successfully in poor soils and moisture stress conditions in rainfed (barani) lands, efficiently utilizing available soil moisture and thriving in areas with scanty rainfall, where other crops might not profitably grow. While no specific study for Pratap Kulthi-2 was cited in the 'stress_reaction' field, an observation from DFRS, Arjia, Bhilwara in 2002, recorded that horsegram variety AK-42 produced a high seed yield (301 kg/ha, 38% higher than check AK-21) during a period when almost all other crops failed, indicating its tolerance to stress.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VL GAHAT 19 (VLG-19) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name and crop notes:
- Release-minute name: "VL Gahat 19". Seednet name: "VL Gahat 10". The evidence below refers to VL Gahat 19 unless a line says otherwise.
- Crop mismatch: the input says chickpea, but every source found describes horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum, gahat/kulthi). Seednet also lists horse gram. No chickpea evidence was found.
- Searches run: 4 (release/agronomy, breeder/contact, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Horse gram as a crop is described as extremely drought-resistant, but no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for VL Gahat 19 was found. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en
- General crop note: horse gram is grown on drylands under low-to-moderate rainfall. Not variety-specific. -- https://krishipatrika.com/2021/05/21425/
- Crop is said to tolerate winter extremes. Not variety-specific. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/metabo13020165

DISEASE AND PEST
- Horse gram yellow mosaic virus (HgYMV) causes alarming yield loss in the crop. No VL Gahat 19 resistance rating was found. -- https://doi.org/10.3390/metabo13020165
- Seed treatment with fungicide is recommended against soil fungal pathogens. Not variety-specific. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en
- No VL Gahat 19 disease or pest reaction data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release table lists VL Gahat 19 with release/notification year 2010 (Kumar 2007 table, cited in a review). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Hill sowing advisory: VL Gahat 15 and 19 for hill Gahat, sown in the first fortnight of June. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/Extension_Edu/02.05.2020_Kharif_season_Advisory.pdf
- Improved package of practice is said to give 6–10 q grain/ha, depending on monsoon. Crop-level FLD figure, not variety-specific. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Horse_gram.PDF
- No VL Gahat 19 yield table or multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker, or genetic study on VL Gahat 19 found. Parentage given in the input (VLG 1 x NIC 2659) was not verified by any source.
- Related but different material: induced mutant and multi-environment studies on TNAU lines and Paiyur 2 (not VL Gahat 19). -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-67282-5

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institute: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. Brand listed as VPKAS on the seed portal. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLGahat19_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%A419
- VPKAS is named as the source of VL Gahat-8 and VL Gahat-10 in the release table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Lead breeder name: not found.
- Uttarakhand's agriculture minister said the state lacks newly certified horse gram varieties and asked ICAR for new ones. -- https://garhwalpost.in/minister-ganesh-joshi-participates-in-icars-97th-agm-in-delhi/

CONTACT DETAILS
- ICAR-VPKAS, Mall Road, Almora-263601, Uttarakhand, India (institute address as listed on an aggregator page). -- https://www.indiamart.com/icarvpkas/
- Name listed: AMIT PASCHAPUR (Scientist), VPKAS. Role and email are not verified against an official page. Phone number was hidden on the page. -- https://www.indiamart.com/icarvpkas/
- No official email or phone number for VPKAS, and no breeder email, was found in the search results.
- Institute website and seed-portal contact pages were not retrieved. Confirm contacts on the VPKAS website before use.

PUBLICATIONS
- No variety-specific paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis on VL Gahat 19 was found.
- Kumar (2007). Varietal releases table, horse gram (cited in a review). Source for the 2010 VL Gahat 19 release year. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Jafarullakhan S. S. et al. (2024). Assessing the yield and nutrient potential of horse gram mutants through a multi-environment-based experiment. Scientific Reports (not VL Gahat 19). -- DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-67282-5
- Metabolomic profiling of horse gram genotypes for HgYMV resistance (Metabolites, 2023). Genotypes not confirmed as VL Gahat 19. -- DOI 10.3390/metabo13020165

SEED AVAILABILITY
- VPKAS seed portal: VL Gahat 19 listed, brand VPKAS, status "In Stock", seed type option shown. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLGahat19_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%97%E0%A4%B9%E0%A4%A419
- Vikaspedia and other pages list VL Gahat-8 and VL Gahat-10 for Uttarakhand, but not as a Seednet or NSC listing. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or dealer listing for VL Gahat 10 on Seednet was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand hills (advisory for hill Gahat). -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/Extension_Edu/02.05.2020_Kharif_season_Advisory.pdf
- The input's "North Zone" was not confirmed by any source found. No CSC notification text was retrieved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TOPIC: Identity and morphology: GJIB-2 is a papdi-type Indian bean (Lablab purpureus) from Junagadh Agricultural University, with flat, medium-long, green pods; plants are about 75-80 cm tall, with 220-230 pods per plant, 8-9 cm pod length, and 5-6 g pod weight -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//vrs_imp_charactristics_of_varities_20260512_1553.pdf
TOPIC: Breeder/institution: Listed among Junagadh Agricultural University vegetable varieties as Gujarat Junagadh Indian Bean 2; the listing marks it as released at state and national level; no breeder names found -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf
TOPIC: Release year: The JAU listings I found name the variety but give no specific release year for GJIB-2; the 2015 date comes only from the input data, unconfirmed -- No evidence found
TOPIC: Recommended states/regions: Recommended for late kharif cultivation in the Saurashtra and Middle Gujarat areas of Gujarat -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Varieties-last-13-years.pdf
TOPIC: Yield and trials: No variety-specific yield trial data found for GJIB-2; a JAU summary mentions a green pod yield advantage over a local check (Virpur local) but the attribution to GJIB-2 is unclear in the excerpt, so it is not used -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Varieties-last-13-years.pdf
TOPIC: Drought tolerance: No evidence found

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is mentioned in two 2023 publications, but only in snippets that are truncated or ambiguous. No stress trait, yield figure, or Gujarat-specific data can be attributed to it with confidence. The 'at least one stress trait' criterion for 60 or 75 is not clearly met. The possible climate-resilience association and the citations nominally place it between 40 and 60, so 50 is assigned as a conservative score. A score of 40 would be defensible if the IIVR listing is judged not to be climate evidence. Full-text verification could raise or lower the score.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Likely IIVR release (2022); inter-varietal derivation; stress and yield data unverified

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Kashi Bouni Sem-9 is a 2022 Indian bean (dolichos bean) variety, apparently from ICAR-IIVR and developed through inter-varietal breeding. The 30 search results are repeats of two ResearchGate documents with truncated snippets, so no stress tolerance, yield, or commercial availability can be confirmed. Evidence quality is low and the Gujarat score is 50.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Dolichos bean variety released in 2022, probably by IIVR Varanasi and developed through inter-varietal breeding. Yield, maturity, adaptation and recommended states are not documented.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Stress tolerance is not demonstrated. The snippets that mention drought, heat, salt, and virus tolerance refer mainly to tomato or other bean varieties, and any link to this variety is unverified. The full IIVR climate-resilience paper should be consulted.
