search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Tirupati Field Bean-2 (CSC name) / Tirupati Field Bean-1 (Seednet name), field bean (Indian bean, Lablab purpureus var. lignosus), RARS Tirupati, code A0307020

Scope note: I ran four searches covering both names. None returned a page that mentions either "Tirupati Field Bean-1" or "Tirupati Field Bean-2" or the parentage "LOCAL (GP-18) x HA-3". Every heading below therefore reports either an institute-level fact or "No evidence found". Nothing here confirms the 2010 release, the parentage, or the variety code.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for either name. (Searched: "Tirupati Field Bean-2 field bean variety"; "Tirupati Field Bean-1 Indian bean RARS Tirupati developed by")

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for either name. Unrelated Indian bean varieties from other programmes report disease scores (for example, Gujarat Junagadh Indian Bean-2 had leaf spot and leaf blight intensities compared with a check) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00207.2 (not this variety).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for either name. The only trial-type result is for a different Indian bean (Gujarat Junagadh Indian Bean-2, green pod yield 112.46 q/ha vs check 89.56 q/ha) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00207.2 (not this variety).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage LOCAL (GP-18) x HA-3 was not confirmed by any source. The HA-3 name appears only as a photo-insensitive vegetable type in an export listing -- https://bwellinternational.com/product/field-beans/ (not evidence of this cross).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Tirupati, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU). RARS was established in 1979 and its stated mandate centres on groundnut and cropping systems, with pulses as a verification function -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we. No breeder or lead scientist name was found for Tirupati Field Bean-1 or -2 -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level information only, as listed on the ANGRAU RARS page: "Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), S.V. Agricultural College campus, Chandragiri Road, Tirupati - 517502, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, India" -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we. This address is given for the RARS campus and a related incubator, not for the bean programme specifically. No official email, phone, or named contact person was found -- https://www.angraurabitpt.org/who-are-we.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for either name. Searches of ICAR and KrishiKosh-type sources (via general search) did not return any paper, report, or thesis on this variety. Sources that came up were on other Indian bean/lablab varieties and are not listed here as publications on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Tirupati Field Bean-1 or -2 from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, the SAU, or dealers. The only dealer results were generic seed-trader listings in Tirupati with no bean variety named -- https://www.tradeindia.com/tirupati/seeds-city-222733.html.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The raw field in the record is "Not specified", and no source names the states for this variety.

Recommended follow-up: check the Seednet portal entry for "Tirupati Field Bean-1" (variety code A0307020) directly, and search the ANGRAU/RARS Tirupati annual reports and the AICRP on MULLaRP (pulses) annual reports, which are the most likely places to record its release notification and trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bayer Mustard 5222 (variety_name) / Bayer Mustard 5450 (seednet_variety_name) / Indian rapeseed and mustard (yellow sarson) / variety code Pro 5222

Name note: the Seednet name "Bayer Mustard 5450" returned no pages at all. Every finding below that refers to the variety is about "5222", "Bayer Mustard 5222", "Crystal 5222", "Crystal Hybrid 5222", or "Pro 5222". None of the pages mention 5450, and none is from Seednet or ICAR.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for this variety. The only related claim is a retailer listing that calls the seed disease-resistant, without any test data. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/crystal-hybrid-5222-mustard-seed

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for official resistance ratings (AICRP or SAU screening). The only claim is a retailer's marketing line describing Crystal Hybrid 5222 as high-yielding and disease-resistant. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/crystal-hybrid-5222-mustard-seed

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Retailer and brand product pages only, not trial data:
- Maturity of about 125-130 days, dark brown seed, plant height 160-180 cm, oil content 41-42%, and yield claimed at 12-15 quintals per acre. -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/seed/detail/5222-hybrid-mustard
- A second page from the same brand gives yield as 9-11 quintals per acre and plant height as 190-210 cm, which conflicts with the first page. -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Mustard/5222
- Sowing in October to November by drilling or broadcasting, with row spacing of 30-45 cm and plant spacing of 10-15 cm; seed rate of 2 kg per acre. -- https://agribegri.com/products/ijj.php and https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/crystal-hybrid-5222-mustard-seed
- Hindi video and blog content describes it as suited to early and late sowing, with more branches and pods. These are informal and are not trial results. -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MfZGeYkRQp0 and https://dearkisan.com/top-sarso-variety-bayer5222/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No marker, QTL, parentage, or hybrid-system information was returned. The parentage field in the record is "Not specified", and the searches did not resolve it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No page names a lead breeder, a developing scientist, or a developing station for this variety. The Bayer pages returned concern unrelated Bayer breeding projects (Bt cowpea, IITA modern breeding) and were discarded. The DMH-11 Wikipedia page is a different variety and was discarded. Pages that sell the seed name the company "Bayer Crop Science" or "Crystal Crop Protection" as brand owners, but that is a marketing attribution and is not a developer record. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/bayer-crop-science-hybrid-mustard-seeds-5222-variety-26824217930.html

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder or institute contact found. The only addresses on the pages belong to seed resellers, not to the developer, and are listed here for completeness only:
- Porwal Hybrid Seeds And Biotech, A-22 Shankarpuri Colony, Chinhat, Lucknow - 227105, Uttar Pradesh, India (reseller; no email or phone shown on the page). -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/bayer-crop-science-hybrid-mustard-seeds-5222-variety-26824217930.html
- Ghazi Malik Beej Bhandar, Siroli Road, Rampur-244922, Uttar Pradesh, India (reseller). -- https://www.indiamart.com/ghazi-malik-beej-bhandar/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed papers, AICRP or ICAR reports, theses, or conference papers for this variety. Indexes such as KrishiKosh were not directly reachable in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Private and state-agency sources only; no NSC, SAU, or KVK listing was found:
- West Bengal State Seed Corporation Limited floated a tender (ref. WBSSCL/MD/KOL/NIT-02/2021-22, deadline 31 May 2021) for supply of hybrid mustard varieties Kesari 5111, Kesari Gold and "Pro 5222" in Kolkata. This is the only state-agency reference found and matches the variety code, but the page does not name the developing company. -- https://www.tendersontime.com/india/details/supply-hybrid-mustard-seeds-var-kesari-5111-kesari-gold-and-pro-5222-327bdc1/
- Dealers in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan sell the seed as "Bayer Mustard 5222" or "Bayer Crop Science Hybrid Mustard Seeds 5222". -- https://www.indiamart.com/vindhywasini-traders/mustard-seeds.html and https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/bayer-crop-science-hybrid-mustard-seeds-5222-variety-26824217930.html
- Listings for Crystal 5222 appear through several online sellers. One is marked out of stock on the listing date. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/crystal-hybrid-5222-mustard-seed
- Kolkata traders list generic dark-brown mustard seed. These do not name the variety and were discarded. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/kolkata/mustard-seeds.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES -- West Bengal is listed as a regional adaptability state for the 5222 hybrid on brand pages, which also list several other states. The brand pages do not give an official notification or CSC source. The West Bengal tender above supports West Bengal as a procurement state for "Pro 5222". -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/seed/detail/5222-hybrid-mustard and https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Mustard/5222

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION -- No evidence found. Searches returned no CSC minutes, notification, or release record for the 2019-06-01 release date given in the record.

salinity.details: CSSRI's technology listing states CS 60 is recommended for saline soils up to ECe 12.0 dS/m and alkali soils up to about pH 9.5, and is highly suitable for saline-sodic soils. CSSRI's varieties page gives lower limits (ECe about 9.0 dS/m, pH about 9.3, and 6-9 dS/m in another passage), so the tolerance ceiling differs between CSSRI sources and should be verified before use. A seedling-stage metabolomics study reports that CS 60 accumulated more differentially expressed metabolites than the sensitive line CS 245-2-80-7 under salt stress, with antioxidant-defence pathways protecting against osmotic and oxidative stress and more active photosynthesis. The reported trial performance in All India Salinity Alkalinity Tolerant Variety Trials could not be confirmed because the abstract is truncated. The level is rated high on the basis of the breeder-site recommendations and the mechanistic study; the discrepancy in stated limits lowers confidence in the precise ceiling.

Units are reported as q/ha in the sources (1 q/ha = 100 kg/ha), whereas the original variety data lists 'Kg/Ha' with no value.

salinity.details: Released as a salt-tolerant Indian mustard for irrigated sodic conditions in Uttar Pradesh, sown by about 25 October. The variety is described as tolerant of sodic soil up to pH 9-9.3 (2022 annual report). Yield is 21-22 q/ha in sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha in normal soil and water, with about 39.5% oil (annual report); the PSA page gives 21-23 q/ha for sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha for normal soil. No salinity threshold values (soil ECe or irrigation water ECiw) specific to CS 61 were found. The general Indian mustard thresholds of 8.2 dS/m soil ECe and 12 dS/m ECiw come from a different source and apply to the crop, not to CS 61. The 2022 annual report describes a sowing-date trial of salt-tolerant mustard varieties on saline Vertisols, but CS 61 results were not separated out in the retrieved text. The 'high' rating reflects the release purpose and reported sodic-soil tolerance; no quantitative salinity threshold for CS 61 was found.

disease_resistance.summary: Annual report 2022 lists CS 61 as resistant to Alternaria blight, white rust, powdery mildew and downy mildew; the retrieved text is truncated after 'powdery and downy'. The PSA page lists CS 61 as tolerant of key diseases and aphids. No independent field-scoring data for CS 61 was found, so the evidence is self-reported by the release sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Name: the evidence uses "CS 13000-3-2-2-5-2 (CS 61)", which matches the Seednet name. The CSC release-minute name was not found separately.
- Released as a salt-tolerant Indian mustard for irrigated sodic conditions in Uttar Pradesh, sown by about 25 October; the variety is described as tolerant of sodic soil up to pH 9-9.3 -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf
- Yield is 21-22 q/ha in sodic soil and 25-28 q/ha in normal soil and water, with about 39.5% oil -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf (the PSA page gives 21-23 q/ha for sodic soil, 25-28 q/ha for normal soil -- https://www.psa.gov.in/livelihood/10096)
- Tolerant of irrigated sodic soils; no salinity threshold values specific to CS 61 were found. General Indian mustard salinity thresholds (8.2 dS/m soil ECe, 12 dS/m irrigation water ECiw) are from a different source and apply to the crop, not to CS 61 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257957254_Assessing_effect_of_salinity_on_oil_quality_parameters_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_using_Fourier_Transform_Near-Infrared_Reflectance_FT-NIR_spectroscopy
- Sowing-date evidence: the 2022 annual report describes a trial of salt-tolerant mustard varieties under different sowing dates on saline Vertisols, but CS 61 results were not separated out in the retrieved text -- https://cssri.res.in/PSSU/Publications/Annual%20Report/2022/Annual%20Report%202022%20-%20English.pdf

Name: CS 13000-3-2-2-5-2 (CS 61).

drought.details: This variety performs well under restricted irrigations. It is also listed among varieties exhibiting drought stress tolerance in Indian mustard.

heat.details: The variety is relevant in the context of high temperature (heat) stress prevalence in India for rapeseed-mustard breeding, suggesting its adaptation to such conditions, though a specific tolerance level is not stated.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield data includes 4.30 (likely quintals/hectare) for the year 2010, and values of 6.50 and 6.60 (units unspecified) from different reports. Mean oil content is 37.48% with a range of 35.8% to 40.1% across different locations.
agronomic_details.stability: The proposed strain has resistance for lodging and shattering. It demonstrates a stable oil content across different locations.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for cultivation under after/relay cropping in paddy fields with come-up/full irrigation. It is advised in ICAR Rabi Agro-Advisories for farmers and explicitly recommended for 'Whole of Chhattisgarh'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. GROWTH HABIT - ERECT 2. APPRISED SILIQUAE. Normal agronomic practices include a seed rate of 7 kg/ha (33% higher seed rate) with partial fertilizer doses of 50:25:25 NPK kg/ha, requiring come-up irrigation and full irrigations.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been evaluated in various trials, with yield data reported in annual and project coordinator's reports from institutions like ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research and IGKVV Jagdalpur.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs or their effects are identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety's parentage is PCR-20 X RH - 819. It has been utilized in breeding programs, forming crosses such as Bio-902 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, ACN9 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, PM-26 x Chhattisgarh Sarson, and Kranti x Chhattisgarh Sarson. These crosses have demonstrated useful heterosis (e.g., PM-26 x Chhattisgarh Sarson with -8.01% heterosis) and are noted for contributing to drought-tolerant rapeseed roots and their hybrid F1 lines under stress.

drought.details: Giriraj is identified as moisture stress tolerant. It exhibits tolerance to drought stress and has been utilized in crosses to develop drought-tolerant F1 lines under drought stress conditions.

heat.details: The variety is heat tolerant at the seedling stage and shows general tolerance to heat stress. It demonstrated higher heat use efficiency in relation to seed yield.

salinity.details: Giriraj was included in evaluations for seed yield under various conditions, but the provided results do not explicitly state its tolerance level to salinity. Another variety, CS 64, is specifically mentioned as salt tolerant in the same context.

flood.details: No information found regarding flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Giriraj is identified as a susceptible genotype to Alternaria blight. It was also part of studies concerning Powdery Mildew disease in Indian mustard, where other varieties demonstrated resistance, implying Giriraj is not resistant.

pest_resistance.summary: No information found regarding pest resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: An average seed yield of 2246-2767 Kg/ha has been reported for Giriraj in Delhi. It is frequently used as a check variety in evaluations of Indian mustard genotypes for seed yield and other associated traits. Its productivity is noted to increase with the application of 100% Recommended Dose of Fertilizer (RDF) supplemented with bio-fertilizer.
agronomic_details.stability: Its consistent designation as a 'check variety' in numerous research evaluations indicates a generally stable and reliable performance baseline across different trials.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is adapted to timely sown irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified beyond its classification as an Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Giriraj has undergone evaluation in augmented block design trials and extensive multi-genotype assessments, frequently serving as a standard check variety for comparison.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (e.g., SNPs, SSRs) explicitly linked to Giriraj for its traits were detailed in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Giriraj has been included in research investigating QTLs for anaerobic germination and tolerance to early submergence, but specific QTLs inherent to Giriraj or their effects for these or other traits are not specified.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No specific molecular mechanisms, genes, or pathways underlying Giriraj's traits were detailed.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to GDJ 1 (Banas Surya). A 2018 water-deficit study at Deesa lists DS 172, which the GDJ 1 paper gives as an earlier trial name, but the study never names GDJ 1, so it was excluded.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to GDJ 1 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to GDJ 1 in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to GDJ 1 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence names GDJ 1 with a disease resistance rating. The statements 'moderately resistant to leaf blight and anthracnose' were attributed to GJ 45 (SDAU Jowar Moti) in the digest and were excluded for GDJ 1.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for a confirmed pest resistance rating in GDJ 1. Shoot fly resistance: the GDJ 1 paper reports 2021-22 work at Deesa on SSR markers linked to shoot fly resistance, but the snippet does not confirm that GDJ 1 was the material studied, so this is not attributed to GDJ 1. The 'lower shoot fly and stem borer infestation' statement belongs to GJ 45 and was excluded. The SDAU Deesa centre page lists 'chemical control of sorghum shoot fly and stem borer' as an achievement, which is not tied to GDJ 1.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean grain yield of 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations (including the preliminary trial); mean dry fodder of 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials.
agronomic_details.stability: Grain and fodder yields were reported across 21 to 22 locations, and North Gujarat results were reported across seven trials against checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. No further stability analysis (e.g., GxE statistics) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Developed and reported for the semi-arid region of Gujarat (per the release paper title). No agro-climatic analysis beyond this was found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Tall plants, very long and broad leaves, semi-loose panicle, medium-bold yellow-white grain. Dual-purpose (grain and dry fodder) per the release paper title.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Preliminary evaluation trial in kharif 2016. (2) State multilocation trials in kharif 2017 to 2019. (3) Entry in the AICRP-Sorghum IVT in kharif 2018 as SPV 2565 at fifteen locations. (4) 2019 location data (Deesa, Surat, Udaipur) appear in a results table of the GDJ 1 paper; the digest gives no values for these. (5) Multilocation summary: mean grain yield 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations and dry fodder 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. (6) North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials versus checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. Agronomic practice trials specific to GDJ 1: not found in searched sources.

Pedigree (not marker data): SPV 2113 x GFS 5, developed by pedigree selection at the Sorghum Research Station, SDAU, Deesa.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GDJ 1 (Banas Surya). The only drought-related hit was a 2018 water-deficit study at Deesa that lists DS 172, which the GDJ 1 paper gives as an earlier trial name. That study never names GDJ 1, so I excluded it. -- https://ndpublisher.in/admin/issues/IJAEBv14n4k.pdf
Shoot fly resistance: the GDJ 1 paper reports work at Deesa in 2021-22 on SSR markers linked to shoot fly resistance, but the snippet does not confirm that GDJ 1 was the material studied. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found that names GDJ 1 with a disease or pest resistance rating. The "moderately resistant to leaf blight and anthracnose" and "lower shoot fly and stem borer infestation" statements belong to GJ 45 (SDAU Jowar Moti), so I excluded them. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396423609_GJ_45_SDAU_JOWAR_MOTI_-_A_NEW_DUAL_SORGHUM_VARIETY_FOR_SEMI-ARID_REGION_OF_GUJARAT_INDIA
The SDAU Deesa centre page lists "chemical control of sorghum shoot fly and stem borer" as an achievement, but this is not tied to GDJ 1. -- https://www.sdau.edu.in/Research/81

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
GDJ 1 is a sorghum entry with a maturity of 100-105 days, tall plants, very long and broad leaves, and a semi-loose panicle with medium-bold yellow-white grain. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017 (DOAJ record: https://doaj.org/article/aaa34372196e43929e59c0c7cede1bdb)
Yield: mean grain yield of 2506 kg/ha over 21 locations including the preliminary trial, and mean dry fodder of 167.0 q/ha over 22 locations. -- https://doaj.org/article/aaa34372196e43929e59c0c7cede1bdb
North Gujarat: 2576 kg/ha grain and 228.7 q/ha dry fodder across seven trials, against checks GJ 39, GJ 42, GJ 43, GNJ 1 and CSV 20. -- https://doaj.org/article/aaa34372196e43929e59c0c7cede1bdb
Trial history: preliminary evaluation trial in kharif 2016, state multilocation trials kharif 2017 to 2019, and entry in the AICRP-Sorghum IVT in kharif 2018 as SPV 2565 at fifteen locations. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017 (DOAJ record) and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396423609_GJ_45_SDAU_JOWAR_MOTI_-_A_NEW_DUAL_SORGHUM_VARIETY_FOR_SEMI-ARID_REGION_OF_GUJARAT_INDIA
2019 location data (Deesa, Surat, Udaipur) appear in a results table of the GDJ 1 paper. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat
No evidence found for agronomic practice trials specific to GDJ 1.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: SPV 2113 × GFS 5, developed by pedigree selection at the Sorghum Research Station, SDAU, Deesa. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017
No QTL or marker-trait association for GDJ 1 was found. The shoot fly SSR study mentioned above is not confirmed as involving GDJ 1 or its parents. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Named authors of the release paper: R. A. Gami, R. N. Patel, P. R. Patel and S. K. Jain. The page does not assign lead-breeder roles. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017
Developing institution: Sorghum Research Station and AICRP Sorghum, Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University (SDAU), Deesa-385 535, Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358562511_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_A_novel_high_yielding_dual-purpose_sorghum_variety_GDJ_1Banas_Surya_for_semi-arid_region_of_Gujarat
The SDAU Centre for Millets Research (Deesa) lists GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) among its developed and released varieties. -- https://www.sdau.edu.in/Research/81
A CV from SKNAU lists Dr. Shailesh Kumar Jain's Deesa posting (2008-2018) and GDJ-1 among his work, but it does not state his role in releasing this variety. -- https://www.sknau.ac.in/uploads/staff/resumes/resume_209_1770999672.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No individual breeder email or phone was found. Institute-level contact from the AICRP-Sorghum cooperating centres list: Officer In-charge, AICSIP, Sorghum Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University, Banaskantha, Deesa – 385 535; phone 02744-223673 (F), 220865 / 02744-220865 (O); email deesa@millets.res.in. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sorghum/partners/list-of-centres/
Postal address for the Deesa centre: Deesa 385 535, Banaskantha, Gujarat. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274254345_Diversity_of_Sorghum_Sorghum_bicolor_L_Moench_germplasm_from_Gujarat_India_Corresponding_Author

PUBLICATIONS
Gami, R. A., Patel, R. N., Patel, P. R., Jain, S. K. (2021). A novel high yielding dual-purpose sorghum variety GDJ 1 (Banas Surya) for semi-arid region of Gujarat. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 12(1): 109-121 -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2021.1201.017
The SDAU research-article page lists the same title under Forage Research without a matching author list. Treat this listing as needing verification. -- https://sdau.edu.in/researcharticlesjournals/0
Not found: KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports naming GDJ 1, or conference papers specific to GDJ 1.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The search returned no seed-sale listing, NSC/State Seed Corporation entry, KVK entry or SAU seed-sales page for GDJ 1. A Deesa licensed-dealer directory was returned, but it names no variety and was excluded. -- https://www.napanta.com/seed-dealer/gujarat/banas-kantha/deesa/
The SDAU Deesa centre mandate includes seed production of released sorghum varieties, but it does not name GDJ 1 for seed sales. --

drought.details: Not confirmed. The GDM-5 abstract is cut off before the full stress list, and drought tolerance was not confirmed in the digest. The variety is described as suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions, which describes the growing system rather than demonstrated drought tolerance. Lodging and shattering tolerance are reported under plant_characteristics.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. Salinity tolerance was not confirmed in the retrieved abstract.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. Flood tolerance was not confirmed in the retrieved abstract.

disease_resistance.summary: Sclerotinia: reported tolerant per the GDM-5 abstract (JOR article 126930). Full disease reaction table was not retrieved. Reaction of GDM-5 against major diseases in Zone II is listed as a ResearchGate profile title, but values were not retrieved. The powdery mildew row in the DRMR report was not attributed to GDM-5 because it is ambiguous whether it refers to GDM-4 or GDM-5, so no powdery mildew resistance is claimed.

pest_resistance.summary: Mustard aphid: reported tolerant to natural infestation per the GDM-5 abstract (JOR article 126930). The aphid infestation index table is listed as a ResearchGate profile title, but values were not retrieved. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to lodging and shattering, with a medium-tall growth habit; evaluated as a rainfed variety for Zone II -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
Reported tolerant to biotic stresses including mustard aphid (under natural conditions) and Sclerotinia; the abstract snippet is cut off before the full list, so drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance were not confirmed -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
Described as suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Tolerant to mustard aphid (natural infestation) and Sclerotinia, per the GDM-5 abstract; full disease reaction table not retrieved -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
Reaction of GDM-5 against major diseases in Zone II and an aphid infestation index table are listed as titles on a ResearchGate profile, but the values were not retrieved -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Aanandi-Jat
Note: the DRMR report row mentioning powdery mildew and aphid tolerance sits in a table where it is ambiguous whether it refers to GDM-4 or GDM-5, so it was not attributed to GDM-5 -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Weighted mean seed yield 2213 kg/ha across IVT and AVT rainfed trials at five locations (rabi 2011-12 to 2013-14), higher than national check Kranti (1758 kg/ha) and zonal checks Geeta, RB-50 and RGN-48 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
Seed oil content 40.50%, average oil yield 897 kg/ha, about 24.6% above Kranti and 81.2% above Geeta -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
Yield range 2081-2360 kg/ha and oil content 38.0-41.4% in an AICRP-style comparison table -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf ; https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/cultivation-of-mustard-in-india
Maturity 134-155 days in the DRMR report; days-to-maturity data for GDM-5 appear only as a table title on ResearchGate, not retrieved -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Field trial of GDM-5 under the AICRP varietal programme, 2020-21 and 2017-18 studies were on other topics (spacing, nutrients) and did not name GDM-5 in the retrieved text, so they were excluded -- No evidence found for GDM-5-specific agronomy beyond the above

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree-method derivation from a cross between BIO 129-97 and NDR 9503 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
QTL or marker studies on GDM-5: No evidence found (search returned only a soybean pod-shattering marker paper by the same group, which concerns soybean and was discarded) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338096032_Validation_of_molecular_markers_for_pod_shattering_tolerance_in_soybean_Glycine_max_L_Merrill

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed at the Castor-Mustard Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University (SDAU), Sardarkrushinagar, Gujarat -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
Authors of the GDM-5 paper (the paper does not separately label a lead breeder): K P Prajapati, P J Patel, J R Patel, B K Patel, S K Shah, A L Jat, G P Gangwar, A G Desai, all at Castor-Mustard Research Station, SDAU -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
Released under the name Gujarat Dantiwada Mustard 5 in the DRMR report, with SKM 518 as the trial code -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Institute background on rapeseed-mustard research at SDAU Oilseeds Research Centre -- https://www.sdau.edu.in/Research/68

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level address only (from the GDM-5 paper affiliation): Castor-Mustard Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University, Sardarkrushinagar-385 506, Gujarat -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930

PUBLICATIONS

Journal of Oilseeds Research, 36(2), 73-78 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/126930
(Year and volume/pages taken from the ResearchGate reproduction of the same article, which gives J. Oilseeds Res. 36(2): 73-78, June 2019 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338096032_Validation_of_molecular_markers_for_pod_shattering_tolerance_in_soybean_Glycine_max_L_Merrill)
Excluded as not naming GDM-5: GDM-4 paper (ISOR vol. 34-4, https://isor.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/vol-34-4.pdf); GM 6 (Banas Sona) paper (https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137209); soybean marker paper (see GENETICS).
KrishiKosh thesis on mustard plot-size uniformity trials (2015): does not name GDM-5 in the retrieved text, so excluded -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/c77998d0-ba15-42c4-a9bf-ed82ebb38fe8/content
AICRP/ICAR reports: DRMR Project Coordinator's Report 2020-21 lists the variety in its release table (https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf); no separate trial report with GDM-5 data was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only unrelated seed sellers (GDM Seeds Inc, spice and garden seed shops, NCDEX mustard futures, mandi price listings) and no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales or dealer listing for GDM-5 -- https://www.ncdex.com/products/RMSEED

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab, Haryana, Jammu, Northern Rajasthan and Delhi, identified for rainfed conditions in the DRMR report -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Notified state list (2008-2019) includes GDM-5 under Delhi, Haryana and Punjab; Jammu and Rajasthan are not shown there -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
Commercial listing gives Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/cultivation-of-mustard-in-india
Discrepancy: the input record says "Rajasthan"; sources say "Northern Rajasthan" (DRMR) or do not specify.

NAME NOTE
variety_name "Gujarat Dantiwada Mustard-5 (GDM 5) (SKM 518)" and seednet_variety_name are the same string here. The Seednet portal itself was not reached, so no Seednet-specific record (crop name "INDIAN RAPESEED AND MUSTARD (YELLOW SARSON)") was verified; the DRMR table lists the crop as Indian mustard (Brassica juncea), which conflicts with the "yellow sarson" label and should be checked on seednet.gov.in.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record states "UT of Jammu & Kashmir", but no search result confirmed this recommendation.

drought.details: While general efforts in rapeseed-mustard breeding aim for drought-tolerant cultivars (RESULT_9, RESULT_30) and some varieties like NRCYS-05-02 are noted as moisture stress tolerant (RESULT_7, RESULT_12), specific drought tolerance for JMC-3 (or JM-3) is not detailed in the provided search results. Research on the genetics of drought stress tolerance in *Brassica spp.* is ongoing (RESULT_3).

heat.details: Heat stress is recognized as a major factor affecting rapeseed-mustard growth and productivity in India (RESULT_14, RESULT_19, RESULT_20). While some mustard genotypes (e.g., DRMRIJ16-3, RGN-403, RH-1556) have shown tolerance to high temperature stress with delayed sowing (RESULT_18), and NRCDR 2 (Indian mustard) is tolerant to high temperature at sowing (RESULT_24), specific heat tolerance for JMC-3 is not described. The reproductive stage is particularly susceptible to temperature stress in Indian mustard (RESULT_17).

salinity.details: Breeding efforts in *Brassica spp.* are directed towards understanding the genetics of salt stress tolerance (RESULT_3). Specific varieties like Pusa mustard-24 are noted as salt tolerant (RESULT_29), and NRCDR 2 (Indian mustard) is tolerant to salinity at sowing (RESULT_24). However, no specific information regarding JMC-3's salinity tolerance is provided.

flood.details: Economically important Brassicaceae crops, including *Brassica napus* (canola) and *Brassica oleracea* (broccoli, cabbage), are generally susceptible to flooding stress (RESULT_36, RESULT_41). No specific information on JMC-3's flood tolerance is available.

disease_resistance.summary: While JMC-3 (JM-3) is mentioned alongside varieties like JM-1 and JM-2 (RESULT_26, RESULT_28, RESULT_29, RESULT_39), and JM-1 and JM-2 are bred for disease tolerance (RESULT_22), specific disease resistance for JMC-3 itself is not explicitly detailed. Sclerotinia rot is a significant disease in rapeseed-mustard (RESULT_22).

pest_resistance.summary: The impact of increasing insect stress on crop production is acknowledged (RESULT_10), but specific pest resistance for JMC-3 or other mustard varieties is not provided in the search results.

agronomic_details.yield: Quantitative yield data for JMC-3 is not provided in the search results.
agronomic_details.stability: Information on JMC-3's yield stability across different environments is not available.
agronomic_details.adaptation: JMC-3 (JM-3) is listed as an Indian mustard variety (RESULT_29, RESULT_39). Indian mustard is a major rabi oilseed crop in India (RESULT_40, RESULT_47). The original data indicates it is recommended for Jammu. Selection efforts for superior Indian mustard plants, including JM-3, have been practiced at various centers (RESULT_26).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in the search results.
agronomic_details.field_trials: JM-3 was involved in selection programs for superior plants/bulk at different centers, and crosses involving JM-3 (e.g., JM-3 x RH9615) have been part of breeding efforts in Indian mustard (RESULT_26).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified for JMC-3. Research on Quantitative Trait Loci (QTLs) for heat stress tolerance has been conducted in *Brassica rapa L.* (yellow sarson), with identified tolerant lines (RESULT_13, RESULT_37). The genetics of salt and drought stress tolerance are also being explored in *Brassica spp.*, often using *Arabidopsis thaliana* as a model (RESULT_3).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs related to heat stress tolerance have been identified in *Brassica rapa*, and tolerant groups showed cooler canopy temperatures (RESULT_13). No specific QTLs for JMC-3 were found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified for JMC-3. General research indicates that molecular responses to stresses like flooding are being studied in Brassicaceae, but specific mechanisms for JMC-3 are not detailed (RESULT_36, RESULT_43).

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage or marker studies were returned. The only parentage information is from the input record: "A SELECTION FROM LOCAL MATERIAL OF GUJARAT" (no source URL; input data only).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. The input record names the institution only as "Regional Agricultural Research Station" with no state, university, or station location. No breeder name was found in the search results.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL was returned for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The sunflower-related results were general breeding slides and unrelated pages, not papers, theses, AICRP reports, or conference papers on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Searches on NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, and dealer sources did not return a listing for this variety. A seed-availability search on "PS-66" returned only unrelated US wildflower seed mixes.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The input record says "Not specified," and no notification gazette or state recommendation was found.

NOTES ON NAMES AND SEARCHES
- The variety name in the CSC minutes is corrupted ("APSH ��� 66"). I searched it as APSH-66, which is my reading and not confirmed by any source.
- The Seednet name is PS-66, but the Seednet crop is listed as "Indian rapeseed and mustard (yellow sarson)", while the minutes list sunflower. This is a crop mismatch in the input data. Searches for PS-66 under sunflower and mustard both returned nothing relevant, so the evidence does not confirm which crop this variety belongs to. The Seednet name and crop should be verified on seednet.gov.in before this record is used.
- Four searches were run, the maximum allowed. The search tool returned no pages on this variety. The next steps are to check the ICAR-IIOPR or AICRP-Sunflower varietal lists, the Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat SAU release notifications, and the Seednet record for PS-66 directly, since those sites were not reachable through this search tool.

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt: moderately resistant (DPD central-release table, 2015, IARI, NWPZ, irrigated) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf. Wilt and ascochyta blight: described as having ascochyta blight and wilt tolerance (IARI best-practice note) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf. Wilt and root rot: described as moderate resistance (Krishi Jagran). Note: in the digest's Stress Tolerance section this Krishi Jagran statement is tied to the seed-size group the variety belongs to, so its attribution to Pusa 3022 specifically is uncertain -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/. A quiz page describes Pusa-3022 as wilt-resistant; this is a low-reliability source and is not independent confirmation. Root rot and ascochyta blight evidence rests on single sources. Resistance levels are not quantified.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest-resistance data specific to Pusa 3022 were found.

agronomic_details.yield: AICRP identification data for the NWPZ: average grain yield 1782 kg/ha; yield potential 3056 kg/ha; mean yield superiority of 56.18% over ruling checks; 10.4% over the best check JGK 1 -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf. Krishi Jagran reports yield potential up to 3 t/ha and 1.8 t/ha average grain yield (10.4% above best check) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data were reported beyond the NWPZ irrigated identification context.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Northern Plains Zone (NWPZ), irrigated conditions, large-seeded kabuli type -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Mean maturity 150 days (AICRP identification and AICRP 2021-22 report); 150-152 days (DPD table)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Large-seeded kabuli type; 100-seed weight 36 g (AICRP identification) or 37 g (IARI best-practice note). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP identification for NWPZ: mean yield superiority of 56.18% over ruling checks, 10.4% over best check JGK 1, average grain yield 1782 kg/ha, yield potential 3056 kg/ha, mean maturity 150 days, 100-seed weight 36 g. (2) Zinc fertilization trial (Springer, 2026): Pusa 547 (desi) out-yielded Pusa 3022 (kabuli) by 19.1% in grain yield; this is a comparison with a different genotype type and is not an absolute yield for Pusa 3022. (3) Frontiers in Plant Science (2025): Pusa 3022 is a check genotype; no quantitative result for Pusa 3022 was given in the digest. (4) Seed Science and Technology (microbial seed coating): Pusa 3022 is one of two varieties tested; no quantitative result for Pusa 3022 was given in the digest. (5) Breeder seed indent figures of 51.6 and 20.0 q appear in an IARI table without a year label; these are seed-production figures, not trial results.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa 3022 (BG 3022), chickpea

Name note: The evidence below refers to Pusa 3022 (BG 3022), the CSC release name. The Seednet name "PUSA-30" is listed under yellow sarson (mustard), so it cannot be the same crop. My search for PUSA-30 returned an error, so I have no Seednet evidence under that name. Four searches were run in total. The results contained no breeder name, breeder contact, or seed-dealer listing specific to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to Fusarium wilt, per the DPD central-release table for Pusa 3022 (2015, IARI, NWPZ, irrigated) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Described as having ascochyta blight and wilt tolerance, with a 100-seed weight of 37 g -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Described as having moderate resistance to wilt and root rot, with yield potential of 20-25 q/ha for bold-seeded types in the group it belongs to -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data specific to Pusa 3022 were found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to wilt and root rot (see Stress Tolerance line above) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- Moderately resistant to Fusarium wilt (see DPD line above) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No pest-resistance data specific to Pusa 3022 were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Identified by the AICRP for the NWPZ, with a mean yield superiority of 56.18% over ruling checks, 10.4% over the best check JGK 1, average grain yield of 1782 kg/ha, and yield potential of 3056 kg/ha; mean maturity 150 days; 100-seed weight 36 g -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf
- Mean maturity of 150-152 days and irrigated management, per the DPD table -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Yield potential up to 3 t/ha and 1.8 t/ha average grain yield (10.4% above best check) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- AICRP 2021-22 report row for Pusa 3022 (BG 3022), with 2015 release, IARI, large-seeded kabuli, 150 days, NWPZ, irrigated -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Field trial, Zn fertilization: Pusa 547 (desi) out-yielded Pusa 3022 (kabuli) by 19.1% in grain yield -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43538-026-00920-w
- Breeder seed indent figures (51.6 and 20.0 q) appear in an IARI table with no year label -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed through desi x kabuli introgression -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Also described as desi x kabuli introgression, extra-large seeded kabuli -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- AICRP table gives a pedigree string of the form "(BG 1083) x (BG 1048 x SBD 377)"; the text is garbled in the extract, so treat it as unverified -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The input parentage "Not specified" is therefore partly resolved by this unverified string.
- No QTL or marker study specific to Pusa 3022 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed at IARI, Pusa, New Delhi (institution and station) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. Chellapilla Bharadwaj, Pusa Chickpea 20211 and Pusa JG 16 sources are different varieties and are discarded.
- A quiz page describes Pusa-3022 as a wilt-resistant kabuli chickpea developed by IARI; low-reliability source -- https://questions.collegedunia.com/exams/questions/match-list-i-with-list-ii-list-i-variety-a-pusa-30-6a75b01685c0aaf2e35b6e90

CONTACT DETAILS
- Official email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL for IARI or a Pusa 3022 breeder: No evidence found. The retrieved pages do not include any contact information. IARI is named only as "IARI, Pusa, New Delhi" (see Breeder line above).

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2026). Zinc fertilization effects on nodulation, enzyme activity, biofortification, and productivity in desi and Kabuli chickpea. Springer journal article -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43538-026-00920-w (DOI 10.1007/s43538-026-00920-w)
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Symbiotic nitrogen fixation for sustainable chickpea yield and prospects for genome editing in changing climatic situations. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1621191/full (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2025.1621191). Pusa 3022 is a check genotype here.
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Developing microbial seed coating for enhancing seed vigour and prolonging storability in chickpea. Seed Science and Technology (ScienceDirect) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0254629924004174 (pii S0254629924004174). Pusa 3022 is one of two varieties tested.
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2023). Annual report 2021-22. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- IARI (2014). IARI News, Vol. 30 No. 4, Oct-Dec 2014 (identification announcement). IARI -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specific to Pusa 3022 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing specific to Pusa 3022 was found. The one seed listing retrieved is for "Pusa Manav" (a different variety), so it is discarded.
- Breeder seed indent figures for Pusa 3022 are listed (see Agronomy and Trials line above) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Seednet listing: No evidence found (PUSA-30 search failed).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified for NWPZ: Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Delhi, per the DPD table -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- IARI's own note lists Punjab, Haryana, western Rajasthan, western UP and Delhi (Uttarakhand not listed) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Release year conflicts across sources: 2015 (DPD), 2016 (IARI best-practice note), 2017 (Krishi Jagran). The DPD table lists 2015 for the notification -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Krishi Jagran source dates release to 2017 -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/

drought.details: The variety is listed for timely sown, restricted-irrigation conditions in Central India, which indicates adaptation to limited water rather than a measured tolerance level. HD 2987 was used as a check in a drought-tolerance study of recombinant inbred lines grown under rainfed and irrigated conditions, so it was tested for drought, but the digest gives no tolerance rating or mechanism for HD 2987 itself.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No variety-specific rust, smut, or other disease resistance data for HD 2987 was found. The AICRP FLD report notes no disease or insect incidence in its demonstration plots, but this applies to all FLD plots and cannot be attributed to HD 2987 alone.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The AICRP FLD report notes no insect incidence in its demonstration plots, but this applies to all FLD plots and is not variety-specific evidence for HD 2987.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. The input average_yield field gives only the unit (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The 2016-17 AICRP social-sciences report lists HD 2987 among 11 improved or newly released varieties reporting yield gains, but gives no figure for HD 2987 alone.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed for timely sown, restricted-irrigation conditions in the peninsular zone and in Central India. The Central India guidance gives a sowing window of 20 October to 10 November for these conditions. A separate IARI page lists HD 2987 for Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Goa, and plains of Tamil Nadu.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Plant height and yield potential were not found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP FLD table (2019-20): HD 2987 at Indore is listed with a value of 49.00, but the column meaning is unclear and it cannot be read as a yield. (2) AICRP social-sciences progress report (2016-17): HD 2987 is among 11 improved or newly released varieties reporting yield gains, with no figure given for HD 2987. (3) AICRP FLD report (2019-20): no disease or insect incidence in demonstration plots, applying to all plots rather than HD 2987 alone. (4) Drought-tolerance study of recombinant inbred lines under rainfed and irrigated conditions: HD 2987 used as a check; no result for HD 2987 reported in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Bahar (HD 2987), wheat

Name check: The variety_name is "Pusa Bahar" and the seednet_variety_name is "PUSA BAHAR". The release-minute name appears as "Pusa Bahar (HD 2987)" in the Bihar notified-variety list, so the evidence below refers to "Pusa Bahar (HD 2987)" under both names. The Seednet crop field says "Indian Rapeseed and Mustard (Yellow Sarson)", but every source found describes HD 2987 as a wheat variety, so the Seednet crop entry looks wrong. "Pusa Bahar" is also a marigold name in one source, so results for that name need care.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION
- Notified in the Bihar list as Pusa Bahar (HD 2987), notification date 25/03/2011, S.O. 632(E). This is one year after the 2010 release date in the input record. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- ICAR's 2011-12 crop improvement report lists HD 2987 (Pusa Bahar) among wheat releases for timely sown rainfed and restricted-irrigation conditions in the peninsular zone. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pusa Bahar is listed for timely sown, restricted-irrigation conditions in Central India. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- HD 2987 was used as a check in a drought-tolerance study of recombinant inbred lines grown under rainfed and irrigated conditions. This shows it was tested for drought, but it does not show its own tolerance level. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Prakash-Nautiyal
- Heat, salinity, flood, and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No variety-specific rust, smut, or other disease resistance data for HD 2987 was found. The AICRP FLD report notes no disease or insect incidence in its demonstration plots, but this applies to all FLD plots, not to HD 2987 alone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343381935_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2019-20_Social_Sciences

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A ResearchGate AICRP FLD table lists HD 2987 at Indore with a value of 49.00, but the column meaning is unclear, so it cannot be read as a yield. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343381935_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2019-20_Social_Sciences
- An AICRP-related social-sciences progress report (2016-17) lists HD 2987 among 11 improved or newly released varieties and reports yield gains for them. The report gives no figure for HD 2987 alone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321482036_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2016-17_Social_Sciences
- Sowing window: The Central India guidance gives 20 October to 10 November for timely sown, restricted-irrigation conditions. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- Maturity, plant height, and yield potential for HD 2987: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No parentage, pedigree, marker, or QTL data for HD 2987 was found. The marker-assisted rust studies found concern HD2967 and HD3209, not HD 2987. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9103291/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi. -- https://www.magazines.cornous.com/downloadpdf/192
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
- Station: No evidence found that HD 2987 was bred at a regional station.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level contact: No breeder contact found. The IARI institute introduction page is the only official institute page located. -- https://www.iari.res.in/en/introduction.php?div_id=28
- Official email, phone, and postal address for the wheat division: No evidence found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Nautiyal, P. C. (year not stated in source). Agronomic and physiological characterization of RILs for drought tolerance in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.). Conference paper; authors and journal not confirmed in the source. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Prakash-Nautiyal
- AICRP on Wheat and Barley Progress Report 2016-17 (Social Sciences). Report; the authors are not listed in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321482036_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2016-17_Social_Sciences
- AICRP on Wheat and Barley Progress Report 2019-20 (Social Sciences). Report; the authors are not listed in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343381935_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2019-20_Social_Sciences
- Full KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed variety paper for HD 2987: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The Pusa Beej portal lists wheat seed from the Seed Production Unit at Pusa Institute, New Delhi, with pickup within ten days of booking. Listing of HD 2987 on this page was not confirmed. -- https://pusabeej.iari.res.in/varieties.php?crop_name=V2V5enlQSkV0anFPaTF6T3JkVTc5dz09
- Seednet, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listings for HD 2987: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Peninsular zone, timely sown rainfed and restricted irrigation. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Central India timely sown restricted-irrigation recommendation. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- A separate IARI page lists HD 2987 for Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Goa, and plains of Tamil Nadu. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- The recommended_states field in the input is "Not specified", so these sources fill that gap.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search note: four web_search queries were run. Nothing matched the release-minutes name "Pusa Bold-", the variety code "WRR2", or the 2022 release date. No Seednet page was returned for "PUSA BOLD". The evidence below refers to the long-standing Pusa Bold mustard variety, not to a confirmed 2022 DU release, so the input record conflicts with the sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pusa Bold is listed among Indian mustard varieties suggested for rainfed drought-prone conditions, alongside RH-819, RH-781, GM1 and Pusa Bahar -- https://www.gcirc.org/fileadmin/documents/Bulletins/B25/B25_06Rapeseed.pdf
- Pusa Bold is named among the Indian mustard varieties in a rainfed Aravali list -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258384157_Advances_in_Agronomic_Management_of_Indian_Mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czernj_Cosson_An_Overview
- Pusa Bold and Pusa Agrani are recommended for late-sown crops because they mature quickly when planted late -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6254
- No evidence found for salinity, flood, submergence or heat tolerance specific to Pusa Bold.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Pusa Bold in the retrieved sources. The searches returned only general variety lists.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pusa Bold is described as irrigated, with average yield of about 18 q/ha and maturity of 110-140 days, and suitable for northern states and high altitude -- https://www.krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/165-mustard.html
- Pusa Bold is grouped with varieties targeted at various agro-climatic zones, yielding above 40% oil content -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6254
- Pusa Bold was among the leading rapeseed-mustard varieties in seed production during 2002-2007 -- https://www.gcirc.org/fileadmin/documents/Bulletins/B25/B25_06Rapeseed.pdf
- No multi-location AICRP trial result specific to Pusa Bold was found; the official DAC oilseeds table retrieved did not show a Pusa Bold row -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx

GENETICS AND QTL
- A marker-study table lists Pusa Bold as IARI New Delhi, pedigree Varuna x BIC 1780, released 1984 -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable (this conflicts with the 2022 release date in the input)
- The same source lists JM-1 (ZARS Morena, 1999) with Pusa Bold as a parent (Pusa Bold x L 6) -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable
- No QTL or marker study specific to Pusa Bold was found beyond this pedigree reference.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The pedigree source attributes Pusa Bold to IARI, New Delhi, not to the Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants, University of Delhi as stated in the input -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable
- No breeder name for Pusa Bold was found in the retrieved sources.
- The Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants (University of Delhi) is named in coverage of DMH-11 GM mustard, led by Deepak Pental. This is a different transgenic line, not Pusa Bold -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DMH-11_Mustard

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder or institute email, phone or address for Pusa Bold was found in the searches.
- Institute-level contact page for the Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants (University of Delhi): not retrieved; no contact details found.
- Suggested check: the IARI division of genetics, or the Seednet/CSC notification record, for the official contact.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (2023 or later review cited as ARCC source). Title and author list not in search result. Agricultural Science Digest (ARCC) article on mustard variety performance. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6254
- Authors not retrieved (year not in snippet). Marker study with Pusa Bold pedigree table. PLOS ONE. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0272914 -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable
- Yadava et al. (2014). Cited within a ResearchGate page on Pusa Mustard 30; full title not retrieved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260917853_Mustard_Variety_Pusa_Mustard_30
- Thesis (KrishiKosh) and AICRP report entries: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer listing: Pusa Bold mustard seed offered at about Rs 140/kg in Sri Ganganagar. Not an official seed source -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mustard-seeds-pusa-bold-26278511397.html
- Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Input list (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh) is not confirmed by any retrieved source. The krishisewa page only mentions northern states and high altitude -- https://www.krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/165-mustard.html
- The official DAC oilseeds table lists recommended states for other varieties, but no Pusa Bold row was found -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx

Discrepancies to resolve before filing: (1) release year 2022 versus the 1984 IARI pedigree record; (2) institution DU CGMCP versus IARI; (3) "Pusa Bold-" and WRR2 do not appear in any source; (4) one ResearchGate source describes Pusa Bold as low erucic, which conflicts with the variety's usual description and should be checked against the CSC notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Mustard 25 (NPJ-112), Indian mustard (Brassica juncea)

Scope note: The search tool hit its limit after four queries, so a fifth check of the Oilseeds DAC table and the Global Agriculture page was blocked. Several headings are thin. Searches were run under "Pusa Mustard 25" and "PUSA MUSTARD-29".

NAME RECONCILIATION
- variety_name "Pusa Mustard 25" (NPJ-112) is matched by the DAC, Global Agriculture, ResearchGate and PMFME sources below.
- seednet_variety_name "PUSA MUSTARD-29" does not match this variety. Global Agriculture describes Pusa Mustard 29 as LET-36, a low erucic acid (single zero) variety with about 21.69 q/ha yield and 37.2% oil, suited to Delhi, Haryana, Jammu, Punjab and northern Rajasthan. That is a different variety. The Seednet record for "PUSA MUSTARD-29" should be checked before any data is merged. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-29-let-36/

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Shekhawat (2012) lists Pusa Mustard 25 (NPJ 112) among varieties described as tolerant in an agronomic review, but the snippet does not state which stress. Also listed in the same review's white rust resistance group. Treat as unverified. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2012/408284
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data specific to this variety was found. Evidence found for stress tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The Shekhawat (2012) review's white rust resistance list includes Pusa Mustard 25 in the snippet. Confirm the rust designation with the original source. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2012/408284
- No alternaria, downy mildew, aphid or other pest data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early maturing variety, developed through a modified bulk method from a cross KRT 5 x NP 200, with a toria pollen parent. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750581_Early_maturing_variety_Pusa_Mustard-25
- Global Agriculture (IARI listing) describes it as highly suitable for Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, plains of J&K and HP, and western UP, and suitable for multiple cropping between September and mid-December. This text is also on the Pusa Mustard 28 page, so attribution is uncertain. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-25-npj-112/
- Yield, maturity days and oil content: not confirmed for this variety in retrieved text. The DAC table likely holds them but its snippet was truncated. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
- Field trial results: No evidence found for Pusa Mustard 25 specifically. The Krishi Jagran item concerns Pusa mustard and lentil varieties at Gogamukh, Assam, and does not name Pusa Mustard 25 in the retrieved text. -- https://krishijagran.com/news/pusa-mustard-and-lentil-varieties-show-good-yield-in-a-field-experiments-at-icar-iari-assam/

GENETICS AND QTL
- An SSR-marker diversity study of Indian mustard varieties places Pusa Mustard 25 in a cluster with admixture from another subpopulation, so it may be a poor choice for recombination breeding within that set. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0272914
- QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder: Devendra Yadava, listed at Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI). Co-author Sujata Vasudev, also IARI. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750581_Early_maturing_variety_Pusa_Mustard-25
- Developing institution: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi (Global Agriculture, DAC listing). Station and division not confirmed. Institution field "Not explicitly stated" in the input is therefore resolved as IARI, though this is inferred from the IARI listing.
- Release year: not confirmed. The Global Agriculture page carries a "July 20, 2023" header, but the same header appears on other varieties, so it is not reliable for Pusa Mustard 25. Parentage: partly given as KRT 5 x NP 200 (see Agronomy). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-25-npj-112/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Named contacts: Devendra Yadava (IARI, breeder). No email, phone or postal address for him was found.
- Institute-level contact: No official IARI email, phone, postal address or contact page URL was found in retrieved results. Recommended: IARI main site, New Delhi, via https://www.iari.res.in (not retrieved; verify manually).
- Seednet portal: not reached; no contact data from it.

PUBLICATIONS
- Yadava, D.K.; Vasudev, S.; et al. (2010). Early maturing variety Pusa Mustard-25. Czech Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding 70(3):307-308. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750581_Early_maturing_variety_Pusa_Mustard-25 (DOI not retrieved)
- Shekhawat, N.S. et al. (2012). Advances in Agronomic Management of Indian Mustard (Brassica juncea (L.) Czernj. Cosson): An Overview. International Journal of Agronomy. DOI: 10.1155/2012/408284 -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2012/408284 (author list partial; "Shekhawat" from the citation string)
- Molecular characterization and genetic diversity analysis in Indian mustard (Brassica juncea L.) varieties using SSR markers (2022, PLOS ONE). DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0272914 -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0272914 (year and authors not confirmed from snippet)
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports and other peer-reviewed trials: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private listing: Sakshi Farms "Pusa 25 Black Mustard" seed on Flipkart. Unverified private seller. -- https://www.flipkart.com/sakshi-farms-pusa-25-black-mustard-seeds-for-seed-sowing-farming-agriculture-kheti-variety/p/itmdff0bbcba08ea
- Official channels (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales): No evidence found. Seednet check needed.
- Other "Pusa" mustard listings found on Amazon are for Pusa Mustard 28 and 32, not this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Recommended for cultivation in the DAC list of notified mustard varieties. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
- Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, plains of J&K, western UP, per the Global Agriculture page (see Agronomy caveat). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-25-npj-112/
- The input's "Jammu and Kashmir (plains)" and "Western Uttar Pradesh" match this list. The input's "Delhi" also matches.

drought.details: No evidence found in the searched sources for drought tolerance or its mechanisms in Pusa Mustard 26.

heat.details: Terminal heat tolerance is reported for Pusa Mustard 26 (NPJ-113) by a seed-company listing and by the IARI variety description, which credits PM-26 with terminal high-temperature tolerance. Both are descriptive claims without quantitative heat-stress data in the digest. A late-sowing study (rabi 2017-18 and 2018-19) included PM-26 but reports impaired biochemical stress mechanisms in Indian mustard generally, and PM-26 was not singled out. Level is rated medium because the tolerance claim is reported by two sources but is not supported by controlled stress data.

salinity.details: A third-party guide lists PM-26 as tolerant to salinity and high temperature at sowing. The digest states this is not confirmed by a primary source, so no level is assigned on the basis of that claim alone.

flood.details: No evidence found in the searched sources for flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence found for white rust, Alternaria, Sclerotinia or other disease resistance in Pusa Mustard 26.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance rating found. An aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) yield-loss study used PM 26 (short duration) as one of the test cultivars, but the snippet reports no resistance rating for it. No other pest resistance evidence found in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Official reference value: 16.00 q/ha under normal conditions (variety data). Multi-location trials over 4 years at 14 locations gave 16.04 q/ha, against 13.45 q/ha (national check) and 12.27 q/ha (zonal check), with higher oil content (secondary copy of the release summary). Conflict: the IARI variety page gives an average seed yield of 14.7 q/ha for PM-26 (NPJ-113). The two IARI-linked values (14.7 q/ha on the variety page and 16.04 q/ha in the release summary) are both recorded here and not reconciled. A third-party guide gives 1481-1895 kg/ha, which is not verified by a primary source.
agronomic_details.stability: The stability analysis reports PM-26 had above-average stability for seed yield per plant. Other cross-environment evidence is limited to the multi-location trials and the Tungabhadra and Assam trials summarised under field_trials.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adaptation ecology is recorded as multiple cropping systems. The release summary indicates 126 days to maturity under late-November sowing. The Tungabhadra command area trial was on paddy fallow land. The release recommendation covers the plains of Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi and western Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Conflicting values. 126 days (Bhawani Seeds listing; IARI-linked page; release summary under late-November sowing). 107 days (IARI variety page, which conflicts with the 126-day figure on the other IARI-linked page). 131.22 days (days to maturity column in the stability analysis table). The digest does not resolve these values.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Morphological characteristics and agronomic features are not specified in the variety data or the digest. The digest records 37.6% oil content (Bhawani Seeds listing) and higher oil content in the multi-location trials.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location yield trials, 4 years, 14 locations: 16.04 q/ha vs 13.45 (national check) and 12.27 q/ha (zonal check), with higher oil content and 126 days to maturity under late-November sowing (secondary copy of release summary, Scribd). (2) IARI variety page: average seed yield 14.7 q/ha, 107 days to maturity (conflicts with 126 days elsewhere). (3) Assam field trial at Dhirpai Chapori, sown late December 2022: 26-28% higher grain yield and about 10% higher straw yield than the local check. This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed paper. (4) IARI research farm, rabi 2020-21, under integrated management: 2,206 kg/ha seed yield and 877 kg/ha oil yield. (5) Tungabhadra command area (paddy fallow): 810 kg/ha seed yield, below PM-25. (6) Stability analysis: above-average stability for seed yield per plant. (7) Aphid yield-loss study (Lipaphis erysimi): PM 26 used as a test cultivar; no resistance rating reported. (8) Late-sowing study (rabi 2017-18, 2018-19): PM-26 included; not singled out in results.
