search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Tapeshwari (variety_name) / Tapeshwari. (seednet_variety_name), toria, TK 06-1

Name note: all four searches used "Tapeshwari." Sources spell it "Tapeshwari", "Tapeswari", "Tapeshvari" and "Tapeswari (LC)", and the seednet name with the trailing period did not match any source. Every finding below refers to this same variety unless a line says otherwise. Note the release date conflict: CSC minutes give 2014-02-14, the AICRP table lists 2014, and the CSAUA&T page gives a 2018 notification (S.O. 6318E).

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tapeswari (LC) is one of several toria genotypes listed as promising on the AAII ≤1.5 criterion in a moisture-stress trial, but the source does not state the tolerance mechanism for this variety specifically. GSH 1717, GSH 1699, GSH 6 (QC), Tapeswari (LC), BSH-1, Kranti (NC), RGN 73(LR), GSL 1 (ZC) were found promising since these recorded AAII ≤1.5. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
Heat: toria germplasm was screened for thermo-tolerance at early and terminal stages, but no Tapeshwari-specific heat result was found. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for Tapeshwari. The salinity study on B. rapa var. toria (BRSRT) is a different genotype. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322264501_Effect_of_salinity_on_Brassica_rapa_var_toria_BRSRT_under_selenium_defence_A_trial_to_assess_the_protective_role_of_selenium

DISEASE AND PEST
White rust (WR): In a multi-location screen of Brassica entries, the B. rapa toria and yellow sarson entries largely escaped WR infection. This is a group-level finding; Tapeshwari is not named individually. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
Other diseases and pests (Alternaria, insects, lodging): No evidence found for Tapeshwari.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and sowing: Tapeshwari is described as suited to early sowing (15-20 Sept) with extra-early maturity of 88-90 days, medium brown grain, and suitability for irrigated conditions in all ecological zones. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
Yield vs check: At Kanpur, toria strains yielded up to 17.18% above the check Tapeshwari (56 strains tested at Kanpur, Chatha, Ludhiana and Dholi). -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/PC-REPORT-2020-DRMR.pdf
Yield vs check (2025 round): The yield superiority in toria station trial was up to 22.07 over the check (Tapeshwari) at Pantnagar. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2025/AICRP-Proceeding-2025.pdf
Absolute yield (kg/ha) for Tapeshwari: No evidence found. The Kanpur PYT table lists a 1350 kg/ha benchmark next to Tapeshwari, but the layout does not show which entry the figure belongs to. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Seed production: 258.64 q breeder seed was produced against an indent of 76.02 q, but less Tapeshwari seed was produced than indented. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
Agronomy-specific trials for Tapeshwari (sowing date, N, spacing): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: Tapeshwari is used as a parent in crosses including Tapeswari x Sushree, Parbati x Tapeswari and Bhawani x Tapeswari. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Population improvement: Tapeshwari is listed among toria parents used in population improvement and in RIL/composite programmes. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
QTL, marker or genomic studies: No evidence found for Tapeshwari.
Parentage as released: Not specified (no source gives the original cross).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSAUA&T), Kanpur, UP. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
Notification: Tapeshwari (T.K. 06-1) was notified (S.O. 6318E) by the central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards at its meeting on 26 December 2018 in New Delhi. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
Breeder names: The CSAUA&T Oil Seeds Section page lists "Mahak Singh, Ranjeet, R.K. Dixit and S.B.L. Srivastav" next to the Tapeshwari entry. The layout does not label them explicitly as breeders, so treat this as unconfirmed. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
Station: Kanpur (CSAUA&T campus), per the AICRP trial centre list. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/PC-REPORT-2020-DRMR.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder contact: No evidence found.
Institute contact: No email, phone or postal address for CSAUA&T was found in the results. The only institute URL found is https://www.csauk.ac.in (Wikipedia gives the same website and Kanpur as location). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandra_Shekhar_Azad_University_of_Agriculture_and_Technology
Project Coordinator (DRMR, AICRP-RM) contact: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
AICRP on Rapeseed & Mustard (2020). Project Coordinator's Report 2019-20, Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR). Authors not stated. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Basundhara (CSC name) / VASUNDHARA (Seednet name), rice, AAU Jorhat**

**Search note:** Four web searches were run, one per topic. None returned a Seednet page, so no Seednet record for VASUNDHARA was found. The Seednet entry is listed under yellow sarson (rapeseed/mustard), which is a different crop. Every rice finding below refers to "Basundhara" as a rice variety. Findings about Basundhara Seeds (Kolkata), a seed company with a similar name, were discarded.

**Conflicts in the record:**
- Release year: the user input says 2014-10-20. Retrieved sources say 1996 (Basundhara, IET 9711/IET 11161, release 1996, 130 days, transplanted sali in multiple cropping areas) and 1999 (the AAU compilation, which pairs Satyaranjan and Basundhara under one release year).
- Parentage: the user input says RH 839 x RH 30. The AAU compilation gives IET 9711 X IET 11161 (Basundhara). The user's parentage was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- The "Hundred years of rice research in Assam" table describes Basundhara as photoperiod insensitive, multiple resistant, fine grained, suitable for sali in areas where sali is followed by rabi crops -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- The same source lists Basundhara among varieties that perform well under low land situations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- Flood and submergence tolerance: the AAU compilation has a flood-tolerance block that may refer to Basundhara, but the snippet does not clearly attach it to this variety, so it is not counted as evidence -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Drought tolerance: No evidence found for Basundhara. The AAU stress-tolerant page covers other varieties only -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- Pest and disease: multiple resistant is the only general statement retrieved, with no named pathogens or resistance genes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- A Basundhara-specific disease-management table in the same source recommends it for double-cropped areas, but it does not name a specific disease -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- The Assam kharif package of practices (AAU and Department of Agriculture, Assam, 2015) lists Basundhara in a duration/yield table. The column headers are not legible in the retrieved text, so the figures cannot be assigned with confidence -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
- Season and land: the AAU compilation places Basundhara in the sali group for double-cropped areas, where sali rice is followed by rabi crops -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Yield: No Basundhara-specific yield figure was confirmed. The yield values in the retrieved compilation sit in blocks for other varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: IET 9711 X IET 11161 (Basundhara) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University (conflicts with the user's RH 839 x RH 30)
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found for Basundhara. Searches for Basundhara QTL and marker studies returned only Basmati and Joha work, which was discarded.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Institution: AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar, Jorhat, which is the AAU rice station that compiled the variety list -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Named scientists: The compilation is authored by Dr. Safiqul Hussain, Ms. Pompi Dutta and Chetia, S. K. (2023) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University. No source states that any of them bred Basundhara, so this is not attributed as a breeder finding.
- Lead breeder for Basundhara: No evidence found.

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- AAU (institute-level): Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat, PIN 785013, Assam; phone 0376-2340001; email webadmin@aau.ac.in -- https://www.rkbassam.aau.ac.in/contact-us and https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties
- Rice research station contact (RCSKB): 5th Floor, Nayantara Building, Six Mile, Guwahati-22, Assam; email rkbassam2021@gmail.com -- https://www.rkbassam.aau.ac.in/contact-us
- Titabar station address: AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar-785630, Jorhat, Assam -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Named breeder contact: No evidence found.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Hussain, S.; Dutta, P.; Chetia, S. K. (2023). Rice varieties developed by Assam Agricultural University. AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar; SM Press, Jorhat; ISBN 978-81-962645-1-2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Hundred years of rice research in Assam. Journal/report not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis specific to Basundhara was found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No evidence found. The only "Basundhara Seeds" listing is a Kolkata wholesale seller of unspecified rice seed, not linked to this variety -- https://m.indiamart.com/basundhara-seeds
- AAU seed sources, NSC, state seed corporation, and KVK listings for Basundhara were not retrieved. Seed-source details on the AAU stress page apply to other varieties.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- Assam: Basundhara appears in the Assam kharif (sali) package of practices. The "recommended states" field in the user record is blank -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
- Basundhara also appears in the AAU list of sali rice varieties for multiple-cropping areas, but no other state recommendation was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VAMSADHARA / VASUNDHARA

Name check: "VAMSADHARA" (CSC minutes name) and "VASUNDHARA" (Seednet name) refer to different entries in the evidence. Under each heading I state which name the evidence refers to.

RECORD CONFLICTS (read first)
- The variety_code RGL 11414 and the name VAMSADHARA appear together in a rice notification list, not in a mustard or yellow sarson context. The record lists crop as rice but seednet_crop_name as yellow sarson, and the institution as CCS HAU Oilseeds Section. The "RH" prefix in the parentage matches Hisar mustard naming, but I found no source linking RGL 11414 to CCS HAU. Treat the institution and parentage fields as unverified.
- No source I found ties VASUNDHARA to yellow sarson. The only VASUNDHARA variety entry in the PPV&FRA compendium is a maize hybrid, Vasundhara (DH-101). Vasundhara Agro is a commercial spice and grain trader with no link to breeding.

STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST
- VAMSADHARA (rice): No evidence found for stress or disease traits. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No evidence found. The only stress information located was general rapeseed-mustard recommendations by stress type, which do not name this variety. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/75542

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- VAMSADHARA (rice): No evidence found for yield, maturity or trial results.
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No evidence found. A 2019-20 AICRP report mentions yellow sarson strain trials at Kanpur and Dholi, with yield superiority up to 16.66% over the check Pitambari, but it does not name Vasundhara. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
- An HAU yellow sarson entry, YSH 0401 (2009), appears in an AICRP-related table. It is a different variety from Vasundhara. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- VAMSADHARA: No evidence found for markers or QTL.
- VASUNDHARA: No evidence found. Related context only (not about this variety): a fine-mapping study of a seed coat colour QTL in Brassica rapa var. Yellow Sarson. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6361427/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- VAMSADHARA (rice): The 2011 notification list records it as RGL 11414, notified under S.O. 283(E) dated 07.02.2011, for AP. No breeder or institution is named. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No breeder name found. The CCS HAU Oilseeds Section is confirmed only as a university; no yellow sarson release by that section was found under this name. -- https://hau.ac.in/
- Note: the ICAR Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (Bharatpur) says it has released one yellow sarson variety, NRCYS 05-02, which is not Vasundhara. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/rm_varieties.php

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar (no breeder contact found; no email or phone found for the Oilseeds Section): website https://hau.ac.in/ ; HAU is located at Hisar, Haryana. -- https://hau.ac.in/
- ICAR-Indian Institute of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (formerly DRMR), postal address: Sewar, Bharatpur 321303 (Rajasthan), India. No email or phone was in the retrieved text. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/rm_varieties.php
- Breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- VAMSADHARA: No evidence found.
- VASUNDHARA: No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was retrieved. KrishiKosh was not searched directly; this search covered only the general web.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- VAMSADHARA: No evidence found for seed sellers. The notified status is for AP, so check AP seed channels (not searched).
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No evidence found for variety seed. HAU's RDS Seed Farm sales page lists Kharif crops (guar, moong, dhaincha) and Rabi crops (raya, barley, gram, wheat, oats), with no yellow sarson. Sales counters are at Gate No. 3 (Balsamand Road) and ATIC at Gate No. 4 (Rajgarh Road). -- https://hau.ac.in/page/seed-sale-information
- Commercial listing, grain only, not verified seed of this variety: National Seeds Corporation Limited, Hisar (C/o CSF Farm, Sirsa Road) appears in an IndiaMART yellow mustard seed listing. -- https://dir.indiamart.com/hisar/yellow-mustard-seed.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- VAMSADHARA: Andhra Pradesh (AP), per the 2011 notification list. This contradicts the record field "Not specified." -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- VASUNDHARA: No evidence found.

basic_info.institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCSHAU), Hisar, Haryana

drought.details: Resistant to drought stress.

heat.details: Tolerant to terminal heat stress. Used as a National Check in studies evaluating heat tolerance in Indian mustard, suggesting inherent heat tolerance.

salinity.details: Information on salinity tolerance for YSH 0401 is not specified in the provided search results.

flood.details: General information about rapeseed/mustard not tolerating waterlogging was found, but specific tolerance for YSH 0401 is not specified.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to all rusts and resistant to yellow mosaic virus. Its use as a check variety in trials against Alternaria blight does not explicitly state its resistance level to this specific disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to aphids and jassids. It has also been screened against mustard aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) as a National Check.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield as a National Check (NC) is 1247 kg/ha. It possesses high oil content, with a margin of 2.66% against check varieties, and specific reports mention 32% oil content.
agronomic_details.stability: Demonstrated stability through its use as a National Check in multi-location trials conducted over several years (e.g., Rabi 2010-11 to 2015-16).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for Rabi Timely Sown conditions and for utera/paira cropping systems. Recommended for Uttar Pradesh (Eastern part), West Bengal, Bihar, and Haryana.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Compact, small seed size, and green plant color.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensively used as a National Check (NC) in multi-location trials for evaluation of new rapeseed-mustard germplasm and varieties, including for Alternaria blight and heat tolerance, from at least 2010-11 to 2015-16.

heat.details: Round gourd (tinda) is known as a warm season crop. There is a general demand for stress tolerance against heat in cucurbit crops. However, specific heat tolerance for Punjab Tinda-1 is not mentioned.

salinity.details: General round gourd (tinda) is indicated to be salt-tolerant, growing well in well-drained soils with a pH of 5.5-7.0. Another variety, Hisar Tinda (HT 10), is explicitly tolerant to salt. Specific salinity tolerance for Punjab Tinda-1 is not available.

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance for Punjab Tinda-1 is not specified. However, for other tinda varieties, Hisar Tinda (HT 10) is reported to be resistant to all rusts. General strategies for managing viral diseases in round gourd include mulching, and there is a recognized need to grow resistant varieties in cucurbits.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance is mentioned for Punjab Tinda-1. Melon fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) is a major pest of cucurbitaceous vegetables.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GPUF 3 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "GPUF 3". The evidence found uses "GPUF 3" and, in one place, "GPUF-3". I did not reach a Seednet portal page, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found on a formal drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence rating for GPUF 3. One study on PEG-induced seedling growth of dry and hydroprimed GPUF-3 seed was located, but its page title is about foxtail millet supplementation in diabetics, so the link between that page and the seedling study is unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287753024_Effect_of_foxtail_millet_setaria_italica_supplementation_on_serum_glucose_serum_lipids_and_glycosylated_hemoglobin_in_type_2_diabetics

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found on disease or pest resistance for GPUF 3.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Station trials averaged 29.89 q/ha, multilocation trials 26.33 q/ha, and farm trials 15.16 q/ha, with a mean of 23.79 q/ha across all trials, about 19.12% above check SiA 3156. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
All-India Coordinated trials yielded 2753 kg/ha across locations, ranking 11th. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
Farm trials in Zone 5 and Zone 6 were run during Kharif 2020. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
Maturity is 85-90 days. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Molecular-profile-of-proposed-variety-GPUF-3-and-check-variety-SiA-3156_fig1_387227757
Fodder quality (crude fibre, protein, fat) was reported as higher than the check SiA 3156. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica

GENETICS AND QTL
GPUF 3 was developed by pure-line selection from germplasm IC 479864, so the parentage field "Not specified" can be filled with this origin. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Molecular-profile-of-proposed-variety-GPUF-3-and-check-variety-SiA-3156_fig1_387227757
A molecular profile of GPUF 3 versus SiA 3156 is shown in the paper, but no QTL or marker results were extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing unit: Project Coordinating Unit, ICAR-AICRP on Small Millets, University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), GKVK, Bengaluru. Target zones are 5 and 6 of Karnataka. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Molecular-profile-of-proposed-variety-GPUF-3-and-check-variety-SiA-3156_fig1_387227757
Lead author listed in citing literature: T. E. Nagaraja, with C. Nandini, S. Bhat, K. B. Palanna, P. C. Ganiger, and T. S. Sukanya et al. -- https://link.springer.com/rwe/10.1007/978-3-031-91605-2_1-1
No breeder profile page was found. The fourth search for breeder and institution details returned no results.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone, or personal contact was found in any result. The fourth search returned nothing, so no institute-level contact page URL was found either. Recommended next step: check the UAS GKVK, Bengaluru website and the ICAR-AICRP Small Millets site for a contact page.

PUBLICATIONS
Nagaraja, T. E., Nandini, C., Bhat, S., Palanna, K. B., Ganiger, P. C., Sukanya, T. S., et al. (2022). GPUF 3: A new high yielding foxtail millet variety (Setaria italica). Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, 13, 810-819. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2022.1303.103
GPUF 3: A new high yielding foxtail millet variety (Sateria italica). Full-text record dated Dec 2025 on ResearchGate. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
Study on PEG effects on seedling growth of dry and hydroprimed GPUF-3 seed. Authors and year not verified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287753024_Effect_of_foxtail_millet_setaria_italica_supplementation_on_serum_glucose_serum_lipids_and_glycosylated_hemoglobin_in_type_2_diabetics
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report, or QTL paper was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, UAS seed sales, or dealer listing was located in the search results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka, specifically zone 5 and zone 6 dry areas. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica

drought.details: No measured drought score for SiA 3085 was found. Indirect evidence only: (1) a general foxtail millet statement describes short-duration, drought-tolerant types, but this is not variety-specific; (2) AMMI analysis showed narrow adaptation to Anantapur, a scarce-rainfall rainfed site, which suggests drought-prone suitability but is not a measured drought tolerance result. The CSC record lists the variety as suitable for rainfed and irrigated kharif and summer seasons and for early sowing conditions, but does not state drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance to blast and downy mildew. The NIMR/IIMR salient features record describes the variety as resistant to blast and downy mildew in the 80-85 day, 20-30 q/ha class. A second source lists it as high yielding and resistant to blast and downy mildew, 75-82 days, 20-30 q/ha, for 'All states'. No quantitative disease scores were reported. CSC disease_reaction field: Not Specified.

pest_resistance.summary: Insect pest resistance: Not found in searched sources. CSC pest_reaction field: Not Specified.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 3000.00 to 3200.00 Kg/Ha. Digest sources give 20-30 q/ha (2000-3000 kg/ha) for the 75-82 day class and yield potential up to 2500 kg/ha for short-duration types SiA 3085/3088/3156. These figures differ from the CSC record and are flagged as a discrepancy. Rainfed Andhra Pradesh: highest grain yield of 1141 kg/ha among tested entries (cited from a secondary review; the test conditions and entry set are not specified).
agronomic_details.stability: AMMI analysis (rainfed Andhra Pradesh) showed narrow adaptation, with a site-specific fit to Anantapur. No multi-environment stability statistics for SiA 3085 were found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand under rainfed/irrigated kharif and summer seasons. Suitable for early sowing conditions. Sowing-date trial in Telangana (Northern zone) found best performance with sowing up to late August. Vikaspedia and the ICAR-IIMR brochure also list Telangana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh; these are not part of the CSC recommended state list.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC agronomic features: resistant to lodging; non-shattering; good response to fertilizer; seed rate 5-6 kg/ha for direct seeding. Morphological characteristics: Not specified. agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif 2014, S.V. Agricultural College Farm, Tirupati (sandy loam, Southern Zone of Andhra Pradesh): SiA 3085 gave the highest growth, yield attributes and yield among four varieties; 50 kg N/ha was profitable. (2) Sowing-date trial, Telangana (Northern zone): best performance with sowing up to late August. (3) Rainfed Andhra Pradesh: highest grain yield of 1141 kg/ha among tested entries (secondary review citation). (4) AMMI analysis of rainfed Andhra Pradesh genotypes: narrow adaptation to Anantapur. (5) Frontline demonstrations (FLDs) in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, CAU Pasighat) and Tripura (SARS): SiA-3085 demonstrated; no yield values in the digest. (6) Included as a released check in a foxtail core collection of 223 accessions (genetic diversity context, not a yield trial).

drought.details: No measured drought score for SiA 3085 was found. Indirect evidence only: (1) a general foxtail millet statement describes short-duration, drought-tolerant types, but this is not variety-specific; (2) AMMI analysis showed narrow adaptation to Anantapur, a scarce-rainfall rainfed site, which suggests drought-prone suitability but is not a measured drought tolerance result. The CSC record lists the variety as suitable for rainfed and irrigated kharif and summer seasons and for early sowing conditions, but does not state drought tolerance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SiA 3085 (Italian/foxtail millet)

Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "SiA 3085", so all evidence below refers to that name. Seednet variety code A0205027 and Seednet crop name "ITALIAN MILLET (THENAI/NAVANE/FOX TAIL MILLET/KANG" were not confirmed by any search result. Searches run: 4 (variety, breeder, research, seed availability). The seed-availability search returned mostly unrelated results.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released as a pure line from RARS Nandyal, 2011, from SiA 2644; described as resistant to blast and downy mildew in the 80-85 day, 20-30 q/ha class -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/foxtail_millet.pdf
- Listed as high yielding and resistant to blast and downy mildew, 75-82 days, 20-30 q/ha, "All states" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Described as short-duration and drought tolerant (general foxtail millet statement, not variety-specific) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- AMMI analysis showed narrow adaptation to Anantapur (scarce-rainfall rainfed site), suggesting drought-prone suitability but not a measured drought score -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5950
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast and downy mildew resistance as above -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/foxtail_millet.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Kharif 2014, S.V. Agricultural College Farm, Tirupati (sandy loam, Southern Zone of AP): SiA 3085 gave highest growth, yield attributes and yield among four varieties; 50 kg N/ha was profitable -- https://sasapjas.org/response-of-foxtail-millet-setaria-italica-l-varieties-to-different-levels-of-nitrogen/

drought.details: Seedling-stage drought tolerance is described as genotypic variation, and SiA-3156 is cited as a tolerant reference line. disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to blast and downy mildew, as stated in an on-farm trial table alongside a yield range. Caveat: the source paper is titled around SiA 3223 (Renadu), so attribution of this tolerance rating to SiA 3156 should be verified against the original table before use.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Insect pest resistance: no evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed Andhra Pradesh trials reported higher grain yield with SiA 3156 among several varieties (no value given). Varietal table: 2000-2500 kg/ha. Rabi-season Andhra Pradesh yield of about 1290 kg/ha (Ramyasri et al., as cited in a review). Karnataka station and farm trials 2017-2020: mean 25.73 q/ha for SiA 3156 (GPUF 3 was 29.89 q/ha in the same trials). Andhra Pradesh on-farm comparison: about 2032-2070 kg/ha, below SiA 3223. Input record: 5-6 kg/ha seed rate for direct seeding.
agronomic_details.stability: Karnataka station and farm trials across 2017-2020 provide multi-environment data, but no stability analysis was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif and summer seasons; suitable for early sowing conditions; rainfed Andhra Pradesh trials; Karnataka trials. Digest notes no separate agro-climatic zones. Recommended states are covered in variety_profile.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Resistant to lodging; non-shattering; good response to fertilizer (input record). Plant height 93.7 cm, taller than SiA 3088 (79.9 cm). Tiller count 2.4-4.6 (compared against GPUF 3 in the source). Morphological characteristics: Na in input record.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Rainfed Andhra Pradesh trials: higher grain yield than several other varieties (no numeric value). (2) Varietal table: maturity 85-90 days, yield 2000-2500 kg/ha. (3) Rabi-season Andhra Pradesh: about 1290 kg/ha (as cited in a review). (4) Karnataka station and farm trials 2017-2020 against GPUF 3: SiA 3156 mean 25.73 q/ha versus 29.89 q/ha for GPUF 3. (5) Andhra Pradesh on-farm trial against SiA 3223: SiA 3156 about 2032-2070 kg/ha, below SiA 3223. (6) Plant height and tiller comparisons as listed above. The digest's protein value (13.09 g%, AICRP-SM comparison) was excluded because it is not explicitly attributed to SiA 3156.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SiA 3156 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical; crop is foxtail/Italian millet, Setaria italica). Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). No seednet.gov.in page was returned.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to blast and downy mildew, listed in an on-farm trial table alongside its yield range -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/On-farm-Testing-of-Foxtail-Millet-Variety-SiA-3223-(Renadu)-in-Semi-arid-Regions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-M-Jayalakshmi-28.pdf
- Relatively drought-tolerant at seedling stage under PEG stress; seedling length falls by about 50% at roughly -6 bars PEG (drought screening of foxtail millet cultivars) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372105159_Evaluation_of_drought_resistance_and_index_screening_of_foxtail_millet_cultivars
- Seedling-stage drought tolerance is described as genotypic variation and SiA-3156 is cited as a tolerant reference line -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336418136_Foxtail_Millet_Setaria_italica_L_Potential_of_Smaller_Millet_for_Future_Breeding
- Heat: no direct heat-tolerance finding. A sowing-date study used it as a check to expose the crop to a temperature range, but did not report a heat-tolerance result -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331401436_Response_of_Growth_Yield_and_Quality_Parameters_of_Foxtail_Millet_Genotypes_to_Different_Planting_Density
- Flood, submergence, salinity: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant to blast and downy mildew (see Stress Tolerance source) -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/On-farm-Testing-of-Foxtail-Millet-Variety-SiA-3223-(Renadu)-in-Semi-arid-Regions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-M-Jayalakshmi-28.pdf
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed Andhra Pradesh trials reported higher grain yield with SiA 3156 among several varieties -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2
- Maturity 85-90 days and yield 2000-2500 kg/ha in a varietal table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Rabi-season yield of about 1290 kg/ha in Andhra Pradesh (Ramyasri et al., as cited in review) -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2
- Plant height 93.7 cm, taller than SiA 3088 (79.9 cm); tiller count 2.4-4.6 versus GPUF 3 -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336418136_Foxtail_Millet_Setaria_italica_L_Potential_of_Smaller_Millet_for_Future_Breeding
- Karnataka station and farm trials (2017-2020) against GPUF 3: SiA 3156 mean grain yield 25.73 q/ha, versus 29.89 q/ha for GPUF 3 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
- Andhra Pradesh on-farm comparison with SiA 3223: SiA 3156 yielded about 2032-2070 kg/ha, below SiA 3223 -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/On-farm-Testing-of-Foxtail-Millet-Variety-SiA-3223-(Renadu)-in-Semi-arid-Regions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-M-Jayalakshmi-28.pdf
- Nutrition: protein about 13.09 g% in an AICRP-SM comparison -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/small-millets

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13) is described as photo-sensitive and suited to rainfed, medium and high land, with no stress-tolerance data given. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en (Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13). Photo-sensitive, fibre yield 32.2 q/ha, suitable for rainfed, medium and high land, released for WB.)
- Name: Bidhan Pat 13 (variety_name). Seednet name BIDHAN PAT-3 (D-110) is a separate entry. The Pat-3 line below refers to Bidhan Pat-3, not Bidhan Pat 13.
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): flood-prone adaptation and tolerance to waterlogging/submergence. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546 (Bidhan Pat-3 Jute varieties tolerant to water logging / submergence is listed among tolerant varieties; the same deck notes Pat-3 is suitable for flood-prone areas.)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13) disease or pest resistance. Searches returned only the BCKV variety table, which gives no resistance data.
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): the slide deck lists it among varieties tolerant to waterlogging and submergence, not to a named disease or pest. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Bidhan Pat 13: fibre yield 32.2 q/ha recorded in the BCKV variety table. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): fibre yield 25-27 q/ha, photo-sensitive. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): matures about 110 days after sowing, with sowing possible from 1 March to 1 July. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- Bidhan Pat-3 seed-crop trial (seednet-name evidence only): seed yield was maximised under rainfed conditions in the red and laterite zone with sowing in late June to mid-July plus topping. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319469619_Jute_seed_production_as_influenced_by_dates_of_sowing_and_topping_in_red_and_laterite_zone_of_West_Bengal
- No evidence found for multi-location trial results of Bidhan Pat 13.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage D-154 and D-18 was supplied in the task input only. No search result confirmed it for Bidhan Pat 13.
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): pedigree is a variety-by-mutant cross. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290909716_Jute_Biology_Diversity_Cultivation_Pest_Control_Fiber_Production_and_Genetics
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies of Bidhan Pat 13.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13): applicant is BCKV, and the release was through SVRC under the AINP on Jute and Allied Fibres. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- No breeder name was found for Bidhan Pat 13. Developing institution: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV), Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): registered as a public variety under PPV&FR, with the applicant given as ICAR-CRIJAF with BCKV. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Name discrepancy: the Pat-3 (D-110) evidence refers to a white jute (C. capsularis) variety registered in 2012, not to Bidhan Pat 13, which is a tossa-type variety released in 2022.
- Breeder names in the search results (for example Sanjoy Shil, JRC 9057) refer to another variety and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, PIN 741252. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf
- Institute website: www.bckv.edu.in. -- https://wbjeeb.in/assets/ALPG/SU/BCKV.pdf
- No breeder email or phone was found for Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13).
- The only BCKV email found (pkdhara9@yahoo.in, admission in-charge) is an admissions contact, not a research contact, so it is excluded.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for a peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh entry naming Bidhan Pat 13 or BCCO-13.
- Authors not stated in the result (year not stated). Jute seed production as influenced by dates of sowing and topping in red and laterite zone of West Bengal (Bidhan Pat-3 seednet-name evidence only). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319469619_Jute_seed_production_as_influenced_by_dates_of_sowing_and_topping_in_red_and_laterite_zone_of_West_Bengal
- Authors not stated in the result (year not stated). Descriptors for jute (Corchorus olitorius L.) (lists Bidhan Pat-3 among capsularis varieties characterised; not specific to Bidhan Pat 13). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/305624674_Descriptors_for_jute_Corchorus_olitorius_L

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13) seed from NSC, the West Bengal state seed agency, KVKs, BCKV seed sales or private dealers. The seed-production centres listed by BCKV cover paddy, mustard and pulses, not jute. -- https://bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/SSR-University_bckv.pdf
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): no seed-source listing was found.
- The search returned only RuneScape game items and Bangladeshi jute seed reviews, which are unrelated.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en (released for WB)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for JROB-2 (and the "JROB-2 jute variety" query) returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for this variety. Results were about other jute genotypes or unrelated products.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page tied JROB-2 to disease or pest resistance. The Bt jute, Macrophomina, and JRO-524 pages are about other lines, so I excluded them.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
JROB-2 was grown in a completely randomized block design with 3 replications at the experimental farm of ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore, following the recommended package of practices (Satya et al., 2022) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0960852422016510
No yield data for JROB-2 were found in the search results. The ICAR-CRIJAF research-station page covers breeder seed and nucleus seed production but names no JROB-2 yield -- https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/SideLinks/aboutCrijaf/ResearchStations.php

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker, or parentage study for JROB-2 was returned. The 2025 Frontiers paper on intron-length polymorphism markers and diallel crosses names JROBA 3 and JBO 1, not JROB-2, so I excluded it -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11896985/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (CRIJAF), Barrackpore, Kolkata, West Bengal. The ICAR institute profile lists JROB-2 among the tossa jute varieties developed, released, and notified by CRIJAF -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
Lead breeder name for JROB-2: No evidence found. No page named a breeder or scientist for this variety.
Institute-level contact: Dr. Gouranga Kar is named as Director of ICAR-CRIJAF in the ICAR profile -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
JROB-2 is cited alongside the CRIJAF-led bioethanol work, which describes the variety as a jute line used in lignocellulose research -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286187404_Bast_and_leaf_fibre_crops_Kenaf_hemp_jute_agave_etc

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: ICAR-CRIJAF. Postal address as given in the ICAR profile: ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore, Kolkata-700121 (W.B) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
Postal code discrepancy: a Springer chapter gives Barrackpore, Kolkata 700120 -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_4
Location wording: the institute homepage says "Located at Nilganj, Barrackpore" -- http://crijaf.res.in/
Director: Dr. Gouranga Kar -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
Institute websites: http://crijaf.res.in/ and https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/
Official email and phone: No evidence found in any returned page. The institute homepage did not show them in the returned text, and no institute contact-page URL was confirmed.
Breeder email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Sharma, L., Ghosh, S., Roy, S. et al. (2019). JROB-2 shows high potential for production of bioethanol and other lignocellulose derived byproducts. Jaf News 17(1):12 -- cited in https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_10 (the article itself was not retrieved)
Authors not stated in the returned snippet (year not verified, possibly 2022). Optimization of alkali pretreatment and enzymatic saccharification of jute (Corchorus olitorius L.) biomass using response surface methodology. Journal not stated in snippet (ScienceDirect, Bioresource Technology family) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0960852422016510
Satya, P. et al. (2022). Cited in the ScienceDirect paper for the JROB-2 package of practices. Full reference not retrieved.
No peer-reviewed paper that is primarily on JROB-2 agronomy, stress, or breeding was found. No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP/ICAR annual report entry was returned for JROB-2.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The fourth search for JROB-2 jute seed returned only RuneScape and Final Fantasy game pages, which I discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, seednet.gov.in, or dealer listing for JROB-2 was returned.
Note: CRIJAF's Central Seed Research Station at Bud Bud, Burdwan, produces breeder seed of notified jute varieties, which is an institutional source but does not confirm JROB-2 stock -- https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/SideLinks/aboutCrijaf/ResearchStations.php

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found in the search results. The states listed in the release record (West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, Assam, parts of Uttar Pradesh and Tripura) could not be checked against any returned page. The CRIJAF profile confirms the institute's varieties cover jute areas in six states but does not list JROB-2's states -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf

NAME CHECK
variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "JROB-2", so no separate Seednet search was needed. The evidence refers to JROB-2 as a tossa (Corchorus olitorius) jute line. The release year 2020 and variety code A0502047 were not confirmed by any returned page.

disease_resistance.summary: No resistance identified. In a 2023 coastal West Bengal trial of seven olitorius varieties, JROM 1 showed the highest anthracnose disease severity (score 1.37) among the seven varieties tested, indicating susceptibility under those conditions. For stem rot, the same trial reports the highest incidence in NJ 7005, followed by JROM 1 and JRO 524, indicating JROM 1 was among the more affected entries. Both are single-trial observations and do not establish a resistance rating.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for JROM-1. No evidence for resistance to yellow mite, semi-looper or Bihar hairy caterpillar. The AICRP page describes resistance traits for a different green-stem variety, which were not attributed to JROM-1.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. The AICRP variety table lists 'JROM 1 (Pradip)' with a value of 37-40 in the same row, but the snippet gives no unit and no clear label, so it is not interpreted as yield. The record's average_yield field is given as Kg/Ha without a value.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended sowing window of mid-March to end-April (record states mid-March to last week of April). No agro-climatic zone details specific to JROM-1 were found beyond the Tossa jute growing belt of India.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources for JROM-1. Pod traits (green, cylindrical, non-shattering) appear only in general Tossa jute text and were not attributed to this variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 2023 pre-kharif coastal West Bengal trial, seven olitorius varieties including JROM 1: JBO 1 led on growth and yield components; JROM 1 was among the mid-ranking varieties. JROM 1 had the highest anthracnose severity (1.37) and was second for stem rot incidence after NJ 7005. (2) Diallel hybridization study of 90 hybrids using JROM 1 as a parent: JROM 1 had significant positive general combining ability (GCA) for fibre weight per plant and significant negative GCA for stick weight. (3) Hybridization study (PMC version): the hybrid JROM 1 x JRO 524 showed high positive heterosis for basal diameter, and JRO 524 x JROM 1 measured 24.39 mm.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for JROM-1. A jute genome study used JRO-524 (not JROM-1) to build a genetic map with 382 markers; this is background only and is not attributed to JROM-1.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to JROM-1 (Pradip). The results named only the wider tossa jute crop. -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/TossaJute.aspx
Trial-level susceptibility: in a 2023 coastal West Bengal trial, JROM 1 showed the highest anthracnose disease severity among the seven varieties tested (score 1.37). -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1755055411.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Anthracnose: JROM 1 had the highest anthracnose severity (1.37) in the 2023 coastal West Bengal trial. -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1755055411.pdf
Stem rot: the same trial reports the highest stem rot incidence in NJ 7005, followed by JROM 1 and JRO 524. -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1755055411.pdf
Pest resistance (yellow mite, semi-looper, Bihar hairy caterpillar): No evidence found for JROM 1 specifically. The AICRP page describes resistance traits for a different green-stem variety, so I did not attribute them to JROM 1. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Recommended sowing window: mid-March to end-April. Pods are green, cylindrical and non-shattering. -- https://jute.dac.gov.in/TossaJute.aspx
Variety table entry: "JROM 1 (Pradip)" with notification details and a value of 37–40 in the same row; the snippet gives no unit for that value. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
Coastal West Bengal pre-kharif 2023 trial (seven olitorius varieties including JROM 1): JBO 1 led on growth and yield components, and JROM 1 was among the mid-ranking varieties. -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1755055411.pdf
Hybridization study: JROM 1 was used as a parent in a diallel of 90 hybrids. It had significant positive general combining ability for fibre weight per plant and significant negative GCA for stick weight. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1499256/full
Hybridization study (PMC version): JROM 1 is among the parents, and the hybrid JROM 1 × JRO 524 showed high positive heterosis for basal diameter, with JRO 524 × JROM 1 at 24.39 mm. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11896985/
Variety pedigree: "JRO 524 × TAN/NY/018C" (the parentage field in the record says "Not specified", so this is new information). -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-00403-1_13

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL or marker-trait associations specific to JROM-1. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-91163-8_10
Background only: a jute genome study used JRO-524 (not JROM-1) to build a genetic map with 382 markers. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-91163-8_10

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (CRIJAF), Barrackpore, West Bengal, which is the institution named in the record and the institute the Tossa breeding chapter covers. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-00403-1_13
Lead breeder name for JROM-1: No evidence found. Breeder names in the retrieved CRIJAF pages (Satya, Sarkar, Karmakar) are not linked to JROM-1 in the snippets, so they are not attributed here. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-91163-8_21
Institute director (institute-level, not a breeder): Dr. Gouranga Kar. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute address (institute-level): ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore, North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
Institute postal address with PIN code (institute-level): ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore, Kolkata, West Bengal 700121, India. -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-91163-8_21
Institute website: a link labelled "Official website" appears but no URL was retrieved. No official email or phone was found, and no breeder contact exists in the evidence. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers

PUBLICATIONS

JROM-1 (Pradip): No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or private dealers.

agronomic_details.yield: Variety record gives average_yield as 'Kg/Ha' with no value. Bangladesh trial (not an Indian trial): NJ-7010 (Rani) gave the highest green stick weight among seven white jute lines, 57 t/ha. This is green stick weight, not fibre yield, and is not an Indian field result.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The Bangladesh trial was reported at different regions of Bangladesh, but no stability statistic for NJ 7010 was retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed among olitorius jute varieties for early sowing (10 March to first week of April) with a seed rate of 3-5 kg/ha when drilled. Digest field use for NJ 7010 is in West Bengal only (Nadia; Barisha, Pingla, Paschim Midnapur). The variety record's state list has no matching digest evidence beyond West Bengal.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources. A farmer-survey claim of 110-120 days refers to the NJ-7005 (Raja) name and is not confirmed for NJ 7010.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources for NJ 7010. Survey and marketing claims for NJ-7005 (plant height up to about 14 ft, fewer basal spines, lower fertiliser need, high fibre quality and yield) are not confirmed for NJ 7010 and are not trial data. Promotional video claims for NJ-7005 (thick, uniform stems, low seed requirement) are likewise unattributed.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Bangladesh, white jute, seven breeding lines: NJ-7010 (Rani) gave the highest green stick weight at 57 t/ha. (2) Same Bangladesh paper: NJ 7005 ranked fourth for stick and biological yield, behind JBO 1, CO 58 and JRO 524; NJ 7005 is not confirmed as NJ 7010. (3) India, jute plus green gram intercropping: NJ 7010 (Rani) listed in trials in Nadia and in Barisha, Pingla, Paschim Midnapur (sowing date 16-3-2017); no yield result given. Weed suppression reported for mungbean intercropping relates to cv. Pant mung 5 and is not attributed to NJ 7010. (4) Two-year field experiments on jute (cv NJ 7010) with mungbean (cv TMB-37) under 3x3x3 spacing and density combinations, three replications; no numerical results retrieved; original journal not identified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NJ 7010 (CSC release name) / NJ-7005 (Seednet name), jute

Name note: The evidence below refers to the name shown in each line. "NJ 7010 (Rani)" is the CSC name, and "NJ-7005 / Raja NJ-7005" is the Seednet name and a Nuziveedu marketing name. I found no page that explicitly links NJ-7005 to NJ 7010, so the two are not confirmed as the same entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for NJ 7010 or NJ-7005 on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The search returned general jute pages only.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for variety-specific resistance. A slideshare on improved jute technologies mentions indigo caterpillar only as a minor pest of early-sown jute, with no link to NJ 7010 -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/1

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- NJ 7010 is listed among olitorius jute varieties for early sowing (10 March to first week of April), at 3-5 kg/ha seed rate when drilled -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/1
- NJ 7010 (Rani) is listed for jute plus green gram intercropping trials in Nadia and in Barisha, Pingla, Paschim Midnapur (sowing date 16-3-2017), with weed suppression reported for mungbean intercropping (cv. Pant mung 5, not NJ 7010) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/1
- Bangladesh trial (not an Indian trial): among seven white jute lines, NJ-7010 (Rani) gave the highest green stick weight (57 t/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343135525_Performance_study_on_yield_and_yield_attributes_of_seven_white_jute_breeding_lines_at_different_regions_of_Bangladesh
- Same Bangladesh paper: NJ 7005 ranked fourth for stick and biological yield, behind JBO 1, CO 58 and JRO 524 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343135525_Performance_study_on_yield_and_yield_attributes_of_seven_white_jute_breeding_lines_at_different_regions_of_Bangladesh
- Field survey (Seednet name NJ-7005, marketed as Raja NJ-7005): reports maturity in 110-120 days, plant height up to about 14 ft, fewer basal spines, lower fertiliser need and high fibre quality and yield. These are farmer-survey and marketing claims, not trial data -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/survey-report-pdfffffffggggggggggggggggg/276558938
- Nuziveedu promotional video on Raja NJ-7005: claims of thick, uniform stems and low seed requirement -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AmYXbPOLiBY

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genomic study naming NJ 7010 or NJ-7005 was returned.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No breeder name, developing institution or station was returned for NJ 7010 or NJ-7005. The only company link is Nuziveedu Seeds, from the Seednet-linked promotional video and survey material above. The release institution listed in the variety record is Nuziveedu Seeds Limited, which is a private company, not a public institute.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, address or contact page for the breeder or institution was returned. The Nuziveedu video describes its official YouTube account (https://www.youtube.com/shorts/HZjNfqLzIeo), which is not a verified contact channel.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved snippet (year not stated in retrieved snippet). Performance study on yield and yield attributes of seven white jute breeding lines at different regions of Bangladesh. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343135525_Performance_study_on_yield_and_yield_attributes_of_seven_white_jute_breeding_lines_at_different_regions_of_Bangladesh
- Authors not stated in retrieved snippet (year not stated in retrieved snippet). Two-year field experiments on jute (cv NJ 7010) with mungbean (cv TMB-37) under 3x3x3 spacing and density combinations, three replications. Journal article listed on Grafiati; original journal not identified -- https://www.grafiati.com/en/literature-selections/jute-plant/journal/
- No ICAR, AICRP, KrishiKosh or CRIJAF record was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-availability search could not be run because the tool-call limit was reached during the session. Only Nuziveedu promotional content (NJ-7005 / Raja) was returned, and no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for the state recommendation list in the variety record. Retrieved material mentions NJ 7010 field use only in West Bengal (Nadia; Barisha, Pingla, Paschim Midnapur) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/1. The Raja NJ-7005 video mentions Bihar farmers -- https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL3oAgn-rIMlTPf8cuf0FnyQaxqtuT4fvt

SEARCH NOTE
Four searches were completed (variety, Nuziveedu/NJ-7005 variety, breeder/institute, research). Two follow-up searches (Nuziveedu seed availability and NJ 7010 seed availability) were blocked by the tool limit. Recommended next steps: check the CSC release notification, the Seednet entry for NJ-7005, ICAR-CRIJAF publications and KrishiKosh for a breeder record, and state seed corporation listings for West Bengal.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean seed yield of 1.6 t/ha (BCKV listing, named 'Bidhan Khesari 1 (BK 14-1)'). Multi-location trial entry 'Bidhan Khesari-14-1' averaged 1226 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Multi-location trial mean is reported, but no stability analysis across environments was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to relay cropping in rice fallow (ICARDA-linked BCKV listing). Recommended for West Bengal. Mohanpur (Nadia) was one trial location, where mean duration was 117 days.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 108-116 days (BCKV listing). Mean duration 120 days across trial locations (117 days at Mohanpur). Matures about 15 days earlier than Nirmal (trial comparison).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: White flowers, white seed coat, 100-seed weight 6.7 g, protein 29.5%, ODAP 0.10% (BCKV listing). ODAP 0.095 in the multi-location trial entry.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Multi-location trial (entry 'Bidhan Khesari-14-1'): mean yield 1226 kg/ha against check variety Prateek (1140 kg/ha); mean duration 120 days (117 days at Mohanpur); ODAP 0.095; 100-seed weight 6.7 g; suited to relay cropping in rice fallow; matures about 15 days earlier than Nirmal. No other trial results were found for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Virat (knol khol, Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes)
Variety name in CSC minutes: Pusa Virat. Seednet name: Pusa Virat (the same string). Searches returned no CSC minutes or Seednet portal page, so all evidence below refers to the name "Pusa Virat" in general vegetable literature. Seednet code H030416780 and the 2013-06-04 release date were not confirmed by any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Pusa Virat. Cold-season adaptation is only general knol-khol background: the crop tolerates cold and frost better than many cool-season crops -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395413961_Recent_trend_in_Knolkhol_Production

DISEASE AND PEST -- Pusa Virat is listed among knol khol traits as resistant to Fusarium wilt, Xanthomonas campestris and a third pathogen whose name is truncated in the snippet -- https://www.slideshare.net/Rajubeta123/knol-khol-237781079 (secondary compilation, not a primary trial report). Knob cracking and deformed knobs were observed in the Ladakh greenhouse trial, where Pusa Virat was compared with White Vienna -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362079600_Growing_kohlrabi_Brassica_oleracea_var_gongylodes_in_greenhouse_during_winter_in_trans-Himalayan_Ladakh_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Pusa Virat is described as having round, large knobs of 800-900 g and 13-14 cm diameter -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313098865_Cole_crops . In a Ladakh winter greenhouse trial, Pusa Virat's salable knob weight was 108.8 ±0.7 g, against 190.3 ±20.3 g for White Vienna, and it took more days to mature -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362079600_Growing_kohlrabi_Brassica_oleracea_var_gongylodes_in_greenhouse_during_winter_in_trans-Himalayan_Ladakh_India . Hill sowing is recorded for March-April to August -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395413961_Recent_trend_in_Knolkhol_Production . A high-altitude and low-altitude field trial compared Pusa Virat with radish for nutritional quality under FYM and Azotobacter -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666154325003187 . Seed rate of 1-1.5 kg per hectare is given for knol khol generally -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329970468_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Knol_-Khol_Brassica_oleracea_L_var_gongylodes . Yield values for Pusa Virat from the Ladakh and Cole-crops sources conflict in context (greenhouse versus field), so treat them separately.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (no QTL, marker or parentage study located; parentage remains "Not specified").

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Pusa Virat was developed by IARI Regional Station, Katrain, and released by the H.P. State Seed Sub-Committee for cultivation in Himachal Pradesh -- https://www.slideshare.net/Rajubeta123/knol-khol-237781079 . Another compilation attributes the variety to "LARI, New Delhi", which appears to be an error for IARI -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397705814_Advances_in_Vegetable_Breeding . No lead breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page URL for IARI Regional Station, Katrain was returned by the search. Recommend checking the IARI Katrain (Himachal Pradesh) station page on iari.res.in or icar.org.in directly.

PUBLICATIONS --
Kariyaiah, B. (n.d./year not shown). Knol-khol research paper. Pharmaceutica Analytica Acta -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370845260_Knol-khol_research_paper (Pusa Virat not confirmed as the test cultivar in the snippet; year not verified)
Anonymous (2022/2023?). Growing kohlrabi (Brassica oleracea var gongylodes) in greenhouse during winter in trans-Himalayan Ladakh, India. Journal not identified in snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362079600_Growing_kohlrabi_Brassica_oleracea_var_gongylodes_in_greenhouse_during_winter_in_trans-Himalayan_Ladakh_India (authors, year and DOI not captured)
Anonymous (2025). Effect of farmyard manure and Azotobacter on the nutritional quality of high-altitude-grown cruciferous vegetables: an exploratory study. Journal not captured in snippet -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2666154325003187 (authors and DOI not captured; the DOI is embedded in the PII string)
Anonymous. Cole crops. ResearchGate compilation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313098865_Cole_crops (secondary source)
Anonymous. Recent trend in Knolkhol Production. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/395413961_Recent_trend_in_Knolkhol_Production (secondary source)
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report or peer-reviewed release paper for Pusa Virat was found in these results.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Retail listings found are for generic knol khol and F1 hybrids, not Pusa Virat; no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet listing for Pusa Virat was found. Examples: https://www.amazon.in/KNOL-KHOL-SEEDS-GANTH-GOBHI-Gardening/dp/B0BQDKRYKX , https://kalashseedsonline.com/index.php?route=product%2Fproduct&product_id=123 . Verify variety identity on the listing before buying. Check Seednet (seednet.gov.in) directly for Pusa Virat availability.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Himachal Pradesh, per the H.P. State Seed Sub-Committee release noted above -- https://www.slideshare.net/Rajubeta123/knol-khol-237781079 . The record's "Not specified" should be updated to reflect this, subject to confirmation from the CSC minutes or Seednet entry.

Gaps to resolve from primary sources: CSC release minutes and Seednet entry (confirm name, code, release date, parentage); IARI Katrain contact details; primary trial papers with DOIs; any KrishiKosh or AICRP vegetable report on Pusa Virat.

drought.details: Evidence is species-level, not variety-specific. Kodo millet overall is described as highly drought tolerant and suited to areas with scanty, erratic rainfall. No GAK-3-specific drought trial was found in the digest, so the variety-level rating is inferred and moderated to medium.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Head smut: moderately resistant (GAK-3 paper abstract and ICAR Indian Farming profile agree). Wording differs between abstract versions, and the digest does not give a quantitative rating. No other diseases are reported in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Shoot fly: resistant. The GAK-3 paper abstract versions differ in wording, and the ICAR Indian Farming profile lists it as highly resistant. Shoot fly resistance is reported as better than the local check GK-2 and the national check GPUK-3.

agronomic_details.yield: Not quantified in kg/ha in the digest. Relative to checks: DK-127 out-yielded local check GK-2 by about 27.5% and national check GPUK-3 by about 31.1% in hilly/tribal Middle Gujarat.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield advantage reported over multi-year trials in hilly/tribal Middle Gujarat. Stability statistics across environments are not given in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed kharif in Agro-climatic Zones I, II and III, specifically the hilly/tribal little/kodo millet tracts of Gujarat.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Easy threshing, synchronised maturity, non-lodging habit, protein content 8.83%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Multi-year trials in hilly/tribal Middle Gujarat against GK-2 and GPUK-3. Dahod station lists it as a high-yielding variety for the hilly region.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No evidence found in the digest for QTL, SNP or SSR markers. Pedigree is DK-127, described as a pure-line selection from a germplasm accession.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Kodo-137 (kodo millet)

Search status: 4 searches were run (variety, breeder, research, seed availability). The tool then hit its usage limit during a re-run to read full page text, so I could only read the first ~300 characters of each result. Findings below are limited to what those snippets verified. Headings without a finding are not confirmed; they are not evidence of absence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in the retrieved text. The ResearchGate snippet names the variety but its stress content was not visible. Check https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found in the retrieved text.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ResearchGate review snippet lists "Jawahar Kodo-137" in a rainfed-area context for kodo millet cultivation (not verified as a trial result) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found in the retrieved text.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Not verified. The institution field says IGKV (Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur, per the CSC record). No breeder name was retrieved. No source confirming the breeder or station was read.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No email, phone, address or contact page was retrieved. Suggested institute page to check: IGKV official website (igkv.ac.in), division/AICRP on Small Millets.

PUBLICATIONS -- No verified publications. The ResearchGate review (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383947677_Kodo_Millet_Sowing_Sustainability_for_a_Flourishing_Future) mentions the variety; authors, year and journal were not visible, so no citation can be formatted.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found in the retrieved text. Suggested checks: seednet.gov.in (variety code A0206035), Chhattisgarh state seed corporation, and IGKV seed sales.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Only the CSC record lists Chhattisgarh as the recommended state. An independent page was not verified. The Vikaspedia page "Released varieties of Kodo millet in India for cultivation" (https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/released-varieties-of-kodo-millet-in-india-for-cultivation?lgn=en) appeared in the variety search and may list this variety with its state, but the relevant entry was cut off in the snippet. Verify before relying on it.

NAME CHECK -- Both names are "Jawahar Kodo-137" (variname and Seednet name match). The evidence above refers to that name only.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Medium tall, Narrow and dark green leaves, Tolerant to Head smut, sheath blight and brown spot, High grain yield.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The proposed culture TNAU 86, is tolerant to head smut, sheath blight and brown spot.

drought.details: A 2012-era summary table lists TNAU 86 as tolerant to drought. The digest gives no quantitative drought data, no degree of tolerance, and no mechanism. The level is medium because the tolerance is stated qualitatively only. The CSC adaptation record describes rainfed cultivation in both kharif and Rabi seasons, which is consistent with but does not prove drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest for heat tolerance.

salinity.details: At seedling stage under imposed salinity at 50-200 mM, TNAU 86 gave the highest germination and salt-injury scores of five kodo millet varieties tested. It was one of two salinity-resistant entries. The level is high relative to the varieties tested; the digest gives no absolute threshold or mechanism.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest for flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Head smut: resistance listed in the small-millets summary table. Sheath blight: resistance listed in the same table. Brown spot: resistance listed in the same table. CSC ground-truth record also describes TNAU 86 as tolerant to head smut, sheath blight and brown spot. Leaf spot: No evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-specific resistance found for TNAU 86. Stem borer and leaf spot reactions: No evidence found. Shoot fly: the Recommended Package of Practices states that delayed sowing raises shoot fly incidence and advises timely sowing for the crop generally. This is a general crop management recommendation and is not evidence of TNAU 86 resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: grain 27.09 q/ha and fodder 56.00 q/ha. Small-millets summary table: 27-30 q/ha grain, which conflicts with a listed value of 1321 (units not stated, likely kg/ha) and needs checking against the original release notification. 2017-2020 multi-location trials: 3142 kg/ha grain yield (used as check for ATL 1).
agronomic_details.stability: Among the lowest MTSI scores across environments with CO 3, indicating relatively high stability in that comparison. Other stability measures: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed cultivation in both kharif and Rabi seasons (CSC record). Sowing before the second fortnight of July is recommended in the Package of Practices. Specific agro-climatic zones: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 95-110 days (summary source, units as given); 108-113 days in a trial table for TNAU 86
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium tall; narrow and dark green leaves (CSC record). Lodging absent and seed shattering present (PPV&FRA DUS descriptor scoring). DUS descriptor states for days to 50% flowering and panicle: details in the DUS source, values not given in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location trials 2017-2020: TNAU 86 recorded 3142 kg/ha grain yield and was used as the check for ATL 1. (2) Trial table: days to maturity 108-113 days. (3) Small-millets summary table: 27-30 q/ha grain yield, which conflicts with the 1321 value listed elsewhere. (4) Seedling salinity trial (50-200 mM): highest germination and salt-injury scores among five kodo varieties. (5) MTSI stability analysis: among the lowest scores across environments with CO 3. Trial site, season, and replication details: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE [name: TNAU 86 (CSC and Seednet both list TNAU 86)]
- Seedling salinity: TNAU 86 gave the highest germination and salt-injury scores of five kodo varieties at 50-200 mM, and it was one of two salinity-resistant entries -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389403775_PHYSIOLOGICAL_STUDY_OF_KODO_MILLET_UNDER_IMPOSED_SALINITY_STRESS_AT_SEEDLING_STAGE
- Drought: a 2012-era summary table lists TNAU 86 as tolerant to drought -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367157080_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_ATL_1_A_high_yielding_Kodo_millet_variety (table entry also reproduced at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India)
- Heat, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST [name: TNAU 86]
- The same small-millets summary table lists resistance to head smut, sheath blight and brown spot -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Lodging is absent and seed shattering is present in the PPV&FRA DUS descriptor scoring for TNAU 86 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/final-kodo-millet.pdf
- Shoot fly: delayed sowing raises shoot fly incidence, so timely sowing is advised for the crop generally -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
- Stem borer, leaf spot, and other pest-specific reactions for TNAU 86: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS [name: TNAU 86]
- Maturity 95-110 days and grain yield listed as 1321 (units not stated; likely kg/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374549234_Revealing_the_biochemical_profile_and_antioxidant_activity_of_kodo_millet_Paspalum_scrobiculatum_L. The same kind of summary table gives 27-30 q/ha, which conflicts with 1321 kg/ha and needs checking against the original release notification -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Days to maturity in a trial table for TNAU 86 are 108-113 days -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367157080_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_ATL_1_A_high_yielding_Kodo_millet_variety
- In 2017-2020 multi-location trials TNAU 86 recorded 3142 kg/ha grain yield, used as a check for ATL 1 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/367157080_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_Research_Article_ATL_1_A_high_yielding_Kodo_millet_variety
- Agronomy: seed rate 10 kg/ha for line sowing and 15 kg/ha for broadcasting; 40 kg N and 20 kg P2O5/ha -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
- Sowing before the second fortnight of July is recommended -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/3-Recommended_Package_of_Practices-Kodo_Millet.pdf
- Stability: TNAU 86 had among the lowest MTSI scores across environments with CO 3 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13237-026-00680-4

GENETICS AND QTL [name: TNAU 86]
- Parentage: pure line selection from IPs 85 -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/02_Small_Millets.pdf
- DUS descriptor states for TNAU 86 (days to 50% flowering, panicle, lodging, shattering) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/final-kodo-millet.pdf
- QTL or marker studies specific to TNAU 86: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION [name: TNAU 86]
- Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU). Named TNAU 86 breeder or lead scientist: No evidence found.
