search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VL MASOOR 133 (VARIETY_NAME) AND VL MASOOR-103 (SEEDNET_VARIETY_NAME) EVIDENCE DIGEST
Crop: lentil (masoor). Variety code VL 133. Release year 2011 per the input record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The central DPD lentil list gives VL Masoor 133 (VL 133), released 2011 by ICAR-VPKAS Almora, as tolerant to wilt, root rot and rust. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found for this variety. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf (the state-released table with the VL Masoor 133 row is in http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf)
- Evidence refers to: VL Masoor 133 (variety_name). No evidence found for the seednet name VL MASOOR-103 in this heading.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The DPD state-released table lists VL Masoor 133 as resistant to wilt, root rot and rust. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- No pest-resistance evidence was found for VL Masoor 133. -- (no URL)
- The Frontiers 2022 disease-resistance review's source tables do not list VL Masoor 133 (they cite VL Masoor 4 and VL507), so they were not used. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2022.1001682/full
- VL MASOOR-103 (seednet name): the only VL 103 evidence found (a 2000 VPKAS release described as rust tolerant) is a different variety and was discarded. Evidence for VL MASOOR-103 under this heading: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The DPD table gives VL Masoor 133 a yield of 12-13 q/ha, maturity of 114-120 days, and a timely-sown recommendation. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- The ISSS bulletin lists VL Masoor 133 among pulse varieties promoted through KVK technology demonstrations under NFSM during rabi 2015-16, though it gives no trial yields. -- https://www.isss-india.org/img/Bulletin31.pdf
- The Madhya Pradesh lentil review reports average farmer-demonstration yields across improved varieties but does not give a VL 133 figure. -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005193
- Evidence refers to: VL Masoor 133 only. No evidence found for VL MASOOR-103 under this heading.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or genetic-study evidence was found for VL Masoor 133 or VL MASOOR-103. -- (no URL)
- The parentage in the input record (selection from VHC2776-1 collected from Bageshwar, UP hills) was not found in any retrieved source, so it is unverified. -- (no URL)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The DPD table names ICAR-VPKAS, Almora (Uttarakhand) as originating centre for VL Masoor 133. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- No breeder name was found for VL Masoor 133 or VL MASOOR-103. The lentil breeder named in the Pakistan/IIPR-linked search results (Dr. Jitendra Kumar, IIPR Kanpur) belongs to a different programme and was not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336360431_Lentil_Lens_culinaris_Medik_Diversity_Cytogenetics_and_Breeding
- The VPKAS seed portal lists VL Masoor 133 as a VPKAS product. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLMasoor133_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0133

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact was found. The only institute-level page retrieved is the VPKAS seed portal product page for VL Masoor 133, which gives no email, phone or postal address. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLMasoor133_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0133
- The DPD record gives the originating centre as ICAR-VPKAS, Almora (UK). No address or phone was found. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- VL MASOOR-103 (seednet name): No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kumar V., Ninama A., Khande D., Amrute S., Pandey S.K., Pandey S. (2019). Current Scenario of Lentil Production in Madhya Pradesh. International Journal of Agriculture Sciences -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005193 (the snippet names VL Masoor 133 as one of the varieties in breeder-seed production; the year comes from the citation line in the snippet).
- Authors not captured (2016 by page age). Dehulling, germination and cooking study of lentil varieties including VL Masoor 133 (nutritional and anti-nutrient data). Journal not captured. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5336446/
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, or conference paper with trial data on VL Masoor 133 was found in the retrieved results. The IIPR MULLaRP rabi 2021-22 report was checked and no VL 133 entry appeared in the retrieved text. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The VPKAS seed portal lists VL Masoor 133 with a "In Stock" status (Uttarakhand Hills seed). -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLMasoor133_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0133
- Breeder-seed production for VL Masoor 133 is mentioned in the Madhya Pradesh review (see PUBLICATIONS).
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing was found for VL Masoor 133. The IndiaMart and Amazon listings returned for "masoor seed" are unbranded or unrelated and were discarded. -- (no URL)
- VL MASOOR-103 (seednet name): No evidence found on the Seednet portal in these results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand, timely-sown hill conditions. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Krishi Jagran's Uttarakhand list includes VL-133. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
- The VPKAS page describes the variety for Uttarakhand Hills. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLMasoor133_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0133
- The input field "recommended_states_raw" was "Not specified"; the above is supplied from search evidence.

SEARCH NOTE
- Four searches were run: variety profile, VL Masoor 103 breeder, VL 133 research, and seed availability. Results were mostly generic lentil or nutrition pages. Evidence for VL MASOOR-103 on the Seednet portal was not found. Evidence in this digest refers to VL Masoor 133 unless stated. Official Seednet and KrishiKosh pages should be checked directly before the record is finalised.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VL Masoor 129 (lentil)

Name note: the evidence below uses the spelling "VL Masoor 129" (dpd.gov.in). I did not see the Seednet listing "VL Masoor-129" in any result, so the Seednet-side evidence is absent, not confirmed.

Search budget note: four web_search calls were made. A fifth call was blocked by the tool limit, so the breeder, contact, and publication searches were not fully run. Gaps are marked below.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the state-release table entry for VL Masoor 129 notes resistance against wilt and root rot. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: VL Masoor 129 is listed as resistant against wilt and root rot. No pod borer or other pest evidence specific to this variety found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the table row for VL Masoor 129 contains the values "7-11" and "145-150" with no column headers in the snippet. These are most likely yield (q/ha) and days to maturity, but this is inferred and needs checking against the source. No multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage "VL 101 x VL 1" comes only from the input record; no independent source was retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the release row names VPKAS, Almora as the developing institution (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora). No individual breeder name was found in the results. Breeder search was not completed.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The breeder-contact search was not completed, so no official email, phone or address has been verified. The institute name VPKAS, Almora is the only institute-level identifier available.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for VL Masoor 129. The PMC article (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5336446/) studies VL Masoor 125, 133, 142, 507 and 514, not 129. No AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI was located.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned the release table but no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: listed as a state-released variety for Uttarakhand. A second source (dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF) lists Uttarakhand varieties, but the snippet I saw was truncated before the VL Masoor 129 entry.

RELEASE YEAR CONFLICT -- The input record says year of release is "NaT" (missing). dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf gives 2009. Treat 2009 as a source-supported value to verify, not as confirmed CSC minutes.

drought.details: Ratan exhibits remarkable tolerance to drought and is described as a drought-tolerant and drought-resistant genotype. It shows seed size consistency under water deficit, a useful adaptation mechanism. While its root growth can be drastically affected and relative water content (RWC) reduced under stress, its overall tolerance is consistently reported.

heat.details: Ratan is considered among heat stress-tolerant crops. Studies have investigated the influence of heat stress on its genome.

salinity.details: Ratan demonstrates enhanced tolerance to salt and is superior in salinity tolerance compared to other legume crops. It is included in screenings of grasspea genotypes for salinity response, indicating its known tolerance to salt stress.

flood.details: Ratan is noted for its tolerance to water logging conditions, which is essential for future production in flood-prone environments.

disease_resistance.summary: Not specified in search results.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified in search results.

agronomic_details.yield: Ratan (Bio L-212) has a reported yield of 15.0 (likely q/ha). It has outperformed chickpea (cv JG-74), lentil (cv JLS-3), and linseed (cv R), and is considered superior in yield compared to other legume crops.
agronomic_details.stability: Ratan is tolerant to various stress conditions, implying good stability across challenging environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Thrives well in all types of soils except high acidic. It is adapted to moisture stress and heat, and is recommended for the North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ) covering East Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 3.5 FEET PROSTRATE ; SIZE OF LEAF : BROAD LEAF ; LEAF WIDTH : 22.6MM ; LEAF LENGTH : 103.6MM ; INTERNODAL LENGTH : 59.0MM ; LEAF AREA : 10.24CM SQUARE ; 100 SEED WT. : 9.29 GM. SEED COLOUR : BOLD REDDISH GREY ; PROTEIN CONTENT : 25-30% ; FLOWER COLOUR : BLUE. It is known for its bold seeds and blue flowers. The variety has a low ODAP (β-N-oxalyl-L-α,β-diaminopropionic acid) content, generally reported as less than 0.1%. Seed size consistency is observed in response to water deficit.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Ratan has been cultivated by farmers in Bihar, with trials conducted over 26.33 acres involving 46 farmers. Seeds for experiments were obtained from Regional Research Station, Karnal, and Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur (Chhattisgarh).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Differential gene expression analysis revealed downregulation of abiotic stress tolerance and redox metabolism-responsive genes in Ratan. Several genes related to chromatin remodeling are differentially expressed in Ratan. β-ODAP biosynthetic genes are also investigated in this cultivar.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs were identified for Ratan directly in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Physiological responses of Ratan to PEG-6000 induced drought stress have been measured. Ratan's genetic mechanisms involve chromatin remodeling and regulation of abiotic stress tolerance and redox metabolism genes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Lime VRM-1 (VRM-1, Agriculture Research Station, Vellore; release recorded as 2015-04-07)

RELEASE/BREEDER: No evidence found confirming the 2015 release date or the Vellore station as breeder. -- No source located
VARIETY IDENTITY: TNAU lists "VRM 1" among acid lime varieties, but another TNAU page calls it a "local variety" and elsewhere pairs it with "Tahithi lime," so its origin and identity need verification. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_fruits_acidlime.html
DROUGHT: No evidence found for VRM-1. A drought-tolerance claim exists only for a different, farmer-developed grafted acid lime selection, not VRM-1. -- https://nif.org.in/innovation/new_acid_lime_variety/292
HEAT: No evidence found.
SALINITY: No evidence found.
FLOOD/SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found. TNAU's general acid lime guidance says water stagnation should be avoided, which applies to the crop generally, not VRM-1 specifically. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_fruits_acidlime.html
DISEASE RESISTANCE: No evidence found for VRM-1. Canker tolerance is reported for other acid lime varieties (Pramalini, Sai Sarbati), not VRM-1. -- https://www.horticultureguruji.in/acid-lime/
PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found for VRM-1. Leaf miner and citrus butterfly tolerance is reported only for PKM 1. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_TNAU_varieties_fc_acidlime.html
QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found for VRM-1. -- No source located
YIELD: No VRM-1-specific yield found. The general acid lime yield guideline is about 25 t/ha/year. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf
TRIALS: TNAU Sankarankovil's 2017–2020 scheme included VRM 1 among four acid lime varieties in an evaluation of acid lime genotypes for year-round production; no results were reported. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-sankarankovil/ongoing-schemes/
PROPAGATION: TNAU recommends layering for VRM 1 (listed as Tahithi lime). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC/State Seed Corporations/KVKs): No evidence found. -- No source located
RECOMMENDED STATES: Not confirmed by a release notification. TNAU's crop guide lists VRM 1 among acid lime varieties and names Vellore among the growing districts, which indicates Tamil Nadu use only. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf ; https://mapmycrop.com/acid-lime-crop-guide/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: ARPITA (JBC-5), jute**

**Name note:** The CSC/release-minutes name is ARPITA (code JBC-5), a white jute (*Corchorus capsularis*) variety. The Seednet name "Arpita" is listed under LINSEED (ALSI). The only Arpita-named Seednet-linked evidence I found is a linseed cultivar from Odisha, so it does not describe this jute variety. I did not access seednet.gov.in directly. Evidence below refers to the jute variety (JBC-5 / Arpita) unless stated otherwise.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The release listing describes it as having resistance to premature flowering. JBC 5 (Arpita) 2010 W.B. S.O. 2137 (E) 31.08.2010 28-30 Suitable for mid-March, pod non- shattering type, resistance to premature flowering, better fibre quality, resistance to major pest and diseases -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to JBC-5 was found in the searches. No evidence found for those traits.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The variety is described as resistant to major pests and diseases, but the named pathogens and pests are not specified. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Same claim from a second source (CRIJAF-derived improved technology deck). -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- No pest- or disease-specific resistance data (for example, stem rot or Ophiomyia) for JBC-5 was found. No evidence found for named pathogen resistance.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. It is recommended for sowing in mid-March, and the reported yield is 28–30 q/ha. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The ICAR 2010–11 report gives a potential of 2.8–3.0 t/ha in rainfed and transplanted-aman systems, and notes non-shattering pods. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Sowing-date recommendation for JBC-5 (mid-March) also appears in a pre-kharif extension table. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/pre_kharif.pdf
- No multi-location trial data specific to JBC-5 were found. No evidence found for trial-level yields beyond the above.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- No evidence found. Parentage is not specified in the input, and no pedigree, marker or QTL study for JBC-5 was found. A 2024 hybridization study on tossa jute (*C. olitorius*) mentions JBO 1 but not JBC-5 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11896985/

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The variety is listed in the CRIJAF variety table as a white jute variety. -- https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/SideLinks/Research/Varieties.php
- The developing institution is ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore. No named breeder or scientist was found for JBC-5. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
- Institution's own description of CRIJAF's role: Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibers (CRIJAF) established in 1953, is a research institute on jute & allied fibre crops under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research of Government of India. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Institute: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (CRIJAF). Address as found: Barrackpore, North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
- Official website: https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/ (institute contact page URL, not fetched)
- Director named on the Wikipedia page: Dr. Gouranga Kar. This may be out of date and was not verified against the institute site. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
- No breeder name, official email or phone number was found in the searches. The institute contact page should be checked directly for these.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Indian Council of Agricultural Research (2011). DARE/ICAR Annual Report 2010–11, Crop Improvement. ICAR annual report, which reports JBC 5 (Arpita) yield and recommended states -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Authors not captured in search results (year not captured). Scientific Cultivation of Field Crops, Vol. 1. Book chapter listing JBC-5 (Arpita) for state recommendations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh) or AICRP report specific to JBC-5 (jute) was found.
- Off-crop item, listed only because of the name match: Naik, B.S., Mishra, D., Lenka, D. and Sahoo, K.C. (2017). Arpita: a new linseed cultivar for Odisha. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 8(1): 84–88. DOI 10.5958/0975-928X.2017.00012.6 -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2017.00012.6 (linseed, not jute)

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No evidence found for JBC-5 (Arpita) at NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK or SAU in the searches. The West Bengal State Seed Corporation availability page lists other jute varieties (JRO-524, Irra, S-19, JRO-204, JBH-2004) but not Arpita. -- https://www.wbsscl.com/availability-of-seeds/
- Seednet portal listing for jute JBC-5 was not accessed. The Seednet "Arpita" entry under linseed refers to a different crop.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- West Bengal, as notified in 2010 under S.O. 2137(E) dated 31.08.2010. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Assam is recommended in the ICAR 2010–11 report. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Additional state lists that include JBC-5 (Arpita) for Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Meghalaya, Tripura and Nagaland. These are from compiled cultivation guides, not the notification. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE
- Release year: the state notification is dated 2010, so year_of_release "NaT" in the input can be replaced with 2010 (state notification). Release origin and institution are not stated in the notification excerpt.

drought.details: The HPKV crop improvement document lists 'Tolerant to water stress conditions' near the KL 215 (Bhagsu) entry, but the snippet does not clearly tie this trait to Bhagsu rather than a neighbouring entry. The Seednet list gives 'drought tolerant' for other varieties. General textbook statements that linseed is fairly drought resistant are crop-level, not variety-specific. The HPKV Research Council agenda mentions a drought mapping population derived from DH 40 (tolerant) and a susceptible parent, with Bhagsu among eight varieties studied, but no Bhagsu drought rating is given.

heat.details: No Bhagsu-specific heat tolerance data. A symposium abstract mentions heat-tolerant genotypes, but Bhagsu is not identified as one of them.

salinity.details: No Bhagsu-specific salinity data. Salt tolerance screening with NaCl is mentioned in a symposium abstract, but Bhagsu's result is not given.

flood.details: No evidence found. Textbook sources note that oilseed crops, including linseed, do not tolerate waterlogging.

disease_resistance.summary: Bhagsu is described as resistant to rust (a Scribd summary lists 'resistant to rust (KL-215)', suited to utera sowing). The PMC release table also describes it as resistant to rust and powdery mildew, though the snippet wording is ambiguous. A symposium abstract lists Bhagsu among genotypes that were highly resistant (disease score 0) in a screening, but the disease is not named in the snippet.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data found in the results.

agronomic_details.yield: The Scribd summary lists 4-5 q/ha, with 37.0 (likely oil content %). The HPKV document's 400-500 q/ha figure appears to belong to a forage crop entry, not Bhagsu.
agronomic_details.stability: In AMMI analysis, Bhagsu and Surbhi were the most unstable genotypes, although both had above-average oil content. A G x E study also reported a 11.69 percent difference for Bhagsu at Dhaula Kuan.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Bred and recommended for Himachal Pradesh, in hill conditions, with dual-purpose and utera use noted in one source.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 178-209 days per the Seednet list (180-185 days per the Scribd summary)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium height, blue flowers, small brown seeds. Pedigree RL-50-3 x Surbhi, developed by the pedigree method at Palampur.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Included in multi-environment G x E trials and in an eight-line genetic analysis of seed, fibre and dual-purpose traits.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No Bhagsu-specific markers, QTL or SNP data found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None reported for Bhagsu. HPKV is developing a drought mapping population from DH 40 (tolerant) and a susceptible parent, and Bhagsu is used in other studies only as one of eight diverse lines.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not reported for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: A release table attributes resistance to rust and moderate resistance to wilt, powdery mildew and alternaria blight to Birsa Tisi-2 (BAU 14-09). Attribution is uncertain because the same block sits next to a tomato entry. A general BAU statement says released varieties resist major diseases and pests, but this has no variety-level scoring and is not measured in the sources. Resistance ratings for Birsa Tisi-1 (high rust and alternaria resistance) are a separate release and are excluded from this variety's profile.

pest_resistance.summary: Only a general BAU statement that released varieties resist major pests was found, with no variety-level scoring. Bud fly resistance is recorded for Birsa Tisi-1 only and is excluded from this variety's profile. No pest-specific resistance evidence for Birsa Tisi-2 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Krishi Jagran reports a potential yield of 19.7 q/ha and 10.46% superiority over the national check T-397. The BAU release table gives conflicting values of 19-20 q/ha potential and 13-14 q/ha average. Average yield in CSC record: Not Available.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described as suited to the drought-prone, dryland (rainfed) ecosystem of Jharkhand. A Punjab recommendation appears beside a Birsa Tisi-2 block but is unverified and excluded.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Open-pollinated (IAUA listing). Flowers blue and bold capsules (BAU release table). Oil content reported as 36.75% (Krishi Jagran) and 42-43% (BAU release table), which conflict.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Krishi Jagran: 19.7 q/ha potential yield, 36.75% oil, 128-130 days maturity, 10.46% superior to national check T-397. (2) BAU release table: 19-20 q/ha potential, 13-14 q/ha average, 42-43% oil, 128-129 days; values conflict with item 1. (3) BAU release set (not specific to Tisi-2): 15-20% yield advantage over traditional varieties. (4) Rabi 2024-25 trial of 30 linseed genotypes including BIRSA-TISI-2 (LC) at the Ranchi-6 research farm, BAU: genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits; secondary branches, capsules per plant and seeds per capsule were the main direct contributors to yield; days to maturity had a negative direct effect. (5) Seed rate guidance of 25-30 kg/ha for linseed comes from an organic trial in which T-397 was the farmer-field variety, not Tisi-2.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as suited to the drought-prone, dryland ecosystem of Jharkhand, with resistance to major diseases and pests (general claim, not measured in the sources) -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Listed as an open-pollinated variety suited to rainfed conditions of Jharkhand -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistance to rust, moderate resistance to wilt, powdery mildew and alternaria blight are attributed to Birsa Tisi-2 (BAU 14-09) in a release table, but the same block sits next to a tomato entry, so attribution is uncertain -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
General statement that the released BAU varieties resist major diseases and pests (no variety-level scoring) -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Do not confuse with Birsa Tisi-1 (a separate, earlier BAU linseed release): high rust and alternaria resistance, moderate wilt and bud fly resistance -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_637852580202036105.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield 19.7 q/ha, 36.75% oil, 128-30 days maturity, 10.46% superior to national check T-397 -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Conflicting values in the BAU release table: 19-20 q/ha potential, 13-14 q/ha average, 42-43% oil, 128-129 days, flowers blue, bold capsules -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Varieties were described as offering 15-20% yield advantage over traditional varieties (BAU release set, not specific to Tisi-2) -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Seed rate guidance of 25-30 kg/ha for linseed, with T-397 cited as the farmer-field variety in organic trials (not Tisi-2) -- https://icar.gov.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Organic-linseed-Tisi-Farming.pdf
Field trial of 30 linseed genotypes including BIRSA-TISI-2 (LC), rabi 2024-25, Ranchi-6 research farm, BAU -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits in the 30-genotype trial, indicating genetic control -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
Secondary branches, capsules per plant and seeds per capsule were the main direct contributors to yield; days to maturity had a negative direct effect -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
QTL/marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Birsa Tisi-2 was developed by BAU principal/chief scientist Sohan Ram -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Developing institution: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand; code BAU 14-09 -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Release was approved at an SVRC meeting on 24 March (year not stated in the page) with Director of Research A. Wadood -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/
Release year conflict: the record says 26 Oct 2022 (CSC), while the news reports describe an SVRC release that appears to be from around 2021 -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/16-all-new-high-yielding-varieties-of-crops-developed-by-this-agri-research-institution/
Institution profile: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, established 1981; the Wikipedia infobox lists a Vice-Chancellor that conflicts with the 2021 news (Onkar Nath Singh) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS
Lead breeder: Dr Sohan Ram, BAU principal/chief scientist. No email or phone found -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/
Director of Research: Dr A. Wadood. No email or phone found -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/

A yield of 875 kg/ha with significant net returns (Rs. 15805/ha) has been observed for Gobhi sarson. agronomic_details.adaptation: Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus) is adapted as a Rabi crop and is suitable for transplanting on raised beds. It demonstrates adaptability to various intercropping systems including Maize-Gobhi sarson, blackgram-Gobhi sarson, rice-Gobhi sarson, soybean-Gobhi sarson, toria+Gobhi sarson, and berseem+Gobhi sarson. It is considered an emerging oilseed crop in India with limited cultivation area. Field trials for Gobhi sarson have been conducted at locations such as Chatha-Jammu, Ludhiana, and Palampur. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as resistant to rust, powdery mildew and wilt -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Listed as moderately resistant to powdery mildew and moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight, under the name "JL 41 (Jawahar Alsi-41)" -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
No evidence found on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to rust, powdery mildew and wilt (DAC notified-varieties table) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Moderately resistant to powdery mildew, moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight (AICRP release table, "JL 41") -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
Named among linseed lines in an IIOR 2022 report where whitefly, leafhopper and aphid populations peaked in late December 2021. The sentence is garbled, so the link between this variety and those pest counts is uncertain -- https://www.scribd.com/document/738239893/56-Annual-Report-IIOR-AR-2022

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release table: irrigated, Madhya Pradesh, State level, year 2011, listed range 1500-1600 with a value of 40, suitable for intercropping with sugarcane (units not stated in the snippet; the "40" may be a days or yield field) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
DAC table: year 2011, released at Hoshangabad, yield potential 40.00 and oil content 1600 (I) as listed; the columns look misaligned, so units are unverified -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
No evidence found for multi-location trial results or maturity days.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage "(RL 102-7X0-7) X J-23" was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Released at Hoshangabad (DAC table); the developing institution is not confirmed as JNKVV or any named station -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
No evidence found naming the lead breeder(s). The breeder search did not complete (see note below).

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, address or institute contact page for this variety was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Results were general linseed reviews and reports, not papers on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seed-dealer, NSC, SAU or KVK sale listings for this variety or for "Jawahar Linseed-9" were not returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Madhya Pradesh: listed among recommended linseed varieties for the state, with the note that the variety suits areas of Madhya Pradesh with limited irrigated facility -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Madhya Pradesh is also given as the release state with "Irrigated" and "State" categories in the AICRP release table -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

NAME NOTES
Variety name "Jawahar Linseed-41" was matched in DAC (also as "PKDL-41") and AICRP ("JL 41 / Jawahar Alsi-41"). Seednet name "JAWAHAR LINSEED-9" produced no evidence for this variety; the ICAR-CRIDA document mentions "JLS-9" and "J-23", which I discarded as different varieties. The ICAR 2024-25 report and the Jawahar Linseed Sagar (JLS 121) entry were also discarded.

NOTE: The search tool returned a usage-limit error partway through, so the breeder/contact search and the seed-availability search did not run successfully, and the publications search returned only general linseed material. Those headings should be re-run before the record is final.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Name used: JLS-73 (variety code SLS-73). Seednet name JLS-79 has no evidence linking it to this entry; see the note under RECOMMENDED STATES.
- Directorate of Oilseeds Development characters table lists SLS-73 (JLS-73) as resistant to rust, powdery mildew and bud fly -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- A ResearchGate table of abiotic-stress-tolerant varieties lists JLS-73 (SLS-73) as "moderately resistant" to an unclear disease (text truncated in snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351224957_Abiotic_Stress_Tolerant_Crop_Varieties_Livestock_Breeds_and_Fish_Species
- Plant-disease reference lists SLS-73 (JLS-73) among rust-resistant linseed varieties, citing "Anonymous, 2022" -- https://www.plantsdiseases.com/p/diseases-of-linseed.html
- Drought, heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found for JLS-73 specifically. The review found lists JLS73 in rainfed-condition tables without tolerance data -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screening (2023–24 isolates) grades JLS-73 as susceptible, with wilt incidence of 30.1–50% -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
- Rust, powdery mildew and bud fly resistance: see STRESS TOLERANCE (DOD source).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Sowing-date trial comparing PKV-NL-260, PKV-NL-97 and JLS-73 in split-plot design; PKV-NL-260 sown in the 44th meteorological week outperformed PKV-NL-97 and JLS-73 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi study in drought-prone area: JLS-73 among three cultivars, with 73.33% root colonisation at site three -- https://ijfans.org/uploads/paper/44d1a9b8e41cd079600968587e2df7a6.pdf
- Yield figure in the DOD table: 38.82 (units not stated; the oil-content column "1090 (R)" appears misaligned) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Excluded: Punjab "LS-73" trials and Nagaland "JLS-95" trials are different genotypes.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker-assisted or pedigree study for JLS-73 was returned. The Fusarium SSR study characterises the pathogen, not the variety's genetics.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Release centre: Sagar, year 2011 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Institution conflict: a ResearchGate table gives LNKVV Jabalpur for JLS-73 (SLS-73), 2011, with the same states -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351224957_Abiotic_Stress_Tolerant_Crop_Varieties_Livestock_Breeds_and_Fish_Species
- Institution listed as "Not specified" in the input record. Release date in the input (2010-12-23) differs from the 2011 year in the sources.
- Named breeder: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. An ICAR IIOR linseed page lists breeder and centre contacts, but it does not name JLS-73, so it is excluded under the strict relevance rule -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed

PUBLICATIONS
- Mane, P. A. (2022). Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal association with different cultivars of linseed in drought prone area. IJFANS, 11(12) -- https://ijfans.org/uploads/paper/44d1a9b8e41cd079600968587e2df7a6.pdf
- Authors not captured (2023/2024). Characterization of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini based on ITS and SSR markers and identification of resistance of Indian linseed. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Growth, Yield, Nutrient Uptake and Quality of Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) Varieties as Affected by Varying Sowing Dates. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- AICRP on Linseed, Varieties Released list (JLS 73, rainfed, 2011) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed: A Comprehensive Review. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

SEED AVAILABILITY
- JLS 73 is among varieties whose breeder-seed indent and production share was tracked for 2007-08 to 2018-19, with a share of 4.8–7.6% -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/b37b/81289b537bdd60a2fba6aac040168c05a884.pdf
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales and private dealers: No evidence found for JLS-73. The only shop result (NY Spice Shop) is for generic flax seed.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Input record: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bundelkhand UP, north-east and central Maharashtra, north-east Gujarat.
- DOD notified-variety table: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- AICRP list: Bundelkhand part of UP, Rajasthan and MP, rainfed, 2011 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- JLS-79 (Seednet name): the DOD table lists JLS-79 as a separate entry for MP. A castor paper states JLS 79 was released in 2016, so it refers to a different variety. No evidence links JLS-79 to JLS-73 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols
- No Seednet portal page was returned, so no evidence under the Seednet name for JLS-79 was found for this entry.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JLS-79 (linseed, variety code A0404091)

Names searched: "JLS-79" (CSC release name and Seednet name, which are identical). Variant spellings found in the evidence: "JLS 79" (AICRP table) and "Jawahar Linseed Sagar-79" (MDPI review). Four searches were run in total. Most results were about other linseed varieties or unrelated flax products, and those were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for JLS-79 was found. The only stress material was general linseed reviews that do not name JLS-79. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2023.1165580/full (general; does not name JLS-79)

DISEASE AND PEST
- AICRP table: JLS-79 is listed as irrigated, released 2016, for Madhya Pradesh, with a "highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to bud fly" rating. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- DOD (Directorate of Oilseeds Development) table: JLS-79 is listed as resistant to rust, powdery mildew, wilt and bud fly. This conflicts with the AICRP table on bud fly and wilt ratings, and the AICRP table does not mention rust. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Field study of insect pests on JLS-79 at JNKVV College of Agriculture, Rewa, Madhya Pradesh (rabi 2020-21). Insect pests were identified on the crop in Rewa district. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342881084_Insect_herbivores_and_their_natural_enemies_in_linseed_and_their_population_dynamics
- Companion study of bud fly (Dasyneura lini) population dynamics, same JNKVV Rewa trial, names JLS-79. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/103-%20Studies%20on%20the%20Qualitative%20Composition%20of%20Insect%20Pests%20and%20Population%20Dynamics%20of%20Bud%20Fly%20(Dasyneura%20lini%20Barnes)%20on%20Linseed%20(Linum%20usitatissimum%20L.).pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield potential is listed as 36.85 in the DOD table and 38.82 in the AICRP table. Neither table states units. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The AICRP table also gives an unlabelled oil figure of 45.10 and an iodine value of 165.49 for this variety. The label is unclear. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- DOD describes the variety as early to medium duration. No maturity days were found. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- The AICRP table describes the variety as suitable for intercropping with pulses. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No multi-location trial results specific to JLS-79 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Searches returned no QTL, marker or pedigree study for JLS-79. The parentage field in the input is "Not specified", and no source supplied one.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The institution is JNKVV (Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya), Jabalpur, per the input record. The DOD table gives the released centre as Sagar. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- The JNKVV Rewa and Powarkheda colleges of agriculture appear in the pest studies, which used JLS-79 in trials. No named breeder was found in any source. The Rewa and Powarkheda colleges are JNKVV units and do not identify the breeder. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/103-%20Studies%20on%20the%20Qualitative%20Composition%20of%20Insect%20Pests%20and%20Population%20Dynamics%20of%20Bud%20Fly%20(Dasyneura%20lini%20Barnes)%20on%20Linseed%20(Linum%20usitatissimum%20L.).pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

- Postal address of the institute or division: No evidence found in the results.
- Breeder email or phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Gautam Kunal and others (2019). Insect herbivores and their natural enemies in linseed and their population dynamics. ResearchGate preprint (year as listed in the metadata; the paper text refers to the 2020-21 rabi trial). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342881084_Insect_herbivores_and_their_natural_enemies_in_linseed_and_their_population_dynamics
- Authors not shown in the snippet (n.d.). Studies on the qualitative composition of insect pests and population dynamics of bud fly (Dasyneura lini Barnes) on linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.). PlantArchives journal, year and volume not shown in the snippet. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/103-%20Studies%20on%20the%20Qualitative%20Composition%20of%20Insect%20Pests%20and%20Population%20Dynamics%20of%20Bud%20Fly%20(Dasyneura%20lini%20Barnes)%20on%20Linseed%20(Linum%20usitatissimum%20L.).pdf
- Authors not shown (n.d.). Performance of elite castor hybrids and varieties under rainfed Alfisols. ResearchGate. This is a castor paper that also reports JLS 79 seed indent data. Authors and year not shown in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report with JLS-79 trial data, or DOI-bearing journal paper specific to JLS-79 was found.

It accounted for about 6.3% of the linseed crop indent in the cited period. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols (this paper cites a Seednet readyreckoner page: https://seednet.gov.in/readyrecknor/Seed_III_VI.aspx)

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC name "Kota Alsi-6" and the Seednet name "Kota Alsi" were both searched. The evidence found uses "Kota Alsi 6 (RL 13165)" (AICRP), "Kota Alsi-6" (Dholi seed directory), and "KOTA ALSI 6 (RL 13165)" (PMC review). No Seednet page was retrieved, so no evidence is attributed to the Seednet name directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Irrigated-condition classification with no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Listed among irrigated-condition varieties in a national linseed genetic-resources table. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to Kota Alsi-6 found in the four searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rated moderately resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to Alternaria blight. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Bud fly resistance is not stated for this entry; bud fly tolerance is attributed to the rainfed sister line Kota Barani Alsi 6 (RL 15584) on the same page, so it should not be assumed for Kota Alsi-6. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early maturity. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Table row shows 1277 and 35.04 with no column labels; these are most likely mean seed yield (kg/ha) and oil content (%), but the page does not confirm this. Presented at Central 85th CVRC meeting. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No multi-location trial report specific to Kota Alsi-6 was found. disease_resistance.summary: Alternaria blight: moderately resistant (MR) per the AICRP release table. Powdery mildew: resistant per the AICRP release entry. Alternaria blight reactions in coordinated IVT-Rainfed trials (2010-11) at several locations were a mix of MR, MS, S and R scores; the digest does not attribute these scores to KB-3 individually at each location. Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini): reaction not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: described as resistant in the AICRP release entry and as tolerant in the release listing. No quantitative bud fly scores were found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Sustainability-index study in the south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan: KB-3 yielded about 12.57 q/ha (approximately 1257 kg/ha). The AICRP release table lists figures of 1370 and 38.73 against this variety, but column headings were not captured, so their meaning (likely yield in kg/ha and oil percentage) is unconfirmed. The CSC average_yield field gives units only (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Sustainability index of 89.79% in the south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan study, where the variety was suggested as a breeding parent. No additional multi-location yield data for KB-3 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed conditions; south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan (sustainability-index study). Recommended state: Rajasthan. Broader agro-climatic adaptation details were not found in the retrieved sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified (days not given in the digest; the AICRP listing describes the variety as early-maturing)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed described as light brown and medium-sized in the AICRP release entry. Other morphological characteristics: Not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Coordinated IVT-Rainfed trials, 2010-11: Alternaria blight reaction recorded at several locations with a mix of MR, MS, S and R scores. (3) Sustainability-index study, south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan: KB-3 yielded about 12.57 q/ha with a sustainability index of 89.79%, and was suggested as a breeding parent. (4) AICRP release table: figures of 1370 and 38.73 listed against the variety, meaning unconfirmed. No additional multi-location trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as rainfed and early-maturing, with moderate resistance to Alternaria blight and powdery mildew, plus bud fly tolerance -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Variety-specific abiotic stress data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) were not found in the retrieved sources. -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Reaction to Alternaria blight in coordinated IVT-Rainfed trials (2010-11) was recorded at several locations, with a mix of MR, MS, S and R scores -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
- Resistant to powdery mildew and bud fly, with the release table recording it as moderately resistant to Alternaria blight -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The AICRP release entry describes the seed as light brown and medium-sized, and lists resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and bud fly -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini) reaction for this variety was not found. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Seed rate and fertility level optimisation under rainfed conditions was tested in 2012-13 (seed yield table present, values not legible in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
- Sustainability-index study in the south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan: KB-3 yielded about 12.57 q/ha with a sustainability index of 89.79%, and was suggested as a breeding parent -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019.v8.i4.8857/studies-on-sustainability-index-for-selecting-stable-genotypes-of-linseed-ltemgtlinum-usitatissimumltemgt-l-in-south-eastern-plain-zone-of-rajasthan
- The AICRP release table lists figures of 1370 and 38.73 against this variety, but the column headings were not captured, so their meaning (likely yield in kg/ha and oil %) is unconfirmed -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No additional multi-location yield data for KB-3 beyond the above was found. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Kota Barani appears as a reference variety in an SSR-marker profiling study of Indian and exotic germplasm; this is not a QTL or variety-specific genetic study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327374930_Analysis_of_genetic_diversity_in_Indian_and_exotic_linseed_germplasm_and_identification_of_trait_specific_superior_accessions
- Parentage: not specified in the variety record. An ISOR table row reads "Kota Barani 2015 Triveni x RL-1011 Kota", but it cannot be confirmed as belonging to KB-3 -- https://isor.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/vol-33-1.pdf
- QTL or marker-trait association studies specific to KB-3: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Release listed under Rajasthan via State notification S.O. 2680(E) dated 01.10.2015, in the AICRP-Linseed varieties table (ICAR-IIOR network) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The DOR/IIOR (ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad, formerly Directorate of Oilseeds Research) publication carries the KB-3 trial data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281279219_Sunflower_genetic_resources_management_at_DOR
- Lead breeder for KB-3 at Agricultural Research Station, Kota: not named in retrieved sources. The AICRP contact page lists Dr. Sandhya Kulhari as "Junior linseed Breeder & In charge" at a Kota (AU) centre, but this does not establish her as the KB-3 breeder. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. A.L. Rathnakumar, Project Investigator, Principal Scientist (Pl. Breeding), ICAR-IIOR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500030; phone 040-24598137 (office), 09427229459 (mobile); email A.Rathnakumar@icar.gov.in -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/ (institute-level/coordinator contact, not confirmed as the KB-3 breeder)
- Dr. Sandhya Kulhari, Junior Linseed Breeder & In-charge, AU Kota: name and role found; no phone or email captured -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/
- Postal address of ICAR-IIOR: Rajendranagar, Hyderabad – 500 030 (the Krishi Bhavan address is ICAR HQ, New Delhi-110001) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/ and https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/contact-us-2/
- Seednet portal entry (name, code A0404085) was not retrieved. -- No evidence found

disease_resistance.summary: Listed as moderately resistant to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt, rust and bud fly on the DOD notified-variety table (Maharashtra). This conflicts with a 2022-23 Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screen in which LSL-93 was graded 4 (susceptible, 30.1-50% wilt incidence). The wilt rating therefore cannot be resolved from the digest; the screen result is the more specific evidence. Resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and rust has no additional independent evidence in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly (Dasyneura lini): LSL 93 (ZC) is listed in the group rated moderately resistant (>10-25% damage) in a 2025 journal PDF screening. The snippet is partial, so this is indicative only. The DOD table also lists moderate resistance to bud fly. No other pest evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: DOD notified-variety table lists a yield potential of 37.95 (unit not shown in the snippet). Nagaland irrigated foothill trial: 671.33 kg/ha seed yield (lowest of seven varieties tested). Latur College of Agriculture, Rabi 2023-24 nano-urea and phosphorus foliar trial: seed yield across treatments 890.31 to 1401.22 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis for LSL-93 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released at Latur, Maharashtra (DOD notified table). The PMC review lists LSL93 among rainfed-condition varieties. Tested under irrigated foothill conditions in Nagaland. No formal agro-climatic adaptation statement was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 132.19 days to physiological maturity in a germplasm evaluation (2,576 accessions, two seasons, ICAR-NBPGR and Akola), where LSL93 was the best check for earliness. In the Nagaland irrigated foothill trial, 50% flowering occurred at 65 days, the earliest of the varieties tested.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Nagaland irrigated foothill trial: fewest capsules per plant (29.13), lowest oil yield among the seven varieties, highest test weight (9.08 g). Parentage, morphology and plant height were not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nagaland irrigated foothill trial, seven varieties including LSL-93: LSL-93 had the lowest seed yield (671.33 kg/ha), fewest capsules per plant (29.13) and lowest oil yield, but the highest test weight (9.08 g) and earliest 50% flowering (65 days). (2) Nagaland University, Medziphema trial: the authors' conclusions on LSL-93 are not in the snippets, so no finding is available. (3) Fertilizer-level trial with LSL-93, RLC-148 and NL-260 under NPK levels 0-30:30:30 kg/ha: LSL-93 was the reference variety and differed from the others in growth and yield; NL-260 was at par except for oil content. Location and year not captured. (4) Latur College of Agriculture, Rabi 2023-24 nano-urea and phosphorus foliar trial on LSL-93: seed yield 890.31 to 1401.22 kg/ha across treatments; protein 18.6-28.54%. (5) Germplasm evaluation (2,576 accessions, two seasons, ICAR-NBPGR and Akola): LSL93 used as best check for earliness, 132.19 days to physiological maturity.

No evidence found for QTL or marker-trait associations specific to LSL-93. The Nature 2024 germplasm study and the Fusarium SSR study use LSL93 only as a check or differential entry, not as a genetic study of the variety -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-71044-8 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
No parentage found. The task form lists "Not specified", and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Released centre listed as Latur on the DOD notified table (2019), with the notification recorded as 2019 S.O. 3220(E), 5 September 2019 in the PMC review. Developing institution given in the task record: VNMKV, Oilseeds Research Station (Latur) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist(s) for LSL-93. The ICAR-IIOR linseed page lists breeder posts and centre vacancies, but does not name LSL-93 or its developers -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
ICAR Nagaland scientist Dr Harendra Verma recommended LSL-93 for seed purposes in an extension report. He is not identified as a breeder of this variety -- https://www.morungexpress.com/icar-nagaland-centre-conducts-workshop-on-promoting-oilseeds

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for an email, phone, postal address or institute contact page specific to LSL-93 or the VNMKV Oilseeds Research Station, Latur.
Not attributed to this variety: the PDKV AICRP linseed breeder entry (Nagpur, phone 0712-2541245) at http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm is a different AICRP centre and is not evidence for LSL-93.

drought.details: No specific drought tolerance level for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified in the provided results. Linseed generally experiences drought as a major abiotic stress, and research aims to develop drought-resilient varieties through multi-environment phenotyping and molecular studies. Pratap Alsi-2, a different variety, is noted as tolerant to drought. (Results 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 31, 32, 37, 38, 40, 43)

heat.details: No specific information on heat tolerance for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified. Elevated temperature (heat stress) is reported to impact Linum usitatissimum production. (Result 19)

salinity.details: No specific salinity tolerance level for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified, though 'Pratap Alsi-1 (RLU-6)' was part of studies involving treatment with neutral salt and alkaline conditions. Salinity is a known detrimental constraint for flax (linseed) production, and research focuses on identifying salinity-tolerant genotypes for breeding. (Results 3, 10, 21, 22, 24, 25, 29, 34)

flood.details: No specific information on flood tolerance for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified. Pratap Alsi-2, a different variety, is noted as tolerant to both submergence and drought. (Result 43)

drought.details: Fairly resistant to drought and tolerant to moisture stress, also indicated as drought tolerant. It can tolerate both submergence and drought situations.

heat.details: Tolerant to heat stress and shows better stress tolerance indices. It is also mentioned as heat tolerant.

salinity.details: Can withstand slight alkalinity and salinity. It is recommended as a salt-tolerant improved variety and is considered a good option for sodic soils. It was part of studies involving neutral salt and alkaline treatment for linseed genotypes.

flood.details: Tolerant to flood situations and suitable for flood-prone Eastern Plain Zone IIIB.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to rust, powdery mildew, wilt, and Alternaria blight. Tolerant to phyllody, leaf curl, and Jammu and Kashmir virus.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant/tolerant to bud fly.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary between 1957 kg/ha (for irrigated conditions, 'I') and 1960 kg/ha. It is also described as a high yielding variety for irrigated conditions, capable of producing 2000-2200 kg/ha (20-22 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly mentioned, but recommended for varied agro-climatic zones and tolerant to multiple stresses, indicating adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Rajasthan, specifically suitable for the climatic conditions of South-Eastern Rajasthan, including the Humid South Eastern Plain Zone V and Flood Prone Eastern Plain zone IIIB. agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record adaptation_ecology: Chhattisgarh and Odisha, where moisture is available in the field of medium to late duration rice varieties; utera (under moisture stress), rabi season, and rice-based relay cropping ecosystem. The rice-fallow listing (see field_trials) supports suitability for rice-fallow cultivation in eastern India. CSC agronomic_features also report 2.20 B:C ratio against national check T-397 (1.68), zonal check Shekhar (2.08) and JLS-9 (1.73) for Zone-IV; non-lodging and non-shattering; responsive to recommended fertilizer doses; broadcasting at milking to drooping stage of paddy. agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nutrient-level (RDF) study with five linseed varieties (RLC-92, RLC-133, RLC-138, RLC-143, RLC-148): the snippet reports RLC-138 among the best-performing entries for yield and cost, but table values are fragmentary and unit-labelled unclearly, so no quantitative result is reported. (2) Rice-fallow cultivation: RLC-138 listed among linseed cultivars judged promising for rice-fallow cultivation in eastern India, alongside RLC-143 and BAU 06-03; no yield data given. (3) Bud fly screen at Bihar AU Sabour (150 germplasm lines, rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24): RLC-138 moderately resistant, with bud fly infestation in the >10-25% range. (4) Bold-seeded genetic variability study (Markandey et al., 2022): RLC-138 used as one of five checks among 40 bold-seeded genotypes, rabi 2021-22; no RLC-138 result reported. The cluster-mean maturity table in that paper is not variety-specific and was discarded. (5) Association analysis study (2024): RLC-138 listed as a check from AICRP Linseed IGKV, rabi 2022-23; no RLC-138 result reported. (6) Characterisation of 23 IGKV released varieties (Acharya et al., 2023), rabi 2022-23: RLC-138 among varieties characterised; no result reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Name matched: RLC-138 (CSC and Seednet names are identical; no Seednet page was retrieved)
Moderately resistant to linseed bud fly (Dasyneura lini), with bud fly infestation in the >10-25% range, in a Bihar AU Sabour field screen of 150 germplasm lines, rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24 -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data specific to RLC-138 were found. The only drought statement retrieved concerns linseed in general -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4912539/

DISEASE AND PEST
Name matched: RLC-138
Bud fly moderate resistance finding above -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf
No powdery mildew, rust, Alternaria blight or wilt reaction recorded for RLC-138 was found. The DOD notified-variety table lists resistance traits only for other varieties (RLC-148, MAU Azad Alsi-2, Utera Alsi/RLC-143) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx (no RLC-138 row)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Name matched: RLC-138 (appears as a variety in a multi-variety trial; "V3 (RLC-138)" in a nutrient-level trial)
RLC-138 was one of five linseed varieties (with RLC-92, RLC-133, RLC-143, RLC-148) in a nutrient-level (RDF) study; the snippet reports RLC-138 among the best-performing entries for yield and cost, but the table values are fragmentary and unit-labelled unclearly -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-7-2020/Vibha%20Sahu,%20et%20al.pdf
RLC-138 was listed among linseed cultivars judged promising for rice-fallow cultivation in eastern India, alongside RLC-143 and BAU 06-03 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332343129_Rice_fallows_in_the_eastern_India_Problems_and_prospects
Yield (kg/ha), maturity days, plant height and branching for RLC-138 were not found; the cluster-mean maturity table in the Markandey paper is for clusters, not for RLC-138 -- https://www.ijcmas.com/11-9-2022/Vidya%20Markandey,%20et%20al.pdf (discarded as not variety-specific)

GENETICS AND QTL
Name matched: none
No evidence found. The only SSR and genetic-diversity hits name RLC-137 or other lines, not RLC-138 -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/46144fef08b6bdc792ee4c3ae8b8152db959385e (discarded)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RLC 164 (linseed / ALSI)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "RLC 164". The AICRP page writes it as "RLC-164", and I treated that as the same variety. No search returned a Seednet portal page, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found. Four searches were run, one per topic plus one extra for seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The AICRP release table classes RLC-164 as rainfed, not irrigated or utera -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to RLC 164. A general statement that linseed is drought tolerant was found, but it is not about this variety, so I discarded it -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4912539/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Under artificial conditions it is moderately resistant to Alternaria blight and moderately susceptible to powdery mildew. Under natural conditions it is moderately resistant to Alternaria blight and to bud fly -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Same table text also contains "highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to bud fly". The snippet does not clearly tie this to the RLC-164 row, so it is unverified -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Bud fly resistance is noted in the same source. No separate bud fly trial data for RLC 164 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The AICRP row gives RLC-164's release details (CVRC 2020) alongside two unlabelled numbers, 1161 and 32.6. The column headers are not visible in the snippet, so I cannot assign them to yield, maturity or oil content -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No evidence found for field-trial or multi-location yield results for RLC 164. The Chhattisgarh sowing-date trial tested RLC-92, not RLC 164, so I discarded it -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025.v8.i9.M.3881
- The IGKV 2023 genetic analysis study names RLC-92, RLC-133 and RLC-143 only, so I discarded it -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2023&vol=12&issue=6&ArticleId=21111

GENETICS AND QTL
- RLC 164 is listed among national linseed genetic resources in a seed-type table. This is a germplasm listing, not a genetic study -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- RLC-164 appears in a DUS descriptor context, with stigma-position and related trait groupings in the linseed variety characterisation -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- No QTL or marker study specific to RLC 164 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is attributed to Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur. This comes from the input record. The AICRP release row retrieved does not show the institution name in the visible text -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The IGKV Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Raipur is the institute-level unit that works on linseed. No lead breeder name for RLC 164 was found -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- The Chhattisgarh linen-fibre paper lists RLC 164 among seven recent IGKV-linked varieties released after 2012, but it does not name a breeder -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, official email, phone or contact-page URL for RLC 164 was found.
- Institute-level address only: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur-492 012 (Chhattisgarh), India -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-8-2-001
- Same address form appears on another IGKV College of Agriculture paper, which names no breeder for RLC 164 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137093
- Individual authors' names on other IGKV papers were not attributed to this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (2023). Title not retrieved. The Pharma Innovation Journal 12(8): 2203-2206. Mentions RLC-164 in a DUS descriptor context for IGKV-released linseed varieties -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- No DOI or full bibliographic record was retrieved for this item. Its author list must be confirmed from the journal before citing.
- No ICAR/AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or peer-reviewed field paper specific to RLC 164 was found. Other linseed papers and a KrishiKosh budfly thesis were retrieved but do not name RLC 164, so I discarded them.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for RLC 164.
- The results were non-Indian linseed sellers and a Scribd Rabi 2025-26 tentative seed availability document. The visible text of that document did not name RLC 164, so I discarded it -- https://www.scribd.com/document/902605334/Rabi-2025-26-Seed-Availability-Tentative

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP release row gives the recommended zone as Jammu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Chhattisgarh, with release by CVRC in 2020 (85th CVRC, dated 09-11-2020) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The input record says "Jammu & Kashmir", while the source says "Jammu".

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for RLC 167 specifically. The four searches returned only generic linseed drought material and studies of other varieties (e.g., RLC-92, RLC-148, RLC-153), which I discarded. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
- The AICRP-Linseed varieties-released table lists RLC-167 and attaches a rating that it is highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, and moderately resistant to bud fly. The rating text sits in a fragmented table, so it may not be cleanly tied to this row and should be checked against the source PDF. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found. The agronomy and trial papers retrieved (PGR foliar sprays, weed control at IGKV Raipur) do not name RLC 167. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137093 ; https://igkv.ac.in/__files/JAI/1/Journal_pub_1__uctfbwn0aq54uzg3dmwcx50h_202204051610516PM046.pdf
- No yield, maturity, or oil data specific to RLC 167 was found. The AICRP table has a fragment with "(45.10)" and "Iodine Value-165.49" that might belong to this row, but it cannot be confirmed. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The retrieved genetics studies used other crosses (e.g., RLC-95 x Indira alsi-32) and do not involve RLC 167. -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-8-2-001

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The retrieved sources give no named breeder or lead scientist for RLC 167. The variety is attributed to Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh, as stated in the release record. Institute-level evidence: IGKV reports that it has released 16 linseed varieties, with RLC 161, RLC 164 and RLC 167 among the seven most recent (released after 2012). -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue3/PartK/8-4-8-452.pdf ; https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- IGKV's linseed work sits in the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Raipur, which hosts an AICRP on Linseed research farm. -- https://www.chemistryjournals.net/archives/2022/vol4issue2/PartA/4-2-50-637.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
- Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Krishak Nagar, Raipur-492012 (C.G.). Telephone directory 2026: IPRO Office 0771-2443220, ipro@igkv.ac.in; Directorate of Extension Services des@igkv.ac.in. -- https://igkv.ac.in/images/Telephone_Directory2025.pdf
- Telephone directory 2021 (older listing): Office 0771-2443419, Fax 91-771-2442302, website www.igau.edu.in, email vcigkv@gmail.com, pa2vc.igkv@gmail.com. These may be superseded. -- https://igkv.ac.in/images/tp2021.pdf
- Journal of Agricultural Issues editorial office: jai@igkv.ac.in, Telefax 0771-2972070, website https://igkv.ac.in/ . -- https://igkv.ac.in/__files/JAI/1/Journal_pub_1__uctfbwn0aq54uzg3dmwcx50h_202204051610516PM046.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Pharma Innovation Journal 2023, 12(8): 2203-2206. Study of IGKV Raipur linseed genotypes in Rabi 2022-23, in which RLC-167 appears among the genotypes and in colour and seed-trait groupings. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- Indian Journal-style list (Biochem journal, IJABR 2024; 8(3): 968-970). Mentions RLC 167 only in a list of IGKV releases; not a trial on this variety. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue3/PartK/8-4-8-452.pdf
- International Journal of Fiber and Innovative Hybrid Materials (inence), charkha paper. Lists RLC 167 among IGKV releases only. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- Note: The Pharma Journal 2023 (12(6)) and IJCMAS 2022 papers name other IGKV genotypes but not RLC 167, so I excluded them. No peer-reviewed trial or thesis on RLC 167 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Seednet and seed-dealer sources were not returned by the search. The results included a National Seed Project at IGKV Raipur (Badshahbhoge), but no page links it to RLC 167, so it is not listed as a source. -- https://cgcert.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/List-of-Individual-Producer.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP-Linseed table lists RLC-167 as irrigated, released by CVRC 2020 (85th CVRC), for Jammu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Chhattisgarh. The source says "Jammu", not "Jammu & Kashmir" as recorded in the input. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

NAME CHECK
- variety_name ("RLC 167") and seednet_variety_name ("RLC 167") are identical. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved, so all evidence above refers to the AICRP/IGKV name "RLC-167" or "RLC 167" and has not been checked against Seednet.

drought.details: A Patna Press article (BAU Best AICRP-Linseed award, 2024-25) describes Sabour Tisei-4 as drought-tolerant and suited to climate-change adaptation. The article uses the spelling 'Sabour Tisei-4' and gives no BRLS code, although the digest treats it as this variety. This is a press claim, not peer-reviewed data, and no quantitative drought trial data, physiological mechanism, or yield-under-stress result was found for Tisi-4.

heat.details: The same Patna Press article describes Sabour Tisei-4 as heat-tolerant. This is an unverified press claim, not peer-reviewed data. No quantitative heat trial data, sowing-date response, or physiological mechanism specific to Tisi-4 was found.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance is credited to Sabour Tisi-4 in any source in the digest. The Patna Press article attributes Alternaria blight and powdery mildew tolerance to Sabour Tisei-3, not Tisi-4. No evidence was found for resistance to any disease in BRLS 121 / Tisi-4.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: Kumari et al. (2024) screened 150 linseed genotypes at BAU Sabour farm (rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24). BRLS 121 appears in a 28-entry list of germplasm, but the snippet does not state its reaction (resistant or susceptible). Status is unresolved. No other pest resistance evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: The original variety data lists an average yield of 13 quintal/ha. The digest does not independently confirm this value. It states that the BAU yield values in the sources refer to other entries. No Tisi-4-specific yield data was found in the digest.

No Tisi-4-specific maturity, grain yield, oil content, or sowing-date trial results were found.
