search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME CHECK -- variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "KMH-3426" and the evidence below refers to that name. The seednet_crop_name (MAIZE (MAKKA)) and the variety code A0207438 did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for KMH-3426.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page attributed disease or pest resistance to KMH-3426. The resistance text in the benchmarking table belongs to a different row (CoH (M) 9), so I did not attribute it to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
Listed as a maize cultivar released by the AICRP on Maize, with the entry "KMH-3426 · Kaveri Seed Company Ltd., Hyderabad · Private · 09-10-2012", a 6.2 yield figure, Kharif season and "Normal" classification -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
Listed among hybrids released from 2000 with year of release 2012, medium maturity, average yield 6.5 and orange, semi-dent kernels -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
Appears in a benchmarking compilation of Indian maize varieties with a medium-maturity classification and a stated yield of about 6.3 t/ha, but the table extraction is garbled and the yield figure could not be confirmed for this row -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
No field-trial or multi-location result specific to KMH-3426 was found -- No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage given in the brief, (KML 5277 X KML 5164) X KML 5253, did not appear in any search result. No marker or QTL study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION --
Developing institution: Kaveri Seed Company Ltd., Hyderabad, a private company -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
The company says its R&D is in-house and that it runs more than 15 research and satellite farms, but no lead breeder or scientist is named for KMH-3426 -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
The company founder, G.V. Bhaskar Rao, is named on company history pages. He is a company founder, not a breeder of this variety, so I have not attributed the variety to him -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/our-story/details-of-business/
No breeder name for KMH-3426 was found.

CONTACT DETAILS --
Institute-level only. The company website is https://www.kaveriseeds.in/ and the corporate profile page is https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
The Hyderabad location comes from the AICRP and benchmarking listings. No official email, phone or postal address for the company or its R&D division appeared in the results.
No breeder or individual contact was found.

PUBLICATIONS --
Authors not stated (year not stated). benchmarking indian maize varieties. ResearchGate PDF listing KMH-3426 among released Indian maize varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
Not found: no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report chapter, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specific to KMH-3426 appeared. Other maize papers that surfaced (Cereal Research Communications, Springer, Cambridge) do not name this variety and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY --
Kaveri lists KMH-3426 among its maize hybrids in its company product lists -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/our-story/details-of-business/
The 2013-14 Kaveri annual report lists KMH 3426 among its marketed maize hybrids -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for KMH-3426 was found. Retailer pages that came up (Indiamart, DesiKheti) sell other Kaveri maize hybrids, such as KMH 25K45 and KMH 8333, and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES --
The AICRP cultivar list gives Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
The benchmarking compilation gives Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, with the list cut off in the extracted text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
The AICMIP list gives UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa and Rajasthan, with the rest truncated -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
The seednet raw field says "Eastern Uttar Pradesh"; the sources above say "Uttar Pradesh" without "Eastern", and only the AICRP list includes Chhattisgarh.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KMH-7148 (maize)

Name check: the variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "KMH-7148", so one name was searched. The evidence below refers to KMH-7148 in the AICRP cultivar list and Kaveri's own product list. I did not search the Seednet portal separately, so no Seednet record was checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for KMH-7148 specifically. Searches returned stress-tolerance claims only for other Kaveri maize hybrids (KMH Profit, Drona). Those should not be attributed to KMH-7148. -- https://agrostar.in/product/kaveri-kmh-profit-maize-35-kg-seeds/AGS-S-2643?language=en&state=gujarat (Profit only, not KMH-7148)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for KMH-7148. The benchmarking paper's snippet covers other Kaveri hybrids (KMH-25K45 and others), not KMH-7148. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The AICRP-Maize cultivar list records KMH-7148 as a privately bred cultivar from Kaveri Seed Company Limited, Secunderabad, with a 10-01-2015 entry date, a recommended zone of Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Western Uttar Pradesh, a Rabi season entry, and a "Normal" class. Its numeric columns (2680 (E) and 10.1) have no headers in the retrieved text, so I did not interpret them as yield or maturity. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/
- Maturity, yield and multi-location trial data for KMH-7148: No evidence found. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for KMH-7148 (parentage, marker or QTL studies). The CSC release minutes do not appear in the search results, and the parentage field in the input is "Not specified". -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Kaveri Seed Company Limited, Secunderabad (listed as the developer in the AICRP cultivar list). -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/
- Kaveri lists KMH-7148 among its maize hybrids. -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
- Named lead breeder or scientist for KMH-7148: No evidence found. A Gubba newsletter names Dr Prabir Paul as leader of Kaveri's maize R&D team, but it does not link him to KMH-7148, so I have not attributed it to him. -- https://www.gubbanews.com/super-maize-hybrids-from-kaveri-seeds/
- Station or research farm for KMH-7148: No evidence found. Kaveri's site states it has a research team and about 600 acres of company-owned farmland, with no station named. -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found.
- Institute-level: Kaveri Seeds corporate website, https://www.kaveriseeds.in/ (no email, phone or postal address was retrieved from the homepage snippet).
- Company profile page with address fields, https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/KAVERI-SEED-COMPANY-LIMIT-15606874/company/ (address heading present, but the address text was not retrieved).
- Phone and email: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specifically on KMH-7148 was found.
Related item (does not cover KMH-7148 in the retrieved text): Kaul, J., Kumar, B., Karjagi, C., and Yadav, O. P. (year not shown in retrieved text). Benchmarking Indian maize varieties. Indian Institute of Maize Research -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No KMH-7148 seed listing was found from an NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer.
- Kaveri hybrids that were listed by dealers (KMH 8333, KMH 8322, KMH-25K45 Bumper) do not include KMH-7148. -- https://www.desikheti.com/collections/kaveri-seeds-maize-seeds-buy-online ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kaveri-bumper-kmh-25k45-hybrid-seed-corn-27284225091.html
- Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) availability: not searched.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Western Uttar Pradesh -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/

RELEASE DATE NOTE
The input gives 2015-06-25 as the release year. The AICRP list gives 10-01-2015. These two dates differ, so verify against the CSC release minutes or the Seednet record before relying on either.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KMH 8322 (maize)

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "KMH 8322". All evidence below refers to that name. No CSC release minutes or Seednet portal entry was found, so the release record could not be verified against either source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for KMH 8322 -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/kaveri-kmh-8322-maize-seeds

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for KMH 8322 -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/kmh-8322-corn

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Kaveri's 2019-20 annual report lists KMH 8333 and KMH 8322 as promising products developed in 2019-2020, suitable for the central and south zone in Kharif and South Rabi -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
Kaveri's Nov 2021 quarterly investor presentation names KMH 8322 and KMH 8333 as two key contributors to its performance -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Q2Presentation-112021.pdf
The same annual report notes that research on improving maize yield potential through genomic selection is underway. It does not name KMH 8322 specifically -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
A retailer listing gives the product as an F1 hybrid, with no yield or maturity figures -- https://www.desikheti.com/collections/kaveri-seeds-maize-seeds-buy-online
Discrepancy: the 2019-20 report already calls KMH 8322 a product developed in 2019-2020, but the input record gives a release date of 26 Oct 2022. The two dates need reconciling against the official notification.
Discrepancy: the input list of recommended states (Punjab through Tamil Nadu, 14 states) is much broader than the "central and south zone" wording in the company report. Treat the state list as unverified.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage given in the input record is KM19SX001 x KM19SY003. No independent source confirmed it. No QTL or marker study was found -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Kaveri Seed Company Ltd. (Kaveri Seeds), per the input record and the company annual report -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
No lead breeder or scientist name was found in any result.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No institute email, phone, or postal address was found in the results. Only the company website domain appeared: https://www.kaveriseeds.in
Unverified, user-generated item: a Scribd document attributes a Haryana farmer's experience with KMH 8322 to the company's annual report. It is not an official source -- https://www.scribd.com/document/728001176/Kaveri-seed-co

PUBLICATIONS
No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, or conference papers on KMH 8322 were found. Searches of the trial and research topics returned only unrelated results.
Company documents only (not peer-reviewed):
Kaveri Seed Company Limited (2020). 33rd Annual Report 2019-20. Company annual report -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
Kaveri Seed Company Limited (2021). Q2 FY22 investor presentation, November 2021. Investor presentation -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Q2Presentation-112021.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
Private dealers list KMH 8322 (Kaveri, 4 kg pack):
Desikheti: listed as sold out at the time of crawl, price Rs 2,199 -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/kaveri-kmh-8322-maize-seeds
BigHaat: listed as currently unavailable/out of stock -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/kmh-8322-corn
IndiaMART: Godamayee Agro Agencies, Aurangabad, Maharashtra, offering a 4 kg pack at Rs 2,120 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kaveri-kmh-8322-hybrid-maize-seeds-4-kg-bag-2855045164133.html
Agribiz: listed as a 4 kg Kaveri product -- https://agribiz.farm/product/kmh-8322/
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Input record lists 14 states: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu. No official notification confirming this list was found. The company report's central and south zone wording conflicts with it (see Agronomy and Trials).

Information regarding 'Kohinoor' exhibiting drought tolerance in the search results consistently pertains to maize or fodder crops, where it is described as 'highly drought tolerant' (Result 8) or listed among 'drought tolerant varieties' of maize (Result 4, 23, 3). 'IGFRI-5450(Kohinoor)' (a forage/pulse variety) is also noted for its 'unique tolerance ability against stress environmental conditions not only drought' (Result 5, 13, 25).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MAH 14-5 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical, so one set of evidence covers both; the seednet.gov.in portal was not returned by any search)

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no page that describes drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for MAH 14-5. -- https://uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/English-varieties.pdf (only the MAH-20-45 entry mentions leaf rust and leaf spot resistance, and that is a different hybrid)

DISEASE AND PEST
AICRP Kharif Maize 2016 progress report lists MAH-14-5 in a zone-wise table with the entries MLB, TLB, CLS, C.RUST and RDM. The column headings are not legible in the extract, so the disease code meanings are unconfirmed. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
The table row does not state a resistance rating, so this is a pathology trial listing, not a resistance result. No other disease or pest finding for MAH 14-5 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
UAS Bangalore Zone-5 release notice (2025-26): maize hybrid MAH-20-45 averaged 110.6 q/ha, which is 14.6% above the check hybrid MAH-14-5 at 96.6 q/ha. This is the only yield figure found for MAH 14-5, and it is as a check in another hybrid's trial. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/English-varieties.pdf
No maturity, plant height, or yield data specific to MAH 14-5 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree, marker, or QTL information was found for MAH 14-5. The parentage field reads "Not specified."

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No page names a lead breeder or developing scientist for MAH 14-5. The release metadata lists "University of Agricultural Sciences" as the institution, and the search results did not confirm which UAS it is.
Not attributed to this variety: the AICRP 2016 report names a maize breeder at Parbhani (Dr V.R. Naik, Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth) on the same page as the MAH-14-5 table, but the page does not link him to MAH 14-5, so he is not recorded as its breeder. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, or postal address for MAH 14-5 was retrieved. The UAS Bangalore pages retrieved carry no contact details, and the UAS Bangalore agri-innovation maize page (https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/maize/) lists MAH-14-5 without contact information.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No journal article, thesis, conference paper, or AICRP report section focused on MAH 14-5 was retrieved. The AICRP 2016 report above is the only official document that names the variety, and it is a table entry rather than a study.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed search returned only a Syngenta listing for "Hybrid Maize Seed Mah 15 84" (a different hybrid, discarded) and unrelated international pages. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sales, or dealer listing for MAH 14-5 was found. -- https://www.indiamart.com/syngenta-121616571/maize-seeds.html (discarded: different product)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Release metadata gives Karnataka as the recommended state. No search result confirms this. The UAS Bangalore Zone-5 notice names MAH-14-5 only as a check, not as a recommended hybrid, so it does not confirm the recommendation. -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/English-varieties.pdf
Other listing: the UAS Bangalore agri-innovation maize page includes MAH-14-5 among its maize entries, but it does not state a recommendation status. -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/maize/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NMH-803 (maize)

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "NMH-803", so one name covers both. The searches did not return a Seednet portal page, so no Seednet-specific evidence is reported. Pages also use the trade name "Shaurya NMH-803", which I treat as the same variety because it carries the NMH-803 designation.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Nuziveedu's own social-media listing for "Shaurya NMH-803" describes it as drought tolerant, with medium plant height and medium maturity (company marketing claim, not independent trial data) -- https://in.pinterest.com/nuziveeduseeds/hybrid-corn-seeds/
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in the retrieved pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for NMH-803.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The AICMIP list of released maize hybrids gives NMH-803 as a medium-duration yellow dent hybrid with a yield of 6.2 t/ha -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- A benchmarking presentation based on AICRP (maize) testing lists NMH-803 (Nuziveedu Seeds) among hybrids notified in 2013, with 6.2 t/ha and orange-yellow, semi-dent grain -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- An Assam state (Dept. of Agriculture) report on RKVY 2016-17 records a farm-level yield of 68.75 q/ha under NMH-803 seed in Assam, a non-recommended state, so it is field-level and not a multi-location trial -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_1/files/Additional%20income%20through%20Maize%20cultivation_0.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or genomic studies of NMH-803. The parentage "(NM-124 x NM-250) x NM-161" comes only from the input record and was not verified by any retrieved source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The release-table and benchmarking sources credit the variety to Nuziveedu Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (no lead breeder or scientist named) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- A company profile lists "Shaurya NMH 803" among Nuziveedu maize products (no breeder named) -- https://theorg.com/org/nuziveedu-seeds-ltd
- No evidence found for a named lead breeder, developing station or ICAR/SAU institute.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or postal address. No institute contact page for NMH-803 was retrieved. Institution-level contacts were not searched, so none are reported.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Benchmarking Indian maize varieties. AICRP (maize) conference presentation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- No peer-reviewed papers, KrishiKosh theses or AICRP annual-report entries specific to NMH-803 were retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A Assam state RKVY 2016-17 scheme distributed NMH-803 hybrid seed through agriculture officers -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_1/files/Additional%20income%20through%20Maize%20cultivation_0.pdf
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or current dealer listings. A BigHaat result for "Divya NMH3" (NEO Seeds, out of stock) is a different product and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Release-table entry: Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- The benchmarking presentation gives a similar list (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, kharif) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

RELEASE YEAR CONFLICT
- year_of_release is missing ("NaT") in the input. The AICMIP table gives 2012, while the benchmarking presentation says the hybrid was notified in 2013. The CSC minutes were not retrieved, so the official year is unconfirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for NUZI 260 (Sweet Corn) returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance for this variety. Results were about sweet maize in general, such as drought effects on sweet corn seedlings, which name no NUZI 260 line. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11495081/ (not used: general sweet corn, not this variety)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The only disease and pest material returned was from US patent documents on other hybrid sweet corn plants (HMX59YS825, AZLAN, and others), which do not name this variety. -- https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/11252891 (not used: different varieties)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial data for NUZI 260 was returned. One Nuziveedu retail page lists a different product, "Mishthi" hybrid sweet corn, with 75-80 day maturity and high yield claims. It is not named NUZI 260, so it is discarded under the strict relevance rule. -- https://krushidukan.bharatagri.com/en/products/nuziveedu-mishthi-hybrid-sweet-corn-seeds (not used: different product name)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage (NSCL-91 x NSCL-202, with the listed pedigrees) was not confirmed by any search result. The genetics pages returned concern sweet corn in general, such as South China Agricultural University GWAS and BIOTEC Thailand sweetness GWAS, and do not name this variety. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13468538/ and https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8235792/ (not used: other germplasm)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a lead breeder or scientist of NUZI 260. The institution listed in the record is Nuziveedu Seeds Ltd. Company-level sources describe it as a private agribusiness, headquartered in Hyderabad, that develops and markets maize and sweet corn hybrids. These do not confirm that the company developed NUZI 260. -- https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuziveedu_Seeds

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No official email, phone, or postal address for NUZI 260 or its breeding division was returned. The only company-level information is a headquarters in Hyderabad, India, and the website nuziveeduseeds.com. This is institute-level only and is not verified for this variety. -- https://www.accesstoseeds.org/index/south-southeast-asia/company-scorecards/nuziveedu-seeds/ ; https://nuziveeduseeds.com/products/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. None of the searches (including KrishiKosh-style and journal-style queries) returned a paper, AICRP or ICAR report, thesis, or trial report naming NUZI 260. Returned papers were on sweet corn in other countries and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for NUZI 260. Nuziveedu-branded sweet corn appears on several retail sites under the name "Misthi" (for example, desikheti.com and beejkart.com). That name is not NUZI 260, so it is discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or official Seednet listing was returned. -- https://www.desikheti.com/collections/nuziveedu-seeds (discarded: different product name)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The recommended-state list in the record (Punjab through Telangana) could not be checked against any source, and no Seednet or CSC notification page was returned for this variety.

NOTE ON NAMES -- Both the CSC name "NUZI 260 (Sweet Corn)" and the Seednet name "NUZI 260 (Sweet Corn)" are identical in this record. Searches under both names returned no evidence for either. Seednet, the CSC minutes, and ICAR sites were not reachable through search results, so an official check still needs to be done directly on seednet.gov.in.

drought.details: Tolerant to moderate drought and water stress conditions, enabling it to thrive in drought-prone environments and enhancing climate resilience. Shows adaptability to water deficit.

salinity.details: Fairly tolerant to salt conditions and salinity.

flood.details: Tolerant to water logging and flood conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Shows strong tolerance to maize leaf blight (MLB) and is resistant to stripe rust, leaf rusts, and loose smut. It is also moderately resistant to turcicum leaf blight and bacterial stalk rot.

General maize research indicates that drought stress significantly reduces plant height, leaf area, biomass, and yield characteristics (RESULT_7, RESULT_37). Breeding for drought-tolerant maize genotypes is a practical approach to address water deficit (RESULT_5, RESULT_9). Several QTLs associated with drought tolerance have been identified and exploited in maize breeding programs (RESULT_10, RESULT_33). Molecular insights into drought tolerance mechanisms are being investigated (RESULT_2, RESULT_23, RESULT_24, RESULT_32).

heat.details: No specific information regarding HPC-4's heat tolerance was found in the provided search results. General maize research indicates that heat stress is a serious issue affecting plant growth, development, and productivity (RESULT_12). Heat stress, along with drought, is a main driver of maize yield losses (RESULT_11). Increasing heat stress and rising temperatures are key abiotic stresses impacting agriculture (RESULT_13, RESULT_18).

salinity.details: No specific information regarding HPC-4's salinity tolerance was found in the provided search results. Salinity is identified as a significant abiotic stress causing crop yield losses (RESULT_13).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SVPMH-101 is a pearl millet (bajra) hybrid, not a maize hybrid. The AICPMIP table lists it as "SVPMH-101 (MSH 361)" under pearl millet hybrids. The Seednet name "PMH 10" under MAIZE refers to a different product, so no PMH 10 evidence is used below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as highly resistant to downy mildew, tolerant to rust and insect pests -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Stress-tolerance claims about drought or heat were not found for this variety. The source lists only disease and pest traits. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Highly resistant to downy mildew, tolerant to rust and insect pests -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Resistant to downy mildew is also listed in the same table row block, which is garbled in the extracted text. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Late maturing, tall, very compact, with long panicles and dual purpose (grain and fodder) use; high grain and fodder yield; grey-brown globular seeds -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- No multi-location trial data or yield numbers were found for this variety. -- No evidence found in search results.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The only parentage record is the AICPMIP table entry, which lists SVMSA-112 x SVR-50 for SVPMH-101. This cell is garbled in the extracted text, so verify it against the original table. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for PMH 10 disease or pest resistance. - No evidence found for BLPMH 109 or MSH 363.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In a spring-maize irrigated trial, PMH 10 (described there as a PAU Ludhiana hybrid) gave about 68.71 q/ha grain yield, below P 1844 (85.46 q/ha) and DKC 9108 (69.55 q/ha). The page shows no trial year or site. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327135097_Evaluation_of_Spring_Maize_Hybrids_under_Irrigated_Conditions

(PMH 13, Punjab hybrid: PAU's kharif package lists PMH 13 among its maize hybrids, and PAU-LCC seed is sold at the PAU Seed Shop, Gate No. 1, Ludhiana, KVKs and Farm Advisory Service Centres. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; earlier PAU releases said PMH 13 seed was available at the same Ludhiana shop and at all KVKs. -- https://www.krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/high-yielding-maize-variety-developed-by-punjab-agricultural-university/)
(Commercial partner: PAU signed an agreement with Nutranta Seeds, Sunam, Punjab, to commercialise PMH 13. -- https://agrospectrumindia.com/2021/07/30/pau-inks-pact-with-nutranta-seeds-to-commercialise-maize-hybrid-pmh-13.html)
(NSC or state seed corporation listings: not searched; no evidence found.)

RECOMMENDED STATES
(PMH 12: The ICAR-IIMR list gives the released zones as BH, JH, WB, OD, CHH and Eastern UP, with public release on 05.09.2019. This partly matches the supplied states (Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand, parts of UP and Odisha) but adds Chhattisgarh (CHH), and the release date differs from the supplied 2019-06-01. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/)
(PMH 13, Punjab hybrid: PAU recommended it for cultivation in Punjab only. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/punjab-agricultural-university-develops-new-hybrid-variety-of-maize-261049 . These Punjab sources do not support the Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand, UP or Odisha recommendation.)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CRIS CHECK: Crop mismatch in the record. The variety record says crop "millet", while the Seednet crop is "MAIZE (MAKKA)". The only page naming Pusa Composite 612 is about pearl millet. Treat the crop identity as unresolved until verified.

Names searched: "Pusa Composite-612" (variety_name) and "PUSA COMPOSITE-1" (seednet_variety_name). No page found named PUSA COMPOSITE-1 with code MP-480 or with the maize/composite 612 identity.

Searches used: 4 of 4 (release/traits; breeder; research papers; institute contact). Seed availability was not searched, because the fourth search was used for contact details.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Pusa Composite 612 (pearl millet, 2010 listing) is described as suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for it were found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/pearlmillet-crop-production-technology/255075507
No evidence found for PUSA COMPOSITE-1 (maize) stress tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for either name in maize. The pearl millet listing gives no disease or pest data for Pusa Composite 612.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Pusa Composite 612 (2010) is listed with an average seed yield, but the value is truncated in the snippet and cannot be read. Crop: pearl millet, not maize. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/pearlmillet-crop-production-technology/255075507
No evidence found for maize yield, maturity or trials under PUSA COMPOSITE-1 or MP-480.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The parentage given in the record (recombination of families from populations A600, A602, A603, A604) matches the pedigree of Pusa 1 (1988), a different variety, so it was not attributed to this record. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found naming a breeder for Pusa Composite 612 or PUSA COMPOSITE-1. The Directorate of Maize Research compendium lists IARI and other breeders for other composites, but its snippets do not name this variety, so no attribution was made. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
The maize breeder listed in the record is at ICAR-IARI, Division of Genetics, New Delhi-110012 (from the record, not independently verified).

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level; no breeder contact found)
ICAR-IARI, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012. Director Dr. Ch. Srinivasa Rao, director[at]iari[dot]res[dot]in, 011-25843375, 011-25842367. General: info@iari.res.in, Pusa Helpline 011-25841670 / 25841039, WhatsApp 9560297502. -- https://www.iari.res.in/en/contact-us.php
ICAR-IARI Director listed on another page as Dr Ashok Kumar Singh, director@iari.res.in, 011-25842367 (older listing, conflicting). -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/indian-agricultural-research-institute-icar-iari
Directorate of Maize Research, Pusa Campus, New Delhi-110012, tel +91 11 258 49725, fax +91 11 258 48195 (2009 data, may be outdated). -- https://www.asti.cgiar.org/india/directory/directorate-maize-research-dmr
ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (contact at Ludhiana): director.maize@icar.gov.in, pdmaize@gmail.com, +91-161-2440048 / 9492430207. -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-indian-institute-maize-research

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a paper, report or thesis naming Pusa Composite 612 (maize) or PUSA COMPOSITE-1. Results on maize composites (Pusa Composite 3 and 4, released 2005) are different varieties and were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Not searched (search budget used for contact details).

RECOMMENDED STATES
Record list (raw): Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh. The pearl millet listing of Pusa Composite 612 (2010) instead gives Zone B: Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh. The two lists differ and cannot be reconciled from these sources. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/pearlmillet-crop-production-technology/255075507

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for DFH-2 (seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 -Female" and variety name "Pant Forage Maize Hybrid-1") returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this hybrid.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for DFH-2 turned up in the search results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
DFH-2 is reported to have high green forage and dry matter yield, with advantages over national checks COHM-8, J-1006 and African Tall; no numeric yields were given -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Its multiple basal/lateral tillers and regrowth potential, combined with higher forage yield, are described as useful for dairy farmers; no trial numbers or locations given -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
No multi-location trial data or agronomic yield figures for DFH-2 were found beyond the above -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4

GENETICS AND QTL
DFH-2 is described as a single-cross inter-subspecies hybrid between maize (Zea mays) and its wild ancestor teosinte (Z. mays subsp. parviglumis) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
A 2026 Springer paper on wild relatives cites DFH-2 as an inter-subspecies hybrid with multi-cut, multi-ear and multi-tiller traits, but marks that source as "Unpublished" -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 is not this page; the source is https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-026-00472-9
No QTL or marker studies for DFH-2 were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Shivam Yadav and N. K. Singh are the authors of the variety notification article -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
DFH-2 was developed at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, under AICRP on Maize, with no funding received during development -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Garhwal Post reports that the university's forage research programme received an ICAR best centre award, and that DFH-2 was the university's major achievement, notified and included in the seed chain -- https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/
Name discrepancy: the Springer article names the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties; the Garhwal Post names the Central Variety Release Committee -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 and https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/

CONTACT DETAILS
Shivam Yadav, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, G. B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, 263145, India (author affiliation; no email or phone listed) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
N. K. Singh, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, G. B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, 263145, India (author affiliation; no email or phone listed) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Official email: No evidence found
Phone: No evidence found
Institute or AICRP contact page URL: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
Yadav, S., Singh, N.K. (2026). Pant Forage Maize Hybrid-1 (DFH-2). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding, 86, 258–259 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 (DOI 10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4, taken from the URL; not separately printed in the results)
Authors not identified in the search snippet (2026). Wild relatives enhance genetic resources for maize (Zea mays ssp. mays) improvement through diversity analysis. Springer -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-026-00472-9 (lists DFH-2 only as an unpublished reference; not a DFH-2 study)
No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports or conference papers on DFH-2 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
The Garhwal Post states DFH-2 has been included in the seed chain -- https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sale or private dealer listing for DFH-2 was found.
Note: the seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1" returned only a different extra-early hybrid (EH-series, 2004 release, Rajasthan/Gujarat/MP) in the AICMIP list -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf. It is not this variety and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified for cultivation in the Northern Western Zone (Uttarakhand plains, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) and Central Zone (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Notification number S.O. 4388(E) is dated 08/10/2024 in the source, while the record's year_of_release is 2024-08-02. The notification date should be checked against the Gazette before the record is finalised -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (EH-number, 2004 release; this is NOT the -2 entry): reported as moderately resistant to stem borer -- Pratap Hybrid 1 (2004), pedigree EI-116 x EI-364, MPUA&T Udaipur, average yield 45 q/ha, moderate resistance to stem borer. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389) drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (2004): moderate resistance to stem borer -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (AICMIP 2000+ hybrid table): listed as white semi flint, moderately resistant; the disease-rating text is truncated in the extract -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: extra early maturity, recommended for Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, in kharif -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: AICMIP table gives an average yield of 3.8 t/ha (2004 entry, extra early, kharif) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: ResearchGate compilation gives 45 q/ha. This conflicts with the AICMIP 3.8 t/ha figure, and the two sources may not refer to the same trial basis -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No trial or yield evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 pedigree (EI-116 x EI-364) is the only parentage found; it is not verified for the -2 entry -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- QTL or marker studies for Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing centre for Pratap Hybrid 1 is listed as MPUA&T Udaipur (Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Institution for Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: not specified in the release record; the -1 centre above is the only institutional link found and is not confirmed for -2.
- Lead breeder names for either entry: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder names, roles, emails, phones, postal address for MPUA&T Udaipur maize division or any institute contact page: No evidence found. Searches did not return an institute contact page. No contact details were invented or inferred.

PUBLICATIONS
- Dass, S.; Karjagi, C. G.; Kumar, Bhupender; Jat, S. L.; Parihar, C. M.; Kumar, Ramesh; Kamboj, M. C. (2015). Single Cross Hybrid: A Potential Technology for Boosting Maize Production. Bibliographic record supplied by ICAR (journal not stated; general review, does not name Pratap Hybrid Maize-2) -- https://agris.fao.org/search/es/records/64747348bf943c8c79830277
- Author not given (year not given). Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010). Compilation listing Pratap Hybrid 1 (2004); no -2 entry seen in the extract -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Author not given (2010). A Compendium of maize hybrids and composites of India under PPV & FRA, Technical Bulletin No. 2010/4, pp. 84. Extract names other Pratap entries; no -2 entry seen -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
- Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, or DOIs specific to Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389): No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 or -2 from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, or verified dealers: No evidence found. Dealer listings returned were generic hybrid maize sellers with no link to this variety, so they were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh (kharif) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: the ResearchGate compilation lists J&K, Uttarakhand, NE hills, HP and Assam, which conflicts with the AICMIP entry -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found. The CSC release record's "Not specified" is unresolved.

NAME AND SCOPE NOTES
- Every item above refers to Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (2004 release, EH-number not confirmed), not Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389, 2010). No source found for the -2 entry or for the code EH-1389.
- The Seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 -Male" may be a labelling error. The evidence supports -1 but says nothing about a male parent line.
- Four searches were run. Coverage is limited: the AICMIP and ICAR-linked sources are the most authoritative results, and the remaining sources are secondary compilations. Verify against the Seednet portal, MPUA&T Udaipur, and the CSC minutes before relying on this record.

basic_info.institution: Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics, PAU

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to this hybrid. The only trait noted in the PAU Kharif package is that it is male sterile and medium tall, so it needs no detasseling. This does not indicate drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to this hybrid.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to this hybrid.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to this hybrid. Dr Tosh Garg's PAU profile lists waterlogging tolerance as a breeding goal for maize in general, not for this hybrid.

disease_resistance.summary: No variety-specific evidence found for disease resistance. The PAU Kharif package lodging and stalk-rot note refers to a different, unnamed hybrid and is not attributed to Punjab Baby Corn 1. A Tribune article states that the husk protects baby corn ears from insects and diseases; this describes a property of the crop product, not a tested resistance in this hybrid.

pest_resistance.summary: No variety-specific evidence found for pest resistance. The only related statement is the crop-level Tribune note that the husk protects baby corn ears from insects, which is not a tested resistance for this hybrid.

agronomic_details.yield: PAU Kharif package: average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears (approximately 20.8 q/ha by conversion at 2.471 acres per ha). This is close to the CSC-recorded average of 21.1 q/ha (CSC record is the ground truth). The PAU figure is for dehusked ears; the CSC basis is not specified. Fodder yield is about 128 quintals per acre after picking (Farming Cosmos).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Punjab (PAU and state variety approval committee). Agro-climatic detail beyond the state level is not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in the CSC record. Crop duration for the baby corn crop is about 60-65 days (PAU Kharif package). Ear picking starts about 52 days after sowing.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Male sterile hybrid; medium tall; no detasseling needed; about three pickings per plant; higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears (Farming Cosmos). Spacing conflict not resolved by the digest: PAU package gives 60 x 15 cm; a Tribune article gives 30 cm rows with 20 cm plant spacing. The PAU package is the official package-of-practices source, but the conflict remains unresolved. Seed production: sow seed crops in the second fortnight of July to first week of August, and plant the female line 3-4 days after the male (PAU Kharif package).
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location or field trial results for this hybrid were found. The only performance statements are the PAU Kharif package average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears and the Farming Cosmos description of higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears; neither reports trial data, sites, or replications.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. The pedigree I 193 (female) x LM 13 (male) comes from the input data and was not verified by any search.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL, marker or genomic study on Punjab Baby Corn 1 appeared in any result.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Punjab Baby Corn 1 (CSC name) / Punjab baby corn 1 (JH 32434) (Seednet name)

Name note: None of the four searches returned a Seednet portal page, and no result mentioned the code JH 32434 or the CSC release minutes. All evidence below refers to the variety name "Punjab Baby Corn 1". The release date of 2022 and the Punjab recommendation are confirmed by PAU and press sources, not by Seednet or CSC minutes. The parentage (I 193 female × LM 13 male) came from your input and was not confirmed by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE (Punjab Baby Corn 1): No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this hybrid. The only trait noted is that it is male sterile and medium tall, so it needs no detasseling -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Ancillary: Dr Tosh Garg's PAU profile lists waterlogging tolerance as a breeding goal for maize in general, not for this hybrid -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=564&intDepTitleID=&intLinkID=9

DISEASE AND PEST (Punjab Baby Corn 1): No variety-specific evidence found for disease or pest reaction. The PAU Kharif package's lodging and stalk-rot note refers to a different, unnamed hybrid in that section, so it is not attributed here -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Crop-level only: a Tribune article says the husk protects baby corn ears from insects and diseases, but this is a property of the crop product, not a tested resistance -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (Punjab Baby Corn 1): The PAU Kharif package gives an average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears for this hybrid and says it is one of the suitable hybrids for baby corn -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Harvest timing: ear picking starts about 52 days after sowing, with about three pickings per plant, and fodder yield is about 128 quintals per acre after picking -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Crop duration: the baby corn crop is completed in about 60-65 days -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Ear quality: the hybrid is described as giving higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Spacing (conflict to resolve): the PAU package gives 60 x 15 cm -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; a Tribune article gives 30 cm rows with 20 cm plant spacing -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/
Seed-production practice: sow seed crops in the second fortnight of July to first week of August, and plant the female line 3-4 days after the male -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Multi-location or field trial results for this hybrid: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genomic study on Punjab Baby Corn 1 appeared in any result. The pedigree I 193 × LM 13 is not verified by search.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Institution: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana. The 2022 release was approved at the state variety approval committee meeting for field crops, chaired by the Punjab director of agriculture -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Date: PAU's own update is dated 26 March 2022 and announces the new maize and black gram varieties -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/new-varieties-of-maize-and-black-gram-released-by-pau/1129
Lead breeder for this hybrid: not confirmed. Maize-section staff named in PAU sources are Dr Surinder Sandhu (Principal Maize Breeder, in charge of the maize section), Dr Tosh Garg and Dr Rumesh Ranjan (maize breeders). The sources do not say which of them led this hybrid -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/pau-commercialises-maize-hybrid-with-andhra-pradesh-based-firm-639085/ and https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/
Garg's profile says he has been involved in developing 19 maize varieties, including speciality corn, but does not list which ones -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=564&intDepTitleID=&intLinkID=9

CONTACT DETAILS:
Dr Tosh Garg, Maize Breeder, Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics, PAU -- Office phone 0161-2401960 (extension not given); mobile 91 9041504496; email gargtosh@pau.edu -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=21&intFacultyID=564&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=
Dr Surinder Sandhu, Principal Maize Breeder and in-charge of the maize section -- email surindersandhu@pau.edu (as printed; the PDF text is broken at this point) -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/pau_faculty_directory.pdf
Dr Rumesh Ranjan, Maize Breeder -- email not clearly extracted; the directory gives a partial street address, 1923/2 Street No. 4 -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/pau_faculty_directory.pdf
Institute level: Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics, PAU, Ludhiana. Postal address and general phone not found; no official department contact page with full details appeared in results. Department page: https://pauwp.pau.edu/plant-breeding-genetics-academic-programs/

PUBLICATIONS:
Sidana, B. K., Priscilla, L., Kaur, G., and Vatta, K. (n.d.). Potential of Maize Crop for Sustainable Agriculture in Punjab. ISADP publication. Mentions Punjab Baby Corn 1 in passing among PAU releases since 2005; the year is not shown in the result -- https://www.isadp.in/publication/download-pdf/241
PAU. (2026). Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab, Kharif 2026. PAU report, containing the variety description and seed-production notes -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Peer-reviewed or AICRP/ICAR paper on Punjab Baby Corn 1: No evidence found. KrishiKosh thesis: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
PAU seed sale counter at the Ludhiana campus, open year-round -- https://pau.edu/dirseeds/
Seed also sold at PAU Krishi Vigyan Kendras, Regional Research Stations and University Seed Farms, and at a PAU outlet at NDRI Karnal -- https://pau.edu/dirseeds/
Kisan Melas at seven locations each kharif and rabi season, where seed is sold -- https://pau.edu/dirseeds/
Advice for certified seed: source hybrid seed from PAU or the Punjab State Seed Corporation, and obtain fresh female and male parent seed from PAU each year -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Private dealers or NSC stock for this hybrid: No evidence found. The Seednet portal was not searched directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
Punjab: recommended by PAU and approved at the state variety approval committee -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/ and https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Central notification under the Seeds Act: a Ministry notification of 8 October covering 201 entries was reported, but this result does not name Punjab Baby Corn 1, so it is not confirmed here -- https://www.uniindia.com/north-india/agri-north-seeds-hybrids/207702
Other states: No evidence found.
